generated_text: Honestly, I’m shattered. Little Leo kept me up half the night. He’s decided 3am is playtime, apparently. How was your night, then? Did you manage to get any peace with the teens glued to their screens? Peace is a strong word. More like…contained chaos. Emily was attempting TikTok dances until midnight which, honestly, is a miracle given how much homework she claimed she had. And Ben… Ben was arguing with someone online about, I kid you not, the correct way to load a dishwasher. Teenagers. What  is  it with dishwashers? Oh, don’t even. Remember when Sarah was convinced the washing machine ate her favourite sock? She was  convinced  there was a sock-eating monster living in there. It turned out it was stuck inside a duvet cover. Oh my god, yes! She was heartbroken. They're so dramatic at that age. Speaking of dramatic, Auntie Brenda is already on about visiting for Leo's birthday. She called me  this morning . It hasn't even been decided  if  we're having a party yet! Brenda and her “dropping in”. Honestly, she’d move in if she thought she could get away with it. I've told her we’ll let her know. I think a small gathering is all I can handle. Between work and a little one… it's exhausting. Did you finish that report for that client? The Henderson one? Almost. Just need to proofread it tomorrow. It’s been a nightmare, though. They keep changing their minds about everything. I’m starting to think they don’t actually know what they want! It’s making me question all my marketing choices, honestly. How’s your proofing going? Any particularly awful errors to share? Oh, you wouldn't believe it. I had a website blurb that read "We provide exellent service."  Exellent . With an 'x'. And the client insisted it was correct. Apparently, they'd hired someone who "knew about spellings." I had to gently… suggest a correction. Sometimes it’s just soul-destroying. People are unbelievable. It’s like they think spelling is optional these days. You're a lifesaver, you really are. So, birthday plans... I was thinking maybe a little woodland themed thing? Leo seems to be obsessed with squirrels at the moment. Oh, that's lovely! He  is  a little squirrel himself, scrambling everywhere. That sounds brilliant. We could do it in the garden, weather permitting?

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of paperwork just to get the van across the Dutch border was unbelievable. Like, three different stamps, two separate forms asking for the same information, and a guy who looked deeply offended when I didn’t know the exact weight of the camping stove. Oh, the joys of post-Brexit travel. Sounds about right. I thought the Italians were bad with their ZTLs - Limited Traffic Zones - but that Dutch bureaucracy sounds on another level. We were nearly fined in Florence last year, you know. Completely missed the sign. ZTLs are a nightmare! We hit one in Siena. Luckily, the hotel rang ahead and sorted it, but the threat of a hefty fine hanging over your head takes the fun out of gelato, doesn’t it? But honestly, it's not just the fines. It's the  effort . Before, it was just…go. Now it feels like applying for a visa every time you want a weekend in Belgium. Exactly! Remember when we just used to drive to France on a whim? "Fancy some wine and cheese?" "Yeah, let's go!" Now you're planning it like a military operation. Passports, insurance, pet passports if you've got the dog, vehicle logbook… it’s exhausting. And then you get there and everything’s more expensive. Don’t even  start  me on the expense. We budgeted for, like, a standard European road trip. Everything was working out nicely until we hit Germany. Petrol prices are ridiculous! And having to pay tolls everywhere… It adds up, massively. I was expecting a bit of a price hike, but it’s genuinely impacting where we can go. It’s hitting students hard, I reckon. My flatmate was trying to get back to Spain to see his family over Christmas, and the flight prices were astronomical. He ended up having to Skype them, which he was gutted about. He’s doing his PhD on EU-UK relations, the irony isn't lost on him. That's awful. It feels…unfair, doesn’t it? Like, we voted for something, and now young people are having their opportunities limited. I'm lucky, I can absorb some of the extra cost, but it’s still a pain. You remember backpacking around Interrail when we were students? Those days are gone, aren't they? Pretty much. Although, I’m thinking of trying to salvage something of that spirit next summer.

…and honestly, the sheer audacity of you two trying to bankrupt me on Boardwalk  again ! It's just not fair play, is it? I barely had a chance to build anything! But Mummy, it  is  fair! You landed on my hotel three times! Three! It’s just…luck. Yeah, luck! And I helped Lily get hotels! We’re a team! You’re just…bad at Monopoly. Bad at Monopoly? I’ll have you know I used to routinely defeat Auntie Maureen at this game. Routinely! This is a conspiracy, I tell you. A tiny, adorable conspiracy. Though, I suppose talking about it won't get my money back. Speaking of which… anyone fancy cheering themselves up with a proper dessert? I was thinking sticky toffee pudding. Ooooh! Sticky toffee pudding! With custard? Please, Mummy, with  lots  of custard! I want ice cream! Chocolate! And sprinkles! Okay, okay, settle down you two. We can have both. Sticky toffee pudding  with  custard for Lily, and chocolate ice cream with sprinkles for Finn. Though, after being rinsed in Monopoly, I’m starting to feel like I need to ration the sprinkles. They’re expensive, you know. They represent hard-earned cash! But Mummy, sprinkles are  joyful ! They’re not about money! That's a very philosophical point, Lily. Very philosophical. Alright, joyful sprinkles it is. But we are talking about money, aren't we? This game is all about managing resources. Like real life, actually. It teaches valuable lessons. Like how to take all of Mummy’s money? That’s… one lesson, yes. A slightly harsh one. More like learning to save, to invest, to anticipate your opponent’s moves. Though mostly, it seems to be about Lily and Finn ganging up on me. We just want to be good at the game! And winning is good! Winning  is  good… within the rules of fair play. Although, honestly, I think you two deliberately landed on my properties. You had that gleam in your eyes. A very calculating gleam. It was a happy gleam! Because we were going to win! A happy, calculating gleam. Right. Well, dessert is going to be ready soon. And maybe, just  maybe , after we've all had something sweet, I can convince you both to play a less… financially aggressive game. Perhaps Snakes and Ladders? Snakes and Ladders is  babyish ! Yeah! Monopoly is way more fun! Especially when you get to charge rent!

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of data is mental. Like, I thought my dissertation was bad, but this is a whole different level. It’s just…text, after text, after text. All needing tagging for sentiment, for named entities, for… everything. It's draining the life out of me, pet. Sounds…thorough. A bit beyond just, you know, reading a load of tweets, is it? What  is  the data even  from ? You’ve been so secretive. Secretive? I just don't wanna bore you with corpus linguistics, love. It’s from online mental health forums. Anonymised, obviously, but still. People pouring their hearts out, and I'm categorising their despair into neat little boxes. Feels a bit…icky, sometimes. Icky? I can see that. So, like, they’re researching trends in online mental health expression? Trying to see what language people use when they’re struggling? Precisely. They’re hoping to build some sort of AI that can flag potentially at-risk users. So, pre-emptive support, theoretically. But it feels really… reductionist, doesn’t it? Boiling down complex emotions to keywords and phrases. Yeah, I get that. Sounds a bit dystopian, actually. Like ‘Minority Report’ but for anxiety. Still, at least it’s  trying  to do something good, right? Better than just passively collecting data. That’s what I keep telling myself. It's just... the users, they're so vulnerable. And reading some of it… proper heartbreaking stuff. One thread was about a bloke his dog had just died, and he was absolutely gutted. And there I am, tagging it as “loss/pet” and “negative sentiment.” Oh, blimey. Right, yeah, that’s rough. You’re not analysing the person, though, are you? You're just… processing the  words  they use. It’s the algorithm that's doing the judging, not you. I know, I know. I’m trying to separate myself from it. But it’s hard. It's a lot easier when it's articles about biscuit recipes, which I did some of last month. "Chocolate chip," "crumbly," "delicious" - much more pleasant, you know? Definitely more pleasant. Though, to be fair, your biscuit tagging probably contributed to a national increase in biscuit consumption. You’re a powerful woman, you are. Don’t be daft. I just labelled some ingredients. Although, I did make a very detailed note on the varying levels of ‘crunch’ in different brands of digestive biscuits… for research purposes, naturally.

…and honestly, Doreen, I’m telling you, the price of a pint these days! Back when I was a student, you could get a perfectly good pint for, oh, I don’t know, a shilling? Maybe two. Now it's… scandalous. Simply scandalous. A shilling, eh, Arthur? You’re showing your age now, lad. I remember when it were sixpence! Sixpence for a good, strong bitter. And you got change back! Times change, Arthur, times change. Though I’ll grant you, it  is  getting a bit…steep. You two and your reminiscing about old money. Honestly. It was all a bit grim back then, wasn’t it? Rationing and everything. I remember my Nan saving dripping. Dripping! And we were supposed to be grateful for it. A pint of beer was the least of anyone’s worries. Grim? Now, Doreen, I wouldn't say grim. Austere, perhaps. But there was a sense of community, you see. Everyone pulling together. You don't get that much anymore. Everyone’s too busy staring at their little screens. He’s got a point there, Doreen. Used to know everyone on the street. Now, you barely nod to the next door neighbour. They probably wouldn’t even notice if I dropped down dead on the doorstep. Oh, don't be dramatic, George. Mrs. Higgins would notice. She's got eyes like a hawk, and she loves a bit of gossip. Though, I have to say, I do miss the days when people actually  talked  to each other rather than just texting. My granddaughter, little Lily, hardly looks up from that phone of hers. It's the world we live in, I suppose. All this… technology. I tried to get my head around this 'internet' thing, but it just baffled me. Took me a week to work out how to send an email. And then I accidentally sent it to everyone in my address book. Twice. Oh, Arthur, you and your emails! I remember that. You were sending pictures of your prize-winning marrows to the local vicar! They  were  prize-winning marrows! And Reverend Thompson is a lovely chap. He appreciates a good vegetable. Honestly, it was the auto-complete. Keeps suggesting “Reverend Thompson” no matter what I’m trying to type. You’re both impossible. Honestly. Speaking of marrows, did you get any seeds for this year, George? I was thinking of trying to grow some again.

…and honestly, the packaging is  still  giving me grief. I thought sourcing recycled cardboard would be straightforward, but finding boxes that are the right dimensions for the serum bottles  and  don’t look like they’ve been through a warzone is proving… challenging. Seriously, I spent two hours yesterday measuring everything and cross-referencing with suppliers. Ugh, packaging. The bane of my existence too. Remember when I was trying to get the right sized boxes for the earrings? Ended up having to buy a whole load too big and stuff them with shredded paper. Wasteful, but hey, at least they arrived in one piece? What dimensions are you looking at? Maybe I can offer some insights from my learning curve. It’s frustrating! The bottles are… let me check my notes… 30ml, so roughly 3.5cm diameter, 8cm high. I need something that allows for a bit of padding, obviously. I was thinking maybe a 5cm x 5cm x 10cm box? But then that feels a bit… wasteful space-wise. And it needs to go through Royal Mail, so weight limits and size restrictions are another headache. Right, okay. 5x5x10  does  sound a bit roomy. Have you looked at those shallow, book-style boxes? Might be a good fit for height, and you can get them in different lengths. And seriously, don't underestimate the power of good tissue paper. Makes everything look premium, even if the box isn't perfect. Did you factor in the extra space for any leaflets or a thank you note? That’s what tripped me up initially. No, you're right about the leaflets! I'd completely forgotten that. I’m planning on including one with information on the ingredients and how to recycle the packaging. That adds another centimetre, easily. Book-style boxes… hmmm, hadn’t thought of that. I was so fixated on the traditional cardboard box shape. I’ll have a look. How’s Honest Skincare generally doing? Have you had a good week for sales? It’s been… steady. A bit quiet after the initial launch buzz, to be honest. I'm thinking I need to ramp up the Instagram marketing. I did a few reels, but no real engagement. I feel like everyone's already seeing  so  many beauty products pushed at them, it's hard to cut through the noise. I was thinking of maybe doing a little giveaway?

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of it! Claiming it was a ‘misunderstanding’. A misunderstanding that cost Mrs. Higgins her entire pension, more like! I read about it in the paper this morning – that investment scam targeting pensioners. Dreadful, simply dreadful. Good heavens, Doreen, you’re all fired up already? It  is  awful, I agree. They really prey on the vulnerable, don’t they? I saw a bit on the news about it. Apparently, they’re very sophisticated now, sounding completely legitimate on the phone. Sophisticated doesn't excuse it, Arthur! It makes it  worse . When I was teaching, we had a whole unit on critical thinking, on questioning everything, on not taking things at face value. It feels like no one’s learning those lessons anymore. Did you hear they’ve arrested someone, a young man, apparently? Yes, a chap in Manchester, I believe. Though whether he's the mastermind or just a foot soldier, who knows? It’s a long shot getting the money back, though, isn't it? I worry about Old Man Hemmings down the street. He’s terribly trusting, always letting anyone help him with anything. He is, isn’t he? A lovely man, but…easily led. I’ve tried to gently steer him towards the Citizens Advice Bureau, but he just waves it off, says he can handle things. Men! Honestly, sometimes they’re just so proud. You’ve been married to one long enough to know, haven't you? Speaking of which, how are things going with the flat? Any luck with finding someone reliable to look after it when we’re away? That’s what’s been bothering me, actually. Old Mrs. Peabody, bless her, offered, but she’s getting on a bit herself. I wouldn't feel right asking her to deal with any potential emergencies. And young Emily, the girl from next door… well, she’s lovely, but a bit…scatterbrained. I found her watering the garden with washing-up liquid last week! Washing-up liquid?! Oh, Doreen! You could not make it up. Perhaps we should just forget about going to Spain this year? It's not the end of the world. Don’t be silly, Arthur. We’ve been planning this for months! It’s just… stressful, finding reliable help. It's not the money, you see. It’s the thought of something going wrong while we’re gone. The flat holds so many memories, doesn't it?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Brussels sprouts my mother insists on buying is criminal. It's like she’s expecting a small army to descend on Boxing Day. Do you think she secretly enjoys watching us all politely choke them down? Aye, sounds like your mam. Mine’s obsessed with parsnips. Every year, it's ‘the perfect parsnip roast’ and every year they’re slightly burnt on the ends. It’s tradition, I suppose. Is it freezing out there still? I nearly skidded coming up the drive. It  is  properly Baltic. I checked the forecast, and it’s going to be sub-zero tonight. I’ve got the heating on a timer, but even so, my flat’s a bit of a fridge at the moment. Honestly, I'm starting to think I need a new boiler, or at least some serious draft excluders. It's costing a fortune just to keep it vaguely habitable. Tell me about it. My workshop is…brutal. Stone floor, high ceiling, loosely fitted doors. I’ve got a little wood burner, but it takes  ages  to warm the place up. Thankfully, I’m mostly building things in there, keeps me moving. Speaking of building things, anyone else been thinking about…well, you know…the “R” word? Retirement? Rhys, you're barely thirty! I know, I know! But I was talking to Old Man Hemmings down the lane, and he was saying how he wishes he’d started planning earlier. He’s got a garden full of greenhouses now, but regrets not having started beekeeping years ago, or learning to do proper stonework. Got me thinking, you know? About what I want to be  doing  when I can’t realistically spend ten hours a day tinkering with wood. I think I'd just like to not have to answer emails for a while. Honestly, the technical support side of things is draining. People and their printers, eh? It’s a constant battle. Though, I've been saving up for a decent metal lathe. Always wanted to learn to turn. That’s cool! I'm trying to finish my PhD, which feels like a full-time job in itself, but afterwards… I’d love to get into permaculture. Grow all my own food, be self-sufficient. Maybe even have a little orchard. Ooh, an orchard! That sounds idyllic. Actually, talking of fruit… the mulberries in the garden are going mad this year.

Honestly, Mum, the cutlery is…a choice. Is this the “special occasion” set? Because it feels a bit mismatched. I mean, forks from one set, knives from another? She’s got a point, love. Remember when we came last Christmas and you ended up with a teaspoon for your roast potatoes? Now, now, don’t be like that! I’ve got perfectly good cutlery. It’s just…over the years, things get…used. And a few pieces go missing. You know how it is. People borrow things, don't bring 'em back. Aye, that's the truth. Lost more spoons than I care to remember in my time. Though, to be fair, mostly to the dog when I was a lad. Old Buster had a penchant for silver polish, he did. Dog ate the silver... sounds about right. Back in my day, we didn’t  have  silver. We were lucky to have enough metal to poke at our dinners with. A good solid fork was a luxury. Right, okay, historical perspective acknowledged, Grandad. But seriously, Mum, where  do  all the spoons go? It’s a universal mystery. It’s like socks in the washing machine. Your Auntie Brenda. She ‘borrowed’ a whole set for a garden party years ago. Never saw them again. I asked politely, of course. Several times. But Brenda’s…Brenda. Speaking of Brenda, is she still going on about her prize-winning petunias? She cornered me for a good twenty minutes at Sarah’s wedding. Oh, God, yes. The petunias are a national treasure, apparently. Though I think she’s slightly revised the story to claim they won an  international  competition now. Brenda always was a storyteller. Remember that time she told everyone she’d met Richard Gere? Turned out it was a bloke who  looked  a bit like him from the bus stop. She’s a character, that Brenda. Keeps us all entertained. Though, I still say, a good solid fork is more important than prize-winning flowers. Now, don’t start on me about Brenda again. Honestly, you lot! It's nice to have a bit of colour in life. Anyway, did you hear about old Mrs. Higgins next door? Her grandson's finally getting married. No! That's lovely. She's been talking about it for ages. Is it the one who moved down to London? That's the one. He’s a lawyer now, can you believe it?

Honestly, this meeting today… it was  endless . Old Mr. Henderson droning on about synergy and ‘thinking outside the box’. As if we haven't heard it all before. Is synergy like… when you build with Lego? Because then all the bricks work  together ? That’s… actually a pretty good analogy, love. A surprisingly good analogy. Though Mr. Henderson probably wouldn't appreciate it being explained by a seven-year-old. It’s supposed to mean everyone working together, making things better. It rarely works like that, though. It usually just means more meetings. Oh. Boring. Are we closer to going skiing now? Much closer! I finally managed to book the ski school for you. They said you're a fast learner from what I told them about your rollerblading. I  am  a fast learner! Faster than Leo at school, definitely. He still falls over just walking. Will I get a cool helmet? One with stripes? We can absolutely get you a cool helmet with stripes! Perhaps even one with little reindeer on it, if you like. I’ve been looking at some online. Though we need to make sure it fits properly when we get to the shop. Reindeer would be awesome! And a fluffy neck warmer, please. It gets  so  cold when you go fast. Consider it done. I’m starting to get excited myself, actually. It’s been ages since I’ve been on the slopes. Remember that time in Austria… When Daddy fell over and did a snow angel? That’s the one! He was not amused at the time, but now he laughs about it. Are you worried about falling over? A little bit. But I’ll be brave! And the ski instructor will catch me, won’t she? She definitely will. They're very good at that. They’ll start you off on the gentle slopes, just getting used to balancing. It’s all about practice. It’s not about being perfect straight away. Like learning to ride my bike? I fell over a  lot  then. Exactly like learning to ride your bike. Lots of little falls, then suddenly, you’re zooming along. It's the same with skiing. Listen, about work… I think I need to have a word with Mr. Henderson. He keeps piling things onto my plate. Is your plate full of peas? You’re not eating your peas. No, my  work  plate is full.

Honestly, Food Tech is  killing  me. Mrs. Davies is obsessed with soufflés. Soufflés! Like, who even  makes  soufflés regularly? It's so stressful, getting the eggs just right. And if it doesn’t rise, she looks at you like you’ve personally offended her ancestors. Oh my god, tell me about it! I thought we’d moved past basic baking. I mean, last week it was choux pastry.  Choux pastry , Liv! It’s all so fiddly. I almost cried when mine collapsed. At least you get soufflés, though. I was assigned éclairs. They looked…sad. Sad éclairs? That’s a very poetic description. But yeah, soufflés are just pressure, pure pressure. And then she’s going on about ‘aeration’ and ‘folding’ like we’re all applying for jobs at a Michelin-star restaurant. Speaking of jobs… have you thought any more about what you want to do? My mum keeps bringing up being a vet, but honestly, I’d probably faint at the sight of a needle. Ugh, mums and their aspirations. Mine’s got me earmarked for law. Apparently, being good at arguing with my brother is a transferable skill. Which is…fair, I guess. But I’m leaning towards something more creative, maybe journalism? Though then everyone says it’s a dying industry. It’s impossible to win! What about Spanish? Are you still thinking about maybe doing that A-Level? I am! I think so. Miss Rodriguez is so good, and I actually enjoy the classes, which is rare for me with languages. I’m just…worried about the maths side of things. Like, will it actually  help  with anything? I’m already struggling with quadratic equations. Mr. Henderson makes it sound like rocket science. Oh, don't even get me  started  on Mr. Henderson. He explains things like we’re all miniature versions of Einstein. It’s infuriating. Spanish is good though, isn’t it? Apparently, it’s really useful if you want to work in…well, pretty much anywhere. And it's just…cooler than French, right? No offence to the French teachers, but… Absolutely cooler. Plus, think of the travel possibilities! Spain, South America… I saw this documentary about Patagonia and it looked incredible. And if I actually became fluent, maybe I could work as a translator? That’s a job that doesn’t involve needles  or  soufflés. Now  that's  a plan. Better than arguing in a courtroom any day.

Honestly, darling, this lot. All explosions and no story. Remember proper films? When you actually  thought  about things afterwards? Gran, you say that about every film that isn’t black and white and starring Cary Grant. It’s just…times change. People want different things. Different things? They want noise! They want flashing lights! It’s all just spectacle. I tried to watch one of those superhero things with young Timmy last week – honestly, my head was swimming. Who’s fighting who? Why are they fighting? It was all just…  bang !  crash ! Okay, fair enough. They  are  a bit much. But there’s some good stuff out there now. Have you seen 'Past Lives'? It's…really lovely. Quiet, you know? Bit melancholy. 'Past Lives'? Sounds a bit depressing, doesn’t it? I prefer something with a bit of…pizzazz. I saw ‘Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again’ last year, and that was fun. A bit silly, granted, but fun. All that singing… reminds me of my youth. That  is  a good one. ABBA’s timeless. But 'Past Lives' isn't depressing, exactly. It’s just…real. About choices, and what could have been. It won loads of awards. Awards don’t always mean good, love. They just mean somebody’s got good PR. I mean, have you seen what they give awards to these days? It’s scandalous. Remember when they gave that Oscar to… oh, what was his name? The one who kept winning, and then turned out to be… never mind. Okay, okay, point taken. The Oscars can be a bit dodgy. But honestly, Gran, you should give it a go. It’s not all doom and gloom. It’s beautifully shot, the acting is brilliant… You're very persuasive, you are. Remind me, what's it  about  without giving away the whole plot? I don’t want spoilers. I might actually give it a watch if you can hook me with a good description. I've got a box set of 'Call the Midwife' waiting, you know! That's quality telly. Right, okay. It’s about two childhood friends who are separated when one's family emigrates from South Korea. Then, decades later, they reconnect. It’s about this idea of 'in-yun' - like, destiny, connection… it’s hard to explain. It’s not a big action thing, it's more…feeling. ‘In-yun’… Sounds a bit foreign for my liking.

Honestly, Mum, this traffic was  horrendous  getting up here. Took me nearly two and a half hours. What is it with Birmingham drivers? They seem to think indicators are optional extras. Oh, you always say that, love. It's just… busy, that's all. And you're coming in from the south, which is always a nightmare. Did you at least put the radio on? Helps pass the time. Though what they  play  on the radio these days… I did, but it was all that auto-tuned stuff. Gave me a headache. I switched to a podcast about linguistics, actually. Quite interesting – looking at the regional variations in pronunciation of ‘bath’ apparently. It’s fascinating how much that one word can give away about where someone is from. Bath. Honestly. All that fuss about how you say a word. I say 'barth', always have. My mother said 'barth', her mother said 'barth'. Never caused anyone any harm. More important things to worry about, like young Daniel and his driving test. Oh, how did that go? You said he was taking it this week. This morning. He  passed ! Can you believe it? First time. He was over the moon, practically bouncing off the walls. Your father’s already talking about taking him to buy a proper car, not one of those little runarounds. That’s brilliant news! I’m so pleased for him. He’s been so anxious about it. What did he say when he found out? And what ‘proper car’ are we talking about? Something sensible, I hope? Sensible isn't a word in your father’s vocabulary, dear. He’s eyeing up a sporty little number. I put my foot down though, said it needed to be insured properly. Those premium prices are ridiculous these days, aren’t they? Especially for young drivers. It's daylight robbery. It is. It’s partly risk, but also just… exploiting a captive market. I've been looking at car insurance myself, actually. Thinking of getting something a bit more practical now I’m doing more travelling for work. The little Fiat's getting a bit cramped with all the teaching materials. You still enjoying the language teaching, then? Still surrounded by teenagers? That sounds exhausting. It's challenging, definitely. But rewarding. I've got a really good group at the moment. And I’m starting to work on a little project – developing some online resources for students who struggle with pronunciation.

Honestly, the students were  exhausting  today. You wouldn’t believe the questions about Foucault. It’s like they haven’t read a single word of ‘Discipline and Punish’ but expect me to summarise the entire philosophical undercurrent in a ten-minute Q&A. Sounds about right. Mine were obsessed with Baudrillard and simulations. I swear, half of them think reality  is  a simulation and are just trying to ‘break the code’ during their essays. It’s… creatively frustrating. Did you manage to get through to at least  some  of them? A few. There’s this one, Mei, who’s genuinely engaged. She actually asked about the connections between Foucault and the surveillance state here in China, which was brilliant. It moved beyond just regurgitating textbook definitions. But the others… it felt like talking to a brick wall. Anyway, enough work talk. Are we still on for that market trip on Saturday? I really need some proper teabags. These local ones just aren't cutting it. Absolutely. Saturday is good. We can hit up that market near the Silk Street – the one with all the slightly-dodgy-but-amazing knock-offs and the really good tea stalls. Though you’ll have to brace yourself for the bartering. They’re ruthless. Ruthless is my middle name. Actually, it's Elizabeth, but ruthless sounds better. I also need to find a new scarf. It’s starting to get a bit chilly in the evenings and I left my favourite cashmere one back in Norwich, of all places. Utter disaster. Norwich! You’re still mourning that scarf, aren’t you? Honestly, you treat that thing like a lost limb. We could look for one at the market, but they might not have the… quality you're after. Maybe we should brave AP Plaza? It’s a bit more touristy, but they have some decent cashmere stalls. AP Plaza… hmm. It's a bit of a scrum, isn’t it? But you're right, the quality is usually better. And maybe I can pick up some decent biscuits for my parents. They’re obsessed with British biscuits, poor things. They keep hinting I smuggle them in. Smuggling biscuits. That’s a new one. They love you, though. So, market Saturday, then maybe AP Plaza? We could grab lunch somewhere in between, that little dumpling place near the Lama Temple is supposed to be amazing. Dumplings sound fantastic!

…and honestly, the way Leo was attempting to ‘help’ with the icing sugar earlier, I was anticipating a kitchen covered head-to-toe. It looked like a blizzard in here for a minute! It  was  fun though, Mummy! I made a snow angel in the flour! I tried to make a dinosaur! But it collapsed. It was a very sad dinosaur. A very sad dinosaur indeed. Well, we salvaged most of the cake, didn’t we? It’s not exactly winning any baking awards, but it’s edible. Right, let’s talk logistics. Auntie Sarah’s offered to have you both on Saturday night, which is amazing, because I desperately need a night with Ben. But…she wants to know what time works best. Can we stay at Auntie Sarah’s  all  night? And watch films? And can we build a fort? A really,  really  big fort! We'll see about all night, you two. We’ll need to consider bedtime. But a fort and films sound brilliant. How about I drop you off around six? That gives her plenty of time to settle you in and get dinner sorted. And I can pick you up Sunday afternoon? Six is okay. Can we take Dino with us? And Captain Calico! They need to come to the fort! Dino and Captain Calico are welcome. Though Auntie Sarah might complain if they require their own chairs at the dinner table. Speaking of which, what are we having for dinner tonight? I was thinking spaghetti bolognese. YAY! Bolognese! Can I help stir? You can definitely help stir! But maybe  after  we’ve finished reading? I promised you both another chapter of ‘The Owl Who Was Afraid of the Dark’. Oh yes! The Owl is so silly. He keeps bumping into things. He does, doesn’t he? Now, before I forget, Ben’s mate, Mark, is coming over next week. He's a photographer. He offered to do a family photoshoot. A photoshoot? Like a proper one? A proper one! He said he'd love to get some nice pictures of you both. But it means we’ll need to think about what we’re all going to wear. And potentially… haircuts. Not haircuts! I  like  my long hair! It’s for being a princess! I don’t mind a haircut. It’s getting in my eyes when I’m building. We can discuss the haircuts later.

… honestly, the library is a  state  right now. Like, people are just setting up camp for the day. Full on picnics, the lot. It’s meant to be a quiet study space, innit? Not a social club. Seriously? It's always bad during deadlines, but picnics? That’s next level. Is it the same in the Penrhyn Road library? Because I’ve been mostly sticking to that one, it's a bit further but generally calmer. Nah, it’s the one over by the Business School. Apparently, there’s a new module everyone’s struggling with, so they’re all ‘collaborating’ which basically means gossiping and eating crisps. Honestly, the rustling… the crunching… it’s enough to drive a girl mad. I just want to finish this essay on post-structuralism in peace! Oof, post-structuralism. Sounds…fun. I’m currently wrestling with marketing. It’s surprisingly boring. Everyone thinks it’s all Mad Men and cool ad campaigns, but it's mostly spreadsheets and market research. Though, I did find out the average Brit spends like, six hours a day on social media. That’s depressing. Six hours?! Blimey. Explains a lot, though, doesn’t it? Speaking of depressing, this canteen food is… questionable. I think that pasta looked back at me. Don’t even  start  me on the canteen. It's like they deliberately try to make everything grey and flavourless. I brought a packed lunch today, thankfully. Adobo, my Nan sent me some. You want a bite? It's proper good. Adobo? Go on then, don’t mind if I do! Ooh, that smells amazing. Proper home cooking, eh? Beats this beige sludge any day. What  is  this stuff anyway? It’s supposed to be a tomato and basil pasta. Looks more like tomato and… sadness. Yeah, Nan’s the best. She always makes a massive batch whenever I come back from Uni. Says I look too skinny. Classic Nan move. She’s always bringing me stuff. Last time it was a whole mango, still rock hard! I felt bad asking her to cut it. Oh, Nans are the best. Mine just keeps trying to set me up with the sons of her friends. “He’s a  lovely  boy, works in finance!” Like, no thank you, Brenda. I'm trying to understand Derrida, not discuss interest rates! Oh my god, that's so cringe! You need to go into hiding when she starts that.

Aye, honestly, this weather is deffinitley not helping with holiday planning. I was looking at Greece, right? Thinking Santorini – all those white buildings and blue domes, lovely. But apparently, it's roasting over there. Like, genuinely  roasting . Roasting is an understatement, I saw a news report. Forty-something degrees! You'd melt. We were toying with Spain, but that's pretty bad too. I'm starting to think a week in Scotland might be the most sensible option. Though, knowing our luck, it’ll be the only week all year with sunshine. Scotland’s not a bad shout, actually. I did a project up near Inverness a couple of years back. The scenery is incredible, and the pubs… well, the pubs are a definite bonus. Though, trying to explain to the locals what a ‘consultant engineer’  actually  does was a challenge. They mostly just thought I was a fancy electrician. Oh, I can imagine! You get that a lot, don’t ya, with fancy jobs? I just tell people I organise words. “Corpus Administrator” means absolutely nothing to anyone, so I just simplify it. Keeps things easy. It’s not exactly setting pulses racing, is it? Like, ‘Oh wow, you work with  language data !’… Na. My uncle always asks me if I design bridges. Like,  every single time . I build bits of infrastructure, mostly drainage, ironically. Not particularly glamorous. Speaking of glamour, have you guys seen that new show, “Glittering Shores”? It’s dreadful, but I can’t look away. "Glittering Shores"? Is that the one with the ridiculously tanned people and implausible plot lines? I caught ten minutes of it while channel hopping the other night. It was… something. My mum’s completely hooked though. Says it’s “a delightful escape”. Oh god, yeah, that one! It’s pure escapism, isn’t it? But the dialogue… it's like it was written by an AI. “But darling, my yacht needs polishing!” Honestly. It’s terrible, but I watch it with a pizza. That’s the key. Pizza is  always  the key. Speaking of pizza, have you guys tried that new Italian place near the market? "Bella Notte"? It’s run by this amazing nonna who just yells at you if you ask for pineapple on your pizza. No, haven't heard of it. Sounds… authentic. I’m a purist, myself. Margherita or Marinara, that’s all you need. Anything else is just showing off.

…Honestly, Doreen, this telly’s gone right rubbish again. Keeps pixellating during the football. Can’t see a thing! Remember when you could get a decent picture on anything? Proper valve sets, they were. Oh, don’t start on the telly, Arthur. You say that every single match. It’s not  that  bad. And honestly, valve sets? You make it sound like the dark ages. I used to enjoy a good programme, myself, before all this… streaming nonsense. Though, I must admit, ‘Bake Off’ is still alright. Morning, you two. What’s the crisis now? Telly again, Arthur? You’d think after seventy-odd years you’d be used to a bit of static. It’s not  a bit  of static, David! It’s like looking through frosted glass! And it’s a matter of principle, innit? Paying all this money for a service and getting a picture a sparrow couldn't make head nor tail of. Remember when we talked about going back to London? Do you think we should book something? London? Oh, Arthur, that’s a big ask. All that travelling. Remember how tired you were after just getting to the garden centre last week? Though, a theatre trip  would  be nice. I’m happy to drive you both. I’ve got a couple of days free next month. What were you thinking of seeing? And are you still thinking of that youth hostel in Cornwall for later in the year? I reckon it would be good for you both, get you out and about. Cornwall sounds… bracing. Too many young folk for my liking, though. And London… well, I’d like to see those horses at the races again. Remember that chestnut mare, Doreen? Lovely animal. Made a right killing that day. Though, selling the house wouldn’t have happened if I’d kept betting like that! That house! Honestly, Arthur, you and your ‘investments’. Luckily, David helped us get a good price. We were getting nowhere on our own. And then buying  this  place… it was a gamble, wasn't it? Needs a bit of doing up, this one. It’s got good bones, that’s what matters. And the garden's a good size. Easier than that postage stamp you had in Costessey, eh, Arthur? Speaking of selling, I'm thinking of updating my car. Something a bit more fuel-efficient. These petrol prices are criminal.

…and honestly, the amount of unsolicited advice is  exhausting . Like, everyone is a baby expert the second you announce you’re pregnant. Aunt Carol cornered me at Christmas and went on for twenty minutes about how bottle feeding is “just not the same” as breastfeeding. As if I hadn't researched both! Oh, don't even  start  me on Aunt Carol. She tried that with me too, with Leo! Said I was ‘robbing him’ of antibodies. Honestly, the guilt trip. It’s relentless. And you're a Research Administrator, you’re practically drowning in data, you’ve probably read all the studies! She thinks she knows better because she had three kids in the seventies. Exactly! It's infuriating. And it’s not just her. My mum keeps sending me links to articles about baby-led weaning, then simultaneously worries I won't give the baby enough purees. Make up your mind! Do you find it hard ignoring it all? Hard? It’s a superpower I’ve had to develop. Especially with my mum. She means well, she really does, but she was a completely different generation. Everything was done a certain way then, and she struggles to understand that things have moved on. With Leo, she’d constantly be saying “He needs warming up!” like he was a car engine. Oh my god, that’s brilliant. I can see your mum saying that. Mine keeps asking when I’m going to start ‘proper’ weaning. The baby’s seven months old, she's happily mushing avocado and sweet potato, what does she mean ‘proper’?! It’s the phrasing, isn’t it? It implies what  you’re  doing isn’t good enough. Honestly, sometimes I just nod and smile and then do exactly what I was planning to do anyway. How’s little Eliza doing with feeding? Is she taking to solids okay? She’s… a bit ambivalent, to be honest. She'll try a mouthful of something, then immediately decide she wants a nap. Or to gum my hand. I think she’s more interested in the experience of  playing  with the food than actually eating it. Which is apparently perfectly normal, but still feels a little stressful. That sounds exactly like Leo was! He used to launch purees across the room. It was a nightmare. We ended up having a dedicated ‘messy play’ bib just for mealtimes. Don’t stress too much, they all find their own way.

Honestly, did you  see  what happened with the water bill this month? It’s astronomical! I swear, someone must be running the taps all day. Astronomical, you say? Let me have a look. Blimey, you’re right. Nearly double what it was last quarter. Have you checked for leaks, Sarah? Remember that dripping tap in the bathroom we meant to fix? Could be the garden, actually. Dad, you were going on about giving everything a really good soak last week with that new sprinkler system. Maybe it was on longer than you thought? Oh, yes, he was! He was so proud of getting it all set up. Said it was “like a miniature rain forest” out there. It  was  quite impressive, I’ll give him that. Although, I did think he left it on a bit late one evening... Now, now, don't gang up on me! I was just trying to keep the petunias happy. They looked a bit droopy. And honestly, a bit of rain never hurt anyone. Though, you’re right, it might’ve been a bit… enthusiastic. Enthusiastic is one word for it. It's enough to give someone a shock when the bill lands! Anyway, what are we all up to today? I’ve got a particularly full shift at the hospital. Old Mrs. Higgins is being difficult again, and apparently, young Master Thompson has decided he  doesn’t  want his injections. A typical Saturday, really. I’m meant to be cracking on with that campaign brief for 'Coastal Living' magazine. They’re wanting a ‘Kentish summer’ vibe – ironic, given this weather! I might head down to Folkestone for some inspiration, see if I can get some decent photos. I’m on my study day. Dr. Davies wants me to focus on wound care protocols. Thrilling stuff, I know. I might pop into the library afterwards, although I suspect it’ll just be me and a couple of students. I’m tackling the garage. It’s become a bit of a black hole in there. Honestly, I’m surprised the house hasn’t started leaning to one side with all the junk we’ve accumulated. I think I unearthed a cricket bat from my school days last time I ventured in. Oh, that garage! Don't get started. We really need to have a clear-out. You keep saying you'll do it, David, but then you just seem to rearrange things… Sounds like a classic Dad manoeuvre!

Honestly, this physics test tomorrow is  brutal . Mr. Davies is just… sadistic, isn’t he? He expects us to know everything about electromagnetic induction! It's just… so much. Tell me about it! I spent all of Saturday trying to get my head around it. Mum tried to explain it, using, like, magnets and wires and… I still felt more confused. Honestly, I think I'm just going to write down everything vaguely related and hope for partial marks. Have you finished the art project yet? That’s due on Wednesday, right? Nearly! I’ve done the initial sketch, it’s a bit messy still, but it’s the botanical illustration, remember? All those ferns and stuff from Gran's garden. Speaking of which, she’s already put up her Christmas decorations! I popped over there after school on Friday. It's a full-on festive explosion already. No way! Already? Gran is  always  the first. Last year she had the tree up in November! It’s a bit early, isn’t it? Though, I will admit, it’s nice. Makes you feel a bit… cosier. I'm supposed to be helping Mum with the Christmas lists tonight. She wants me to think of actual  useful  things this year, not just Ed Sheeran merchandise. Oh, the pressure! Trying to be practical at Christmas is a crime. Though, I did ask for that new watercolour set. That’s… kind of useful for art, right? It's a good excuse. Have you started thinking about what you want to do for your GCSEs? Ugh, don't even  mention  GCSEs. It feels so far away and terrifying. I’m pretty sure I’m sticking with English Lit and History. But I’m seriously wavering on Maths. I just… don't  get  it. You’re so good at it though, aren’t you? I'm alright. It's just practice, I think. I do my homework straight after school and Gran helps me sometimes. She used to be a maths teacher! She’s brilliant. She collects stamps too, did I ever tell you? Has like, albums and albums of them. It’s a bit… niche. Stamps? Really? That  is  niche! Gran's hobbies are usually more… gardening related. She was showing me her new winter-flowering heathers on Friday. Apparently, they're called ‘Calluna vulgaris’. She knows the Latin names for everything. It's impressive, but slightly intimidating.

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  the face young Thomas pulled when I showed him Reginald. Absolutely priceless! He thought Reginald was a proper, live rat at first, you know. A proper little squeaker. Oh, Arthur, you and your puppets! Reginald, was it? Sounds… charming. Though, a live rat  would  be a bit much for a little’un, wouldn’t it? Still, good to see you’re keeping busy. It’s better than moping, that’s for sure. Morning, you two. Heard mention of a Reginald? Sounds like classic Arthur. Keeping the little ones entertained, are we? Though I suspect entertaining  you  with Reginald is half the battle, Arthur. Now, now, George. Don't you go getting cheeky with me. Reginald is a sophisticated fellow. He understands existentialism, you know. Or at least, I make him  seem  to. And Thomas, he’s a lovely boy. My great-grandson, of course. Always a pleasure. He is a sweet boy. Reminds me a bit of my grandson, Liam, when he was that age. Always getting into mischief. Speaking of which, Arthur, you were saying something about going for an eye test? Did you manage to book an appointment? Your reading seems to be getting worse, dear. Oh, that. Yes, I phoned up Specsavers. Dreadful hold music, it was. Nearly sent me to sleep. Got an appointment next Tuesday. They said they’ve got some fancy new machine that does all sorts. Says it can tell if you’ve got glaucoma or something. Sounds terrifying, doesn’t it? Glaucoma’s easily managed if they catch it early, Arthur. Don't go borrowing trouble. Good on you for going though, it's important. I had mine checked last month. Everything’s still remarkably intact, thankfully. Allows me to continue enjoying my Sudoku. Sudoku! Pah. Give me a good crossword any day. Now  that’s  a proper test of the ol’ grey matter. I’m trying to get back to handbell ringing, you know. But it’s proving… challenging. Can't quite make out the numbers on the music sheets. Oh, the handbells! I always enjoyed hearing you practice. It was so peaceful. But with your eyesight, Arthur, is it really sensible to carry on? You'll trip over something or bump into Mrs. Higgins. Mrs. Higgins is a hazard to navigation  regardless  of my eyesight, Doreen. Honestly, the woman’s a whirlwind! No, I’m being careful.

…and honestly, that lecture on post-structuralism just fried my brain. I swear, Professor Davies  enjoys  watching us suffer. Right, caffeine is a necessity now. This latte is already doing wonders, though. So, you got anything planned for today, Auntie Val? Aside from, you know, bringing life into the world? Oh, don't I know the feeling about those academics! They think we all have time to dissect Derrida whilst juggling life. No, thankfully a relatively quiet day. Just a couple of home visits, checking on new mums. It’s lovely, truly, but draining. I was thinking after that, maybe we could actually  do  something with the day? You suggested Venice, and I realised I haven’t properly explored it in years. Not since…well, not since your Grandad was still around. That’s a brilliant idea! It feels ages since we’ve just, you know,  done  something properly. And you're right, Grandad loved this place. He used to bring me here for chips when I was little. Do you remember how different it was then? It was proper bustling, wasn’t it? Not all fancy Italian restaurants and boutiques. Oh, bless him. He always had a soft spot for this end of town. You're spot on, love. It was all chip shops, newsagents, and that horrible betting shop on the corner. And Mrs. Higgins’ sweet shop, of course. That was the best bit. Venice was  our  Venice back then. Everyone knew everyone. Now it’s…well, it’s trying to be something it’s not, isn’t it? Little Italy in Bolton. Exactly! It’s lost some of its grit, hasn’t it? Though, I’m not complaining about the Italian restaurants. I’m craving a proper carbonara, actually. We could do that for lunch? There's that little place, 'Bella Notte', everyone says is authentic. Oh, Bella Notte  is  lovely. Their tiramisu is to die for. Your Grandad would have scoffed at it though, wouldn't he? “Too fancy,” he’d say, before polishing off a portion of mushy peas. He wasn’t one for sophistication. No, definitely not. Mushy peas were his culinary peak. After lunch, maybe we could walk along the canal? I was reading about the history of it, apparently it was built to connect the mills. It's a bit sad how neglected it's become. That’s a nice idea. It  is  a shame.

…and honestly, the leg press felt like it was going to swallow me whole. I swear, Dave loaded another plate on without me even noticing! My quads are still screaming. How was your session? Did you manage to actually  avoid  Mark trying to ‘spot’ you again? Oh my god, don’t even  mention  Mark. He literally hovered around the dumbbell rack for a good ten minutes just to be within a five-meter radius of me. I think he’s convinced I need constant supervision. I had to pretend to be on a very important phone call to escape. My session was… okay. Focused on upper body, felt a bit weak after that awful sleep I had. Work was manic yesterday, barely switched off. Speaking of switching off, this peri-peri chicken is  exactly  what I needed. Seriously! He's like a particularly persistent puppy. Just… leaves you alone! Glad you escaped. And ugh, work. Tell me about it. I had three deadlines loomING at once yesterday. Felt like I was just running on caffeine and sheer willpower. This is significantly better than the sad desk salad I was contemplating for lunch. So, are you still thinking about Portugal for your holiday? Portugal is still the plan, thankfully! Booked the flights last week, just need to sort accommodation. Found a cute little Airbnb in Lagos, looks right on the beach. I’m picturing lots of sun, sea, and… not Mark, thankfully. Are you doing anything exciting this summer? Still thinking of Interrailing? Oh, that sounds incredible! Lagos is beautiful. Very jealous. Interrailing is… complicated. I was super keen, but the cost is honestly terrifying. Plus, Chloe’s pulled out, says she needs to ‘save for a deposit’ – adulting, ugh! Now I’m not sure anyone else is really up for it with me. It's just not the same without a core group. That’s such a shame! Interrailing is one of those bucket list things, isn’t it? Deposits… the bane of our existence. Maybe you could try and find someone else to go with? There are always groups on Facebook and stuff. Or, you know, a solo adventure? It could be empowering! I’ve seen some of those Facebook groups, a bit intimidating, honestly. Feels like you need to be a seasoned backpacker already. And a solo adventure… maybe one day. I’m just picturing getting lost in Budapest with no one to blame but myself.

…and honestly, the sheer  weight  of it all. Holding little Leo for the first time. It just…rewrites everything, doesn't it? He was born in Paris, you know. Perfectly healthy, screaming blue murder – a proper little Brit abroad! Though, technically, a dual national, I suppose. A proper little cosmopolitan, then. Paris. Good choice, although I always said France is…complicated. They make a fuss about things we wouldn’t even blink at. Property there, for example. An absolute nightmare to navigate. All those  notaires  and endless forms. Oh, I gathered that. Sophie and Jean-Pierre have been banging on about it for months. They're trying to buy a small place in Brittany, a little  gîte  to restore. It's like climbing Everest made of paperwork! And the land – apparently, even getting permission to prune a rose bush requires three signatures. Precisely! And don't even get me started on enterprise. They talk a good game about supporting small businesses, but the bureaucracy is crippling. You’ll find an anarchist running a café one moment, and a bureaucrat demanding a permit for the awning the next. A strange mix. I had a rather unpleasant experience with one of their tax inspectors, years ago. A very stern woman. Sounds… stimulating. We had some French visitors staying last month, a couple from Lyon. They were utterly flabbergasted by London. Said everything felt… rushed. And the politeness! They kept expecting people to be more formally addressed. They were particularly baffled by the lack of bollards protecting pavements. Bollards! Don't  remind  me. I had a terrible argument with Mrs. Higgins about bollards last week. She wants them outside her gate to stop people parking, but young Timmy down the road cycles home from school that way. It’s a constant battle. Speaking of battles, did you hear about Chichester Cathedral? Dreadful business about the spire. Vaguely. Something about structural instability? It's a wonderful building. It's Porden's work, you know. The architect. Absolutely remarkable man. They're having an open day next month, a photo exhibition of the restoration work. I thought you might be interested. You always had a good eye. And there's an art competition linked to it, apparently. Local artists. That sounds lovely, actually. A bit of light relief from everything. Though, relief is the last thing we've had recently with this new landlord. They're supposed to be managing the estate, but it's a complete shambles.

Honestly, this sweet and sour chicken is…questionable. It tastes like it’s been swimming in ketchup. And is that pineapple? Seriously? Nah, it's alright. You’re just being a fussy eater, aren’t you, Liam? It's a bit sweet, yeah, but it's chips and chicken, what's to complain about? Besides, Auntie Mei always makes a good effort. Effort doesn’t always equal good, Raj. Remember her Christmas pudding last year? It was… dense. Like a brick. I think my Nan still talks about it. Oh god, the pudding! It nearly chipped a tooth. My mum had to discreetly hide hers in a napkin. Speaking of hiding things, how’s that history essay coming along, Liam? You looked proper stressed in school today. Don’t even  mention  the essay. Mr. Davies is expecting a dissertation on the causes of the First World War. A dissertation! We're sixteen, not PhD students. I’ve barely scratched the surface and it’s due next Wednesday. Wednesday? Oh, crikey. I finished mine ages ago. Just… summarized a few websites. Davies is a bit of a pushover if you use enough big words. You didn’t actually  summarize  websites, did you, Raj? You plagiarized, didn’t you? Don’t lie. I wouldn’t say… plagiarized. More like, heavily…  inspired  by. Anyway, it got an A-. Trust me, it works. You’re terrible. Truly terrible. I’m actually enjoying my food, though. These spring rolls are banging. Anyone want one? No thanks. I'm still trying to decipher the mystery sauce on these chips. It's… orange. It shouldn’t be orange. You know what else is orange? Ethan's face when Miss Johnson caught him trying to sneak out during double maths. Oh my gosh, yes! He turned the colour of… well, these chips! She gave him detention 'til the end of term. Served him right, the little rascal. He deserved it. He was trying to go and meet Chloe, apparently. Very dramatic. Honestly, the drama in our year is more exhausting than Shakespeare. Shakespeare is exhausting too, to be fair. Have you read  Macbeth ? It's just… murder, murder, murder. And witches. Yeah, but the language is amazing. "Double, double toil and trouble…” Gives you chills. Have you seen the new Batman comic? It's got a proper gothic vibe, reminds me of  Macbeth  actually. Ooh, is it good? I’ve been meaning to pick it up.

Honestly, Jonathan’s birthday… it just creeps up on you, doesn't it? Seems like only yesterday we were celebrating his fortieth. And now… well, now he's nearly halfway to sixty! Though he’d never admit it, the daft lad. Are we still thinking of that pub lunch, Margaret? The Black Bull’s doing that new menu.      Yes, Agnes, the Black Bull sounds lovely. I’ve provisionally booked a table for twelve. Though, knowing the family, twelve might turn into fifteen… young Thomas is a growing lad, isn’t he? And Edward always brings a friend.      It's not  always  a friend, Mum. Sometimes it's two. Liam and Ben both wanted to come. They said Uncle Jonathan lets them have extra chips.      Chips are a cornerstone of any respectable birthday celebration, Thomas. Though, speaking of stones… Agnes, have you started on that attic clear-out yet? It’s a bit of a disaster up there, and I need to get to the Christmas decorations. They're probably buried under a mountain of… well, everything.      Oh, don’t remind me, Edward. It's like excavating an archaeological dig up there. Boxes and boxes of things your father insisted on keeping. "Might be useful one day," he’d say. Useful for what, I never did find out. I started yesterday, found a whole collection of those old Cadbury's selection boxes… the ones with the proper caramel creams! They were practically fossilized.      Fossilized Cadbury's, you say? Sounds like somethin' you could sell on that 'Antiques Roadshow'! Everything's 'vintage' these days, Agnes, even sticky toffee.      Doris, you’re terrible! Though, you're right about the vintage thing. Everything’s ‘curated’ now. Remember when it was just called ‘old junk’? It’s all branding, isn’t it? Makes a difference to the price.      It absolutely is. And the price of  everything  is going up. I was at the supermarket yesterday, and a pint of milk is practically a luxury item. It’s ridiculous. Makes you long for the days when you could get a decent loaf of bread for a few pence.      You guys are ancient. Milk's, like, a normal price. Anyway, I was looking at these new gaming headphones online. They're supposed to have noise cancelling so you can really get into the game. They’re really expensive though…      Gaming headphones? Goodness me. When I was your age, we were happy with a wireless and a bit of imagination.

Honestly, I’m stressing about options week  so  much. It feels like everything hinges on what we pick now, doesn’t it? Like, if I don’t pick the right things, my entire future is ruined! Dramatic, I know. You're not wrong to be stressed, but ruined is a bit strong, don’t you think? Everyone changes their minds. Remember when you were absolutely convinced you wanted to be a vet and spend all your time with animals? Before you realised the… less glamorous bits? Oh god, don’t remind me. The  less glamorous bits  is putting it mildly! Honestly, the injection training video Mrs. Davies showed us… I nearly fainted. But still! This feels different. Like, choosing History or Geography actually feels… grown up. Grown up and terrifying. I’m leaning towards Art, but Mum keeps hinting I should do something ‘practical’. She keeps saying, “Think about jobs, darling!” As if Art doesn’t lead to jobs! Loads of people make a living off being creative, you know. Tell me about it! She's the same with my clarinet. "Lovely hobby, darling, but what about something you can  use ?" Ugh. Like music isn't useful! Have you seen the money some YouTubers make playing instruments? Exactly! Like, look at that girl, Clara Juno. She just plays ukulele covers and she's got millions of subscribers. Millions! Though, I did fall down a rabbit hole watching "day in the life of a digital nomad" videos and everything looks exhausting. Constant filming, editing, the pressure to be “on” all the time… It does look mental. I’d rather take my chances with GCSEs, honestly. Speaking of mental, PE is killing me. Mr. Harrison is  obsessed  with ‘perfect duty’ in netball. Like, what  is  perfect duty anyway? It's just running around aimlessly hoping the ball doesn’t come near you. It's a Cambridge thing, I think. Every sports teacher here is obsessed with some obscure metric. Remember when Mrs. Peterson tried to explain ‘optimal trajectory’ in rounders? I zoned out after ‘arc’. Oh, don't even start. It's just a game! Anyway, what are you thinking career-wise if you go for Art? Like, realistically? Honestly? I don’t know! I was thinking maybe graphic design, or illustrating children's books. Or even being a… a lifestyle blogger! Though I do worry about being another one of those people who just posts sponsored content for teeth whitening kits.

…and honestly, the state of that roundabout on the A47. Utter chaos, I tell you. They’ve redesigned it three times now, haven’t they? Each time, worse than the last. Used to be a simple thing, a quick loop. Now you’re dodging lorries and hoping for the best. Reminds me of the Roman roads, really. All that planning, all that engineering…and  they  still managed to get things wrong sometimes. You and your Romans, Arthur. Always back to the Romans. Though I’ll grant you, that roundabout  is  a mess. Spent near on twenty minutes trying to get onto the Drayton High Street last week. Dreadful. More to do with the speed of folk, if you ask me. None of ‘em seem to understand the concept of ‘give way’ these days. Oh, don’t even  start  on the driving, George. I had young Thomas’s mother, Sarah, moaning to me just yesterday about someone nearly running her off the road near Hellesdon. Says they were on their phone. Honestly! It's a miracle anyone gets anywhere safely. Though, speaking of journeys, did anyone see that documentary on badger setts? Fascinating. Actually, Mum, I did! The one with the thermal imaging cameras? They’re incredibly intelligent creatures, badgers. They plan their setts so meticulously. It’s almost… architectural. Which, I suppose, brings us full circle to Arthur and his Romans! See? I told you! They understood structure, you see. Proper foundations. These modern builds… flimsy, I say. Speaking of flimsy, I tried to get my printer to work again yesterday. Complete waste of time. That new software update has buggered it completely. Keeps saying ‘error 404’ or something. Utterly baffling. Error 404? Sounds like something out of a science fiction film. I gave up with printers years ago, Arthur. All that ink, all that paper… just a headache. I got myself one of them old-fashioned typewriters. Solid as a rock, that thing. Never lets me down. Although, I haven't used it much since… well, you know. I remember those typewriters, George. My father had one. Clickety-clack, clickety-clack all day long. He was a solicitor, always writing letters. Though, I’m more worried about the squirrels at the moment. They’re raiding the bird feeders again. Little bandits. I tried a squirrel baffle, but they just found a way around it! They’re resourceful, aren’t they?

…and honestly, Doreen, the state of them young’uns these days! Young Timothy next door, he tells me they're learnin’ about…  influencers  at school now. Influencers! What good’s that gonna do ‘im when he needs to change a washer on a leaky tap? Oh, Arthur, you and your taps! Everything always comes back to practicalities with you, doesn’t it? It’s a different world, love. Though I do agree it’s a bit… frivolous, isn’t it? My grandaughters are all on that ‘TikTok’ thing. I haven’t a clue what it  is , but they spend hours glued to their phones. Morning, you two. Influencers, eh? Sounds about right. I had a kid in my Year 10, absolutely convinced he was going to be a gaming streamer. Said his education was secondary to 'building his brand.’ Honestly, you try explaining the importance of fractions to someone who’s dreaming of digital fame. Fractions! Now  there’s  a useful thing. I remember old Mr. Grimsby, he used to make us work them out with apples. Real apples! Not these fancy electronic calculators. Though, I must say, I wouldn't mind a delivery of apples now, would you? Speaking o’ deliveries, had a right shambles yesterday. Delivery man tried to leave a parcel with Mrs. Higgins next door – she’s practically blind! Oh, that’s dreadful! They really do need to be more careful. They just ring the bell and disappear. I had a rather charming young man delivering my gardening catalogues last week, though. Actually stopped for a chat about roses. A rare treat these days. Reminds me, Arthur, have you finally tackled that wardrobe in the spare room? The one that’s threatening to collapse? Don’t you start on that wardrobe, Doreen. It’s structurally sound!… Mostly. Just needs a bit of… encouragement. A few well-placed wedges, that’s all. It's been there since before you were a twinkle in your mother’s eye. It's practically an heirloom! An heirloom held together with wedges. Sounds about right. It's like the NHS, really. Held together with goodwill and a lot of sticky tape. Speaking of which, did you hear about old Mr. Davies? They finally got him an appointment with a specialist, six months after the referral. Six months! It’s scandalous, isn't it? They say they're putting more money into it, but I don’t see any improvement.

Oh, look at it coming down now! Proper snow, this. Not that slushy stuff we got last week. It’s actually…pretty. Though, I’m having serious regrets about suggesting we repot the hydrangeas today. Hydrangeas can wait, love. Honestly, they’ll be fine. They’re hardy things. More importantly, this means potential for a  very  cosy night. Hot chocolate, terrible reality TV… possibly attempting to recreate a Come Dine With Me starter? Oh, don’t even  think  about it. Remember when we tried that Moroccan tagine? It nearly set off the smoke alarm and tasted… vaguely of burnt disappointment. We’re sticking to simple tonight. Though, Come Dine With Me is objectively brilliant. The drama! The passive-aggression! Absolutely. It's a sociological study disguised as a cooking competition. But seriously, the garden can wait. Think of the poor seedlings! Although, Mrs. Higgins next door is already out there, trying to build a snowman. She’s relentless. She  is , isn't she? She’ll be out there all day, layering that thing. Makes me feel guilty for just…watching. Though my back’s been playing up, so I’m using it as a legitimate excuse. Speaking of relentless, have you made any progress on booking anything for Ben's stag do? It's only, what, six weeks away? It's a battlefield, honestly. Everyone having very strong opinions. There's the "Paintball and pints" contingent, the "Escape Room and sophisticated cocktails" crew, and then Dave, who genuinely suggested a LARP-ing weekend.  LARP-ing . For Ben. No! Don’t tell me he's serious. Ben would be horrified. He’d rather spend the weekend alphabetising his spice rack. Thankfully, I managed to shoot that one down. I’m leaning towards a weekend in the Peak District. Hiking, pubs, maybe a slightly ridiculous outdoor activity like archery. It strikes a balance. What about Sarah's hen do? Have  you  had any input? Just a little. They’re thinking of going to Brighton. Loads of shopping, cocktails, and... karaoke. Which is my personal nightmare. I’ve volunteered to handle the decorations – safer territory. And I’m secretly hoping they’ll end up doing that ridiculous escape room instead. Anything’s preferable to listening to Sarah attempt Whitney Houston. Sensible. Brighton sounds…loud. Right, chocolate's ready. Snuggle up. We can finalize the ridiculously complicated spreadsheet of holiday options later. Remember that little cottage in Cornwall we looked at?

Now, this is a proper roast, this is. Not like that stuff they try to pass off in pubs these days. All gravy and no substance. Mind you, pubs ain’t what they used to be, are they? Used to be a proper bit of Norfolk beef you’d get. Oh, don't get me started, Arthur. You’re right. Everything’s pre-packaged now. No flavour. Your daughter, bless her, she does a good job, doesn’t she? Though I do miss your wife’s Yorkshire puddings. They were…well, heavenly really. Light as a feather. Thanks, Mum. I tried to follow Gran’s recipe, but it’s just not the same. She had a knack, didn’t she? I think it was the oven, honestly. This one just doesn’t get hot enough in the right places. It  is  a good roast, honestly, Sarah. Really well done. And the Yorkshire puddings are perfectly respectable! Don’t let your dad diminish your efforts. He’s just a connoisseur of Gran’s baking. Respectable? Respectable’s a polite way of saying “not quite as good!” No offence, love. Just stating a fact. Your gran, she used dripping. Real beef dripping. That's the secret, you see. None of this sunflower oil nonsense. I did use oil, actually. I’ve read it's healthier. Gran always used dripping, you're right, but… it’s a bit much for a modern diet, isn't it? Oh, a little bit of what you fancy does you good, dear. We all lived on butter and dripping as children and we turned out alright! Mostly. Though Arthur here’s always complaining about his cholesterol. I’m not  always  complaining! Just being sensible. Doctor keeps going on about it. He says I need to cut back on the rich stuff. Easier said than done when you’ve got a daughter who makes a lovely roast. It's a trap, I tell you! It’s a tricky balance, isn't it? Trying to enjoy good food while also looking after yourself. I mean, I lecture about nutrition all day, but I still have a weakness for a good pie. That's the thing. Everything becomes so politicised, doesn’t it? Eating is supposed to be pleasurable, but now it’s all about ethical sourcing, reducing your carbon footprint, healthy fats versus unhealthy fats… It's exhausting! Oh, don’t get me started on all that!

Honestly, Mum, this is  exactly  how my grandma used to make it. The seasoning is spot on. It’s a proper Sunday dinner, isn’t it? Not like some of the…attempts…I’ve seen while at Uni.      Mmmph. You’re right, it’s brilliant. So much better than anything I could manage. My flatmate tried to roast a chicken once. It was… a learning experience. Mostly for the smoke alarm.      Oh, you young’uns! You think you're clever, don't you? I remember when  your  Dad tried his first roast. Nearly set the kitchen on fire he did. Thought he could just leave it and go watch the footie!      Aye, that was a disaster. Maureen – that's your mother – she wasn't best pleased. The smell lingered for days. Though, to be fair, he’s a much better cook now. Mostly sticking to sausages and bacon, mind you. Can’t take risks with anything too complicated these days.      Sausages… good sausages. Used to get 'em from old Mr. Henderson down the street. Best pork sausages in Lancashire. He knew a thing or two about flavour, that man did. Not like this…processed stuff you get now.      Grandpa, you always have the  best  stories about food. Did you ever actually  cook  anything, or just expertly critique everyone else's efforts?      I made a mean stew, lass. A  mean  stew. With rabbit. Now,  that  was a proper meal. Needed a good day’s foraging for the rabbit, mind you. Don’t see folks doing that anymore.      Rabbit? Seriously? I don’t think I’ve ever even  seen  rabbit on a plate.      Oh, it was lovely! A bit gamey, but with dumplings… perfection. We had it quite often during the war, you know. Had to make do with what you could get. This chicken's a real luxury, mind.      Speaking of houses, have you two looked at those new builds down by the old mill? Apparently, they’re quite spacious. Might be a good investment, you know.      Dad, we’re trying to enjoy dinner, not talk about mortgages. We've barely finished paying off student loans! And honestly, those new builds all look the same. No character. I’d rather save for something a bit older, even if it needs work.      I’m with Amy on that one. I like a bit of history. Those new builds feel… sterile. Plus, the gardens are tiny.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of students just  expected  to passively receive information. It's like they’ve never been challenged to actually  do  anything with it. It reminded me of that viral video of the guy trying to explain basic physics to a group of…well, let’s just say not particularly engaged individuals. Hilarious, obviously, but a bit depressing when you think about it applied to higher education. Oh, the one with the water bottles and the reluctance to believe gravity exists? Yes, I saw that. Distressing, isn’t it? Though, I think you’re hitting on a core problem. We’ve created a system that rewards memorisation over application. My students at secondary level are starting to exhibit that, and the university lecturers I speak to are pulling their hair out. What did you have in mind, though? You were muttering about ‘gamification’ earlier while staring into the kangaroo-filled wilderness. Well, not  just  gamification, although that’s a part of it. Think back to when we were at uni, remember Professor Alistair Harding’s History lectures? Dreadful. Just…dates and names. He delivered them like he was reading a shopping list. But if he’d framed it as a detective story – 'solve the mystery of the missing treaty!' – even back then, I think it’d have resonated more. I’m thinking modules structured around real-world problems. Like, instead of ‘Corporate Finance 101’, it’s ‘Save this failing local business – develop a turnaround strategy.’ I like that! Problem-based learning is excellent, but it needs to be genuinely challenging, not artificially inflated difficulty. And it would require a complete overhaul of assessment, wouldn’t it? No more three-hour exams regurgitating facts. More practical simulations, group projects with tangible outcomes… Exactly! And scoring needs to reflect  effort  and  process  as much as the final result. Look at the start-up world. So much of success isn’t about having the perfect initial idea, it’s about how you iterate, how you pivot when things go wrong, how you collaborate. We need to build that into the curriculum. I was talking to Ben over in Sydney last week – he’s just launched a biotech firm – and he said finding graduates who can actually  debug a problem  is like finding hen's teeth. They can all explain the theory, but… …but they can’t actually  do . It’s the difference between knowing the rules of cricket and actually being able to bat.

…and honestly, the spreadsheets nearly defeated me today. Mr. Henderson wanted a pivot table doing  specifically  with conditional formatting based on… I don’t even know what anymore. It was just colour-coding chaos. How was your shift? Please tell me it involved less Excel and more… calming people? Oh, honey, you have  no  idea. It was…a lot. We had a patient experiencing a really intense panic attack, and then another convinced the pigeons outside were government drones. Honestly, spreadsheets sound positively relaxing right now. Did you manage to actually  eat  lunch amidst the chaos? You looked a bit peaky when I got in. Briefly. A slightly-squashed cheese and pickle sandwich at my desk. Peaky is a good word for it, actually. I’m thinking we  need  a proper meal tonight. Something…comforting. Perhaps a roast? It feels very autumnal, doesn’t it? Ooh, a roast is a brilliant shout! I’m happy to do the Yorkshire puddings, if you’re up for the rest? My nan’s recipe, you know, the one I’m convinced holds the key to world peace. You are a legend. Seriously. Okay, roast it is. We need to go shopping tomorrow, then. Speaking of tomorrow, any plans? I was thinking of heading down to Brighton for a bit, just to wander around the Lanes. Haven’t been in ages. Brighton sounds lovely! I’m on call all weekend, sadly. Just…existing in a state of readiness should someone have a crisis. Glamorous, I know. But you definitely go! Get some sea air. Maybe bring me back some rock? Though I’m trying to cut down on sugar…it's a losing battle with Halloween approaching. Right, Halloween. Are we doing anything this year? Last year was a bit…understated, wasn’t it? We carved a pumpkin and watched a scary film. Understated is putting it mildly! It was practically a quiet Tuesday evening. I was thinking maybe a proper party this year? Lisa from work is throwing one, a ‘Haunted Manor’ theme. Apparently, she’s gone  all out . It’s in…oh, what is that village just outside Tunbridge Wells? Penshurst, I think? Penshurst! I know it! It’s gorgeous. All those beautiful Wealden houses. Sounds amazing. We should totally go. Honestly, sometimes I forget how pretty Kent is. We’re always so London-centric. Exactly! It’s easy to get stuck in that bubble.

…Honestly, this is lovely. Proper quiet. Not like when your cousin Darren brings all the noise with ‘im, bless ‘is ‘eart. Remember ‘im tryin’ to fix that wireless last Christmas? Nearly took the whole house with ‘im! Oh,  god , Darren. Yes. That was…an experience. Mum kept saying, "Darren, dear, just  leave  it!" and he just kept insisting he knew what he was doing. It ended with Dad having to call an actual electrician on Boxing Day. Exactly! A professional! That’s what you need sometimes, love. Not everythin’ can be fixed with a bit o’ duct tape and a “can-do” attitude. Though your father, ‘e’s just as bad, tryin’ to mend things ‘round the ‘ouse. I swear ‘e makes ‘em worse just for the sake of havin’ somethin’ to do. He does, doesn’t he? It's a man thing, I think. The need to  fix . Speaking of which, I’m really stressed about this project at work. We’re launching the new line next month, and everything feels like it’s falling apart. Oh, dear. What’s up then? You usually ‘andle these things so well, you do. Always organised, you are - unlike Darren! It's mainly Mark. He's the lead designer, and he’s completely dropped the ball on the packaging approvals. They were due a week ago, and he’s just…not responding to emails. I’ve tried calling, but he’s “in meetings.” It’s all just a bit chaotic.
