Spends more time obsessing over his sleep score than actually sleeping! He nearly had a breakdown when it told him he’d been restless during a perfectly good night. Classic Leo. Always needing quantifiable data for everything. I’m more analogue, myself. Just… feel tired, go to bed. Though, I did see an advert for some sort of protein powder that claims to build muscle in your sleep. Sounds a bit dodgy, to be honest? Dodgy is an understatement. It's probably just glorified sugar. I'm convinced half these health products are just marketing hype. Reminds me of what my nan used to buy - miracle creams and tonics for everything. She swore by cod liver oil for her arthritis. Smelled dreadful, apparently. Crikey, nan's remedies are a whole other level. Mine just insists on sending me links to articles about the dangers of 5G. Says it’s turning frogs gay or something. It's exhausting trying to explain it's… probably not true. Oh, parents and the internet. A dangerous combination. Mine keep forwarding me chain emails about Nigerian princes needing help to transfer millions. I’ve told them a thousand times it’s a scam! It’s the sharing aspect that gets ‘em, isn’t it? They feel like they’re doing good, warning the family. Speaking of family, anyone hear from Ben recently? Haven’t seen him since graduation. Last I heard he was trying to get into coding bootcamps. Yeah, I messaged him last week. He's in Manchester now, doing one of those intensive courses. Says it's brutal, but he’s enjoying it. Apparently, he's living off ramen and ambition. Sounds about right for Ben. Remember how he used to live off Pot Noodles at uni? He’d have a different flavour for every lecture. It was a personal challenge, he said. Oh, good lord.

Right, so, shopping list. Mum, are we still needing bin bags? I swear we went through a pack in, like, a day last week. And milk, definitely milk - I’m practically living on cereal at the moment with these essays. Aye, bin bags, good shout, lass. And you’re right about the milk, your dad gets through that quick enough too. We’ll need bread, I think, and… ooh, some tomatoes for a salad. Did anyone spot any decent ones at the market on Friday? The ones at Smith’s were a bit mushy, Mum. Proper squishy. But they had loads of strawberries, really nice-looking ones. Though I probably ate half of 'em before we even got home. Sorry. Sounds like someone had a good Friday. Speaking of eating, we’re having a barbecue tomorrow, aren’t we? I volunteered to pick up the burgers and sausages. Anything specific anyone wants? Ooh, halloumi! Can we have halloumi? Please? I'm trying to eat a bit less meat, and halloumi on the BBQ is just… perfection. Halloumi it is. I’ll add that to the list. Now, before we forget completely... this blasted fly. It's been buzzing around for hours. I swear it’s mocking me. I tried to swat it earlier with me homework, but nearly took out the telly. Dad went absolutely mental. Flies are the bane of my existence. Aggressive little things. I have some fly spray somewhere, I'll look later. Though frankly, I’m more concerned about this mosquito bite I got on the golf course yesterday. It’s absolutely  massive  and itchy as heck. Oh, no way! You got bitten? You're usually covered head to toe in protection. What did you do? I thought I was! Apparently not effectively enough. I've put some antihistamine cream on it, and I've been trying not to scratch - a truly Herculean effort, I assure you. Dab a bit of vinegar on it, love. That takes the sting right out. Me grandma always swore by it. Works a treat. Better than any of those fancy creams. Vinegar? Really? That smells awful! Well, you don’t have to  drink  it, lad. Just a little dab. Actually, talking of awful smells...did you hear about the new signing for Bolton? Apparently, he’s brilliant, but his pre-match ritual involves a tin of sardines. No! You're joking!

Honestly, PE was  brutal  today. Miss Harrison really went for it with the shuttle runs. I thought my lungs were gonna actually explode. Did you have to do them too, Chloe? Ugh, don't even  mention  it, Maisie. I'm still recovering! She’s on a mission to ‘build character’ apparently. It feels more like building lactic acid. And then she made us do press-ups after! I could barely manage five. Five? I think I got to, like, seven before collapsing in a heap. It’s so unfair. Benji managed like twenty, showing off as usual. Honestly, he's got springs in his legs or something. Benji's just…Benji. Always gotta be the best. Speaking of unfair, did you hear what Mr. Davies said in Science? About the extended project? Oh god,  that . Yeah! He was going on about needing "original thought" and "deep research." Like, we're fifteen, not PhD students! What is he expecting, a cure for cancer? I’m thinking of just doing mine on the migratory patterns of garden snails. So low-stakes. Snails is good! Safe. I was toying with something to do with the psychology of colour, but then I watched a YouTube video about it and realised it’s way more complicated than I thought. Have you seen that new video from Kurzgesagt about dopamine? It completely messed with my head. Kurzgesagt is amazing but terrifying. Every time I watch one I feel like my brain is expanding and shrinking at the same time. Ooh, and have you seen what happened with that beauty influencer, Willow Bloom? She got called out for editing her photos  again . Oh, yes! The whole 'waist-snatching' scandal? It's ridiculous, isn't it? She's so pretty anyway! Why does she feel the need to change herself so much? It's so bad for girls our age, always seeing these unrealistic images. Exactly! It's exhausting trying to live up to that stuff. I spent like an hour yesterday just scrolling through Instagram and feeling rubbish about myself. Then I remembered I have a history test on Tuesday and suddenly Snapchat felt less important. Haha, relatable. Mrs. Peterson is going to  kill  us if we haven't revised. She was giving us the side-eye today in class. Did you notice? Like, she  knows  we were all chatting about TikTok instead of the Tudors.

Honestly, I feel  awful . Proper, head-splitting, can't-taste-a-thing awful. I think this is a proper cold, not just a bit of fluff. Oh, love, you do sound rough. Here, drink this lemon and ginger. Made it fresh. You were saying earlier you felt a bit off after that Thai green curry last week? Could be lingering effects, you know? Food poisoning can mess you up for ages. Aye, well, the Thai was lovely at the time… but now I’m questioning all my life choices. It wasn’t  immediately  after, so I didn't link it. Just gradually felt worse. It’s just the classic cold symptoms, really. Nose like a tap, throat like sandpaper. It’s just… draining. It is. Remember that time we both went down with that stomach bug after that dodgy pub lunch in York?  That  was truly miserable. Though, thinking about it, at least then we had a good story to tell. This… just feels dreary. Have you taken anything? Paracetamol? Aye, loaded up on the paracetamol. Makes a dent, but it comes back. Honestly, I’m worried this is going to knock me out for the week. I’ve got that big presentation to prep for on Thursday. It’s about the new body language recognition software we’re trialling. Oh, that sounds fascinating, actually! Is it working well? I saw something on the news about that sort of thing – a bit ‘Minority Report’ isn’t it? Detecting pre-crime based on facial expressions? It’s not quite  that  dramatic, thankfully. It’s more about analysing micro-expressions during interviews – helping to assess truthfulness, gauging emotional responses. It’s surprisingly accurate, if a bit… unsettling when you really think about it. It’s all based on algorithms, of course, but it makes you wonder what information we’re unconsciously giving away all the time. Anyway, try not to distract me with dystopian futures and focus on the lemon and ginger! Sorry, sorry. Just easily fascinated by that stuff. It's a bit like when we were kids and obsessed with surveillance cameras in public. Remember thinking every lamppost was hiding one? Speaking of TV, did you catch that new Lloyd Grossman show? Lloyd Grossman?! Is he still… doing things? I thought he’d retired to a quiet life of chutney-making or something. Actually, now you mention it, I think I saw an advert with him for… something.

Right. “Quixotic.” Twenty-two points. Honestly, I think I’m playing a better game than you two combined. Though, admittedly, having ‘Q’ is a bit of an unfair advantage. Unfair? It's a letter, Fiona! You just happen to have drawn it. And, frankly, I’m battling a truly appalling rack. A, E, I, O, U and… a Z. A  Z ! What am I meant to do with a Z in Scrabble? Oh, don't be such a grumble, Alistair. A Z is a challenge. It builds character. Though, I must say, Fiona  is  on a roll. It reminds me of when young Hamish used to play – ruthlessly strategic, that boy always was. Reminds me of Beatrice, actually. Always had a knack for spotting the double and triple word scores. Though, she’d spend ten minutes calculating just to eke out an extra point. Drove me mad sometimes! Oh, you two and your reminiscing. It's lovely, truly, but can we focus? I’m trying to strategically dominate this game. Speaking of dominating, did you see the absolute gridlock at the Trafford Centre yesterday? Took me an hour just to park! Don't even  start  on the Trafford Centre. I needed new laces for my trainers and it was… a battlefield. Honestly, it’s worse than trying to get a spot in the queue at Mr. Henderson’s butcher shop on a Saturday morning. Mr. Henderson does make a lovely black pudding, though. Worth the queue, I say. Though I did hear Mrs. Higgins complaining about the price of the lamb chops this week… Lamb chops are extortionate! I’m thinking of just sticking to chicken from now on. Though, I did see a rather tempting recipe for Moroccan tagine in that new food magazine… the one with Prue Leith on the cover. Prue Leith’s a sensible woman. Good, solid recipes. Not like some of the nonsense you see nowadays. All foams and deconstructions. Give me a good roast dinner any day. Speaking of sensible, I finally got around to subscribing to that classic rock magazine. The one with the long interview with Roger Daltrey. It’s been ages since I’ve properly listened to The Who. Oh, The Who! Good choice. I've been rediscovering Joni Mitchell lately. Absolutely brilliant lyrics. Though my daughter keeps showing me these…TikTok songs. It's just noise, frankly. TikTok? Is that one of these newfangled social media things?

Oh, this is lovely. Just what I needed. All that talk about bylaws and membership drives… gives me a headache, it does. Though, bless ‘em, they mean well, don't they? Proper dedication, these TME folk. Dedication and a fondness for detail, Margaret. A fondness for  excessive  detail, if you ask me. Still, someone has to keep the steam engines running, so to speak. Though I confess, I was thinking about Germany just now, listening to old Mr. Henderson drone on about insurance policies. Germany? Oh, go on then. You always had a fondness for a bit of foreign air, didn’t you, Arthur? What put Germany in your head? Were you remembering those printing exhibitions? Precisely! The IPEX shows, mostly. Though we did a few others. Goodness me, that feels a lifetime ago. You wouldn't believe the hoops we had to jump through just to get a decent stand. And the translation! Everything had to be in German, naturally. Though my German was limited to ordering beer and asking where the loo was, I’m afraid. Oh, I can picture you! You always were a practical man, Arthur. No time for fancy language. But you were brilliant at what you did, you know. Inventing those printing systems… truly remarkable. My late husband, God rest his soul, was always in awe of your ingenuity. He said you could practically  smell  a good mechanism coming. Your Thomas was a kind man. Always generous with his praise. And it wasn’t all me, you know. I had a cracking team. But yes, I did have a knack for seeing how things could be…  better . Faster, more efficient, less messy. And then convincing people they  needed  that better system. That was the real trick. Marketing, wasn't it? You always said it was half the battle. More than half, I reckon. A brilliant idea is no good if nobody knows about it. Did you find the Germans particularly… difficult customers? I always imagined they were very precise, very demanding. Precise? Margaret, you’ve hit the nail on the head! Demanding is an understatement! They wanted everything laid out, quantified, proven. No room for fluff. Which, in a way, was good. They forced us to be truly rigorous in our testing. And they appreciated quality. If it worked, truly worked, they’d buy it in their droves. I remember one year, we had a new rotary system… Oh, do tell!

Right, so Mr. Harrison  insists  we need to know the origins of ‘ubiquitous’ for the English Language A-Level. Like, seriously? Who cares where ‘ubiquitous’ came from when we need to understand postmodern literature? It's just… so much. Well, your Mr. Harrison sounds like a proper traditionalist, lass. He’s probably thinking understanding where words  come  from helps you understand how they work, how they’ve changed. It's a bit like knowing the history of a place helps you understand the people who live there now, isn’t it? Ubiquitous… Latin roots, that one. ‘Ubique’ - everywhere. Makes sense, doesn’t it? I suppose. It still feels like a waste of time when we've got stuff on Derrida to read. Honestly, deconstruction is a lot more…relevant. Derrida! Right. Sounds complicated. Still, a bit of Latin never hurt anyone. Speaking of complicated, are you sure we’re going the right way? This looks a bit…rural. We should’ve hit the M5 by now, shouldn’t we? Dad! I set the satnav! It said take this route to avoid the traffic around Bristol. And honestly, it’s nice to see some proper countryside after Manchester. It’s practically all concrete there. True enough. Concrete jungle. Still, I’m already picturing a service station coffee. They’re not exactly gourmet, are they? But they do the job. Fancy stopping at Gloucester Services? I’ve heard they’re alright. Gloucester Services is supposed to be amazing. Dad, can we  please  go there? Apparently, they have a proper farm shop. Maybe we can get some of that…quinoa stuff Mum’s been on about. Quinoa. Don’t even mention it. It looks like birdseed. And tastes a bit like it, if I’m honest. But alright, Gloucester Services it is. Speaking of farms and things…did you see that bike race was on in Yorkshire last week? Vaguely. Mum was obsessed. She kept saying the scenery was gorgeous. Something about rolling hills and dry stone walls. She's right. It's beautiful up there. Reminds me of some of the bits around here, actually. It’s a shame about all that rain though. Proper thunderstorm. Did you see that lightning strike near Bolton last week? Lit up the whole sky. I did! It was scary. I always get a bit squeamish with storms. It's stupid, I know, but the noise… No shame in that.

Right, so I reckon we’ve got enough veg for a proper Yorkshire pud feast, even if yer Southern softies aren’t used to proper portions. Though, honestly, this kitchen is lovely, proper modern. Not like me mam’s, bless her, still got an Aga that could roast a whole hog. Yorkshire puds, eh? You bringin' that up already? I’m already feelin’ inadequate. Mum’s roasties were always the thing, always crispy. And don’t start on the Aga, my Nan had one. Thing was a furnace, honestly. You could iron your clothes on it. Oh, Agas. A menace and a blessing all rolled into one. Your mothers both sound like proper characters, the two of ‘em. Keeps you on your toes, mothers do. Though, I confess, I never did get the hang of cookin'  on  one. Always felt a bit intimidated. Intimidated? It’s just…heat, innit? Me mam used to say it had a ‘personality’. Would sulk if you didn’t treat it right. She made the best crumble though, seriously. All golden and bubbly. You’d forget it tried to burn down the kitchen every other Tuesday. Speaking of which, Jamie, you alright choppin’ onions? You’re lookin’ a bit watery-eyed there. Yeah, yeah, just… these onions are  strong . It's nothin’. I'm a labourer, I deal with tougher things than onions, believe me. Although, actually, concrete dust is probably easier on the eyes. What about your family, Anon? They all doin’ alright back in West Sussex? Haven’t seen your mum and dad for ages. They're… managing. Dad’s arthritis is playin’ up something awful, keeps him housebound more and more. Mum’s takin’ it hard, naturally. Used to be the pair of ‘em were always out gardenin’ or visitin’ the village. It’s quiet now, very quiet. She’s got a cleaner comes in twice a week, bless her heart, but it’s not the same as bein’  useful , you know? She always needed to be useful. Oh, that’s rough. Tell ‘em I said to look after themselves, alright? It’s awful seein’ folks lose their spark. Me granddad, he was always fixin’ things, buildin’ sheds, always busy. When he couldn’t do that anymore… well, it wasn’t him anymore, really. I send ‘em a box every month, with biscuits and tea, little things. Keeps me feelin’ like I’m doin’ somethin’.

…and honestly, the shift last night was  mental . Stag do. Absolute chaos. They were all trying to order different cocktails at once, shouting requests… It aged me about ten years, I swear. How was your weekend, actually? Anything less… enthusiastic? Significantly less enthusiastic, thankfully. Grading essays. The glamorous life of a language teacher. Though, honestly, after a week of teenagers attempting existential French poetry, a noisy stag do sounds… almost appealing. Did anyone at least  tip  well for the trauma? A couple did, yeah. Enough to cover the extra caffeine I needed this morning. You teaching A-Levels then? That sounds…intense. I remember French being a right pain at school. All the genders and agreements… brain-melting. What are you teaching, specifically? Mostly A-Level, yeah. And a bit of GCSE. This lot are doing the poetry unit. It's Baudelaire, mostly. They  think  they're being profound when they just haven't grasped the subtext. It’s… a process. What did you study at uni, out of curiosity? Apart from mastering the art of cocktail making, obviously. Haha, that was a… supplementary course. I did History, actually. Surprisingly useful for remembering obscure facts to impress pub quiz teams. It was alright, although I’m not doing much ‘historying’ these days, am I? More like ‘pint-pouring’. Thinking about doing a bit of further study, maybe, but I haven’t a clue what. History’s good. Solid foundation for, well, thinking critically. And it's surprisingly adaptable. Further study… that’s interesting. What kind of things are you considering? And is it something you’d do alongside work, or are you thinking about a career change? Don’t know, honestly. Thinking maybe something law-related? A friend of mine’s doing the GDL – Graduate Diploma in Law – and says it’s hard work, but rewarding. But it feels like a big leap. I’m alright where I am, you know? Pays the bills, keeps me busy. Though, I really need to get my driving test sorted. It’s a nightmare getting here on the bus, especially on late shifts. Law is a big commitment, definitely. But if you're good at analysing things, History would give you a good starting point. As for driving… oh, the stress! I only passed last year. Put it off for  years . I was convinced I’d fail every time. The parallel parking still haunts my dreams.

Blast and botheration, look at the time! Nearly quarter past, isn't it? We’re supposed to be having our elevenses. Gertrude, you’ve got us rabbiting on again, haven’t you? About what, I’ve hardly a clue, but it’s always  something  with you. Oh, don’t be like that, Arthur. It wasn’t  me  entirely. It was David wanting to tell us all about his plans for that…donation box. And then we got onto the banners for the bell ringing. It just sort of…snowballed. Though I did mention the Gambia, I confess. Always lovely to think of a bit of sunshine. Right you are, Gertrude. Perhaps I was a little verbose. The donation box idea is for the church roof fund, you know. A bit more visual than just passing a plate around. And the banners will help publicise the bell ringing recruitment drive. We’re desperately short of ringers. Honestly, it's a dying art. Bells, bells, bells. Always bells with you, David. Good as they are, a bit much for a Tuesday morning. Though I suppose it’s better than you going on about that…well, you know. That medical business. Arthur! That’s not kind. David was just reading an article. And it  was  fascinating, actually. Munchausen Syndrome, wasn’t it? Rather sad, really. People deliberately making themselves ill. It is a complex condition, certainly. The psychological roots are… well, quite profound. It raises all sorts of ethical questions, doesn't it? But let’s not dwell. The donation box – I was thinking a sturdy wooden one, maybe with a little window so people can see how much is accumulating. Should we varnish it, Gertrude? Or paint it? Ooh, varnish! Definitely varnish. Shows the wood grain. And maybe a little brass plate with ‘Church Roof Fund’ engraved on it? Though you'd need to get young Michael to do the engraving, wouldn't you? He's the artistic one. Michael’s a good lad. Always helping. Reminds me of myself when I was that age… though I wasn't much good at engraving. More of a… a thinker, I was. Though what I  thought  about, I couldn’t rightly tell you now. This coffee's gone cold. Needs another splash of milk. Gertrude, love, could you…? Coming right up, Arthur. Honestly, you'd think a retired man would have the energy to pour his own milk.

…and honestly, the interface is just  awful . It’s supposed to be this revolutionary plant identification app, right? But you spend ten minutes scrolling through options that all look vaguely leafy, and then it tells you your Monstera is a dandelion. A  dandelion ! Seriously? That’s rubbish. I used one last summer when we were hiking in the Peak District and it was pretty spot on. Identified all sorts of wildflowers. What’s it called, this disaster app? Oh, you mean ‘BloomBuddy’? I saw an advert for that on TikTok. Looked…ambitious. Probably relies on user-submitted photos, doesn't it? Which explains the dandelion situation. Exactly! And the ‘community’ section is just people arguing about whether a particular fern is British or not. It’s a whole…horticultural warzone. I deleted it. Life’s too short. Speaking of things that are stressful, did anyone see that new horror film, ‘The Hollow’? I nearly had a heart attack. Ooh, I’ve been meaning to watch that! Is it genuinely terrifying or just jump scares? Because I hate jump scares. They’re just cheap. No, it’s proper psychological stuff. It messes with your head. There’s this…thing…in the woods, and the sound design is  brilliant . I had to sleep with the light on. You are such a scaredy-cat, Liv! Remember when we watched ‘The Ring’ at Sarah’s and you hid behind a cushion the entire time? That was different! I was like, twelve. And that well scene was genuinely creepy. Okay, maybe I am a bit of a scaredy-cat. But ‘The Hollow’ is genuinely unsettling. Right, well, I need something lighthearted after that description. How’s everyone’s week been, aside from potentially being haunted by woodland creatures? I finally finished that report for Mr. Henderson, and I swear the man breathes spreadsheets. Mine’s been hectic. We're launching the new website at work next week, so it’s been all hands on deck. Honestly, I’m dreaming in code. How's Finn? Still glued to his guitar? Oh, constantly. He’s convinced he’s going to be the next Ed Sheeran. Keeps trying to write songs about… pigeons. It’s a phase, I hope. Pigeons? That  is  a phase. Ben’s been really quiet this week, actually. I think he’s trying to impress someone new at work. He’s suddenly taken up… bread making.

…and then, honestly, young Timmy nearly backed right into Mrs. Higgins’ new Fiesta. A Fiesta, of all things! Bright yellow, you wouldn’t believe. Could’ve been a right mess, it could. He said his reversing sensors weren’t working. Reversing sensors! What good are they if you don't  look ? Timmy, eh? Always was a bit of a rush-head, that one. Reminds me of your brother, Arthur, back in the day. Nearly wrote off old man Peterson’s Morris Minor trying to show off at the village fete. Nearly, mind you. Peterson held onto that car like it was made of gold. Oh, don't get started on village fetes and bad driving! It's a recipe for disaster. Though, honestly, I'm just glad we're  here  now. That drive was…stressful. Especially with the A140 being the way it was. Stressful is an understatement, Margaret. Absolute chaos. I swear, every other vehicle was a lorry. And they just barrel along, they do. No consideration for anyone. I’ve driven bridges that felt more stable than trying to navigate that stretch of road these days. Remember when it was just fields either side, George? Course I do. Used to cycle down there, I did. No bother at all. Just hedgerows and the occasional tractor. Nowadays, you're practically dodging missiles. And the speed! They all seem to think they’re in a Formula One race, don't they? It’s not just the speed, it’s the lane discipline. People just  pull out  without looking. I was genuinely worried a couple of times. And then that roundabout near Attleborough… a complete free-for-all. Roundabouts. Don’t get me started on roundabouts. People treat ‘em like suggestions, not rules. Especially those tourists. You can tell ‘em a mile off – going too slow, looking bewildered. It’s a wonder there aren’t more accidents. I used to design roads, you know… should’ve put more roundabouts in, perhaps. No, no. Too many would just make it worse. You always were a clever lad, Arthur. Designing roads and all. Shame you weren't still at it. Might have sorted out this mess we have now. Although, knowing the council, they'd probably choose the cheapest option regardless. Remember that pothole on Dereham Road they took six months to fix? Oh,  please . Don’t remind me of Dereham Road. I nearly lost a tyre in that one.

Honestly, this is bliss. Proper tea, proper biscuits… a world away from those awful airport coffee things, wouldn’t you say, Sarah? Remember that time in Heathrow? They tried to charge us a fiver for a lukewarm cup.      Oh,  don’t  remind me, Mary. Five pounds for something that tasted like dishwater. Though, to be fair, airports are designed to fleece you. It’s a business model. Speaking of which, how’s the packing going? Still finding things you ‘absolutely need’ that you haven’t touched in ten years?      The packing is going… slowly. She’s unearthed a collection of commemorative thimbles, apparently. Each one representing a different village fete we attended in the nineties. A whole history of floral arrangements and questionable baking.      They’re  memories , George! And perfectly good thimbles! You wouldn’t understand. You just want to chuck everything in a box and label it “Miscellaneous”. Honestly. And it's not just thimbles, it’s the  principle  of leaving things behind. All this downsizing… it feels like shedding layers of yourself.      I get that, truly. But downsizing to a place with a garden and no draughts sounds like a good trade. And closer to me, which is a massive bonus. Less M6 slog for visiting. Though even  I  dread the M6. Saw a car practically spinning on the hard shoulder earlier.      That stretch near Knutsford is notorious. Too many lorries, not enough common sense. Speaking of cars, did you confirm the removal company can handle all the… thimbles? And the antique dining table? That thing's a beast.      Yes, dear, they’re perfectly capable. They’ve dealt with heavier things than my thimbles, I assure you. Though I am a little worried about the table. It was my grandmother’s, you know. Such a lovely piece of mahogany. And they promised to wrap it in a special blanket.      They should do! Good removal companies are worth their weight in gold. I used one when I moved here and they were fantastic. I remember being so stressed about all my books. They treated them like Fabergé eggs! Speaking of stress, how’s your knee, Mary? Any better after the physio?      A little. It's the damp, I think. This weather gets right into your bones. The physio says I need to do more walking, but with this knee, it’s a bit of a catch-22, isn’t it? Walk to make it better, but walking makes it worse.

Mum? You won't  believe  what Chloe posted on Insta… honestly, it's a whole drama with Ben and… oh. You look… relieved? Hello darling. Yes, a bit relieved is putting it mildly. You're right to notice. Come and sit down a minute. I have good news. Good news? Better than Chloe potentially being dumped over a dodgy selfie? Because that’s  big  news. What is it? You're not winning the lottery, are you? No lottery win, though that would be nice. Remember my bike? The Raleigh, the one that went missing last month? Oh!  The  Raleigh! The one you were gutted about? The one Dad got you for your 40th? You found it?! Better than finding it, actually. The police recovered it. Apparently, it was being used in a series of… well, petty thefts around town. A teenager was going around on it, apparently. Seriously? That’s awful! But amazing you got it back! Was it damaged? Oh, let me see! Is it in the shed? It’s in the garage, a little dusty, but mostly fine. A few scratches, but nothing major. The police think they've got the lad who took it too. It’s good to hear that, at least. It felt so violating, you know? Having something stolen like that. I can imagine. It's just…  stuff , but it’s  your  stuff. And that bike meant a lot. You used to cycle everywhere with it! Remember all those rides to Camber Sands? I do. And to Winchelsea. Good times. It’s funny, isn’t it? I’d almost resigned myself to it being gone for good. Which is why I was so chuffed when PC Davies called this morning. He said they’d traced it through some security camera footage. That’s so cool! Honestly, the police are getting better with all that tech. Although, did they not think to check cameras  immediately  after you reported it stolen? Bureaucracy, darling. It’s always bureaucracy. Anyway, it’s back, and that’s what matters. Now, about this Chloe drama… what’s going on? While I finish stirring this – it’s a shepherds pie, by the way. Your favourite. Ooh, shepherds pie! You’re the best. Okay, so basically, Chloe posted a picture with Ben at the pier, and someone has zoomed in and apparently, Ben is holding hands with  another  girl in the background. Oh dear.

Right, I officially surrender. Rhys is a  monster  at Ticket to Ride. Honestly, building routes across Europe like it's nothing. Now, now, Seren. It’s just good planning. Strategic thinking, you might say. Though, I’ll admit, I did get lucky with a few long routes early on. Did you manage to complete any of your destination tickets? Just snagged Glasgow to Newcast… oh, and blocked Rhys’ potential route to Liverpool. Petty, perhaps? A little! But a valid tactic, Iolo. A very valid tactic. All this talk of trains… reminds me of a journey I took from Singapore to Kuala Lumpur, back in '87. The engineering was just phenomenal. These little train carriages chugging up incredibly steep gradients. You wouldn’t believe it. Oh, I remember you telling us that story, Gareth! About how the train practically  climbed  the mountains? And the monkeys trying to get on board? The very same! Cheeky little things. One almost made off with a woman’s handbag. Complete chaos. Much more exciting than placing plastic trains on a board, though I appreciate a good game, mind. Monkeys stealing handbags… sounds a bit more thrilling than my current predicament. I swear, Rhys is deliberately hoarding the grey cards. He's a bit of a grey card fiend, I’ll give you that. Right, I’m going to try and connect Rome to Istanbul, if Iolo hasn’t blocked  that  off as well. Speaking of food, anyone fancy a proper Welsh Rarebit later? I was thinking of making it – proper, with mustard and Worcestershire sauce. Ooh, yes please, David! That sounds absolutely lovely. Something warm and cheesy after all this strategic warfare. Seren, you look like you need fortifying. Absolutely. I'm fuelled solely by humiliation at this point. Rarebit sounds… divine. Though, I'm no expert on train dynamics, but mustn't they have incredible gearing for those steep inclines Gareth mentioned? It's not just brute force, is it? Like, the wheel diameter, and the… Actually, it's a fascinating piece of engineering. Rack and pinion railways are often used on those incredibly steep gradients. Essentially, a toothed wheel engages with a toothed rail. It's more about a mechanical grip than raw power. Iolo, showing off your engineering knowledge again? Just sharing, David. And it explains why the trains don't just roll backwards. It's beautifully simple, really. See? More interesting than a board game!

Right. That's… underwhelming. Seven points for 'elm'. Seriously? I thought I was being clever with the 'm'. Clever is a strong word, darling. You were hoping to snag that double letter score, weren't you? I saw the glint in your eye. Though, to be fair, the board isn't exactly cooperating. It’s all vowels and awkward consonants. It  is  a dreadful board. It’s like the Scrabble gods are actively punishing us for daring to play on a Sunday afternoon in Norfolk. It’s far too…peaceful for competitive Scrabble. Needs a bit of a London edge, frankly. A London edge? Meaning what, aggressive tile placement and accusations of cheating? You know your mum keeps a very close eye on our scores. She's convinced I subtly move your pieces when she’s getting tea. She does! Honestly, you'd think she’d trust me more after ten years. Though, to be fair, my competitive streak  does  come out sometimes. It’s the lecturer in me, I suppose. Debating points, meticulously constructing arguments…it translates surprisingly well to Scrabble. And to everything else, let’s be honest. Speaking of translating, I was thinking about that article we were discussing – the one about differing drinking cultures in the UK. It made me think about how… restrained things are here in Norfolk, compared to London. Oh, yes! The “pints at lunchtime are practically mandatory in the city” versus “a nice glass of elderflower cordial with the scones”. It’s a significant difference, isn’t it? And it’s not just the amount, it’s the  occasion . In London, going for a drink is an event. Here, it's…more considered. Exactly! It’s almost…polite drinking here. Like, you’re acknowledging the social niceties. In London, it feels like a performance sometimes. Everyone trying to appear effortlessly cool while simultaneously downing pints. It’s a weird energy. And the entire pub culture is different. Pubs in London feel…transient. People popping in and out, quick pints before something else. Here, people settle in for the afternoon. It’s community-focused in a way that’s harder to find in a city. It feels more rooted. Actually, it's a bit like board games, isn't it? How so? Well, in London, board games are often ‘eventised’. Board game cafes, competitive gaming clubs… It’s very…structured. Here, it’s more likely to be a slightly dusty box pulled out of a cupboard on a rainy day with family.

…and honestly, the estate agent was  insisting  that beige was ‘neutral’ and ‘appealing to all’. Beige! It’s the colour of sadness, isn’t it? I said, ‘Look, I’ve just spent the last three years researching 18th-century textile dyes for my thesis, the least you can do is let me choose a slightly more interesting shade.’ Oh, bless him. They always say beige. It’s the default setting for mass appeal, apparently. Doesn't mean it's  appealing . How’s the actual decorating going, then? Are you knee-deep in paint samples and swatches? It’s a nightmare, moving, isn't it? An absolute nightmare. I remember when Gareth and I moved to this house… thirty years ago, it was. The state of the kitchen! Avocado green everything.  Everything . Took us a month to get rid of it all. Avocado green… at least that’s a  colour . Beige is just… nothing. Decorating is slow going. I’m trying to do it bit by bit, otherwise I’ll completely lose it. I spent all day yesterday assembling that ridiculously complicated IKEA wardrobe. I think I aged ten years. IKEA is the enemy. A necessary evil, admittedly, but still the enemy. I'm offering my services for future flatpack assembly, for a small fee, naturally. Being a project coordinator has its advantages; I’m basically a professional instruction reader. You’re a clever boy, you are. My grandson, Rhys, he tried to build a bookcase last month. Ended up with bits sticking out everywhere. Looked like a modern art installation, it did. He had to call his father in the end. Speaking of needing help… the washing machine in the new place is ancient. I'm talking, probably pre-dates my birth certificate ancient. It sounds like a jet engine taking off when it spins. Right, that’s a health and safety hazard waiting to happen. Are you covered for white goods in the rental agreement? You should definitely be getting the landlord to sort that. I think so… I need to double-check. Honestly, dealing with landlords is the worst. It’s always ‘reasonable wear and tear’ when something breaks, but apparently, I’m not allowed to have personality. Oh, don’t even get me started on landlords. I had one once, tried to charge me for replacing a perfectly good door because he said it ‘didn’t match the aesthetic’.

Honestly, Mum, this traffic is mental. We've barely moved since Canary Wharf. I swear, every single person in London decided to go to Hampstead at exactly the same time. It  is  rather busy, isn’t it? Though “mental” feels a bit strong, darling. You’re starting to sound like your father when he gets behind the wheel. Remember that time on the M25? Nearly caused an international incident with a lorry driver. Oh god, don't remind me. The 'M25 Incident' is family legend. But seriously, this is… frustrating. And I've got that meeting with Professor Davies in an hour. I’m already late. You’ll be fine. Davies is a reasonable man. And look, we’re moving now. Slow, but moving. So, how was the TLS party last night? Did you manage to corner any editors and badger them about your short stories? Don’t use the word “badger”. It implies… desperation. It was alright, actually. A bit stuffy, if I’m honest. Lots of tweed and quiet murmuring. I spoke to Amelia Hayes – you know, the fiction editor? – and she said my stuff “has potential.” “Potential” is good! That’s editor speak for “send me more.” Don’t underestimate the power of ‘potential,’ Leo. It’s kept my career afloat for thirty years. Speaking of which, things are… interesting at work. We're having another debate about print versus digital. Let me guess, the digital team are pushing for more online content and less space for reviews? Precisely. They think print is dying a slow death. I argued, rather passionately I might add, that there’s something fundamentally different about holding a beautifully typeset book in your hands versus scrolling through a website. It’s a tactile experience. It’s… considered. I get that. Though, I do most of my reading on my tablet now. It’s just so convenient. Less clutter. Convenience isn’t everything, Leo! Although… I suppose you're right. It's the world we live in. Anyway, are you sorted for your Aunt Carol's birthday? She’s expecting something thoughtful this year. That's… a work in progress. She’s notoriously difficult to buy for. She says she doesn’t  need  anything. Which is unhelpful. I was thinking maybe a weekend away somewhere? France, perhaps? Oh, that’s lovely! She always did adore France. Though she'll complain about the language barrier.

…and then, honestly, the seagull  dive-bombed  me for my chips! Right over the harbour in Whitby. Absolute menace, it was. I screamed, dropped half me chips, the lot. Proper embarrassing. You? Screaming at a seagull? That’s a new one, Liv. You're usually dead stoic, even when old man Hemmings is breathing down your neck at work. It was a  big  seagull, alright? And it had intent in its eyes. Pure, chip-stealing intent. You’d have screamed too, Dan. Honestly. Oh, god, that reminds me of our trip to Newquay last year. Remember that one that nicked your sausage roll, Chloe? You chased it halfway down the beach! Aye, and nearly took out a toddler in the process. You were a sight, love, flapping your arms and shoutin' “My sausage roll!” It was a  really  good sausage roll! And I’d only just bought it! It was a pork and apple one, you know, the fancy kind. Classic Chloe. Always prioritising the snacks. Though, I gotta say, I’ve had some disasters on holiday too. Remember that time in Amsterdam, when I tried to cycle everywhere? Oh,  please  tell the story. For those who don't know, Ethan thinks he’s Mark Cavendish. I’m not! I just… underestimated the Dutch. They are serious about their cycling. I ended up in a canal. A  small  canal, but a canal nonetheless. You ended up in a canal?! No way! How did you even manage that? It involved a tourist, a map, a very narrow bridge, and me trying to simultaneously navigate and apologise for being in the way. Let’s just say gravity won. Serves you right for thinking you could out-cycle the locals. They live and breathe it! I remember when me and me dad went to Holland, he was proper gobsmacked by how many bikes there were. So, were you soaked, Ethan? Did anyone help you out? Soaked is an understatement. And yeah, a lovely old woman fished me out with a grabber thing. A grabber! Like, for litter. It was deeply humiliating. She didn't understand a word I was saying, just kept pointing at the bike in the water and shaking her head. Brilliant. You're a walking disaster, you are. But a funny disaster, mind you. Speaking of disasters, remember that camping trip we all took to the Lake District? The one where it rained for three solid days?

…and honestly, the frost on the tent in the morning, it was  spectacular . Like a spun-glass palace. Though, getting out of the sleeping bag… that was a different matter entirely. Felt like wrestling a polar bear, I tell you. Oh, Arthur, you and your…extreme hobbies. Wild winter camping? You’re a brave man, or mad, one of the two. I much prefer a nice, warm duvet and a good book when the weather’s like that. Though I do enjoy hearing your stories. It sounds… invigorating, in a terrifying sort of way. It  is  invigorating, Aunt Morag. Dad’s been doing it for years. It's not just about the challenge, though that’s a part of it. It's the complete disconnect, you know? No signal, no people, just you and the elements. Clears the head like nothing else. Precisely, Callum! That's the point. It strips everything back. All the noise, all the…fuss of modern life. You’re forced to focus on basic survival – finding shelter, staying warm, water. It’s remarkably grounding. And the silence... absolute silence. You don't get that in London anymore. Grounding, aye, but also potentially dangerous. I’ve seen enough cases as a nurse to know how quickly things can go wrong with exposure. Hypothermia’s no joke, Arthur. Do you at least have a proper emergency plan? A beacon? Tell someone where you are? Of course, of course! I’m not  completely  reckless. I’ve got a PLB - Personal Locator Beacon - a proper four-season tent, and always tell someone my route. And I’ve been doing it long enough to recognise the warning signs, the shivers, the confusion. It’s all about preparedness. It’s not about bravado. He’s incredibly methodical about it, honestly. He’s got checklists for checklists. And he's learned so much about reading the land, predicting the weather… It’s a genuine skill. It’s not just ‘roughing it’. He’s actually a bit of a wilderness expert now. Still. It sounds awfully lonely. Do you ever worry about just…being out there all alone? It used to bother me, I'll admit. In my younger days. But now… now I find the solitude rather comforting. A chance to really think. To be present. To connect with nature. It's a different kind of companionship, if you see what I mean. More… elemental.

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt  pointless . Like, beautifully shot, don't get me wrong, Denis Villeneuve knows how to make a pretty picture, but Dune Part Two? Two-and-a-half hours of sand and brooding. Honestly, I was expecting more payoff for all that build-up. Woah, hold on a sec. Pointless? I thought it was brilliant! The scale of it, the world-building… it felt genuinely epic. And Zendaya finally got something to  do  this time around, which was good. I mean, the first one was mostly exposition, really. This one had… consequence. Consequence? It was all prophecy and chosen ones and… spice? Look, I appreciate a good sci-fi, but I need a bit more  humanity  in it, y'know? Give me something relatable. Like, I was reading ‘Normal People’ by Sally Rooney last week, now  that  was emotionally devastating, and actually said something about… well, people. Not giant worms. That’s a bit of a leap, isn’t it? Comparing 'Normal People' to 'Dune'? They’re aiming for completely different things. Rooney’s all about internal landscapes, and ‘Dune’ is a space opera about political intrigue and ecological disaster. It’s about power, and religion, and… And sand. Let’s not forget the sand. It was  always  about the sand. Honestly, I felt like I needed a good plate of chips and gravy after that film. Something grounding. Speaking of, d'you fancy grabbing some haddock and chips when we get back? Proper chippy chips, none of that posh ‘hand-cut’ nonsense. You and your chips. Alright, a deal. If we get chips, we can revisit this ‘Dune’ debate. I still stand by it being a proper cinematic achievement though. It's not  supposed  to be 'relatable' in the same way as a novel focused on university students. It's a myth. A myth involving an awful lot of beige. Though, I’ll admit, the sound design was amazing. Those vibrations… you could feel it in your chest. But still! Give me a good book any day. Have you read anything good recently apart from…well, whatever engineering manuals you get stuck into? Harsh! Actually, I've been ploughing through ‘Project Hail Mary’ by Andy Weir. It’s fantastic. You might like it, it’s got problem-solving and science and a surprisingly endearing alien. It's less 'brooding messiah' and more 'slightly panicked space teacher'. Ooh, an endearing alien?

…and honestly, the whole evening was just a flurry of badges and slightly sticky fingers. Honestly, Brownies. It’s a commitment! Did you both enjoy it, though? Even with all the knot-tying? It was okay. Elsie got the ‘Friend to Animals’ badge. She helped Mrs. Higgins hold a worm! A worm?! Ewwww! Was it slimy? I wanted the ‘Creative’ badge, but I messed up the friendship bracelet. It looked like a tangled mess of string. Well, practice makes perfect, darling. Elsie, holding a worm  is  rather brave. You're a very good friend to animals. Now, are we all comfy? Because I'm trying to avoid thinking about marking thirty essays on the symbolism in  The Great Gatsby  tomorrow. I'm comfy. Can we talk about Lego after? I designed a spaceship. It has lasers! Mine’s bigger! It’s a castle! With a dungeon! And a dragon! A dragon, excellent. We’ll definitely talk Lego. But first, you both were asking about what I  did  before being a teacher, right? Before endless marking and Brownie meetings? Yeah! You said you used to work with…computers? But not PlayStation computers? No, not quite. These were the really old-fashioned ones. Big, clunky things. Before everything was…touchscreen-y. I used to work with something called Excel. Ex-sell? What’s that? Does it sell things? No, no. It’s a program. It helps you keep track of numbers and information. Think of it like…a really organised list, but on a computer. It’s incredibly useful for, well, for things like school budgets, or calculating averages. Very grown-up stuff! But before  that , I actually worked in an office that had…a typewriter. A type…writer? What's  that ? Oh goodness. Imagine you want to write something, but instead of typing on a keyboard, you have to press little keys that hit a ribbon, which then prints the letters onto the paper.  Clack, clack, clack!  It was very noisy. And if you made a mistake…you had to start the whole page again! Or use something called ‘white-out’ which was a smelly liquid. Wow! That sounds…slow. It  was  slow. And messy! It took ages to write anything. That’s why computers were such a huge thing. Everything became so much faster. Do you know how your dad uses a computer for work? It’s very similar, just much more powerful.

Now then, Arthur. You look like you’ve been wrestling badgers again. Honestly, a bit of effort, even for a Saturday. You didn’t raid the charity shop, did you? Badgers are surprisingly strong, you know. No, no charity shop today, Brenda. Just…comfortable. Don't fuss. It’s a weekend. Besides, you’re looking rather spick and span yourself. Something special planned? Just because I haven’t given up on civilisation doesn’t mean something's planned! I like to  maintain  standards. Although, I did think about those fruit farms down near York this morning. Remember old Mr. Higgins? Used to practically give the plums away. Higgins… a grand old fellow. Though I always suspected he was undercutting everyone else just to get rid of 'em before they rotted. He had a good heart, though. Reminds me of a project I did down near Ripon once. Surveying land… stumbled across the remains of one of those deserted medieval villages. Proper eerie. All overgrown and stone foundations just…gone. Oh, I love hearing about those. So much history just swallowed up by the earth. It’s sad, isn’t it? Like all those old pubs closing. Speaking of swallowed up…have you seen the state of the roadworks on the way into Bradford? Absolute chaos! Took me nearly an hour to get from Saltaire. Roadworks. The bane of my existence. Always seem to be strategically placed to maximise disruption. They started on the A650 just outside Shipley last week, didn’t they? Dreadful. Still, at least they’re finally doing something about that pothole that’s been threatening to launch vehicles into orbit. More coffee? Please. And maybe another slice of this toast. Your wife makes a brilliant jam, Arthur. Seriously, what’s her secret? It's not too sweet, and it has…depth. She uses a touch of ginger. Old family recipe. She's a wizard in the kitchen, my Margaret. I mostly stick to engineering problems. Far less palatable if you get it wrong. You’ve been growing herbs again, I see? That rosemary smells lovely. Trying to. The slugs are having a field day, though. It’s a constant battle. I think I need to invest in some copper tape. It's supposed to deter them. It’s just… frustrating. You get to a certain age, and things just take  longer . Tell me about it. Bending down to tie shoelaces is an expedition these days.

Honestly, David, you wouldn’t  believe  the state of Mrs. Higgins this morning. She'd gotten her wires crossed with her medication  again . Took her blood pressure pills with her breakfast, then wondered why she felt so faint! Honestly, some days… it’s a miracle they’re still upright. Oh, bless her. She's a character, that one. Though, it  is  worrying, isn't it? You’d think after all this time, she’d have a routine nailed down. Did you have to call the doctor? Thankfully, no. Just a cup of strong tea and a lie-down. I explained it to her, slow as you like, about taking them with water, not a full fry-up. It's like talking to a brick wall sometimes, honestly. Speaking of fry-ups, are we still on for bacon sandwiches tomorrow? I’m craving something proper greasy after the health food kick we’ve been on. Ooh, bacon sandwiches sound  divine . Though, I’m still feeling slightly… sluggish from all the Christmas pudding. I think I’ve officially reached peak festive bloat. Found the most ridiculous thing on Facebook though. Let me guess, another one of your auntie’s conspiracy theories? Last time it was about 5G causing the pigeons to… what was it? Worse! It’s a photo of a cat apparently ‘driving’ a mobility scooter. The caption is something about a rebellion of the feline overlords. It’s… unsettlingly well-edited. Oh, you’re awful! Honestly, Facebook. It’s a cesspit, but I still check it religiously. Did you get everything sorted with your Mum’s present? You were stressing about it last week. I did! Finally. I got her one of those ancestry DNA kits. She’s obsessed with genealogy. It was either that or a lifetime supply of lavender bath salts. I think the DNA kit is marginally less terrifying. Though, she'll probably find out we're all descended from Vikings or something. Your Mum  would  love that. Speaking of gifts, I still haven’t figured out what to get your Auntie Maureen. She has  everything . She spends all her time travelling. Last I heard, she was in Uzbekistan. Uzbekistan! Honestly, that woman. Always chasing the exotic. She sent us a postcard with a picture of a camel. A  camel , David! And a rambling story about getting lost in a bazaar. Sounds about right. She’s a force of nature, that one.

Honestly, this Earl Grey is  saving  me. Week’s been a right blur, hasn’t it? Feels like I’ve been writing slogans for dog food all day, every day. It’s… creatively draining, to say the least. Tell me about it. I’m drowning in survey questions about biscuit preferences. Biscuit preferences, Liv! Who needs that level of detail? Though, admittedly, I'm now very aware of the nation's obsession with digestives. How’s the copywriting going generally? Still at "Pawsitively Delicious" pet supplies? Still there. It pays the rent, which, let’s be real, in London is a miracle in itself. And it’s good practice, I suppose. Though the brief for the new cat litter campaign was… something else. “Evoke feelings of serene woodland glades.” It’s  cat litter , Elsie! Oh my god, that’s brilliant. Seriously though, you’re good at that stuff. Remember that Christmas ad you did for that local bakery last year? Everyone was talking about it. You’ve got a real knack for making the mundane sound lovely. Thanks! It’s nice of you to say. What about you? How’s the postgrad life treating you? Still wrestling with… what is it, computational linguistics? Sounds terrifyingly clever. It is, a bit. It's fascinating, but also… deeply frustrating sometimes. I’m basically trying to teach computers to understand sarcasm. It’s harder than it sounds. And the part-time work is keeping me afloat, even if the biscuit data is soul-crushing. Mum keeps dropping hints about "realistic career paths," which is code for "get a proper job”. Oh, mums. Mine’s the same. Constantly asking if I’ve “thought about something more… stable." As if copywriting isn't a perfectly valid profession! She still thinks I should have gone into teaching, like my sister. It's the classic, isn't it? My brother's a solicitor, so that's the gold standard in her eyes. He keeps sending me links to training contracts. Honestly, I think he’s trying to preempt Mum’s lectures. Bless him. He sounds sensible. Speaking of family, how’s your Nan doing? I haven't seen her since Christmas. She’s good, surprisingly sprightly for 92. She's taken up online bridge, can you believe it? Apparently, she’s a bit of a shark. Keeps winning all the time, and then bragging about it on family WhatsApp.

… honestly, I’m starting to think the sourdough starter is winning. It’s demanding more attention than a toddler. Another two hours and it  still  hasn’t doubled. You and your bread. Honestly, Fiona, you’re putting way too much pressure on yourself. It’s just bread. Though, I admit, when it  works , it’s glorious. I still remember that loaf you brought round at Christmas. Oh, don’t even  mention  Christmas. The expense of it all! Honestly, I'm already dreading it. And speaking of expenses… have you two seen the latest Rightmove updates? This market is insane. Don't get me started, Margaret! I was just looking at places in Richmond - just  dreaming , you understand - and a two-bedroom terrace is going for more than we paid for our first house! It’s ridiculous. Even the fixer-uppers are extortionate. Edinburgh’s not much better, apparently. My sister was saying she’s looking to downsize now the kids have flown the nest, and she’s practically having a nervous breakdown trying to find something affordable. It’s all these Londoners buying second homes, driving up the prices. It’s the investment, isn’t it? People treating houses like stocks and shares. Remember when owning your own home felt… attainable? Honestly, I'm glad I snapped up this place when I did, even if it  does  need constant attention. Speaking of attention, are either of you actually doing any exercise these days? You both look… comfortable. Ouch! Margaret, that’s a bit blunt. I’ve been trying to get back into my walks, but with the transcription work being so busy, and the bread… well, my schedule’s a bit full. It’s mostly chair-based activity, I’m afraid. I’ve been doing a bit of cycling, actually. Nothing major, just around Holyrood Park. It's a good way to clear the head and avoid the emails. Though I did nearly get taken out by a rogue tourist on a hire bike last week. Terrifying. Cycling! Good for you, David. I used to love cycling. Now it’s just… less appealing. Too many cars. I’ve been doing Pilates, which is lovely, but my instructor keeps telling me I need to ‘engage my core’. Honestly, what  is  engaging my core supposed to feel like? It feels like you’re trying to pull your belly button towards your spine. It’s very subtle, but apparently crucial.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of data is mental. Like, we’re talking terabytes of transcribed speech just  from  last month. It’s all for building this massive linguistic corpus, right? Sounds fancy, but 90% of the time it's me cleaning up mis-transcriptions and tagging things. Did I tell you they changed the tagging system  again ? No, you didn’t! Seriously? Changed it  again ? That sounds… exhausting. I thought the whole point of a corpus was consistency? It feels like they’re deliberately making it difficult for you. I’m still battling with drainage calculations that are being re-evaluated because of this new climate change modelling. It’s a similar vibe, just with pipes instead of phonemes. Exactly! It's infuriating. They said it was to be “more nuanced,” but all it’s done is add another layer of complexity. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm drowning in semi-colons. Speaking of drowning, did you see the Budget announcements? Absolutely brutal, wasn’t it? Brutal is an understatement. I was half expecting them to announce they were selling off bits of Cambridge University to pay for everything. VAT on private school fees is a big one, isn’t it? My auntie’s practically having a meltdown – she teaches at one in Sevenoaks. Though, admittedly, she’s usually having a meltdown about  something . Aye, and the freezes on council tax… it doesn’t even cover inflation, does it? It’s all a bit… performative, isn’t it? Like they’re  doing  something, but it won’t make a blind bit of difference to most folks. They wouldn’t know what real life’s like down here in Sunderland, anyway. Everything’s always so rosy in London. It's a disconnect, definitely. It feels like they’re operating on a different planet. Though, I suppose that’s politics, innit? Anyway, enough doom and gloom. What are you up to this weekend? Need a break from the linguistic minefield? I’m thinking of maybe trying to get tickets to see  Wicked … it’s touring near Newcastle. I know, I know, it's a bit… mainstream. But I've always loved the soundtrack. And I need some sparkly escapism after wading through academic papers all week. Have you seen it?  Wicked ? Actually, yeah! My sister dragged me along to it in London a few years ago. It was surprisingly good. Properly enjoyed it, even.

Right, that's another section done. Honestly, this fence was  begging  for a makeover. Looks a bit brighter already, doesn’t it? Though my back's screaming at me. Brighter? Lad, it’s practically glowing now. You’d think it was auditioning for a role in a film. Speaking of, did you ever get round to that audition for the community theatre lot? The one for ‘Hamlet’ they were advertising? ‘Hamlet’? Don't be daft, Kevin. Me? Playing the melancholy Dane? More like the melancholy fence-painter. No, I didn’t. I considered it briefly, purely for the amusement value, but I know my limits. I can  lecture  about Shakespeare, dissect his language for hours, but  being  him? That’s a different kettle of fish. Aye, fair enough. Still, you’ve got a good voice for it, you have. Dramatic, y’know? Remember that time you were reading out that poem by Auden at the pub quiz? Had half the room in tears, nearly. That was a particularly bleak poem about the Blitz, Kevin. I think the tears were more about remembering the bombings than the poetry itself. Honestly, though, I prefer observing the drama. Like watching that documentary last night about the redevelopment of the docks. Absolute shambles. Oh, aye, that. A right mess. Trying to make Liverpool into some sort of fancy, glass-and-steel city. It’ll lose its soul, it will. They’re knocking down buildings with history, replacing them with luxury flats nobody local can afford. It’s criminal. Precisely! It's the same story everywhere, isn't it? This relentless pursuit of ‘progress’ that homogenises everything. I saw a lovely little antique shop go last week. Been there for forty years. The owner, old Mrs. Higgins, had an eye for genuine finds. Found a rather splendid oil painting there myself a few years back – a little Dutch landscape. Cost me a song. Second-hand’s the only way to go, mate. Everything's overpriced and poorly made these days anyway. I picked up a proper armchair from a car boot sale last month, cost me a tenner. Comfier than anything you’d find in a shop. Speaking of finding things, you still got that ladder of yours? Mine’s gone walkies. Think me young Liam borrowed it to try and fix the gutters but I can't find him or the ladder anywhere. The green aluminium one?

Oh, this is lovely, isn’t it? Just… rolling hills. It’s a world away from Cambridge, that’s for sure. Though, truthfully, even Cambridge feels a world away right now. Did you see that stork nesting on that telephone pole back there? Majestic. I did! Absolutely enormous. Feels very…Polish, somehow. I’ve seen loads since we crossed the border. Makes a nice change from the grey skies of Bury, doesn’t it? Though, speaking of changes, how are we doing on the fuel front? I filled up in Slovakia, but that was… a while ago. We're alright for another hundred kilometres, I think. I’ve been keeping an eye on the gauge. Poland isn’t  horrendously  expensive for petrol, is it? Though compared to what I remember from…well, a long time ago…everything’s gone up. This whole trip is proving to be more expensive than I anticipated. I’m trying not to dwell on it. It’s definitely a bit pricier than I budgeted for too. But honestly, worth it. And you're not exactly living on a trust fund, are you? It’s good to get away, even if it’s a little tight. How are you finding the driving, by the way? I’m happy to take a stretch soon if you’re getting tired. I'm fine, honestly. It’s…therapeutic. All this open road. It gives you space to think. Which, admittedly, is sometimes a bad thing. I’ve been doing a lot of thinking about…well, everything. Especially the house. I  really  need to sort through all that clutter when I get back. Honestly, decades of accumulated…stuff. Oh god, the clutter. Tell me about it. I’m dreading going home to my flat. It’s not  as  bad as your house sounds, but I definitely need to have a clear-out. I’ve been trying to adopt a more minimalist approach, inspired by all this travelling and living out of a van. Less stuff, more freedom, you know? Precisely! It's liberating. It’s just… letting go. That’s the hard part. Speaking of freedom, did you see that guy hitchhiking with the guitar back there? I almost stopped. You did? Seriously? You’d have invited a complete stranger into  our  campervan? That’s a bit…bold, even for you. I was just…considering it. He looked harmless. And a musician!

Right, are we  sure  this is the right way, Mam? It feels like we've been going round in circles since Blackpool North station. I swear we passed that garden centre with the gnomes three times now. Honestly, love, I think you’re exaggerating slightly. But relax, I'm using the satnav. It said to take this route to avoid the traffic on the A522. Though, admittedly, it’s not exactly speeding things up, is it? Your Dad's probably regretting letting me navigate now. Nay, I’m alright. Just wish I’d remembered my reading glasses. This small print on the map… it's a joke. Though, honestly, I reckon your Mam's got a point. Seems a bit… scenic for a trip to Preston. More suited to the Hay Festival, this is. Remember that time we went, Elsie? Absolute chaos, but brilliant book stalls everywhere. The Hay Festival? Wasn't that ages ago, Dad? Before I was even properly reading, like, proper books? I remember there being loads of welly boots though, because it was mud everywhere. It was! You were tiny. You spent the whole time trying to feed a biscuit to a sheep. And yes, it was spectacularly muddy. I think I still have a photo somewhere. Speaking of reading, how are the revision notes coming along for your English Lit exam? Anything interesting you're studying? Ugh, don't even. It’s  The Handmaid’s Tale . It's proper depressing, to be honest. All that stuff about controlling women… It's just… grim. I’d rather be reading something with magic and dragons. Like, anything! Aye, well, books can be a bit heavy sometimes. When I was your age, it was all Biggles and the Famous Five. Nothing political about that! Though, your Gran used to make me read poetry. Dreadful, that was. All flowery language and things I didn’t understand. Your mother loved poetry, Arthur. You just pretended you didn’t. Remember how she used to say she felt…connected to it? Actually, thinking about her…it’s almost the anniversary. It feels like only yesterday. Oh, Mam... I know. It does. Do you think…do you think if she was still here, she’d be worried about me with these exams? She always pushed me to do my best. She’d be proud, love. She always said you were a bright spark. And worried, aye, she’d be worried.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of ‘stuff’ is astonishing, isn’t it? I mean, your mother’s always been a collector, but this is… a lifetime of collecting, condensed into one small Thirsk semi. It is a bit, isn't it, love? She says she ‘needed’ all those porcelain cats. Needed! As if a house full of feline figurines is a necessity. Honestly, I warned her when she moved from Kendal. Downsizing is hard, but she just wouldn’t listen. Said she’d find room. Found room alright. Room for about fifty more! I think I saw one in the bathroom. He’s not wrong, your mother  did  put one in the bathroom. Beside the toilet. Perhaps for company? Oh, don’t encourage him. He’ll be telling all his mates about Nana’s obsession with cats. Though, to be fair, the boy’s got a point. It’s a bit much. But it's not just the stuff, is it? It’s… well, she's not been herself since Arthur passed. This is her way of coping, I think. Filling the emptiness. What is  this ? Looks like something from a museum. Does it even work? Is this how you used to change the channels, Nana? With…bricks? That, my dear, is a very early remote control. Yes, it's ancient. No, it probably doesn't work. And no, it wasn’t made of bricks, though it feels like it! Technology’s moved on a bit since then, hasn’t it? You wouldn't believe the size of the televisions when I was a girl. Wooden cabinets, enormous things. And we were grateful for three channels! It's a good reminder of how far we've come. Remember when we got the first digital box, Thomas? You were convinced it was wizardry. It  was  wizardry! All those channels! And on-demand stuff! Although… Nana doesn’t really use any of that, does she? She still records things on VHS. It’s reliable! And I know how to work it. All this new technology… it just overwhelms me. It's like trying to learn another language. Plus, doctors said… well, they said I get anxious easily. The fast pace of everything. They said  potential  anxiety, love. Don’t overthink it. And that was six months ago. You’re coping brilliantly. She just needs a little help navigating it all, that's all.

Right, so… Windows 11. Bit flash, innit? Feels a bit…much. Still gettin’ used to it. You two are the tech heads though, tell me straight – is it actually  better  than 10, or is it just dressed up? Honestly? It's a bit of both. They’ve massively cleaned up the UI, which is nice, but under the hood…it’s demanding. It wants a lot more resources. Yours seems to be handling it okay though, considering you built it yourself from practically nothin'. What specs are we lookin' at again? Eight gigs of RAM, Ryzen 5, and a… … 512 gig SSD. The graphics card's the weak link, I reckon. A Radeon RX 570. Gets me by for gaming, but I wouldn't push it too hard. 512? Blimey. I’m still chugging along with a 256 gig in me desktop. Gets full faster than I can blink. Mind you, I mostly use it for checkin' emails and watchin' YouTube videos of fellas growin' enormous pumpkins. Pumpkins?! Seriously? Dead serious! There's a bloke in America, he grows 'em massive. Like, car-sized. Proper mental. It's therapeutic, seein' somethin' grow that big. Unlike my tomatoes this year, which are lookin' a bit peaky, to be honest. Need to get some feed on 'em. Speaking of YouTube, have you seen that Korean mukbang channel I showed you, Olly? The one with the woman who eats, like, ten bowls of noodles? Oh yeah! The one that made me feel profoundly ashamed of my portion sizes. It's somethin' else, innit? Proper competitive eating. Makes me think I need to actually  start  workin’ out again. Been slacking lately. Slackin’? You? The fella who used to box? I remember you were proper good. Had a right hook on ya. That was…a  lifetime  ago, Liam. Sixth form. Used to train down at the gym in Kempston. Now I get out of breath walkin' up the stairs. Thinking about maybe tryin’ some MMA, see if I can get back in shape. MMA's good. It's got that discipline aspect. Plus, learning self-defence is never a bad thing. Although, realistically, the biggest threat we face around here is probably Mrs. Higgins complainin’ about the noise. Don’t even mention her. She reported me to the council last week because my bins were "aesthetically displeasing.” Aesthetically displeasing! They were full of cardboard boxes, for goodness sake.

Honestly, I’m so glad we found this place. It's a little slice of…well, not Cambridge, certainly, but  nice . Much nicer than the usual Polish milk bars, don't you think? Though I do have a soft spot for a good  pierogi . You and your pierogi! It is lovely, isn’t it? A bit…aspirational for Tarnow, almost. Everyone’s been raving about the cakes. They’ve clearly aimed for a different clientele. Less…functional. Though, honestly, I’m still getting used to the pace of life here. It’s a bit slower than Manchester, to say the least. And people actually  talk  to you in shops. Oh, the talking! Don't get me started. It's charming, isn’t it? But it does throw a spanner in the works when you're trying to quickly grab a loaf of bread. Back home, you could practically have a transaction without uttering a single word. It’s just…different. Still, preferable to the loneliness, I suppose. Absolutely. And you’ve settled in okay? I know you were worried about being so far removed from everything familiar. It’s… a process. It's triggered a lot, actually. Trying to rebuild something that feels like  me  when so much of my identity was wrapped up in…well, in things I no longer have access to. It’s a bit like breaking an addiction, isn’t it? Only the addiction wasn’t a substance, it was…a lifestyle. A particular social circle. And a feeling of being ‘somebody’. That’s…a really good way of putting it, actually. Breaking patterns. And you  were  very wrapped up in things. People, places…events. It's brave of you to move so far. I’d be terrified. Brave or foolish, I’m not entirely sure. I just…felt suffocated. And the therapy helped, of course. Realising I was clinging to ghosts. Funny, isn’t it? All those years of education, and it took realizing I’d built my life on sand to actually understand anything. I’ve started going to a yoga class, you know. Trying to get…physical. It's awful. Yoga? You? I can’t picture it. You always struck me as more of a sherry and a good book kind of woman. And you always struck me as a relentlessly optimistic whirlwind. But here we are. The sherry is harder to come by, and the books don’t feel quite as comforting.

Honestly, Grandad, you wouldn’t  believe  the queues for the Dorset Steam Fair tickets online. I’ve been trying for half an hour! It says they’re releasing them in batches, but it’s a free-for-all. Batch releases… sounds like a right palaver, that does. Used to be, you just walked up to the gate and paid your money. Everything's got to be complicated these days. Is there any chance we can get them at the entrance on the day? I wouldn’t risk it, Dad. I heard Doreen down at the care home went last year and said they completely sold out. She ended up having to watch her husband wandering around the burger van looking glum all day. Said he’d been looking forward to the engines for months. Exactly what I thought, Mum. It's worth battling the internet for. I just… I need to know if Uncle Barry’s coming with us. And if he is, we need to sort out his accessibility needs. Remember last time? The uneven ground nearly sent him tumbling. Barry's definitely coming, love. He wouldn’t miss it for the world. Says it reminds him of his own father, tinkering with engines. As for the ground… it  is  a bit dodgy, isn't it? I remember nearly going over myself a couple of years back. They've improved things a bit, I think. Added some temporary walkways over the worst bits. But you’re right, it’s not exactly designed with wheelchairs in mind. Have you looked at their website, Chloe? I bet they have an accessibility guide. I have! It’s… vague. Says there’s designated parking and accessible loos, but doesn’t really go into detail about navigating the site. I’m thinking maybe we could hire a mobility scooter for Uncle Barry for the day? It would give him a bit more freedom. Now that’s a good idea, Chloe. A really good idea. He’d enjoy that. He’s always been fiercely independent. Wouldn't want to be burdened. Though… remembering moving that armchair for him last month… He'd probably want to  drive  the scooter through the steam engines! Oh, you know Barry! He's a character. Speaking of moving things, have you two sorted out that dresser for your new flat yet? You said the stairs in that building are a nightmare.

…and honestly, the removal van was  awful . Didn’t wrap a single thing properly. I was convinced the antique dresser was going to be reduced to splinters. Honestly, you’d think they'd have a bit more pride in their work, wouldn't you? Pride, Dorothy? That’s a rare commodity these days. Everything’s rushed, isn’t it? Back in my day, men took  care  with things. Your grandfather, God rest him, would build something to last a lifetime. Not this…flatpack nonsense. Is the dresser alright, at least? It’s miraculously unscathed, Mum. A few minor scuffs, but nothing a bit of polish won't fix. Though I did have a strong word with the driver. A very strong word. He didn't seem overly concerned, mind you. Did you see what that bloke, 'AngryYorkshireMan' tweeted about the traffic on the A19? Said it was like a car park. Oh, don’t even  start  with Twitter, Liam. It’s just a breeding ground for negativity. Honestly, sometimes I think people forget there are actual humans on the other end of those screens. Twitter? Is that one of those…internet things? I tried to understand it once, your brother explained it, but it all sounded terribly confusing. A lot of shouting into the void, as far as I could gather. It's…complicated, Mum. It’s a microblogging site. People share thoughts, news, opinions… mostly complaints, if we're being honest. It's good for finding out stuff, though. Like when the buses are cancelled. Happened yesterday, nearly missed school. Speaking of school, how was your French test, Liam? Did you manage to remember all the irregular verbs? Ugh, don’t remind me. It was horrible. Madame Dubois is trying to turn us all into pretentious Frenchmen. I think I got…some of them right. French! I used to be quite fluent, you know. Spent a summer in Normandy after university. Beautiful place. Though the cheese…rather strong. You’ve never mentioned that before, Mum. Normandy, I mean. Oh, it was a long time ago. Before your father, before all this. Seems like another life. Now, is anyone thinking about supper? I'm famished. This travelling has taken it out of me. I was thinking of a shepherd’s pie. Comfort food for a stressful day. And afterwards, maybe a game of cards? Can we watch something after? There's a new sci-fi show on… We’ll see, Liam.

…and honestly, the dentist said Leo’s getting a bit sloppy with his brushing again. Honestly, it’s like talking to a brick wall. I tell him, ‘Two minutes, Leo,  two  minutes!’ But he’s off, thinking about… well, probably video games. Is it nearly Easter? Can I have chocolate eggs then? Pleeease? Leo  always  forgets brushing properly. He says it's boring. Can I have a purple egg? Yes, Easter’s coming. And yes, you can both have chocolate eggs. But  after  you’ve eaten something that isn’t pure sugar, alright? And Leo, that applies to you too when you're home. Speaking of which, did you remember to book that hearing test for Ashaad? He mentioned it was bothering him again. Ashaad? He’s the one who’s really good at maths, isn’t he? Better than me. He lets me copy sometimes! But Miss Periwinkle says that's cheating. That's good he’s good at Maths, but copying isn't the answer, darling. And yes, I did book Ashaad’s hearing test. It’s next Thursday. I’m hoping it’s nothing, but he’s been complaining about a ringing in his ears. It worries me. Honestly, teenagers… so many things going on. My ears sometimes feel funny when I'm really quiet. Like… humming. That's probably fine, sweetie. It’s different if it’s constant and bothering you. Speaking of things bothering me…have you two given any thought to what you want to do for your birthday? It’s a combined one, remember? I want a Monet painting party! Like the one we saw in that book? We can all paint water lilies! No! I want a trip to the science museum! They have a dinosaur exhibit now. A  real  one! Well, bones of one. A Monet painting party  and  a dinosaur exhibit? That sounds…ambitious. It’s the same day, you know. You share a birthday. It’s already a miracle you tolerate sharing a cake. I don't mind sharing cake. Especially if it’s chocolate. But dinosaurs are cooler than flowers! Flowers are boring. Unless they’re really smelly. Like…radishes. Radishes aren’t flowers! And I thought you hated radishes! I do! But they smell strong. Like a dinosaur breath. We  could  go to the science museum  and  paint water lilies. We could paint dinosaurs  in  the water lilies!
