Honestly, I’m still wrecked from that commute. Two hours each way is  brutal , even for a Friday. How was yours, Liv? Did you manage to avoid the M25 chaos? You poor thing! Two hours? No, thankfully my route was relatively clear. I cut across the A20, a bit of a detour, but so much better than sitting on the M25. Though, honestly, seeing you now, slumped on the sofa with a glass of wine already…makes me want to join you. Rough day with Mr. Henderson, bless him. Swallowing difficulties, and he just kept trying to explain quantum physics to me  while  trying to eat a biscuit. Oh, Liv! Only you. Quantum physics and biscuits – sounds…complex. I swear, sometimes copywriting feels easy after hearing your work stories. Though today was mostly just rewrites on that toothpaste ad. "Brighten your smile!" Honestly. I'm starting to dream in dental hygiene. Oh god, the toothpaste ads. The relentless positivity! Still, pays the bills, yeah? Speaking of which…have you started thinking about saving for a deposit yet? We were talking about it, and frankly, it’s terrifying looking at house prices around here. Ashford is creeping up, you know? Don’t even  mention  house prices. It’s enough to give anyone a panic attack. I’ve got a bit stashed, but nowhere near enough for anything decent. Plus, I'm thinking about doing that online course in SEO…that’s another few hundred quid gone. It feels like I’m constantly running to stand still, financially. What are you and Ben doing? Are you thinking of sticking around Ashford long-term? Ben’s dad keeps offering us a plot in his garden, to build an annexe. Tempting, actually. Avoids the deposit madness, and we’d be near his care. He’s getting a bit more forgetful, you know? Mum’s taking it hard though, constantly worried. It’s…a lot. But moving away doesn't feel right just yet. We talk about maybe renovating the garden shed into a little office space for both of us, working from home more. That’s a lovely idea. Honestly, your family is so sweet. Mine…well, Mum's still convinced I need to get a 'proper' job. She keeps sending me civil service job adverts. As if! She doesn’t understand this whole creative thing at all. Remember when I tried to explain what a brand voice was at Christmas?

…and honestly, the hills around Almondsbury were  brutal . Not like these gentle Cotswold slopes you get now. Proper, teeth-gritting hills. We’d cycle for miles, just me and my brother, delivering messages for old Mrs. Higgins. She always paid in barley sugars, which was the real reward, of course. Mind you, the bikes were ancient. Heavy, clunky things. Nothing like these fancy racing bikes people have now. Barley sugars! That takes me back. Though my cycling was more about escaping my mother’s piano practice. Ramsgate wasn't exactly hilly, but the sea air… that was something. Though I remember getting hopelessly lost trying to cycle to Broadstairs once. Ended up in a farmyard, covered in mud, and the farmer wasn’t best pleased. Escaping piano practice. A noble pursuit. Manchester wasn’t exactly known for scenic cycle routes either, back then. Mostly cobbles and trams. Though, thinking about it, my father used to take me on long rides out to the Cheshire plains. Completely flat, thankfully. My own adventures were more…academic. Always buried in a book. You lot and your cycling! I was always more interested in dismantling things. Even as a boy. Took apart my mother’s radio once. Didn’t go down well. Dentistry felt like a natural extension of that, actually, fiddling with tiny things. Early days with the NHS were…interesting. Perks, you know. We used to get incredibly cheap sailing holidays. Sailing? Really, Arthur? Oh, absolutely! The Department of Health had a fleet of yachts, apparently. "Continuing Medical Education at Sea!" they called it. I remember one trip – lectures all at sea with your oral surgeon! Absolutely bizarre. Good wine though, admittedly. Nothing like that now, of course. Everything’s tightened up. Everything’s tightened up and expensive! I was looking at Prague the other week – a little break. Flights are reasonable, but the accommodation… still pricey. Heard it’s beautiful though. The bridges, the architecture. Prague is stunning. I was there a couple of years ago. Managed to get into the Mucha Museum even though it was fully booked. A bit of a polite word with the attendant, a bit of knowing wink… still works sometimes, you know. People are surprisingly accommodating. I suspect a bit of grey hair helps. It  always  helps! Speaking of accommodating…have we finalised the jive night? Is the barn still available? Yes, fully booked. Old Man Hemmings has done a cracking job with it.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of content on TikTok is… exhausting. But you can't  ignore  it, can you? Especially if we're talking about grabbing the attention of, say, fifteen-year-olds learning film studies. Absolutely not. It’s a different language, though, isn’t it? I mean, I can  use  Instagram, mostly to see pictures of my niece, but TikTok feels… frantic. And trying to distill a nuanced understanding of Eisenstein’s montage theory into sixty seconds? That feels…sacrilegious, almost. Sacrilegious, perhaps a little dramatic, love. But I get your point. It’s the challenge, isn’t it? Not dumbing it down, but making it  accessible . I was thinking, maybe short-form case studies? Breaking down significant scenes – like the Odessa Steps from  Battleship Potemkin  – into five or six bite-sized clips. Focus on the editing, the pacing, the emotional impact. That’s… better. Still feels like we’re fighting against the platform, though. Everything’s about trends, dances, challenges. How do we make film analysis a ‘challenge’? “Recreate a shot from  Citizen Kane  using only household objects!”? It feels…forced. Haha, well, maybe not  that  forced. But you’re right, it needs to be engaging. What about focusing on the  process ? Showing behind-the-scenes stuff? Like, “How did Hitchcock build suspense in  Psycho ?” – and then show clips illustrating the techniques. We could even use student work, if we got permissions, of course. That makes it relatable. I like the student work idea. Authenticity. And potentially builds a community, too. We could run a competition, or feature good examples. But permissions will be a nightmare. School boards, parental consent… ugh. Still, it's worth considering. The competition angle is smart. Everything feels better when there’s a little gamification. Exactly! And it builds a bank of content. Look, the core idea is providing supplementary learning materials. This isn’t about becoming TikTok stars, it’s about filling a gap. Loads of students struggle with the practical application of theory. They can  describe  montage, but can they  do  it? This would give them examples, inspire them... maybe even kickstart a portfolio. That’s a good way to frame it. And the portfolio angle is clever. Attracts students who are thinking about further education, or even a career in the industry. What about other platforms, though? YouTube feels a bit more… curated. Space for longer-form content, maybe more in-depth analysis?

…and honestly, the tide was  enormous . You know how Cromer pier gets almost completely cut off at high tide? Well, it was threatening to do that at  low  tide, it was coming in so fast. Old Man Hemmings nearly lost his fishing gear, I swear. Hemmings and his fishing gear. That man’s lived and breathed the North Sea for eighty years, you’d think it wouldn't surprise him anymore. Still, sounds dramatic. We haven’t had a proper coastal walk in ages, have we? It's good to be back, even if it’s just around here. London feels so… landlocked. Absolutely. I missed the smell. That incredibly specific smell of salt and seaweed and… well, just  sea . It’s in your blood when you grow up near it, isn’t it? I was thinking about Sarah the other day, actually. She always said she felt claustrophobic anywhere more than a couple of hours from the coast. Sarah? Oh, yes. It’s been a while. How  is  she? Last I heard she was still trying to get that marine biology research grant. She got it! Finally. She's off to the Maldives in September. Can you believe it? Studying coral bleaching. She’s ecstatic, obviously. She sent me the most rambling email, full of scientific jargon I didn’t understand, but the general gist was ‘dreams are coming true!’ That’s brilliant! She deserves it. Always been fiercely dedicated. Remember that trip we all took to Flamborough Head? She practically spent the whole time identifying every single piece of seaweed. And lecturing us all on the migratory patterns of guillemots. Honestly, she was in her element. Though, poor David looked utterly bewildered the entire time. He's much more of a mountains man, isn’t he? He is. He always did prefer solid ground under his feet. It’s funny, isn’t it? How people gravitate towards different landscapes. He finds the sea… unsettling, I think. Says it’s too vast, too unpredictable. He’s a control freak, darling. Everything needs to be neatly categorised. The sea refuses to be categorised. It just  is . Speaking of unsettling, have you spoken to James recently? He sounded dreadful on the phone last week. Not since then, no. He just mentioned a bit of stress at work, didn't he? Something about budget cuts and department restructuring? It’s more than that, I think.

Ooh, look at that dress! Proper fancy, innit? Though I reckon it'd look a bit daft tryin' to walk in that 'round Doncaster market. You'd be tripped up by a rogue cabbage before you could blink. It  is  dramatic, isn't it? Very avant-garde. Not exactly practical for a Tuesday at the factory though, is it? I mean, I deal with deadlines and deliveries, not flowing silks and impossible hemlines. What do  you  think, Chloe? You're the one with the artistic eye. Hmm, it’s definitely a statement piece. A bit much for a primary school classroom, definitely. Though, I do appreciate the colour blocking. It's surprisingly inspiring - maybe I can incorporate some bolder colours into my lesson plans. Think bright yellows and teals for the autumn displays. Colour blockin’s good. I’ve been tryin’ to get a bit more adventurous with me wardrobe, but it’s hard when everything in town is either beige or floral. Beige and floral! Where’s the  edge ? It’s depressing. I saw this leather jacket online the other day… proper biker-style. Ooh, send me the link! I’ve been meaning to upgrade mine. The one I have is… well, it's seen better days. It’s mostly held together by hope and a lot of safety pins at this point. Though, honestly, I’m slightly obsessed with wide-leg trousers at the moment. They’re so comfortable and somehow still look put-together. Wide-leg are good. Practical for chasing seven-year-olds around a playground, actually. You need freedom of movement! Though, I’m currently on a vintage kick. I found a brilliant little boutique near the market on Saturday. Got a gorgeous 60s shift dress for a steal. A vintage shop, eh? Cambridge is good for that sort of thing. Doncaster’s… well, let's just say charity shops are mostly full of things me grandma wore. Bless her, but her taste was… questionable. Did you see that cardigan she had, covered in cats? Oh dear! My nan had a similar one, but with dogs. The fashion cycle is truly terrifying sometimes. So, this boutique, Chloe, is it expensive? I'm trying to be sensible with my money, you know, save for a deposit. It’s not  cheap  cheap, but definitely reasonable. They specialise in properly vetted vintage, so you know it's not just falling apart.

…and then Mr. Harrison  actually  said my composition looked like a ‘splattered seagull’. A  splattered seagull ! Honestly, Mum, the audacity. It was abstract! It was meant to evoke… feeling! Oh, darling. Mr. Harrison does have a… particular way with words. He said my dissertation looked like a ‘wall of text held together by enthusiasm’ once. Seriously? He said that to a  postgraduate  student? That’s awful! Though… I suppose it wasn’t entirely inaccurate. I really did just ramble. But a splattered seagull?! I’m seriously considering switching to photography. It feels… safer. Less open to artistic interpretation, you know? Safer? Photography? You think so? It’s just a different kind of critique, love. People will still have opinions on your framing, your lighting, your subject matter. Though, I can see the appeal. It’s a lot less messy. Have you been taking many photos lately? That new camera is gathering dust, I suspect. I took some down on the beach yesterday. Trying to get the light on the waves, but it’s so hard! It always looks… flat in the photos. It never  feels  like being there. It’s frustrating. It makes me think I’m not very good at anything creative. Don't say that, sweetheart. You’re brilliant. It just takes practice. Remember when I first started trying to paint? Everything looked like a blurry mess. It was horrific. Speaking of things being horrific, work was a nightmare today. Mrs. Periwinkle decided  she  knew better about scheduling the doctor's appointments. She’s a nightmare. Honestly. Oh no, not Mrs. Periwinkle! She sounds…intense. Is she still going on about her prize-winning begonias? Constantly. She genuinely believes her begonias are the key to world peace. And she tried to rearrange the whole schedule based on when they needed watering! I had to politely, but firmly, explain that doctor's appointments tend to take priority over floral hydration. You’re amazing, Mum. You deal with so much. It puts my seagull-related artistic trauma into perspective. It's all perspective, isn’t it? And besides, you’ll learn to laugh at things like that eventually. What about college applications? Have you started looking at prospectuses properly yet? They’re starting to drop through the letterbox like confetti. Ugh, don’t remind me. It’s terrifying. I keep thinking about what if I choose the wrong thing? What if I don’t get in anywhere?

…Honestly, Doreen, this application form. It's a blooming nightmare. 'Please detail your digital literacy.' Digital literacy! At my age! They might as well ask if I can fly to the moon. Oh, Arthur, you and technology. It won't kill you. Just put 'basic email and internet browsing'. That's probably the truth of it, isn't it? Though I suspect you’re a bit more savvy than you let on, watching those YouTube videos about… what was it, 3D printing little gnomes? Don't remind me. Nearly set the shed on fire trying to calibrate the thing. And those gnomes were a disaster. Looked more like melted goblins, if you ask me. No, it's the principle. They want a life history, too. Seems like they want to know where I buried the treasure, not if I can fill in a form for a blooming library card. Morning, you two. Sounds like Arthur’s wrestling with bureaucracy again. Need a hand? I spent half my life filling in forms for the education authority. I’m practically an expert in pointless detail. Mark! Thank goodness. Maybe  you  can translate this into English. They want to know about ‘challenging behaviours’ I’ve encountered. Challenging behaviours! In a library? What, people arguing over the latest Jackie Collins novel? He’s exaggerating, dear. He’s trying to volunteer at the local library, helping with the kids' story time. It’s very sweet, actually, even if he pretends to be horrified by the whole idea. That’s brilliant, Arthur. Though, after a day dealing with thirty seven year sixes, a quiet library sounds idyllic. We had little Timmy Nelson yesterday – wouldn't sit still for five seconds, kept trying to build a fort out of the chairs. Honestly, some of them… Sounds like a handful. Reminds me of young Kevin, next door. Absolute terror. Always kicking a football at the house. His mother… well, let's just say she wasn’t the strictest parent. Speaking of outside, did you see the state of old Mrs. Higgins’ new fencing? Utterly shambolic. Oh,  terrible . Bob did it, didn’t he? Bob the Builder, more like Bob the Bodger! All wonky and leaning. Honestly, you pay good money and get that. It’s the younger generation, they haven’t been taught a proper trade. It's the rush job mentality. Everyone wants it done yesterday. Quality suffers.

…and honestly, Arthur, the paperwork is  exhausting . Just mountains of it. Visas, proof of funds, tenancy agreements… you wouldn’t believe. It’s not like when I was teaching and had to mark essays, this is a different kind of bureaucratic nightmare. Goodness me, sounds a proper faff, doesn't it? Still, worth it, though, eh? Getting Maisie settled here. You’ve been wanting this for ages. Though, I must say, Brighton's gotten expensive since  I  started teaching. Finding a decent flat within your budget… that’s the tricky bit, I imagine. That’s exactly it. It’s not that I can’t  afford  it, exactly. It’s just… I’m trying to be sensible. I don’t want to deplete everything, you know? I want a cushion. Things aren’t getting cheaper, and well, let's just say my pension doesn't stretch  quite  as far as I’d hoped these days. Being a retired teacher isn’t exactly a path to riches, is it? Especially one who… well, didn’t continue working after retirement. Now, don’t start on that again, Elsie. You dedicated your life to those children. That’s worth more than any salary. And you’ve always been careful with money. Remember when you clipped coupons religiously? Though I admit, you drove me mad with it at the time. Oh, you always did exaggerate. It was strategic saving! And yes, I  was  good with money. But things have changed. And having Maisie here… it means more than just rent. It’s setting her up. Helping her with job hunting. Maybe even helping with a deposit if she wants to eventually get a place of her own. That’s a generous thought, Elsie. She’s lucky to have you. How is she feeling about the move, anyway? Sounds like a big leap, leaving everything behind in Australia. She's… apprehensive, naturally. She loved her life out there, the weather, the lifestyle. She's built a good career, but she's feeling… adrift lately. She said she misses having family around. Properly around, not just Christmas cards and video calls. And she’s worried about finding work here, especially in her field. Graphic design is competitive, even in London, never mind Brighton. Well, she’s a talented girl. She always was. Remember all those drawings she used to do as a child? Covered the fridge, they did.

…and honestly, the whole thing with the Scottish referendum again… it’s just exhausting, isn’t it? Feels like we’ve been here before, countless times. I was reading some analysis this morning suggesting Humza Yousaf is really walking a tightrope. Exhausting is the word, David. Absolutely exhausting. I remember the last one so vividly. The worry, the uncertainty… Brighton felt incredibly tense, surprisingly. A lot of holidaymakers having very pointed political discussions on the beach! And you’re right about Yousaf. He needs a miracle. The polls aren’t looking good for them, are they? Not particularly. And it's not just the polls, it's  how  they’re polling. It feels like the momentum’s entirely gone the other way. It's a tough sell convincing people another referendum is what the country needs right now, especially with everything else going on. Speaking of needing to convince people… did you hear back about the Head of Department role? Oh, good question. Yes, actually. Had the second interview on Tuesday. It went… adequately. Honestly, I'm not holding my breath. The panel were very focused on my experience with digital learning platforms. Which, as you know, isn't exactly my forte. I managed to bluff my way through, but I think they saw right through me. Oh, that’s a shame. You’d be brilliant at it, honestly, the way you explain complex ideas… digital platforms aside. But I can see how that might be a sticking point. Did Dr. Albright have a strong presence on the panel? She can be… formidable. Formidable is putting it mildly! She completely dominated the conversation. Asked me three times about incorporating AI into lesson plans. AI! Honestly, at my age, I'm just trying to work the interactive whiteboard without embarrassing myself. She’s a bright woman, no question, but she’s all about the ‘new’, and I’m… less so. Well, don’t write yourself off yet. You’ve got years of experience, and that counts for a lot. They can’t all be obsessed with the latest tech. Anyway, enough about work stress. How’s Emily doing? I haven’t seen her since last Christmas. She’s good, she's good. Just finished her first year at university – studying History, of all things. Can you believe it? After all my efforts to steer her towards something… practical. History, that’s fantastic!

Right, so the crucial element, obviously, is the cheese. Not too strong, mind you. You don't want to overpower the…suspense. Honestly, building this mousetrap game is proving far more complex than I anticipated. It’s supposed to be a simple Rube Goldberg machine, ending with a tiny flag being raised when the mouse… well, attempts a heist. Simple for  you , perhaps, Penelope. You're the engineer of the family. I’m just here to hold things and occasionally offer unhelpful suggestions. Though I still maintain a catapult would be far more dramatic. A catapult  would  be cool, Dad. Imagine launching a tiny felt mouse across the living room! Although, Grandma might not appreciate the collateral damage. Collateral damage is my specialty! Though usually involving pasta sauce, not felt mice. Just saying. Almost got the béchamel right this time. Jamie, darling, perhaps focus on the béchamel before contemplating potential mouse-related destruction. Penelope, are you sure this little spring is strong enough? It looks a bit…limp. It is, Margaret, it is! It’s calibrated for a miniature Swiss cheese cube. It’s all about the physics, you see. Though it does remind me of that time we were in Ohio… Remember, darling, the county fair? The mechanical ducks? Ohio… Yes. The sheer  volume  of deep-fried everything was a shock to the system. And the obsession with those games of chance. Every other stall was trying to get you to throw a ring onto a bottle. I’ve seen videos of those. Insane. And the prizes! Giant stuffed animals no one needs. Right? Like, who  needs  a six-foot-tall banana? It’s a cultural thing, I think. American children are encouraged to win, to collect. It's very… competitive. I read an article about it once, the pressure they're under from a very young age. It’s quite different from how we were raised. Different is an understatement. I remember taking little Thomas – that was your nephew, wasn’t it, Margaret? – to a birthday party in Connecticut. Every child had a personal assistant essentially dedicated to ensuring they enjoyed the festivities. Honestly, it was bizarre. Like tiny, highly-strung emperors. That sounds about right. I spent a month in Washington D.C. on a secondment a few years ago. The work ethic was relentless. No one seemed to take a proper lunch break. Just fuelled by coffee and sheer ambition.

Right, operation “wardrobe refresh” is officially underway. Honestly, this heat is  killing  my sensible Norwich layering strategies. Oh, good lord. How many bags is that? And “wardrobe refresh”? More like “wardrobe overhaul” at this rate. Did you find anything you actually  needed , or did the lure of the silk market just get to you again? Needed is a strong word, darling. Let’s say… strategically acquired. And it wasn’t  just  the silk market! There was that little boutique near the university too. They had some lovely linen things. You know I struggle in this humidity. Everything feels so… constricting. Linen, alright. That’s… marginally sensible. Though I seem to recall a similar "strategic acquisition" of cashmere last winter, which proved remarkably unsuitable for a Tianjin January. That was a  different  situation! I was feeling homesick and the cashmere reminded me of Mum’s favourite jumper. This is practical! Look. This is a linen dress, see? Flowy, breathable, will hide the fact I’ve been eating too much dim sum. And this… …is just beautiful. Proper silk, hand-painted. Beautiful and… entirely useless for lecturing on post-structuralism, I presume? You'll be looking like a particularly flamboyant art history professor. Oh, don’t be such a pedant. It’s for evenings! And weekends! Sometimes a lecturer needs a bit of pizzazz, you know. We’re not robots. Besides, I got a really good deal. The vendor practically  begged  me to take it off his hands. I suspect he's very good at the art of the sale. Let me guess, you bartered him down to half his original asking price while simultaneously offering him life advice? Perhaps. He did seem rather stressed about his daughter’s upcoming Gaokao exams. Anyway, look at this! These are amazing. They’re supposed to be really comfortable for cycling. I thought I could cycle to the university sometimes, instead of taking the Didi. Cycling in this traffic? Are you mad? You'll need a helmet, reflective gear, and a comprehensive life insurance policy. Plus, those trousers look like they've been designed to get caught in a bicycle chain. You're such a pessimist! They're a bit bold, I admit, but I thought they would cheer me up on dreary mornings. And honestly, I’m tired of looking like everyone else. All the beige and navy. I want a bit of colour in my life.

Ah, now  that  was a match, wasn’t it? Absolutely brutal out there. Sexton was lookin' a bit rattled towards the end, I thought. Nearly cost us, that last penalty. It was good! But I still think France are better. They just… play differently. More, like, attacking all the time. You say that every time France play, darling. You’re a bit biased, aren’t you? And you haven’t even been to a proper rugby match yet, have you? Well, no. But I watch them on telly! And my mate, Alfie, he says France are going to win the Six Nations. Alfie needs to spend less time listenin' to blather and more time learnin' the offside rule. Though, I'll grant you, the French have a flair. But Ireland has the grit. Grit, you say? Sounds like my old students! All teeth and determination, they were. Though usually directed at avoiding homework, not tackling opponents. Oh, I imagine so, Mary! A different kind of scrum altogether. Speaking of which, Oisin, you were quiet as a mouse during the match. Did you enjoy it? Yeah, it was cool. Though it went on  forever . Can I be excused, please? I need to finish signin’ everyone’s birthday cards. It’s Gran’s birthday tomorrow, right? That's right, sweetheart. And be careful with the glitter glue! Last time… well, let’s just say we were finding glitter for weeks. I know, I know! I’ll be careful. Can I go now? Go on, lad. And don’t forget to wish your Gran a happy birthday properly. None of this mumbled ‘Happy birthday’ stuff. Fine, fine… He’s a good lad, that one. Active, too. Is he still playin’ football at school? He is, yes. Although, honestly, I’m not sure he’s terribly… gifted. He tries, bless him, but he’s not exactly scoring goals left, right, and centre. He's more interested in the social aspect, you know? Ah, sure isn’t that half the battle? Learnin’ how to be a team player. More valuable than a fancy footwork any day. Though, a bit of footwork wouldn't go amiss, mind you. True. He’s also started trying out for the school athletics team. Says he wants to do long jump. Long jump! Now  that  takes courage. And a good run-up. Reminds me of young Hamish MacIntyre… terrible at maths, but could leap like a salmon.

…and honestly, the estate agent was  insisting  on “character features.” Character features! It's damp, Sarah, undeniably damp. Lovely fireplace, sure, but sprouting moss isn’t a ‘character feature’, it’s a structural issue. Honestly, Lincolnshire must be blissfully free of this sort of thing. You know it! We get flooding, obviously, being so flat, but rarely anything as…atmospheric as moss-ridden walls. Though Auntie Brenda’s cottage near the Fens had a certain damp charm. Are you still looking around Aylesbury then? I thought you were leaning towards Leighton Buzzard? I was, but everything there felt…new. All these identikit houses. I need wonky walls, you know? Something with a  history . And Aylesbury’s closer to Mum and Dad, which is a big factor now, especially thinking about… well, you know. Babies? Everyone’s at it. Even Ben’s got a friend who’s expecting. It's a proper contagion. Are you and Tom thinking about it seriously then? You've been dropping hints for months. Hints doesn’t cover it. We’re…discussing. Tom’s very practical. Costs, space, career impacts. It’s all spreadsheets and risk assessments with him. I’m just picturing tiny jumpers. And needing a bigger car. It's daunting, isn't it? Absolutely. Though tiny jumpers  are  exceptionally cute. And honestly, you’d be a brilliant mum. All that patience you have dealing with phonetics students… that’s proper training! Speaking of clothes, did I ever give you back that navy blue coat? The one I borrowed for the conference in York? Oh! Yes, you did. It’s in the wardrobe, I think. Though knowing my wardrobe, it’s buried under a pile of research papers. I need a serious clear-out. Maybe when we’ve found a house. Decluttering before bringing… another human into the mix. Sensible. I'm trying to be more mindful about what I buy now. It all feels so wasteful when you think about how quickly things get outgrown. My little brother, Leo, was a  machine  for growing. Mum was constantly sewing hems down! Leo! God, I remember him. The terror of family gatherings. Always dismantling things and asking incredibly detailed questions about how things worked. Did he ever learn to speak anything other than Lincolnshire dialect? He’s remarkably eloquent now, actually. He did a year abroad in Spain during uni. Became completely fluent. Quite the contrast with me trying to grapple with German in sixth form.

… honestly, I still reckon your nan thinks I’m a bit of a layabout, even after explainin’ what an artworker  actually  does. She just sees ‘artist’ and assumes I’m paintin’ landscapes all day. She's a product of her generation, mate. Anything vaguely creative is a bit… suspect, in her eyes. Though, to be fair, explainin’ the complexities of digital art to someone who still thinks a mobile phone is witchcraft is a losing battle. Did you manage to sell that print you were workin’ on last week? The Bedford skyline one? Ooh, yeah, that was a good one! Proper moody, innit? I saw it on your Insta. Sold it quick, did ya? She’d probably like that one, actually – it’s got buildings in it, looks…productive. Yeah, went to a fella in Brighton. Online, obviously. Turns out he’s a proper guitar enthusiast. Kept goin’ on about the tonal qualities of mahogany. Which, frankly, went right over my ‘ead. I just make the pretty pictures, I don’t  play  ‘em. You still thrashin’ about with yours, Liam? Trying to. Been busy teaching, so less time to practice. Although, I’m thinkin’ of gettin’ back into MMA again. Need to do  something  to de-stress after a day of explainin’ the subjunctive to teenagers. MMA? Blimey. You’re a brave man. I’d rather wrestle a badger. I'm stickin’ to the garden, cheers. Less chance of gettin’ your face rearranged. Though, old Mrs. Higgins’ poodle  did  try to take a chunk out of me last Tuesday… Poodles are evil. Pure evil. My Auntie Shirley had one. Used to glare at you like you owed it money. Speaking of animals, did you see that thing on telly about battery farms? Absolutely disgusting. How people can treat animals like that… Horrific, isn't it? Makes you want to go vegan, almost. Though then I'd have to explain to my uncle why I’m not eatin’ his roast beef. That’s a battle I’m not prepared to fight. He’s still convinced a good bit of red meat builds character. He’s not wrong, though! A good Sunday roast  does  sort you right out. Don't knock it ‘til you’ve tried it. Anyway, you two are gettin’ all serious. Anyone fancy a board game? Got ‘Ticket to Ride’ here. Or we could risk ‘Monopoly’ and end up with a full-blown argument about property ownership.

Honestly, this Bolognese is taking  forever . And you promised you’d chop the onions… Hey, I did! Eventually. I was just… researching. Very important research. “Research”? Into what? The optimal onion-chopping technique? No! Cars, actually. I was looking at… well, realistically, getting something a bit more reliable. This bus commute is killing me. Especially now the weather’s turning. Oh, here we go. The ‘I deserve a new car’ speech. Again. We literally just talked about this last week. It's not a speech, it's a… a logical assessment of my needs! The 8:15 is constantly delayed, I’m standing room only, and Brenda from accounts keeps breathing down my neck. A car would solve  so  many problems. It would also solve  new  problems. Like, the one where we have absolutely no savings because you’ve spent all your money on petrol and insurance and… car washes? Okay, okay, fair point. But think about the time saved! I could actually get some work done during the commute, instead of battling for space with a suitcase and a damp umbrella. Plus, think of the spontaneous weekend trips! We could actually  go  somewhere. We went to Whitby last month. And the month before that we went to York. Both involved trains, which you conveniently forgot to complain about. That’s different. Those were planned trips. I’m talking about freedom! Being able to just… go. And it doesn’t have to be something fancy. I was looking at older models, something sensible. Like a… a Ford Focus. Sensible. Right. Knowing you, "sensible" will quickly morph into “needs racing stripes and a spoiler”. I resent that! I’m a mature adult. Mostly. Look, I’ve been looking at finance options too. Maybe a small loan, repayments spread out… Absolutely not. We’re saving for a deposit on a flat, remember?  That's  our priority. A car is a luxury, not a necessity. You manage perfectly well on the bus. It builds character. Builds character and gives me a permanent crick in my neck. Plus, you benefit too! I could pick you up from work sometimes, save you the walk in the rain. I enjoy the walk. It clears my head. And frankly, after a day of dealing with spreadsheets and impossible deadlines, the last thing I want is to be trapped in a metal box with you singing along to 80s power ballads.

“Right, that’s lovely. Proper brew. You wouldn’t get this down south, would ya, lad? All weak and wishy-washy. Now, are you sure you've got all yer homework sorted, Ethan? Your grandma’s been givin’ me the eye all afternoon, expectin’ me to quiz ya.” “Yeah, yeah, Grandma. Sorted. Mostly. History’s a bit of a nightmare though. The Tudors. So boring.” “Boring?! The Tudors were  anything  but boring, Ethan! Kings wi’ six wives, plots and betrayals, a right royal mess! Your great-grandad – bless ‘is soul – used to say Henry VIII were a bit like a spoilt bairn, gettin’ rid of anyone who didn’t tell ‘im what he wanted to ‘ear.” “Aye, that’s right. And didn’t ‘e have a fondness for a good roast, that ‘un? Heard tell he could put away a whole ox single-handed.” “Seriously? A whole ox? That’s…intense.” “Your grandad’s pullin’ yer leg, love. Though the man  did  ‘ave a good appetite, I'll give ‘im that. Now, Ethan, about the leaky tap in the bathroom… I’ve had a look, but it’s one o’ them fancy mixer things. I’m not touchin’ it. Your dad’s useless with DIY. I was thinkin’ maybe young Matthew, your cousin, could pop round tomorrow? He’s a dab hand at most things, that lad.” “Matthew's a good lad, aye. Always willing to lend a ‘and. Though he’s puttin’ on weight, that one. Far too many takeaways, I reckon.” “He’s building muscle, Grandma! He’s been going to the gym.” “Gym? What for? Back in my day, a good day’s work  was  your gym. Diggin’ trenches, carryin’ bricks… that built yer muscles!” “Times change, Arthur. Times change. Speaking of changes, I’m thinking of re-papering the hallway. That floral one’s been up for…well, let's just say a long time. Something a bit more modern, maybe?” “Oh, don’t you dare! I like the floral. Reminds me of your mother. She picked it out herself, you know. Said it brightened the place up.” “I know, Mum, I know. It’s just… it’s a bit faded, isn’t it? And honestly, it clashes with everything. I was thinkin’ maybe a nice, neutral beige?” “Beige? Sounds like a hospital ward. A bit of colour’s good for the soul, Edna. Keeps things lively.”

…and honestly, the amount of glitter that came with the pirate eye patches is  shocking . It's everywhere. I found some in the dog's water bowl this morning! Captain Bluebeard's glitter beard! Mine shot glitter when I sneezed! It was awesome! It certainly was… messy. Right, who wants more toast? We need fuel for all this piratical energy, and then we need to talk about something completely different - Shakespeare Week. Shakespeare? Is that like pirates, but with… fancy clothes? It’s a bit different, sweetheart. Pirates are about adventure and treasure. Shakespeare wrote plays – stories told through talking and acting. He was a really, really famous writer a long, long time ago. Did he fight pirates? Hmm, that’s a good question. Probably not  personally  fighting pirates. But his plays sometimes  featured  pirates, or kings, or fairies... all sorts of exciting characters. We’re doing a whole week of it at school, and then… guess what? What?! We’re going to Stratford-upon-Avon! That’s where Shakespeare was born. We’ll see his house, maybe even a play! A  real  play? Like, with costumes? Exactly! A real play, with costumes and actors. It’ll be amazing. It's a long drive though, so we’ll need audiobooks. Any requests? Maybe a pirate story  about  Shakespeare? I doubt one exists… Can we go to the circus workshop  after  Stratford? Please, please, please! You remembered! Yes, we can. It’s the one in that real circus tent, isn't it? The one just outside Cambridge? With the trapeze! I want to learn the trapeze! We’ll see about the trapeze, darling. It’s more juggling and balancing, I think. But it's a proper circus family running it, so it will be brilliant. It's next Saturday, right? After our Easter picture hunt. I'm making Easter pictures of pirates and Shakespeare! They’re having a sword fight! That sounds… ambitious. Very creative, though. Are you using glitter on those too? Maybe a little. I'm building a pirate ship for the Easter hunt! It'll be hidden in the garden! Excellent! Okay, next on the list… remember that stop motion animation app I downloaded? We talked about making a short film? The one with the little figures? That’s the one! I was thinking, maybe we could do a scene from one of Shakespeare’s plays? A tiny, tiny Shakespeare play?

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of it all! They just hauled us off the boat, didn’t they, Derek? Like we were common criminals. All because we were attempting to sail from Jeddah to Cyprus. Audacity is putting it mildly, Margaret. More like utter lunacy! You and a small sailboat tackling the Red Sea… Honestly. I remember you calling, practically hysterical, explaining the situation. Something about ‘misunderstanding the port regulations’? Misunderstanding? That’s a generous description, Derek. She’d ‘misunderstood’ that needing explicit permission to leave Saudi Arabian waters was, shall we say, a formality. And that attempting to bribe a port official with a box of Turkish Delight wouldn’t raise eyebrows. Now, Arthur, don't exaggerate! It wasn't a bribe, it was a… a gesture of goodwill! They were very fond of Turkish Delight, apparently. And the regulations  were  confusing. Everything is in Arabic, you know. And the man just wouldn’t listen to reason. He kept pointing at a document I couldn't read, shouting. Reminds me of attempting to explain the complexities of root canal treatment to a Bedouin chieftain. Different language, same glazed look of incomprehension. Although, thankfully, no arrests were involved. You actually treated a chieftain, Geoffrey? Tell us about that. Your time in Riyadh must have been… eventful. Oh, it was. Riyadh in the seventies was a world unto itself. Very isolated, very conservative. Finding decent dental supplies was a nightmare, let alone explaining modern procedures. This particular chieftain had a dreadful abscess. Took three sessions, a considerable amount of charm, and a truly enormous pot of strong coffee to get it sorted. Saudi Arabia… teaching there was certainly an experience. The women, naturally, had to be completely veiled. And alcohol was, of course, strictly forbidden. Though, rumour had it, there were ways… extremely expensive ways… to obtain it. A friend of mine, teaching English at the university, managed to cultivate a network. Apparently, diplomats were the key. Everything went through them, at exorbitant prices. He said it tasted like victory, even if it  was  watered down and cost a month’s salary. It's a strange thing, isn't it? How different cultures deal with alcohol. I spent a summer in Spain once, and you practically swim in the stuff. Everywhere, all the time. Then you go to places like Saudi… total prohibition. Makes it all the more attractive, I suppose. Absolutely.

… honestly, I don't know  where  he gets it from. Leaving wet towels on the bathroom floor, AGAIN. Honestly, it's like living with a teenager who actively  tries  to cultivate mildew. Oh, don't I know it! Liam was the same. Remember the great sock epidemic of '08? Found them… well, let’s just say in places socks shouldn’t be. A teenage boy’s sense of hygiene is a mythical beast. It’s not  that  bad! I just… forget sometimes. It’s not like I’m deliberately trying to grow a science experiment in the bathroom. “Forget?” Leo, darling, it’s a towel. It’s a singular item. And the bathroom is literally five steps from your bedroom. It's not like scaling Everest to hang it up. He’s at that age, love. It's all about testing boundaries. Though, I still think your mum had a hand in Liam’s sock-related shenanigans. She always seemed to foster a bit of mischievousness. Mum? She was a saint! Though, she DID have a soft spot for Liam, admittedly. Speaking of which, are we still on for Cornwall this year? I was looking at cottages near St Ives. Cornwall sounds good. Maybe I could take my skateboard? They’ve got a decent skatepark there, apparently. As long as you promise to be careful! Remember what happened to young Tom Henderson last summer? Broken arm, the poor lad. And no having friends round at the cottage without asking, eh? We need a bit of peace and quiet too. Exactly. It’s a family holiday, not a teen rave. Though, thinking about it, Tom Henderson’s mum was furious. Said he’d been trying to impress a girl. Honestly, the drama! Are you seeing anyone at the moment, Leo? Mum! Seriously?! That's… personal. Oh, go on, lad. Your mum and I have been through worse than teenage crushes. Though, honestly, some of the stories I heard at school… it was like a soap opera. It's just… I want you to be careful. And I want to know who you're spending your time with. Remember what happened with Sarah Jenkins? That was  ages  ago! And it wasn't my fault! She was the one who… ugh, never mind. Can we talk about something else? Like, what you two were doing before I walked in? We were just discussing work.

Right, honestly, that  burek  was proper good, wasn’t it? Best thing I've eaten all week, and that's saying something considering all the seafood. Could eat about five more right now, easy.      Aye, it was lovely. Proper flaky pastry. Old Mrs. Petrovic makes a beautiful one, bless her. It’s a world away from anything you get back in Bolton, eh? Though I still miss a decent Eccles cake, mind you.      Can we put some music on, please? This countryside is nice, but it’s a bit…quiet. And I’m  starving  again. Is there anywhere else to get food near where we're going?      Hold your horses, young man. We’re heading to the truffle farm, remember? Apparently, the chef there does a phenomenal truffle pasta. They even cultivate their own. It's supposed to be a real experience. Though, I must say, I’m still slightly dubious about the hype around truffles. Overpriced fungus, if you ask me.      Oh, don’t be like that, David! Truffles are amazing! It’s an  experience . And honestly, after seeing that demonstration in Motovun, I’m practically a truffle expert now. They said the scent is what makes them special - like, it mimics a pheromone for wild boar.      That’s right, it's because of the wild boar that they used to use pigs to find them, but the pigs would eat them all! Now they use dogs, much cleverer, don't you think? Speaking of clever, did I tell you about young Emily Carter at the hospital? She’s doing her Masters on stem cell research, fascinating stuff. Completely different world to delivering babies, but brilliant.      Stem cells, eh? Interesting. Always seems like a bit of a moral minefield to me, but the potential is undeniable. Sounds like a brighter future for medicine. How’s your teaching going, Sarah? Still battling with teenagers and TikTok?      You have no idea. They’re obsessed! Actually, I'm marking their History essays on America at the moment. It's all about the roaring twenties and the jazz age. It's funny because they're all trying to sound like they're in  The Great Gatsby . One of them actually started an essay with "Old Sport!" Honestly.      America’s cool. I wanna go to America. They have, like, way better football. Proper football, not this…Premier League stuff.      Proper football? That's a bold statement, lad!

…and honestly, the sheer volume of data is just  wild . We’re looking at dialectal shifts in younger speakers using social media, and it's nothing like the gradual changes we’ve seen historically. It’s almost…instantaneous. Like, a new slang term originates in TikTok and is ubiquitous within a week. Blimey. That sounds…exhausting, actually. I deal with trends, but usually in terms of algorithms and user engagement. Which is bad enough. Trying to track  language  evolving that fast? That’s a different beast. Though, I suppose it makes your job consistently interesting. Interesting is one word for it. Terrifying is another. I mean, I barely understand what my younger cousins are saying half the time. And I  live  with them when I'm home. It's like they've developed their own secret language. It’s not entirely secret, thankfully. That’s where the social media data comes in handy. But yeah, it’s intense. We’re seeing grammatical structures being actively reshaped, not just vocabulary. It’s fascinating, but also…potentially disruptive. What about you two? Keeping busy? Still beating the Cambridge rush hour, Leo? Sadly, yes. Though I managed to snag a parking space practically outside the Printing House today, so I’m feeling unreasonably triumphant. It’s mostly running campaigns at the moment. Trying to get people excited about…well, mostly textbooks, let’s be honest. Not the most glamorous world of digital marketing. Textbooks? Right. Sounds…stable. I’m mostly buried in spreadsheets, trying to keep the new museum exhibit on track. The one about the history of printing. Ironically, I spend all day on a laptop. It's a bit meta. The history of printing  here ? That’s brilliant! This building must be a goldmine for research. You’re surrounded by it. Do they cover the impact of movable type on vernacular languages? Because that’s a huge area. How readily accessible language became… Oh, that’s a good point, actually. I remember reading something about that in my history lectures. Didn't it contribute to the standardisation of English, ironically, after a period of massive dialectal variation? I think so. Old Man Hemmings – he’s the lead curator – is really passionate about it. He’s probably got a whole section dedicated to that. I’m more concerned with getting the interactive displays to  work  at this point. One of the touchscreens keeps freezing.

Oh, this is lovely, isn’t it? Just… open road, even if it  is  mostly motorway. Feels good to be moving again after that overnight stop. Though honestly, that campsite was a bit… basic. Basic is putting it mildly, Auntie Carol! More like a field with a leaky tap and a family of very opinionated geese. But hey, it was cheap, and it got us this far. Are you sure you’re comfortable? The suspension in Brenda isn’t exactly Rolls Royce quality. Perfectly comfortable, dear. A little bumpy, perhaps, but I’m used to a bit of a rattle, aren’t I? Besides, it’s a small price to pay for bypassing all those dreadful airports. Honestly, flying feels so… impersonal these days. This is much more civilized. Though I  do  miss having a proper cup of tea on demand. This travel kettle is a bit slow. Tell me about it! I’ve become intimately acquainted with instant coffee on this trip. I'm just glad we decided on driving, even with the extra time. It’s so much more…  real . And we’re seeing things! Remember that little village we passed with all the storks’ nests? Amazing. Oh yes! Quite picturesque. And the fields of sunflowers... Honestly, it's a world away from Cambridge. Though, speaking of which, have you remembered to forward my mail? I’m worried about bills piling up. Yes, Auntie Carol, I did that the day before we left. Everything's being redirected to my flat. I even put an out-of-office reply on your email, saying you’re ‘enjoying an extended period of adventurous exploration’. Sounded suitably mysterious, don’t you think? Very good! You always were a clever one. Right, Tarnow then. Is Kasia expecting us for lunch, or just tea? I didn’t quite catch that on the phone. Lunch, I think. She said she’s making  pierogi . Apparently, she's been practicing. She’s very excited to show off her skills. She also mentioned something about her neighbour bringing a homemade plum brandy. Oh my goodness.  Pierogi  and plum brandy! We’re in for a treat. Though, I’ll have to be careful with that brandy. It always goes straight to my head. Actually, perhaps I should warn Kasia. I don’t want to be regaling her with tales of my youth by 3 o'clock. She'll love that! Kasia  adores  hearing your stories, even the slightly embarrassing ones.

… honestly, that was a shocking tackle. Even with the sound off, you can  see  it was dodgy. Proper late. Though, looking at the kit, it's almost distracting, innit? That new City strip… it's just… busy. All those lines. Busy is putting it mildly. It looks like someone sneezed a load of graffiti onto a sky-blue canvas. What  is  it with these modern kits? They've completely abandoned subtlety. Remember when it was just colours and maybe a stripe or two? Aye, simpler times. My grandad used to have a Sunderland one, proper red and white stripes, felt like sandpaper but he loved it. This City one… it’s trying too hard. And it's a shame because the actual game, when they  do  actually play football and not just perform theatricals, is decent. Did you see that Newcastle game last week? I did, caught the highlights. Isak's goal was a beauty. Though, it got me thinking, all this money sloshing around in football, and these ridiculously overpriced shirts… and who's bankrolling it all? It's usually some betting company or, even worse, a fast-food chain. Oh, don’t even  start  on the sponsorship. It’s grim. I saw an article the other day about how many kids are influenced by the advertising. Like, having your favourite player associated with McDonalds… it’s just… irresponsible. Utterly. And it’s not just McDonalds, is it? It's everything. Gambling ads everywhere, crypto scams plastered across shirts… it feels like every aspect of the game is being commodified. I mean, remember when it was breweries and car manufacturers? At least they felt... slightly less insidious. Slightly! Though I’m not saying Carling Black Label on a Newcastle shirt was ethically sound, mind. But McDonalds… that's a different level. They actively target families and kids. It’s just… yuck. And then they wonder why childhood obesity is a problem. Exactly. It's a self-fulfilling prophecy. And they pay a fortune for it. I wonder how much City are getting from whatever deal they have. It must be astronomical. Enough to design a less visually offensive kit, you'd think. Probably not. Money talks, doesn't it? Though, if I was designing a kit, I’d go completely retro. Proper block colours, maybe a simple badge. Something classic. What's your dream kit design? Oh, that’s a good question.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of her, posting pictures of her new kitchen online! Like she hasn’t a clue how lucky she was. Gran left her the house  and  a decent chunk of money. It’s just…flaunting it. Yeah, well, Sharon’s always been a bit like that, innit? Always had to have the best, the newest. Remember when we were kids and she refused to play with anything that wasn't Barbie? Even then, she was a bit…much. It’s just, I know you’re struggling, and seeing that just… rubbed salt in the wound, didn’t it? You were telling me the other day about the Jobseekers Allowance, still waiting for a call back? Weeks. Weeks, Liv. They say they’ve got a duty of care, helping people back into work. Right. More like a duty to make your life a misery. All the forms, the interviews where they just ask the same questions over and over… Honestly, I feel like I'm being deliberately ground down. It's awful. So bureaucratic. I’m lucky, finishing up my Masters is keeping me busy, but seeing how hard it is for people who  want  to work… it’s just infuriating. Did you manage to sort out that eBay order? The George Foreman grill? Oh, ironically, yes. Arrived yesterday. Apparently, that's the height of my ambition now – cooking sausages on a George Foreman. Little Leo was chuffed though, proper excited. He wants 'flat sausages' all the time now. "Like on the telly, Dad!" That’s sweet! He’s growing up so fast, isn’t he? Seems like yesterday he was a tiny baby. Remember that trip to Margate? He was convinced the donkeys were dinosaurs. Don’t remind me! He screamed blue murder when one actually  brayed . Thought it was roaring. But yeah, they do grow up fast. Maya's starting to get really opinionated now. Says everything is 'unfair'. Where does she learn that from, eh? I wonder. Probably observing the adult world! She's a clever cookie though. Speaking of unfair, have you seen the gas and electricity bills lately? Mum was having a meltdown earlier. She said they’ve gone up another fifteen percent. Fifteen percent?! Bloody daylight robbery. I'm already dreading winter. It's bad enough trying to keep the flat warm now, without it costing a fortune. I keep meaning to get quotes for better insulation, but… well, you know.

Honestly, Mum, the traffic getting here this morning was  atrocious . Sat nav kept trying to reroute me through those tiny village lanes. Absolutely ridiculous. I swear it’s deliberately trying to send me down roads not designed for a Smart Car, let alone my Audi. Oh, you get used to it, love. Sat navs ‘round ‘ere are hopeless. They don’t understand ‘cut-throughs’ and ‘little bits o’ road’ like we do. Mine tries to send me the long way ‘round to get a loaf of bread! That’s right, Doreen. They think they know best, those machines. Back in my day, you just  knew  the way. Peterborough ain’t that big, you see. Though it’s changed somethin’ awful, hasn’t it? All these new estates… Changed is an understatement. It’s barely recognisable. And then, just as I was finally getting closer, there was this… well, I don’t even know  what  it was. A right kerfuffle on the A47. Slowed everything to a crawl. Apparently, something about a broken-down lorry. Sounds like Tuesday. Seems like there’s always somethin’ holdin’ things up on that road. Though, speakin’ of holdin’ things up, did you hear about that little plane crash near Norwich? Awful business. I did see something on the news. Dreadful. Makes you think, doesn’t it? Flying seems so… fragile. Though, I suppose driving isn’t much safer when you’ve got half the county trying to get to Tesco at the same time. Tesco… bah! Used to be Smith’s the greengrocer, down the market. Proper food you got there. None of this plastic-wrapped nonsense. And old Mr. Smith always gave ya an extra apple if you were a regular. Aye, and Mrs. Higgins at the butcher’s. Best sausages in Peterborough, they were. Now it’s all pre-packaged, and tastes like cardboard. Still, needs must, I suppose. Makes life a bit easier, even if it doesn't taste as good. Easy is good! I’ve got that big presentation on Friday. Thinking about ordering in some Thai. Too exhausted to even contemplate cooking. It’s been one of  those  weeks at work. Mr. Henderson is breathing down everyone's necks about the quarterly targets. Targets, targets… always targets. When I was a girl, people just  worked . Didn’t need all this fussin’ about numbers. My Horace, bless him, he worked at the brickyard all his life.

Honestly, I’m  dreading  double Biology on Monday. Mrs. Davies is… well, she  means  well, but she's a trainee, innit? And you can just  tell  she hasn't quite figured out how to explain things so we actually understand. Like, the Krebs cycle? Utterly lost cause. Tell me about it! I sat next to Leo in that lesson on Friday and he was literally drawing little cartoons of mitochondria fighting. It was the only way he could cope, I reckon. He said it sounded like a complicated recipe he didn't want to follow. Oh, Leo. He’s the best. But seriously, it's not funny when it's a test next week! I’m already panicking. I'm pretty sure I'll fail if I have to explain it without a diagram. Did you even attempt the practice questions? I did, and I think I got, like, two out of ten right. Two! And one of those was just guessing. It’s just… so much information. And she keeps saying “think about the energy flow!” Like, yeah, but  how  does it flow, Mrs. Davies? Does it have little wings? Little energy wings! That’s brilliant. I’m using that. Honestly, though, it’s a shame. She’s really enthusiastic. She just needs… a bit more practice, maybe? It's better than Mr. Henderson, though. He just reads from the textbook and sounds bored even  he  doesn’t understand it. True. Mr. Henderson could narrate paint drying and it would be less exciting. At least Mrs. Davies  tries  to make it interesting. Speaking of things that are interesting… have you seen Freya’s art project? It’s insane. The one for English? The one about ‘isolation’? I saw pictures online. It’s amazing, isn't it? All that charcoal and the way she’s used light and shadow…She’s ridiculously talented. I wish I could draw like that. I'm stuck on stick figures, even when I try to be all artistic. I know, right? It’s unfair! I could barely manage a palatable cloud in art last week. Mrs. Peterson said it looked “structurally unsound.” Structurally unsound! It's a CLOUD! Oh, Mrs. Peterson. She's brutal, but fair. She really pushes you, though. Have you finished the essay on 'Macbeth'? I'm still wrestling with Lady Macbeth's motivations. Is she just ambitious, or completely mad? Ugh, don’t even remind me.

Honestly, Mum, it's just… weird, innit? All this stuff about believing things without, like, proof. Old Mr. Henderson at school was going on about the Bible again, and it’s just stories, right? Stories people  told  to explain stuff before science. It's a bit more complex than that, Leo. It's about faith, about finding meaning. It's about community, too. Mr. Henderson probably gets a lot of comfort from his beliefs. Besides, you’re suddenly very interested in religion? Seems a bit out of the blue after you spent the whole of last week obsessed with whether or not we’re living in the Matrix. Mama! More peas! Coming right up, Finn. Hold on, sweetie. See? Finn here doesn’t worry about existential crises. He worries about peas. Finn's three, Mum! He doesn’t even understand the concept of reality yet. And it’s not just Mr. Henderson. I was reading this thing online about Scientology… that’s  proper  weird. Paying loads of money to climb up a secret ladder and communicate with aliens? Oh, Scientology. Honestly, Leo, steer clear of that one. That’s… a different kind of weird. More manipulative, definitely. And it’s expensive. Remember when Auntie Maggie got a bit involved with a group like that back in London? It caused such a mess. That’s what I mean! Like, people joining stuff without thinking. And then there’s nuns. I saw a documentary about nuns, and they  choose  to not have families or, you know, normal lives. Just to… pray all day? It's about devotion, darling. They dedicate their lives to God, to service. It's not for everyone, obviously. But it’s a calling. It’s a way some women find fulfillment. It’s not necessarily sad or… restricted, even if it looks that way from the outside. Remember Sister Mary from primary school? She was lovely. Always had time for a chat. Yeah, she was alright. But still… giving up everything? It feels like… a waste. Like, you only get one life, shouldn't you  live  it? Go travelling, have kids, learn to play the guitar… not just sit around in a habit. Life is about choices, Leo. And what constitutes ‘living’ it is different for everyone. Some people find fulfilment in those things – travelling, music, family – and some people find it in something else entirely. It's not about what  you  would do, it’s about respecting what others choose to do.

Right, so if we take the A19 all the way 'round, it’ll add about twenty minutes, but it completely avoids that nightmare roundabout near Doncaster. Remember last time? I swear that thing is designed to induce road rage.      Twenty minutes is twenty minutes. Good call. I’m happy to avoid any potential for vehicular manslaughter, frankly. Though, I did think my parallel parking was  impeccable  under pressure.      Impeccable? You nearly mounted the pavement, Liam! And then blamed the camber of the road. Honestly. Speaking of things near disasters… how are the dancing lessons going? Still feeling like a two left feet situation?      Okay, okay, the camber  was  questionable. And the dancing… well, it's…developing. Apparently, I have “potential, but a distinct lack of rhythm.” The instructor said it with a straight face, which somehow makes it worse. It’s a lot harder than it looks on  Strictly Come Dancing .      Oh, they always make it look effortless. Pure illusion. Though, I'm not convinced half the judges even know what they’re talking about. Remember that whole debacle with Shirley Ballas last year?      Vaguely. I’m more of a LoveFilm kind of guy, to be honest. Been re-watching ‘The Wire’ again. Still holds up, doesn't it? Truly masterful.      It does, it really does. Though I did get thoroughly sucked into that new series, ‘Shogun’ on iPlayer. Absolutely stunning cinematography. It made me want to go and study Old English or something. Proper historical dramas are so good.      Old English? Seriously? That's a bit niche, even for you. You were always the history buff, though. Remember when you tried to convince everyone at uni that Beowulf was basically a proto-action movie?      It  is ! Dragons, monsters, heroic quests! It’s got everything! Though, the translation is… challenging, to say the least. Speaking of challenging, how’s work? Still battling corporate… stuff?      The usual. Spreadsheet wrangling, endless meetings. Mostly trying to convince people that using metric is actually  easier . You wouldn't believe the resistance. Apparently, everything was better "in my day", measured in inches and pints. Honestly, it's a form of ageism, I reckon. They think being old automatically means being right.      It's daft, isn't it? My grandad is the same. “Everything was better when…” fill in the blank. It applies to football, TV shows, celebrity gossip…everything. He still thinks Cliff Richard is a musical icon.

Right, honestly, this is  much  better than I thought it’d be. Croatia is… proper lovely. Not what I expected at all. Though, Dad, are you  sure  you know where you're going? We’ve been “just five minutes away” from that olive oil place for, like, half an hour.      Now, now, Sarah. Your father's got a good sense of direction, generally. He’s just… appreciating the scenery. Aren't you, love? Besides, getting lost is half the adventure, isn't it? It’s how we stumbled upon that gorgeous little winery yesterday.      Adventure is a strong word, Margaret. Let’s call it strategic route deviation. And yes, I’m aware I’ve taken a… less direct path. These Croatian roads aren’t exactly labelled with the precision of the M6. Plus, the views  are  rather stunning. Look at those vineyards.      Can we just put it in the sat nav, please? I'm losing signal trying to upload this video of us nearly going into that ditch earlier. It’s gold.      Leo! Don’t put that online! Dad will kill you. Honestly, you documented the near-death experience for TikTok?      It’s not a near-death experience, it’s a bit of fun! And it’ll get loads of likes. Everyone loves a bit of Dad’s dodgy driving.      Leo, put the phone away. And your father is a perfectly competent driver, thank you very much. It's just... he prefers the scenic route. Sarah, didn’t you say you were interested in seeing a proper market today? I read about one in Rovinj - fresh produce, local crafts… sound good?      Rovinj sounds brilliant! Definitely better than another olive oil tasting, no offence, Dad. Though, that stuff  was  good. I’m thinking after the market, maybe we could find one of those Konobas everyone’s talking about? The little taverns? I want proper Croatian food, not just tourist menus.      Excellent idea. I did a bit of research; apparently, the Istrian truffles are phenomenal. I read a review of a place just outside Pula that specialises in them. It’s a bit pricey, admittedly, but we’re on holiday, aren't we?      Truffles? Sounds… posh. Can we at least stop for ice cream after? I swear, Croatian ice cream is a whole different level.      Always thinking with your stomach, you are. We can definitely do ice cream, Leo. Now, about the caravan.

Right, so you will  not  believe what happened last night. It’s mortifying, honestly. And it involves Ben, and… well, a very questionable game of Truth or Dare. Oh dear. Ben? The Ben who thinks he's a comedian? Colour me intrigued. And potentially braced for embarrassment on  your  behalf. Spill. Ooh, go on then, Lizzie. Don't leave us hanging. I’m betting it involves a terrible impression of our History teacher. No, thankfully not Mr. Henderson. It’s… worse. He dared Sam – Sam, you remember, quiet Sam from Art? – to ask someone what their… what their experience was with, uh,  certain  activities. Oh. Oh wow. That's… bold. And incredibly awkward. Who did Sam ask? Please tell me it wasn’t someone he likes. That’s the kicker! He asked Ben. And Ben, bless him, decided to answer with a  very  detailed story involving – and I'm censoring myself for the sake of Grandma’s ears - involving experimenting with… recording things. Recording? As in… video recording? Apparently. He mumbled something about wanting to "document everything" because it was "artistic expression". I nearly choked on my crisps. Honestly, the entire room just froze. No. Way. Ben is… something else. I’ve never met anyone who can make a situation  that  bizarre. Did Sam look horrified? Horrified doesn't even begin to cover it. He went bright red and started rambling about needing fresh air. Then Ben tried to backpedal, saying it was inspired by a documentary he saw, but it just made it worse. Wow. That's… a lot. And the recording part is just… unsettling. Was anyone actually… involved in any of this recording? That’s what  everyone  was trying to figure out! He was so vague. He kept saying "a friend," but wouldn't say  which  friend. And now everyone's side-eyeing everyone else. It’s ruined movie night. Rightly so. That's seriously crossing boundaries. And recording without consent is… frankly, illegal. This is way beyond a simple awkward dare. It is a bit dodgy, innit? I mean, even Ben being Ben, that's a bit much. You’d think someone would’ve said something. Did anyone stick up for Sam? I did, eventually. I just stared at Ben until he shut up. It felt like an eternity. Honestly, I think everyone was too shocked to speak. Then we just sort of awkwardly changed the subject to...games.

… honestly, I’m still regretting that Vindaloo last night. Should’ve known better, really. Thought I could handle a ‘medium’ spice level. Aye, a right fool I was. My stomach’s still protesting. Oh dear, Dave. You say that every time. You  always  underestimate the spice levels. I swear, they deliberately ramp them up in those places just to catch people out. Did you have enough water with it at least? He always says that, don’t you, Dave? Remember that Thai green curry in Stockport? He was walking around like a constipated robot for the rest of the day. Now, now, let’s not dwell on past culinary disasters. The point is, I’m needing something gentle today. Something… bland. Thinking maybe just a biscuit with me coffee. Though the coffee in this uni is… well, let’s just say it tastes like it’s been brewed since last Tuesday. You’re not wrong about the coffee. It's consistently disappointing. I brought a flask today, thank goodness. And a pack of those ginger biscuits. Want one? They’re not exactly bland, but they  are  soothing. Might help settle your system. Ginger? Now that’s an idea. Actually sounds quite good. Aye, go on, I’ll take one. Thank you, Sarah. Sometimes a bit of ginger is exactly what a lad needs. Though nothing’s gonna fully counteract a Vindaloo attack, let’s be realistic. Speaking of needing something, I’m starving. I skipped breakfast, thinking I’d grab something from the cafe here. But the queue’s insane. It’s full of students cramming for exams, all needing their caffeine fix. Oh, it always is at this time. Exams week is a nightmare for the food outlets. What were you thinking of getting, Mark? I was eyeing up that sausage roll. They look pretty decent, all flaky pastry and… well, sausage. Though I'm trying to be good. Supposed to be starting a new diet on Monday. A diet, eh? That’ll last five minutes. We all say that. It’s easier said than done, especially when surrounded by temptation. Manchester's got some proper good food places, mind. You can’t be dieting  in  Manchester. It's against the law, probably. Don't encourage him, Dave! He'll be demolishing a full English before we even finish this coffee break. I was thinking of trying that new Vietnamese place on Chapman Street.

… honestly, I still don’t get TikTok. My daughter’s glued to it, naturally. Says I’m ‘ancient’ if I don’t understand the dances. Ancient! I’m only forty-six. Ha! Tell me about it. My nephew tried to explain ‘challenges’ to me last Christmas. I think I nodded politely for a solid ten minutes, pretending I grasped the concept of filming yourself doing something deliberately silly for internet points. It felt…exhausting. Oh, you lot are hopeless. It’s not  that  difficult. Though I confess, I stick mostly to Facebook. Keeps me in touch with family back in New Zealand, and there’s a rather active librarian group, surprisingly. Lots of sharing of resources and, frankly, venting about difficult patrons. Facebook's alright. Bit of a digital graveyard, isn’t it? Seems like everyone just posts photos of their meals and political rants these days. I tried joining a professional networking thing on LinkedIn, but it felt so…forced. Everyone just bragging about their ‘achievements’. LinkedIn is the worst. It's like a constant job interview even when you're not looking for one. I had someone message me last week asking for ‘synergies’. Synergies! What does that even mean in a library context? Oh dear. ‘Synergies’. Sounds like something out of a corporate training manual. Honestly, I think the appeal of these platforms is just the connection, isn’t it? Even the silly dances and meal photos. People wanting to feel…seen. Seen, aye. Though sometimes I think people just want to be  heard . The comments sections can be…vibrant. Let’s say that politely. I saw a thread about a local council decision on library funding that descended into absolute chaos. Don't even get me started on local council decisions. I swear, they think libraries are just glorified book-lending services. They have no idea about the community work, the digital access points, the…everything! It’s infuriating. It’s a constant battle, isn’t it? Promoting our value. That’s why I’m a big fan of using Facebook to showcase what  we  do. Photos of the children’s story time, announcements about workshops…little things. It can make a difference. Good shout. We’ve been trying to do more with our Twitter account, but it feels like shouting into the void sometimes. Though I did get one reply from a bloke saying he appreciated our ‘consistent commitment to bibliophilia’.

…and honestly, Geoffrey, the sheer scale of it is quite daunting. A brand new hospice, not just a refurbishment, but a completely new build. It feels… enormous. We've been talking about expanding capacity for years, but actually  doing  it feels different. Are you completely confident Tunbridge Wells is the right location, though? It feels a little…gentrified, doesn't it? Will we really be serving the people who need it most? Margaret, you’re right to push me on that. It  is  a significant undertaking. And yes, I’ve wrestled with the location. Rotherham, where I grew up, well, things were… different. But Tunbridge Wells, despite appearances, is a strategic hub. We’ve done the demographic modelling, you see. The catchment area extends further than you might think – a surprising number of referrals already come from across the border in East Sussex, and even parts of West Kent that are severely underserved. The existing services are stretched to breaking point. Demographic modelling is all well and good, but I worry about accessibility. Public transport isn’t fantastic in the surrounding villages, and parking… well, you know how it is. Have we really considered how people will  get  here, especially those who are frail or already dealing with significant emotional stress? I’ve been speaking to a few of the local GPs and they are concerned. Excellent point. That’s where the consultation process is critical. We need to actively seek that feedback, not just present a fait accompli. I’ve already instructed Sarah in Comms to begin arranging a series of public forums – village halls, church halls, even the local Women’s Institute. We need to listen, genuinely listen. And perhaps look at a shuttle service, or collaborating with local volunteer drivers. Logistics, logistics. It all comes down to logistics. What about the business case itself? Are you happy with the projections? The business case is…robust, shall we say. But I’m still slightly uneasy about relying so heavily on charitable donations. We’ve modelled different scenarios, of course, but the higher end relies on a truly exceptional fundraising campaign. And health budgets are becoming increasingly squeezed. I worry about long-term sustainability. We need a solid plan for securing recurring income. Agreed. Recurring income is key. We’re exploring a potential partnership with some of the private healthcare providers in the area – offering complementary therapies, perhaps. And I’ve had a preliminary chat with a local estate agent, actually.

Oh, look at this one! Remember Sarah’s hen do? Absolute chaos. She nearly fell in the harbour dressed as a pirate. Good Lord, yes! Portsmouth, wasn’t it? She was furious when someone got it on video. Still, a brilliant weekend. Seems a lifetime ago, though. Are we even still in touch with Sarah? I think so. I saw her post something on Instagram a few weeks back, looked like she’d had another little one. Tiny human number three, I think. I sent her a quick ‘congrats’ but haven’t had a reply yet. She gets busy, you know? She does. Always has. Right, this one’s from Ascot. 2017, wasn’t it? Your hat was… ambitious, darling. Ambitious?! It was  fashionable . Bold, even. And it kept the sun out of my eyes. Besides, you spent the entire day complaining about how uncomfortable your shoes were. They were pinching! And truthfully, it was a long day. All that sparkling wine and polite conversation… exhausting. Did you manage to actually  watch  any of the racing? Speaking of long days, I had the most terrifying job interview today. It was for that content writer role at ‘Bloom’. They kept asking me about SEO and keyword density, my brain just went blank! Oh, love, that sounds awful. It's always the technical stuff that gets you. What did you say? I think I mumbled something about ‘organic reach’ and ‘engaging content’. It felt incredibly vague. The interviewer, a woman named Bethany, just stared at me. I’m pretty sure I blew it. Don’t be so hard on yourself. Interviews are designed to stress you out. Remember when  I  interviewed for Head of Department? They asked me to explain the intricacies of supply chain management using only a banana… Oh, I remember that story! You came home and swore you’d never touch another banana again. It was deeply traumatic. But seriously, you're a talented writer. They’d be foolish not to see that. Don’t dwell on it. What did you think of the office, at least? It was… very beige. And smelled faintly of air freshener and desperation. But the team seemed nice, actually. A couple of the people I spoke to afterwards were really encouraging. That’s something, isn’t it? Now, about dinner. I’m attempting a risotto. Hopefully, it won’t be a disaster. I’m thinking of adding some mushrooms… Risotto, ambitious again!

Right, that was…intense. Honestly, I think I jumped about five times during that last bit with the, y’know, the thing in the well? Gave me proper willies, that did. You did! I was trying not to laugh  at  you jumping, but it was difficult. It's a classic scare tactic, isn't it? The dark, the water, the  implication  of something horrible. It didn’t even  show  much, and it was terrifying. Though, I maintain, ‘The Babadook’ is still infinitely scarier. Psychological horror trumps jump scares any day. Oh, don’t even  start  on ‘The Babadook’. That one… that one stayed with me for days. It wasn't about what you  saw , it was about what was happening to the mum. Properly unsettling. But a good jump scare? Gets the adrenaline going, doesn't it? Makes you feel alive! Though my heart’s still hammering. Did you see my face when it proper lunged out? I did! You looked like you’d seen a ghost. Honestly, you're such a scaredy-cat, El. But that’s why I love watching these with you. Your reactions are gold. It’s far more entertaining than the film sometimes. Hey! I am not  always  a scaredy-cat. It's just… this one had a creepy vibe from the start. All that folk horror stuff, the isolated village, the weird rituals… it’s just unsettling, innit? It reminded me of those stories Gran used to tell about the moors around Sheffield. Proper dark stuff. Gran always had a knack for a good spooky tale. Mine just talked about Cambridge college gossip, which is a different kind of terrifying, I suppose. But yeah, folk horror is brilliant. It plays on really primal fears, doesn't it? The fear of the unknown, of tradition gone wrong, of being cut off from everything. Exactly! And the music! That constant, droning music… it just built and built the tension. It’s clever, really, how they do it. It’s not just about monsters jumping out, it's about creating this feeling of impending doom.
