Do you think they'll do a sequel? I don't know if it  needs  a sequel. It felt quite contained, you know? A perfect, self-contained nightmare. Though, I suppose everything gets a sequel these days. Speaking of needing things, I need more chocolate. This horror movie watching requires serious fuel. Good shout.

Honestly, Grandad, I still don’t understand why you’re so against ordering groceries online. It saves  so  much time. I was thinking of getting a delivery tomorrow - fancy any biscuits with your tea? They do those lovely ginger snaps you like. Ginger snaps, eh? Tempting, very tempting. But all this…online business…it feels awfully impersonal, dear. I like  seeing  the biscuits, having a proper look, you know? Picking out the best one. And what about the young lads and lasses who used to deliver? Supporting the local shops. It’s all changing too fast, that’s what it is. I get that, I really do. But the local shops are…well, a bit pricey, and honestly, sometimes they’re out of stock of everything I need. Plus, I can compare prices online, find deals. It’s just practical. I did order that new armchair for the living room online, remember? And you seemed quite happy with that. That armchair  is  comfortable, I’ll give you that. Though I still maintain it’s not the same as going to a proper furniture shop and having a sit down, getting a feel for it. It felt a bit…risky, buying something so important without trying it first. And all that packaging! Mountains of cardboard. They take the old packaging away with the delivery now, thankfully. Speaking of deliveries, have you had a look at Airbnb for when Auntie Maureen comes down next month? I thought we could rent that little cottage near the moor. It has a lovely garden. Airbnb? Is that one of those…gadget things? I’m still getting my head around this iPad you got me. I can just about manage emails, but that’s about it. Young Thomas tried to show me TikTok the other day…absolute nonsense. It  is  a bit addictive, TikTok. But Airbnb is simple, honestly. I’ll show you tomorrow. It’s like a website for renting out rooms or whole houses. Much nicer than Maureen squeezing into the spare room, you know she snores! She does have a trumpet for a snore, that one. Alright, alright, show me this…Air Bee and Bee. Though I still don’t trust putting my card details on the internet. Remember that scam a few years back with the fake emails? Almost lost a good chunk of my pension. That was awful, I remember. Everything’s much more secure now though, with two-factor authentication and all sorts.

…and honestly, the sheer scale of it, Hamish. Just  immense . You think you've seen libraries, you think you've seen bookshops, and then you walk into El Ateneo Grand Splendid in Buenos Aires. It's a converted theatre, you see. The bookshelves are built into the boxes, on the stage… it's breathtaking. Did I tell you about trying to find a first edition Borges there? A fool's errand, of course. Aye, you mentioned the Borges hunt. Sounds about right. Buenos Aires, eh? Always meant to get there. Though, I confess, my recent travels have been a bit… less exotic. Mostly conferences in bloody Birmingham. Still, a decent library in the university there. Though it’s nae a converted theatre, I’ll grant you that. It sounds like ye were properly lost in it, though. Lost in books is a good place to be. Lost doesn’t even cover it. I spent a good four hours just wandering, soaking it up. It reminded me a bit of the National Library here, but… amplified. More theatrical. It got me thinking, you know, about how  places  shape what we read, and what we want to read. I was suddenly desperate for South American magical realism. Before that, I’d been plodding through a biography of Disraeli. Disraeli! Honestly, Alistair. Always with the Victorian heavyweights. You need more lightness in your life. Perhaps some Calvino?  If on a winter's night a traveler … that’s a book that practically demands a European train journey. Speaking of which, have you managed to lock anything in for next year? Fiona and I were toying with the idea of Morocco. Morocco sounds brilliant! We were looking at Japan, actually. Trying to time it with the cherry blossom. A bit cliché, I suppose, but I've always wanted to see it. And I’ve been reading about Japanese literature lately – Mishima, Kawabata… It’s so different from anything I normally go for. All that constraint and symbolism. Japan’s a good shout. Very different pace of life. And the food… Och, the food. Listen, though, don’t get too bogged down in Mishima straight away. Start with something a bit more accessible. Perhaps some Haruki Murakami? He bridges that gap nicely, don't you think? A touch of the surreal, but still grounded in everyday life. Less… intense. Actually, I’ve got  Norwegian Wood  on my Kindle.

Honestly, Mum, this job description is…intense. “Lead Architect on a multi-million pound eco-development, requiring extensive experience in sustainable design and BIM Level 2 proficiency.” It feels like they’ve just compiled a list of everything I  don’t  fully have yet. Oh, love, don’t get discouraged before you’ve even properly looked at it. It’s always going to sound intimidating on paper. They  want  the best, remember. That doesn't mean you aren't capable. Which firm are we talking about, anyway? Foster + Partners. I know, I know, it's…a stretch. But it’s  Foster + Partners . It’s practically a pilgrimage for architects, isn't it? And the project… it's this whole redevelopment of a brownfield site down by the Thames, focusing on green spaces and energy efficiency. It’s exactly the kind of thing I’m passionate about. Foster + Partners…blimey. Right, well, that's ambitious, isn't it? Still, apply! What's the worst that can happen? They say no. And honestly, you’ve got a brilliant portfolio from uni already, and that little extension you designed for Mrs. Henderson down the road was lovely. They said it really opened up the space. That was a garden shed, Mum, not exactly a showcase of architectural prowess. And the portfolio… it’s mostly theoretical stuff. I haven't actually  managed  a project of this scale before. The BIM Level 2 thing worries me the most. I did the course, obviously, but it wasn't exactly… immersive. Well, you always were a quick learner. And you’ve been using it at Mitchell & Hayes, haven’t you? Even if it’s not the full Level 2, you've got experience. Don’t undersell yourself, darling. You’re always so hard on yourself. Remember when you were little and convinced you couldn't ride your bike? Oh, God, don't remind me. I cried for a solid hour. But this is different. This is my career. I don’t want to look foolish applying for something I'm clearly not ready for. Foolish? You’re 26! You’re  supposed  to be pushing yourself. Look, I was still working at the library when I was your age. Didn't even finish my A-Levels, to be honest. I didn't have the opportunities you have. You went to a good school, then a fantastic university, you've got a Masters…you’ve done everything right.

…and honestly, Doreen, the price of diesel now! It’s criminal. Used to fill up the old Ford for thirty quid, easy. Now? Nearly sixty. Sixty! And for what? So they can line their pockets? Aye, Arthur, you’re tellin’ me. Though I haven't driven in… well, near on ten year now, have I? Too many aches and pains to trust myself behind the wheel. Still, I read about it. They say it's all to do with what’s happenin’ over in… where is it again? Ukraine, that’s it. Ukraine. It’s more complex than just Ukraine, George. It's supply and demand, a bit of geopolitical maneuvering, and frankly, the oil companies taking advantage of the situation. Remember when petrol was over £1.70 a litre last year? Madness. I was glad when young Emily switched to that little electric car, even if she  does  go on about the charging times. Electric, eh? All very well and good for short trips, but try tow’in' a caravan with one of them things! You need a proper engine, a bit of grunt. Remember me and Margaret, used to go all the way to Cornwall every summer, caravan on the back, not a bother. They don't make 'em like they used to. Cornwall… good times, those were. Margaret loved a cream tea, didn’t she? Though she always insisted on jam first, which, let’s be honest, is the  wrong  way round. George, you and Margaret had that argument every single year. It was practically tradition! She was a stubborn woman, your Margaret. A lovely woman, mind, but stubborn. Stubborn as a mule, she was. But a good sort. Different times, though, innit? You could afford to go on holiday, tow a caravan, without havin' to remortgage the house. Housing is the real problem now. Young people can't get on the ladder. That's the truth of it. Our David and Sarah, they’ve been savin’ for years, and still barely afford a poky little flat outside Norwich. When I bought my first house, back in '68, it was a fraction of what they’re paying now. And the quality! These new builds… all cardboard and promises, that’s what they are. They’re building so many on green fields, too. It’s dreadful. I read an article about it the other day, they’re concreting over farmland at an alarming rate.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of bags people are leaving in the art room is becoming a liability. It’s not a storage facility, you know? We need to be firmer with the Friday night life drawing class. They treat it like a cloakroom. Yeah, I noticed that on my rounds yesterday. Absolutely rammed. I mentioned it to Brenda, but she said they’re a good bunch and don’t want to upset ‘em. Brenda’s a soft touch. Brenda is lovely, but sometimes lovely doesn’t cut it, does it? We're running a charity, not a lost property office. It's a fire hazard, frankly. Speaking of which, have you had a chance to check the fire escape routes on the second floor? Old Mrs. Higgins complained again about boxes blocking access to the one near the yoga studio. Did 'em this morning. Cleared a right mess. Mostly donations we haven't sorted. Folks just leaving stuff outside, thinking we’ll magically process it. I reckon we need to put up clearer signage – “No Unattended Donations” sort of thing. And maybe a quick chat with the volunteer co-ordinator, Sarah. She needs to brief the team on turning things away. Good thinking. Signage is a must. It’s all well and good wanting to be welcoming, but it’s impacting everything. It’s impacting  how  we can use the space. Which brings me back to the old boiler room… I’ve been sketching out some ideas for converting it into a small workshop space. Think pottery, maybe some jewellery making. Something that could generate a bit more income. Oh, that’s a good shout! We've been banging on about needing more revenue streams for ages. The café does alright, but it’s not exactly turning a huge profit. Pottery would be popular, definitely. Though we'll need to sort the ventilation first. Smells can travel, and Mrs. Higgins would have a field day if she smelled clay all the way to the yoga studio. Absolutely. Ventilation is key. And proper flooring. It needs to be durable and easy to clean. I was browsing some options online last night – there’s this lovely recycled rubber flooring that's quite affordable. We’d need to get a quote though. And benches… sturdy workbenches. I can do a quick sweep of suppliers. I know a place down in Croydon that does good deals on workshop furniture.

Honestly, Rhys, you haven't  tried  the parsnips? They're divine. I swear, even  you  couldn't complain about slightly sweet root vegetables. Though knowing you, you'd probably find something. Alright, alright, don't go poking the bear, Elodie. They  look  alright, I'll give you that. But Ms. Cape Town-raised-on-sunshine probably has a different standard for ‘good’ vegetables than a Cardiff boy. Besides, I’m still reeling from the Yorkshire pudding situation earlier. Oh, the Yorkshire puddings were a triumph! Though I maintain, a proper Yorkshire needs Lard, not olive oil. Olive oil is for salads, not structural integrity! They were good, Dad. Really. Just… a lot. Everything is a lot. Don’t push yourself, love. You've not been yourself since we got here. Just eat what you fancy. There’s plenty. Plenty is an understatement, Nesta. Gareth’s been in that kitchen since breakfast! He’s determined to feed us all into oblivion. Reminds me of your mother, bless her soul, always worried everyone was losing weight. Even after a roast like  this . It's amazing, Gareth, honestly. Everything is so good. But are you sure you haven't single-handedly depleted the local butcher's stock? That beef was… substantial. Substantial is the word! Needed a challenge, didn't I? After years of catering to fussy students - “no gluten,” “no dairy,” “organic only” – it's liberating to just  cook . And Hereford beef is fantastic. Worth the trip just for that, really. Liberating for  you , maybe. Try explaining to a student why their vegan burger is made with… well, actual beef. That’s not liberating. Rhys! You're terrible. You told him about the 'accidental' beef burger, didn't you? A man’s gotta have some stories, Ieuan. It kept the exam hall buzzing for a week. Though, the head of catering wasn't amused. Honestly, boys. Think of your auntie Margaret. She’d be horrified at the talk of accidental beef. Gareth, would you pass the cranberry sauce? It’s lovely with the turkey. Speaking of Margaret, remember that Christmas she tried to make a pavlova? It collapsed before it even made it to the table. She blamed the humidity, naturally. Oh, God, yes! It was a sticky, meringue-y disaster! We all pretended to love it, though. She’d have killed us if we didn’t. Are you sure you’re alright?

…and honestly, the traffic on the A19 was mental. Absolutely mental. I swear, every single person from Newcastle decided to go to the Metrocentre at once. Took me nearly an hour just to get to the Washington services. Oof, sounds grim. Glad I wasn’t behind the wheel. I took the train down, thankfully. Though even  that  was packed. Everyone’s trying to get a last minute summer holiday in, I reckon. Where were you heading exactly? Just back from Mum and Dad’s? Aye, well, dropped a load of stuff off for them. Mum’s starting one of her ‘decluttering phases’ again. Basically, she wants me to take anything I’ve ever given her that she doesn’t fancy anymore. She’s ruthless, our mam. And then I was heading to see Sarah. She's trying to convince me to go to Berlin with her. Berlin? No way! That sounds amazing. What’s the plan? She found some ridiculously cheap flights, like, suspiciously cheap. She reckons it’s a cultural experience. I’m mostly picturing kebabs and techno, to be fair. Do you think it's a bit… much, though? I mean, I haven’t really done much travelling on my own, or even with just Sarah. It's always been a big group thing. No, not at all! Berlin’s brilliant. I went a few years back with the lads for a stag do – completely different vibe to what Sarah’s after, obviously – but it’s a really cool city. Loads of history, amazing food… and yeah, great nightlife if that’s your thing. You should definitely go. It’ll do you good to get away. See, you’re saying the right things. It’s just… stepping outside my comfort zone, y’know? I’m more of a ‘stay in with a takeaway and a boxset’ kinda girl. Speaking of which, did you see that new series on Netflix, ‘The Diplomat’? Heard about it, haven't got round to it yet. Is it any good? I’ve been stuck re-watching old Top Gear episodes. Honestly, Clarkson, Hammond and May are just comedic gold. It's proper gripping. Political intrigue, a bit of romance… and the main character’s wardrobe is immaculate. Though, it’s made me realise how little I know about actual international diplomacy. It's all very ‘West Wing’ meets ‘Homeland’. Though less explosions, hopefully. Sounds intense.

…and honestly, the hospital just feels like a conveyor belt these days, doesn’t it? I mean, Mum’s scan was barely five minutes, and then the doctor just rattled off probabilities. Probabilities! As if her life is a percentage. Tell me about it. My sister, Brenda, had that hip replacement last month. They were in and out like a revolving door. She said the nurses were lovely, bless ‘em, but there just wasn’t  time . It's all about getting through the lists, isn’t it? Not actually  seeing  the person. Exactly! And it’s particularly hard when you’re… dealing with something serious. She’s not coping well with the waiting for test results. Keeps saying she feels like a burden. I try to tell her she’s not, but… you know. Oh, they  all  say that. My George, bless his soul, used to say that whenever he had a cough. "Don't want to bother you, Doreen." Men are funny like that, aren't they? Bottle everything up. It was the same with my Dad, right up until… well, until he went. That’s it, isn’t it? It's awful seeing them shrink inwards. My brother, David, he’s being… well, David. All logical, trying to find solutions, fix things. He can’t  feel  anything, or won’t let himself. It’s driving me mad. I need to  grieve , you know? Not have a schedule for processing sadness. Grief does what it wants, love. Doesn’t follow rules. And everyone does it differently. David’s just… coping in his way. Probably scared stiff himself. Losing your Mum… it shakes you, doesn’t it? Brings up everything. It does. It's brought up a lot of old family stuff, too. Remember Auntie Margaret always saying Mum was too thin? And then criticising me for putting weight on as a teenager? Honestly, the woman. Now  she’s  gone, and I find myself thinking about her obsession with appearances… and how much of that rubbed off on all of us. I've been avoiding the scales, to be honest. Oh, Margaret. A handful, that one. Always on some new diet. Grapefruit and black coffee, wasn't it for a while? And you shouldn’t worry about the scales. You look lovely, you do. Brenda’s been trying one of those meal replacement shakes. Says it's easy, but she misses proper food.

Right, that was a lovely dinner. Honestly, slow-roasted lamb is just  the  best, isn’t it? And the Dauphinoise potatoes…heaven.      Yeah, it was good. Can I have a look at TikTok now? I promised Ben I'd see his new skate video.      Typical. Though I can’t blame you, the stuff on there  is  addictive. I’m still trying to understand what a ‘duet’ is. Eleanor, how’s work been? You mentioned a big proofing job earlier?      It  was  big. A whole marketing campaign for a new artisanal cheese company. Sounds glamorous, doesn’t it? Mostly it was correcting Americanisms. They kept using ‘utilize’ instead of ‘use’! Drives me mad. And ‘impactful’ as a verb. It's horrifying! It took ages. Thankfully, the pay was good, though. Needed it, considering the price of…well, everything.      Cheese companies have marketing campaigns? I didn’t know that.      Oh, absolutely. Everything has a marketing campaign, dear. Even cheese! They have to convince you that  their  brie is better than everyone else’s. It’s a ruthless world.      It is, isn't it? Similar in manufacturing, really. It's all about perception. Trying to make a slightly better widget seem absolutely essential. I had a nightmare last week with a shipment delay. Apparently, a lorry broke down on the M6. Held everything up. Spent the whole day on the phone trying to mitigate the damage.      The M6's always jammed. It's like a permanent car park. Dad, remember that time we got stuck on there for, like, three hours on the way to…where were we going?      Peak District. Three and a half hours, actually. And you were convinced we’d run out of biscuits. A national emergency, as you saw it.      I was hungry! That was a really long time ago, though.      Speaking of long times ago… remember that ski trip to Austria, David? The one where you nearly ended up down a black run?      Please don't remind me. My pride still hasn’t recovered. I thought I was much better than I was. Thought I could handle anything. One minute I’m confidently schussing down a red, the next I’m clinging to a tree, desperately trying not to plummet into oblivion.      Did you film it?      No! Thankfully, no one filmed it. It was mortifying enough as it was. Eleanor was laughing so hard she nearly skied into a snowdrift herself.

…and honestly, looking at this one of you in Shibuya crossing, it feels like a different lifetime. You look  so  young. And utterly overwhelmed! Oh, I  was  overwhelmed. I’d just stepped out of the station, and it was… a wall of people. Absolutely a wall. I remember thinking, “Right. This is it. This is Japan.” And immediately regretting wearing bright pink. I felt like a beacon. A very fashionable beacon, admittedly. Though I think the pink did attract the attention of that street performer dressed as Pikachu. Don’t remind me! He kept trying to get me to pose for a photo. I eventually had to mime running away. Did I ever show you the picture he  did  manage to sneak? I don't think so. Let's have a look… Oh. My. Goodness. You're looking directly into the camera with a look of absolute horror while Pikachu is attempting a peace sign behind you. This is gold. It's mortifying! I genuinely forgot about that. Speaking of photos, why are we suddenly on an archaeological dig through the digital archives? Just… thinking. Thinking about how long ago that was, and about how much has changed. And I was looking at some of the badger photos I took down by the river last week. Oh, the ones you were obsessed with getting a ‘perfect’ shot of? The ones that involved you lying prone in a muddy field for three hours? It was a strategically positioned muddy field! And they’re fascinating creatures, you have to admit. Their markings…the way they move. It’s almost…Zen. Zen badgers? You’re losing it, aren't you? Though, I will say, the one photo where it's looking straight into the camera is pretty amazing. It looks like a tiny, masked bandit. Precisely! A bandit with impeccable taste and a fondness for earthworms. I was trying to get a similar composition to that one portrait you took of Old Man Hemmings in Camden Market. Remember that? The one where he looked like he’d seen it all. Oh, Hemmings! The guy who sold vintage maps? Yes! He  had  seen it all. He told me he once sold a genuine pirate map to a chap who turned out to be a tax inspector. The irony! Brilliant. You always had a knack for finding the stories behind the people. I was always focused on the… composition.

Right, honestly, that brisket is  something  else, Anya. Seriously. You’ve outdone yourself. It’s a million miles away from anything I attempted during lockdown – which, let’s be honest, was mostly burnt toast and existential dread. Glad you like it, Leo. It’s my nan’s recipe, tweaked a bit. Though, honestly, you could probably set fire to water and still manage a better brisket than some of the things I’ve seen attempted. You were a student, though, give yourself a break. It  is  good. Reminds me of my auntie Moira’s, actually. Though she’d add a dollop of horseradish, which nearly blew your head off. You ever try making gefilte fish, Anya? That’s a proper challenge. Gefilte…what now? Sounds intimidating. I stick to pouring coffee, thanks very much. Though I  did  try and recreate an Irish coffee once. Didn't quite nail it. Ended up with lukewarm coffee and a sad little dollop of cream floating on top. Ireland! That’s what I wanted to ask you about, Ben. You said you spent a month backpacking around it last year? What was that like? Apart from the coffee disasters, obviously. Yeah, it was…wild. Beautiful, mostly. Loads of green, obviously. But the people were amazing. I ended up skinny dipping in the Atlantic with a bunch of farmers after a trad session in a pub. Proper mad stuff.  Skinny dipping ?! Ben! Honestly. You’re incorrigible. Was the water freezing? Ice cold! But you know, after a few pints of Guinness, you don’t really notice. It’s more the shock when you get out. Honestly, though, it was a highlight. Felt properly…free. Sounds like you. I've always wanted to go to Ireland, but I'm terrified of the midges. Absolute nightmare. Worse than Birmingham in summer, and that’s saying something. Speaking of nightmares, Anya, you remember that photo app I was showing you earlier? The one that puts your face onto historical paintings? I put mine onto ‘The Scream’ and it genuinely captured my mood when I’m trying to study for exams. Oh, you  have  to show me that! You always look like you’re about to have a breakdown when deadlines loom. Although, with the way the world is going, maybe ‘The Scream’ is just a permanent expression these days. Don’t even get me started. Honestly, if there  was  a zombie apocalypse, I’m setting up shop in the café.

… honestly, I still can’t believe you’ve never had proper roasted peanuts with your pint. Like,  never ? It’s a North East institution, man. Every pub worth its salt has ‘em. Proper salty, dusty ones. Not those posh honey-roasted things. Right, okay, I concede. You’ve made me feel deeply culturally deficient. Birmingham pubs are…different. More about the pork scratchings and maybe a bowl of crisps. Peanuts just aren't a thing. Though, I  am  open to being educated. Maybe we can find some decent ones before we head back? Deal. We  will  find you the perfect pub peanut. It’s a mission now. Speaking of missions though… how’s the PhD going? Still wrestling with algorithms and existential dread? You know me too well. Algorithms are winning, I think. I spent the last three days debugging a single line of code. It was a semi-colon. A  semi-colon , Alice! It nearly broke me. I briefly considered taking up competitive eating instead. Oh, the joys of research. I thought  my  job was stressful, managing trials and whatnot, but at least I don’t get to battle rogue punctuation. Though, trying to get funding applications approved feels a bit like that sometimes. Have you at least been escaping into anything fun? Like, have you managed any gaming lately? Remember how obsessed you were with that space strategy game? Stellaris? Vaguely. I did fire it up last week, but everything felt… slow. It needs that immediate gratification, you know? I’ve been falling down a rabbit hole of retro games actually. Rediscovered  Sonic the Hedgehog . It’s surprisingly therapeutic to just  go fast . Oh, good man! Classic. I’m more of a  Mario Kart  girl myself, but I respect the Sonic dedication. You need something mindless when your brain’s fried. Speaking of mindless fun, are you up for Alton Towers next month? They're doing that new VR experience on Nemesis. Alton Towers? Hmm… I’m not the biggest thrill seeker, you know that. I’m generally the one holding the bags while everyone else braves the big one. And VR on a rollercoaster? That feels like a recipe for disaster. I'd rather watch a good film. Have you seen anything decent recently? They’ve apparently completely revamped it, made it less scary. More immersive. Though, yeah, you're right. Holding bags is a vital service. As for films, I saw that new sci-fi thriller, ‘Echo Bloom’.

…and honestly, the blisters are  brutal . I didn’t realise how much pressure you put on your hands learning to row. It's nothing like the erg machine at the gym, is it? That’s all smooth motion. This is…gripping for dear life against splintered wood. Oh, rowing. You’re brave! I did a bit at university, but found it incredibly demanding. My hands never recovered! You’re much more the outdoorsy type though, aren’t you? I’m more of a gentle kayak kind of girl. Flat water, a little breeze… bliss. Remember that time we went kayaking in the New Forest? Nearly capsized trying to avoid a swan! Oh,  don’t  remind me! That swan was terrifying. It was like a feathered, hissing torpedo. But that was fun, wasn't it? Though, this is different. I’m trying to join the college boat club. Proper, competitive rowing. Which means needing proper kit. And that’s where the expense starts! Have you seen the price of waterproof trousers these days? It's ridiculous. I need something that will actually keep me dry, you know? Not just  water-resistant . Tell me about it! I remember needing a decent waterproof jacket for tutoring outdoor sessions last year. Had to remortgage the house, practically. You want something breathable too, otherwise you end up steaming up inside. Have you looked at Rohan? They’re pricey, but last forever. Rohan… I’ve seen the ads. A bit beyond my budget at the moment, I think. It's all a bit overwhelming, really. Everything's new. It reminds me of when I first agreed to meet Aunt Margaret. Aunt Margaret? Your mother’s sister? The one you’d never met? That’s right, isn't it? That’s the one. After Mum died, I discovered she’d kept in touch with Margaret all those years, but Mum never introduced us. Apparently, there was…a falling out, years and years ago. Something to do with a shared boyfriend, if I remember the whispers correctly. Anyway, Margaret reached out after the funeral. I was so nervous meeting her for the first time. It felt so strange, like meeting a stranger who somehow held a piece of my family history. That must have been difficult. Especially so soon after your mum. It’s odd, isn’t it? How families can be so fragmented? My cousin Brenda and I barely speak now, and we were inseparable as children.

Right, so seriously Dad, I was trying to send Maya a message earlier, a  proper  message, not just a meme, and I remembered Gran showing me, ages ago, how to do Morse code. I tried to tap it out on her phone, but it just came up as random letters. Is there an app for that or something? It felt way quicker in my head. Morse code, eh? Your Gran always was a bit of a whizz with that. No, love, not really an app for tapping it out  onto  a phone, unless it’s a specific one designed for signal fires or something. You’d need a way to translate the taps into text. It's a bit like trying to write a letter with a fork, isn't it? Though I suppose, back in the day, it  was  the quickest way. It's all texting and emojis now. Speaking of which, did you get your results today? Yeah, this morning. I’m… mostly happy. Got the grades I needed for Uni, thankfully. A and B in History, C in English Lit. Maths was the killer, as always. D. But it doesn’t matter for my course. I'm just relieved it’s over. All that stressing… remember how I nearly had a meltdown over the practice papers? Do I ever! You were convinced your entire future hinged on knowing the quadratic equation. Honestly. Look, a D in Maths isn't the end of the world, especially if it doesn’t affect your uni place. You’re going to be brilliant at history, you always have been. University is a whole different ball game anyway. It's less about remembering  what  to think and more about  how  to think. That’s what Ms. Davies said. It’s just… daunting. And expensive. Have you sorted out the student finance stuff with Mum? I keep forgetting bits of the application. My head’s a sieve. Aye, mostly. Your mum’s been on it like a terrier. We’ve filled out all the forms, sent everything off. Should hear back soon. Don't worry about forgetting things, you’re juggling a lot at the moment. It’s funny, isn't it? I remember when I was your age, I couldn’t forget a single football score! Now… I walked into the kitchen earlier and couldn't remember if I’d already made a cuppa.

…Honestly, mate, this essay is killing me. ‘The Sociopolitical Impact of Early Internet Forums.’ Sounds fancy, right? It’s just… endless scrolling through Geocities archives. Seriously, who even  remembers  Geocities? Blimey, Geocities? That’s deep cut, even for us old timers. Sociology, yeah? Still plugging away at that then? Thought you were gonna switch to something a bit more… practical? Like computer science, given your obsession with building PCs. Nah, Mum would kill me. "Get a  real  degree, darling," she’d say. Sociology pays the bills, apparently. Though, honestly, right now, I’d trade it all for a week in Tokyo. Tokyo? Now  that’s  talking. What sparked that? You never struck me as the Japan type. Saw this documentary on Netflix, yeah? About the tech scene in Shibuya. And the food! Honestly, the ramen looked… transcendent. Plus, I'm completely sick of London. Same old pubs, same old faces. Need a proper culture shock. I get that. London can feel small, even though it's massive. I’ve been thinking about travelling too, actually. Not Japan, though. Always fancied Southeast Asia. Thailand, Vietnam… maybe even backpacking through Indonesia. Indonesia sounds… ambitious. You and backpacking? I picture you demanding room service in five-star hotels, to be honest. Rude! I’m adaptable, innit. Besides, my cousin lives in Bali. Said I could stay with him for a bit, get my bearings. It’s cheaper than London, that's for sure. Speaking of cheap, you ever tried that new ramen place, ‘Menya Musashi’, near campus? Proper authentic stuff. No way! Is it good? Because my usual ramen haunt, ‘Wagamama’, just isn't cutting it anymore. It’s lost its edge. All style, no substance these days. It’s miles better than Wagamama, trust me. Proper tonkotsu broth, the works. Though, be prepared to queue. It's popular. We should go next week, maybe after our awful exams are finally done. Please, let’s not talk about exams. I have three next week, and I genuinely feel like my brain is turning to mush. This internet forums essay is taking up all my cognitive function. It’s like, I know how the internet  works , but explaining why a forum dedicated to collecting Beanie Babies was important to society… it’s a stretch. Sounds rough, fam. You need to break it up. Come with me to that climbing wall next Wednesday? Good stress relief.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of photos Brenda posts on Facebook is astonishing. Every single plant in her garden gets its own photoshoot! It’s lovely, truly, but it’s a commitment just scrolling through it all. Did you see the one of her cat wearing a tiny hat? Oh, Brenda. She’s a character, isn’t she? Bless her. I try to keep my Facebook presence minimal. Mostly just sharing articles about silly things, or pictures of the Dartmoor ponies. Though I did put up a few from Buckfast Abbey last week. It was so peaceful there, really needed that quiet. Buckfast Abbey, eh? Went there once, decades ago. More interested in the Buckfast Tonic Wine, if I’m honest! Though my doctor wouldn't approve of me admitting that now. Everything's a health hazard these days. Used to be able to have a proper drink without someone tutting. Grandpa! You haven’t changed a bit. Mum, you took some beautiful photos at Buckfast, though. I saw them. You’ve finally mastered the panoramic setting on your phone, I see. Took me long enough! It’s this new phone, it's so complicated. All these apps and settings… I don’t understand half of it. I’m still convinced it’s listening to me, too. Mentioned needing new gardening gloves to Brenda on the phone and BOOM, an advert for them appeared! Listening to you? Hah! They've been listening to  me  for years, thanks to that blasted David Cameron and his tax avoidance schemes. Now  that's  something to be angry about. Not a cat in a hat. Though, admittedly, the cat is a bit ridiculous. Oh, here we go. Politics before elevenses. Grandpa, breathe. It  is  frustrating, the whole thing with offshore accounts, but let’s not ruin a perfectly good cuppa discussing it. We were talking about trips, weren’t we? Thinking about maybe a short cruise next year? A cruise! Oh, that sounds lovely! I’ve always fancied one of those Mediterranean ones. Italy, Greece… all that history. Though I worry about the insurance. It’s getting so expensive to cover everything these days. Especially with my knees acting up. We can look into dedicated cruise insurance, Mum. There are policies specifically for pre-existing conditions. Honestly, it might be easier than flying. Less queuing, less stress. Grandpa, would you be up for a cruise?

Honestly, you two look  relaxed . Proper relaxed. Did Belgium live up to the hype, then? You’ve been planning this for ages! Oh, it did, love, it really did. A bit different to our usual Bournemouth trips, that’s for sure. Though, I say, driving over there… that was an experience. Don't even  start  with the driving, Arthur. I’m still having flashbacks to those roundabouts. They’re just… everywhere! And massive. Roundabouts? Oh, Dad. You and roundabouts. What happened? Did you get lost? I told you to download offline maps, just in case. Offline maps are all well and good, darling, but the Sat Nav kept trying to send us down what were basically cycle paths! Seriously, cycle paths! Narrow little things with people whizzing past. Nearly took the wing mirror off three times. He was convinced it was the quickest route. 'Trust the technology,' he kept saying. Technology clearly doesn’t understand British stubbornness and a fear of cyclists. Oh, Dad. You’re incorrigible. Was it all stressful, though? Or did the food and sightseeing make up for it? Mum, you were raving about the chocolate before you even left. The chocolate was glorious, absolutely glorious. And the waffles, don't even get me started! We went to Bruges, and there was this little market… oh, the cheeses! And the lace… I bought a little tablecloth, and a couple of those Brussels biscuits. Bruges was lovely, yes. Though a bit touristy. Ghent was better, much more… authentic, I’d say. And the beer! Don’t forget the beer! Though, I had to be careful, my bladder isn't what it used to be. Good to know! Any recommendations for smaller towns? I’m always looking for somewhere a bit off the beaten track for a little weekend trip. Well, we stumbled across Deinze by accident, actually. The Sat Nav did something silly again, and we ended up there. It’s on a canal, really pretty. Lots of cycling routes too, actually. Cycling? Dad would have a heart attack. Now, now, I’m not  that  opposed to cycling. Just not in cities, and not when it’s mandatory! They expect you to use those cycle lanes, you know. It's the law. Speaking of laws, how about the driving regulations? Anything particularly bizarre? They’re very strict on drink driving, obviously. And speed cameras are  everywhere . Arthur nearly got caught twice.

Honestly, this risotto is taking  forever . I thought I’d be a culinary whiz after all those cooking programmes during lockdown, but no. It’s just…sticky. Risotto  is  a commitment, love. It needs constant attention. Though, you've managed worse, I recall that attempt at soufflé… Don’t you dare bring up the soufflé! That was a disaster of epic proportions. It resembled a pancake more than anything else. Still, at least it tasted alright. Did you remember to get lilies for the living room? They really brighten the place up. I did, they're in the hall. White ones, as you like. Though Mrs. Higgins at the florist was going on about some new hybrid rose. Apparently smells like… sandalwood and raspberries? Utterly bizarre. Sandalwood  and  raspberries? Good grief. Florists are getting creative. Sounds a bit much, frankly. Give me a classic lily any day. It reminds me of… well, it just  smells  proper, doesn’t it? Not like some of those overly sweet perfumes everyone’s wearing these days. All bubblegum and… something artificial. You and your perfumes. You could identify a fragrance from fifty paces. Though I must say, your new one  is  rather nice. Is that… fig and something spicy? It’s fig and black pepper. Very subtle. I wanted something a bit different. It’s supposed to be very sophisticated. Although, honestly, half the time I think people just say sophisticated to justify spending ridiculous amounts of money. Probably. Speaking of ridiculous amounts, have you seen Brenda’s latest Facebook post? She’s bragging about a weekend in the Cotswolds, complete with a wood-fired hot tub. Brenda? Oh, honestly. Always has to one-up everyone. It feels like every post is a competition. Last week it was her husband's promotion and the week before that, the new kitchen. Though, a wood-fired hot tub  does  sound rather lovely. Especially with this weather turning. It does. We should get one. For the garden. Imagine, sitting out there in December with a glass of something warming… Slow down, ambitious. We barely have room for the barbeque as it is. Besides, remember what happened when we tried to build that pergola? Let’s not revisit that particular DIY disaster. Point taken. Perhaps not a hot tub then. But we  should  get the fireplace cleaned. It's been ages. It'll be much cosier sitting in front of a proper fire once it gets really cold.

…and honestly, the heat! I’d prepared for warm, of course, but Queensland in November is another thing entirely. You practically  melt  the moment you step off the plane. Though, it did make shopping for linen rather enjoyable. Queensland, you say? Never been myself. Always fancied Australia, though. Bit too far for a quick hop, isn't it? Spent most of my business trips closer to home – Germany, the States, mostly. Always had to look the part, you know? Sharp suit, tie, the works. Trying to impress the Yanks especially. They’re very particular about presentation. Oh, suits. My brother-in-law was in sales, always had a wardrobe full of them. Said it was armour. Though I’ve always been more of a jeans and jumper woman myself. Australia… I spent a year in Perth, a lifetime ago, doing research. Different kind of heat to Queensland apparently. Drier. And the flies! You wouldn't believe the flies. Flies are universal, aren’t they? Though I must say, the Australians seemed remarkably unbothered by them. It was the humidity that got to me. And the sheer  scale  of everything! Everything's bigger, bolder. I remember trying to get a bank loan sorted out while I was there – to buy a little apartment, you see – and the paperwork... it was endless. Endless! Nothing like a simple bank transfer back home. Bank loans… now  there’s  a story. I remember a deal falling through once because the bloke on the other side couldn’t get his financing sorted. Trust me, dealing with finance is a headache anywhere in the world. They all speak their own language, don’t they? Are you from Bristol then? I picked up a bit of an accent. Almondsbury, actually, just outside Bristol. Grew up there. Lovely countryside. Then I spent thirty years teaching English as a Foreign Language. Mostly in Europe, but that year in Australia was a bit of a whim. Trying to escape a particularly grim English winter, you see. Teaching, that's admirable! I’m a lecturer myself, at the University of Sheffield. History, mostly. Though lately, it’s been a lot more admin than lecturing, sadly. Speaking of places, you wouldn't believe the variations in dialect even within Yorkshire. Where I grew up, just outside of Sheffield, they talk a language all of their own. Sheffield dialect, eh? I’ve heard tell. Supposed to be pretty strong.

…Honestly, I just don’t  get  TikTok. Everyone’s glued to it, especially at family gatherings now. My niece, Elsie, barely looks up from the screen. It’s all dances and…challenges? What  are  they challenging each other to do these days? It feels incredibly shallow. It's a bit of both, isn’t it? Shallow  and  surprisingly clever sometimes. It's not just dances, though that’s the stuff that goes viral. There’s a lot of political commentary, little comedic sketches, people sharing skills… I use it a bit for finding language teaching resources, actually. Short, snappy explanations of grammar points. It's good for grabbing attention. Language teaching resources? On TikTok? Good heavens. That’s…unexpected. I thought it was just teenagers lip-syncing. Still, I prefer a good book. Or even a reasonably intelligent television programme. Have you seen anything decent lately? Everything feels so…formulaic. You’re right about the formulaic stuff. I was hooked on  Severance  on Apple TV+, though. That was brilliantly weird. And properly thought-provoking. It’s a bit slow burn, but worth it. Have you heard of it? It’s about this company where employees have their memories surgically divided between their work and personal lives. Sounds…disturbing. A bit  too  relevant, perhaps, considering the state of the modern working world! I tried to get into  The Crown , everyone was raving about it, but I found it rather tedious. Overly dramatized. I much prefer documentaries. David Attenborough, naturally. He’s a national treasure. Oh, Attenborough is always good. Can’t argue with that.  The Crown  is guilty pleasure territory, I think. But I’ve been getting into podcasts more and more. They're perfect for the commute, or for marking student essays…when I really need to drown out the internal monologue of despair. Podcasts! Yes! I’ve dabbled. I listen to a gardening podcast sometimes. Very soothing. And I found one about the history of Cambridge, which was rather nice. A bit self-indulgent, perhaps, but still! What sort of podcasts do  you  listen to? Something educational, I presume, given your profession? A mix, actually. I listen to a true crime one – don’t judge! – but also one about linguistics. It’s fascinating. It's called 'The Allusionist'. It looks at the origins of words and phrases, how language evolves… it's brilliant for a language teacher, obviously, but even if I didn't do what I do, I'd be hooked.

…and honestly, the way she just  launched  herself off the side! I thought for a moment she was going to bellyflop, but she tucked everything in and it was a perfect little entry. Didn’t even shiver! Was it warmer than the paddling pool, Mummy? The paddling pool is ALWAYS freezing. It was, darling, yes. Much warmer. It’s a proper heated pool at the leisure centre. And you were so brave going under the water with your goggles, weren’t you? I did a starfish! I floated like a starfish! You  did  do a starfish! A magnificent starfish. Right, who wants toast? You two have been swimming like little fishes all morning, you must be starving. With jam! Strawberry jam, please. Chocolate spread! And sprinkles! Chocolate spread  and  sprinkles? We'll see. First, let’s talk about yesterday. You two had a lovely time with Anon, didn’t you? She said you were both very well-behaved. She let us build a fort! A  really  big one, with all the cushions. And we pretended it was a spaceship! We went to Mars! Wonderful! She's a good egg, that one. She told me she’s got her travelling circus coming to town next month. Might be something fun to do. A circus?! With elephants? Possibly! I don’t know about elephants, but definitely acrobats and clowns and probably some amazing animals. We’ll have to look into it. It reminded me, Anon was telling me about trying to get a Blue Peter badge. What’s a Blue Peter badge? It's a special badge you get if you send something really good to the Blue Peter programme – a drawing, or a story, or something you’ve made. She sent in a lovely photograph of you two playing with her, but they said they need… proof of age. Proof of age? What's that? Well… it’s a bit silly, isn’t it? They want to know how old you are. They want a copy of your passports! Honestly. I told Anon it was a bit much. I don’t  have  a passport! Not yet, love. We haven't been abroad since you were tiny. Though, maybe we should start thinking about it. We could go to France next summer! Ooh, France! Do they have strawberry jam in France? I’m pretty sure they do! Everything has strawberry jam, somewhere in the world.

Right, so… he just… froze. Mid-everything. Like a startled rabbit. Honestly, it was mortifying. For  both  of us. Oh, blimey, Liv. That sounds… awful. Seriously. Were you… okay? Did you know what was happening, or did you just think he’d… gotten bored? Bored?! Honestly, Chloe. No. It was… obvious. He went all clammy and just… stopped. Didn’t say a word. Just kinda… lay there. I asked him if he was alright, like five times, and he just mumbled something about feeling a bit hot. Oh, love. That's not good at all. It sounds like… well, it sounds like he might have had trouble, you know… getting an erection. Don’t say it like that! It’s embarrassing enough  having  it happen, thanks. But yeah, that's… that's what it looked like. He hasn’t said a word about it since. Just been acting all… distant. Men are rubbish at talking about this sort of thing, aren’t they? It's awful. They get so wrapped up in pride. My cousin’s boyfriend went through something similar, and he refused to even acknowledge it for weeks. Ended up making things ten times worse. Exactly! He's a right stubborn lad, is Ben. Proper Yorkshire grit, you know? Won't show weakness for anything. But it's not weakness, is it? It’s a physical thing. Like getting a cold. Precisely! It could be stress, anxiety, a million different things. It's not a reflection on you, Liv, definitely not. You're amazing. He's lucky to have you. You think so? I just feel… I don’t know. Like I did something wrong. Like I wasn’t attractive enough or… or something. It’s stupid, I know, but that’s what goes through your head, isn’t it? Don't even  go  there. That's completely ridiculous. You're gorgeous, and he clearly fancies you, otherwise you wouldn’t have even gotten to  that  point, would you? It’s almost certainly not about you at all. Have you noticed if he's been more stressed lately? Work, family, anything like that? He’s been really worried about his dissertation, actually. He's doing History, and it’s a massive thing for him. He’s putting so much pressure on himself. And Dad’s been on at him about getting a proper job after uni, which isn’t helping.

Right, honestly, this cauliflower cheese is going to be  amazing  with the roast tomorrow. I’ve used a proper béchamel, but lightened it up with some fat-free yogurt. I’m hoping it doesn't end up a gloopy mess. How’s your chilli coming along? It’s…chilli-ing. Ha! Get it? No? Okay. It’s fine. It’s mostly kidney beans and tomatoes, honestly. Trying to bulk it out. I'm being  super  careful with the mince, though. I weighed it all out. This Slimming World stuff is exhausting, isn’t it? Especially the Healthy Extra B choices. I swear, finding genuinely nice ones feels like a full-time job. Tell me about it! I spent a solid hour yesterday trying to decipher if I could have a specific type of wholemeal bread. It’s ridiculous. And the 'free' foods... sometimes I suspect they're not  actually  free. Like, a massive bag of spinach? Sounds good, right? But then you feel guilty about eating too much! Oh god, the guilt! It's a whole new level of food anxiety. And don't even get me started on syns. I was looking at those zero-calorie syrups the other day, and honestly, the ‘artificial flavour’ list was longer than the actual ingredients list. It feels… wrong. It absolutely is wrong! I use them occasionally for my tea, a tiny squirt of caramel, but then I feel like I’m poisoning myself. Speaking of tea, I need to make another pot. Fancy one? It's Earl Grey. And we  are  having treat day on Saturday, aren't we? I'm already mentally planning. Yes! Treat day is sacred. I'm thinking a proper burger and chips. And maybe a tiny bit of cheesecake. Just a tiny bit. I’ve been so good all week. Did you manage to get anything booked for Saturday evening? We talked about that film, right? I tried! Siri wouldn't cooperate. Honestly, that woman needs retraining. Kept trying to book me a flight to Sydney. I ended up just opening my calendar and manually checking availability. It's easier that way, even if it's a pain. We need to get organised, though. Life becomes chaotic otherwise. Honestly, Siri is a menace. Don't even mention technology to me right now. My phone battery is draining faster than my willpower when I walk past a bakery. Speaking of willpower, the scales are being stubbornly unhelpful.

…Honestly, I’m still leaning towards Italy. Tuscany, specifically. Imagine, waking up, having coffee overlooking vineyards… it just  sounds  relaxing, doesn’t it? Much more so than battling for a sun lounger in Barbados. Barbados has its merits. Guaranteed sunshine, rum punch… you know I relax with a good rum punch. But Tuscany does sound…civilised. Expensive, though, isn’t it? Have you actually started looking at places to stay? Because “vineyard views” usually comes with a hefty price tag. I have been! Not extensively, but I’ve had a poke around. There are agriturismos – that's farm stays – that are surprisingly reasonable. And we could self-cater a lot. I was thinking maybe a week? Or ten days if we really push the boat out? What do you think? Ten days sounds…ambitious. Especially considering the state of my current workload. Though, to be fair, if I get this new contract through at Fleming Tech, I might be able to dictate a longer holiday. They’re pretty decent about that sort of thing. It’s the Head of IT, Brian, who’s the issue. Thinks holidays are a sign of weakness. Brian sounds… delightful. Honestly, work, work, work. It’s all you think about sometimes. I'm worried you burn yourself out. Anyway, new contract aside, even a week in Tuscany would be amazing. We could even take a pasta-making class! Pasta making… now  that  I’m on board with. Although, knowing my luck, I’d probably end up flour-bombed and covered in tomato sauce. Speaking of messy things, did you see that article about the MP who got called out for… well, everything? The expenses, the dodgy dealings, the truly appalling haircut. Don’t even get me started on politics. It’s just one scandal after another, isn’t it? It feels like everyone's lining their own pockets. Honestly, it's depressing. I sometimes think about just emigrating and pretending it doesn’t exist. Maybe to Tuscany permanently! Now there’s an idea. We could open a little  osteria . You could manage it, I could… I don’t know, fix the plumbing. I'm surprisingly good at plumbing, you know. Just don’t ask about wiring. Fixing plumbing in Italy? Sounds about right. You’d fit right in. Though, you’d need to sort out that sleeve tattoo first. Not everyone's a fan of nautical anchors in the Tuscan countryside.

…and honestly, the bougainvillea was absolutely thriving. Didn’t realise they could get  that  colourful in the Algarve. Sent you a postcard, did I? Should’ve arrived by now. Though with Royal Mail these days, who knows where things end up. Aye, got it, thank you. Lovely photo. Makes me wish I'd come with you, to be honest. Though knowing my luck, it would've rained the entire time. Still, makes a change from spreadsheets, doesn't it? Speaking of changes, have you given any more thought to what we’re doing for Margaret’s birthday? It’s…what, the 18th? The 18th it is. And no, not really. I was hoping  you’d  had a brilliant idea, given your… organizational prowess. I was thinking perhaps a nice lunch somewhere? Somewhere not too noisy. Her hearing isn’t what it was. A lunch is good. But the family are getting bigger, aren't they? Matthew’s got another one on the way, which is brilliant, mind you. But a restaurant… could be a bit chaotic. I was half-thinking we could do something at the house? Catered, of course. I’m not unleashing my culinary skills on Margaret’s special day. Remember the soufflé incident of '08? Oh, don't remind me. The kitchen looked like a bomb had hit it. Yes, at home is probably better. More manageable. We'd need to clear out the conservatory, though. It's become a bit of a dumping ground for my books, hasn't it? All those first editions… It has. But it’s a lovely space. And we can enlist Eleanor’s help with the decorating. She’s got a good eye for that sort of thing. Right, so, catered lunch at the house. I’ll start getting quotes. What about this weekend, though? Any plans? I was hoping we could finally tackle that shed in the garden. It’s listing dangerously, and I’m worried it’ll end up taking out the fence. The shed… Good Lord. I'd almost forgotten it existed. Ideally, I'd like a quiet weekend. I've been marking essays non-stop. The students this year seem to think semicolons are optional. It’s deeply distressing. But if the shed is a genuine safety hazard… Honestly, it's a hazard to my peace of mind, more than anything. It's leaning like the Tower of Pisa.

…and honestly, the headmistress’ email was just… well, a bit much, wasn’t it? “A demonstration of empathy through artistic expression.” Honestly, sometimes I think she just enjoys using long words. Mummy, what’s ‘em-pa-thy’? Oh, sweetheart. Empathy is…it’s trying to understand how someone else is feeling. Like if Leo’s upset because he can’t build his Lego tower, you feel a little bit sad  for  him, even though your tower’s fine. Does that make sense? I built a HUGE Lego tower yesterday! It had a dragon on top! That sounds amazing, darling. We’ll have to see it later. But right now, we’re talking about what Mrs. Davies asked us to do. She wants us all to draw pictures for the Syrian families coming to Comberton. Syrian? Are they lost? Not lost, exactly. They had to leave their homes because it wasn’t safe there. It's… complicated. They’re coming here to find a safe place to live. And Mrs. Davies thought it would be nice to give them something welcoming. Can I draw a spaceship? Spaceships are welcoming! They take people to new planets! That’s a very thoughtful spaceship, Leo. You absolutely can. But she also suggested… thinking about what things  they  might need. She mentioned drawing things like… a chair. A chair? Why a chair? Well, she thought it would be nice to draw things that make a house a home. Comforting things. Things people use every day. What kind of chair would  you  draw, Lily? A bouncy chair! With sparkles! And a crown! I’d draw a racing car chair! With flames! Vroom! Those sound fantastic! Very… energetic chairs. I was thinking more along the lines of, you know, a normal chair. Like the ones we have in here. But actually… that makes me think… it’s funny, isn’t it, how many  types  of chairs there are? There’s the armchair, obviously. Grandma’s favourite. Then there’s dining chairs… school chairs… School chairs are HARD! They make my bum hurt! They’re not designed for comfort, are they? They're supposed to help you sit up straight and concentrate. Though, I agree, they’re not the most luxurious. I wonder what kind of chairs they  had  back home? In Syria? Maybe beautiful, ornate wooden ones? Or simple plastic ones? Maybe they didn’t have any chairs!

…and honestly, the sheer volume of tiny clothes is terrifying. I mean, they grow out of things  so  quickly, don’t they? It feels incredibly wasteful. It does, doesn’t it? Everyone keeps telling us ‘they grow out of them before you even get a chance to properly use them!’ It’s the cycle of babyhood, I suppose. Though, I’m already picturing mountains of miniature socks. Did Sarah ever mention if she’s planning on a capsule wardrobe approach? She always seemed so…organised. That’s Sarah all over. She mentioned something about borrowing a lot from Amelia, which is sensible. Amelia’s already had two, so she’s got a whole archive. Honestly, it's lovely seeing her so happy, but it’s also making me realise how much things change. Remember when we were all just going out, having cocktails… no thought for needing to be home by 8 for a bedtime routine? Vaguely! It feels like a different lifetime. Though, I don't  entirely  miss those hangovers. Speaking of Sarah, did you hear back from her about the conference next month? I was hoping we could both go. Yes! She said she's definitely in. She’s presenting on her work with augmented reality in the classroom, apparently. Sounds ambitious. I'm worried about leaving the little one for even a weekend, though. It feels selfish, doesn't it? Don’t be silly. It's important we still do things for ourselves, and for our work. Besides, your mum and dad are more than capable. They're practically itching for a grandparent weekend. And it’ll be good for us, a bit of intellectual stimulation that  doesn’t  involve discussing feeding schedules. You’re right, of course. It’s just… a shift. Everything’s a shift. I was thinking about Mark today, actually. I haven’t spoken to him in ages. He was so vehemently anti-kids. Said they were the antithesis of freedom. Mark. Right. That was a strong opinion. I wonder how he’s feeling now that half our friendship group is popping out babies. He always was a bit… uncompromising. Exactly. I texted him a congratulations message when Sarah announced, and he just replied with a thumbs up emoji. A  thumbs up ! It felt so…distant. Ouch. That's a bit cold, even for Mark. Maybe he’s just processing it. He's always been a bit awkward with displays of emotion.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Fresh air, no student emails… just fields. Though, I'm starting to suspect every scarecrow is judging my outfit choice. You and your fashion anxieties. It's a fleece and jeans, love, you blend right in with the rural aesthetic. Besides, scarecrows don’t have opinions, which is more than can be said for half the faculty at the university. You're just saying that. Though, Professor Davies  does  look remarkably like a particularly stern scarecrow. All angles and disapproving glances. Speaking of stern, did you hear about old Sergeant Miller from Norwich? Apparently, he tried to give a parking ticket to a sheep. No! Seriously? A sheep? That's…magnificent. Only in Norfolk. What was the alleged infraction? Blocking a fire hydrant? Apparently, it was “obstruction of the public highway.” Apparently, Mrs. Higgins reported it, claiming it was causing a traffic hazard. Honestly, the things people complain about. Reminds me of that student last year who complained her essay mark was lowered because his aura was ‘negative’. Oh,  that  one. The self-proclaimed mystic? He was convinced the grading system was influenced by astrological alignments. Still, Sergeant Miller and a sheep...that’s comedy gold. It’ll be in the local paper, guaranteed. Which, knowing our luck, will somehow lead to us being asked to comment for a ‘Local Experts on Rural Eccentricities’ piece. Don't even  say  it. The last time we got any publicity it was because someone overheard me ranting about footnotes in the university coffee room and it ended up on a ‘Lecturers Losing It’ Twitter account. It took weeks to live that down. It was a genuinely passionate rant about the Chicago Manual of Style, I’ll give you that. And it  was  funny. Though, I did enjoy watching you try to explain it to my mother. Footnotes are not something she understands. She thinks they're just…extra writing. She thinks a lot of things are just extra writing. Remember when she asked why university courses had 'reading lists' instead of just 'the book'? Anyway, let’s not tempt fate. No publicity. Let Sergeant Miller have his moment with the sheep. So, holiday plans…any closer to a decision? We need to book something soon, or we’ll be stuck in Norwich during November, which frankly, is a fate worse than being interviewed about rural eccentrics. I was looking at Cornwall.

Honestly, Dad, you wouldn’t  believe  the signal in my room at uni. It’s dreadful. I’m trying to download this lecture and it’s taking ages. You’d think in this day and age... I keep telling them, they need to sort out the Wi-Fi! It's like going back to the dark ages. Dark ages, eh? You young 'uns and your… whatchamacallits. Your interwebs. Back in my day, if you wanted to talk to someone, you wrote a letter. Took a week, mind. But it was a proper connection, that was. None of this instant gratification. Though, I suppose I do enjoy a bit of Facebook now and then, just to see what the grandkids are up to. Yeah, but a letter takes a week! I need to submit this assignment by Friday. Speaking of which, I was thinking about needing a van next month. Mrs. Henderson is finally getting rid of that hideous sideboard and I promised I’d help her move it. It’s massive. A van, you say? You know Old Man Hemmings down the road, the one who used to go fishing with me? He rents out vans now. Says it keeps him busy since he had to pack in the angling. Bad knees, poor bloke. Used to catch a cracking perch, he did. Remember that one, practically the size of your arm? Vaguely, yeah. You tell a lot of stories about your fishing days, Dad. Hemmings, you say? I’ll give him a call. It’s just everything is so expensive these days. Hiring a van, petrol… It's all adding up. It always has been, love. Just seems to go up and up. That’s why I always said the lottery was a mugs game. Waste of money, mostly. Though, I did have a fiver on last week... didn’t win, naturally. Don’t tell me you’re getting into the lottery now? You always said… I know, I know. But Doreen, bless her, bought me a ticket. Said it might cheer me up. And I’ve been thinking… about the house. The house? What about it? You weren't thinking of moving again, were you? You only just settled! No, no, not moving  again . Just… downsizing, maybe? This place is a bit big for one person, isn't it? And all these antiques… lovely things, truly, but a faff to look after.

… honestly, the sheer audacity of it! Demolishing the library? After all this time? It's just… vandalism, isn’t it? Pure and simple. It  is  pretty shocking, isn’t it? I saw the notice on the council website. Said something about ‘redevelopment opportunities’ and ‘modernising community spaces’. Code for putting up another block of flats, I reckon. Exactly! “Modernising.” As if books are  outdated . Honestly, some people. Old Man Hemmings will be absolutely beside himself. He practically  lives  there. Do you think he’s started that petition yet? I heard he was. Apparently, he’s got Mrs. Davies from the bakery on board, and she’s a force of nature when she gets going. Good. Someone needs to be. Though I’m not convinced the council will listen. They’ve got their plans, haven't they? They always do. It’s the same everywhere. They pretend to consult, then do exactly what they wanted to do in the first place. It's infuriating. Speaking of things needing preserving, have you had a chance to look at those fabric samples I ordered? For the armchair? Oh, yes! They arrived this morning. Quite a selection. A bit overwhelming, actually. Lots of… texture. I know, right? I was trying to go for something that would fit with the building’s age, you know? A bit of that Arts and Crafts vibe. Something that wouldn’t look out of place if we  did  live in a period drama. You're incorrigible. Though I do get it. It's a lovely house. And you're right, something with some weight and substance. That pale floral one is a bit… flimsy, isn't it? Flimsy and tragically predictable. I was thinking maybe that deep burgundy velvet? It’s a little… bold, perhaps? Bold, yes. But I like it. It would really stand out. And it  feels  durable. Like it'll last. It’s funny, isn’t it? We worry about demolishing old libraries, then we obsess over making sure our furniture will stand the test of time. It’s all connected, isn’t it? A respect for things that have history. This town is losing its character bit by bit. Remember that old shop on Market Street? The one with the beautiful Victorian facade? They painted it grey.  Grey ! Don’t remind me. It was a travesty. It completely ruined the streetscape. I read an article in  The Guardian  the other day about preserving architectural heritage.

…Honestly, this station’s playlist is atrocious. All manufactured pop. Where’s the substance? Remember proper music, eh? Fleetwood Mac, Dire Straits… now  that  was music.      Oh, grandad, here we go. Same rant every time we get in the car. It’s not  all  bad, is it? At least it’s something to sing along to, even if it's ironically.      He has a point, though. Everything sounds so…processed these days. I was listening to some Kate Bush earlier, and the difference is incredible.      Kate Bush is timeless, isn't she? Though I’ll admit, a bit of a guilty pleasure for me. I was more of a The Police man, back in the day. Sting had a good voice.      The Police were alright. Solid. But nothing beats a good guitar solo. Anyway, we're supposed to be discussing presents, not my musical tastes. Christmas is looming, you know. Have you two given any thought to what you want? Don't say 'nothing' - it's a blatant lie.      Well… I  was  thinking about those ghd straighteners, the new ones with the ultra-heat setting. They’re a bit pricey, though. And honestly, you'd probably say I don't  need  another hair tool.      Technically true. You have enough to open a salon of your own. But, alright, alright. Noted. It’s practical, at least. What about you, Clara? Still obsessed with those antique books?      Actually, yes. There’s a first edition of  Wuthering Heights  I’ve been eyeing at a little shop in Winchester. It’s…a significant expense. But it's a genuine passion. I spend all my free time reading. It's way better than endless scrolling on social media.      Winchester? That's a nice little town. Perhaps we could make a day of it, browse the shops. Though, a first edition  Wuthering Heights … that’s a serious collector’s item.      Very serious. Are we talking hundreds, thousands? Don’t get your hopes up, dear. I’m a business analyst, not a lottery winner. Though, I did have a rather successful month with that new project...      Oh, don't be so modest, grandad. You always downplay it. You're brilliant at what you do! So, what about you and Mum? Anything on your list?      I’m rather hoping for a new set of golf clubs. Mine are falling apart. Keeps me active, you know. Gets me out of the house.

Honestly, lad, this insurance quote is lookin' a right mess. Forty-two hundred for a year? For a Ford Focus! They’re robbin’ us blind, they are. Forty-two  hundred ?! Blimey. What’ve you told ‘em? You haven't mentioned about… you know… Dad’s speeding ticket from last year, have you? Don’t you go accusin’ your mother of dishonesty, young man! Of course not. But they’ve obviously factored in your age, see? Young drivers are gold dust to these companies. Basically, they assume you’ll crash it into a lamppost within the first week. That’s not fair! I’m a really careful driver. I've only had my provisional for six months and I’ve been practicing with you loads. And I passed my theory first time! I know, love, I know. You  are  a careful driver. But that’s not how these things work, is it? It’s risk assessment. They don’t know you individually. They just see “17-year-old male, newly qualified” and automatically think expensive. It's all algorithms now, isn’t it? No common sense. So, what can we do? We  need  a car. I need to get to college, and you’re always moaning about tramping around taking me everywhere. I do have a point there, don’t I? Right, well, we can try a few things. Have you considered adding a black box? They track your driving – speed, braking, time of day – and if you drive sensibly, it can lower the premium. A black box? Like in a spy film? Sounds a bit… Big Brother-ish. It’s not quite James Bond, love. It just sends data to the insurance company. Think of it as proof that you  are  a responsible driver. It might be worth the invasion of privacy for the savings. We could also look at increasing the excess. Increasing the excess? What does that mean? It means the amount you have to pay towards any claim. So, if you have an accident, you pay the first, say, five hundred pounds, and the insurance company covers the rest. Increasing it lowers the premium, but it's a bigger hit to your pocket if something  does  happen. It's a bit of a gamble. Hmm. That sounds risky. What about the car itself? Is a Focus really the most expensive to insure? It’s not the  most  expensive, no.

…and honestly, the whole system upgrade at work is a disaster waiting to happen. They want it live by Friday.  Friday!  Like we’re magicians, producing rabbits out of hats. I’ve barely slept all week, just churning through code and trying to anticipate every possible failure point. It’s… draining. Sounds awful, Dad. Like, really awful. Is it… like, pressure from your boss? Or just the work itself? Bit of both, to be fair. The boss is breathing down everyone’s neck, and the project  is  a beast. I was reading an article actually, about measuring stress levels. Apparently, there's a thing now where they analyse your word choice in emails? See how often you use ‘I’, ‘me’, ‘mine’ versus ‘we’, ‘us’, ‘our’. Supposedly, more self-focused language indicates higher stress. That's… remarkably Orwellian, isn't it? Big Brother is watching your inbox. Though, I suppose it’s a clever idea. I always find I get awfully terse when I'm stressed. Short sentences. Lots of exclamation points. Exactly! I’ve been firing off emails like a machine gun. And then I remember back to the marriage equality vote here.  That  was stressful, in a different way, but still… the weeks leading up to it, the arguments, the feeling like everything hinged on it. Remember, love? You and I were glued to the results. Oh, I do. It felt massive. Such a relief when it passed. A real moment of progress. Still can't believe it was only… what, 2015? Feels like a lifetime ago. Was that before I was born, Mum? Or just really young? You were about six, darling. You wouldn't remember the specifics, but you definitely felt the atmosphere. Everyone was talking about it. Speaking of atmosphere… anyone fancy a Chinese? I'm starving, and honestly, I can’t face cooking. Ooh, yeah! Can we get those little spring rolls? And loads of prawn crackers? That sounds lovely. Though, I do wish the quality of the chicken in their curries was a bit better. It's always so… rubbery. Now,  there’s  a first-world problem. Though I agree. They scrimping on the chicken, they are. It's the overuse of words, you see. "Chicken". They use it far too often on the menu. Google it, I bet it’s one of the most frequently searched words. Dad, you're just rambling now. Am I?

Honestly, Dad, are we  still  talking about parking? It's just a space, innit? We found one, didn't we? Though, it’s a bit of a squeeze with Uncle Geoff’s Land Rover parked next to us, isn’t it? Looks like a proper David and Goliath situation.      Now, now, Sarah. Parking  is  a serious issue in Bolton. Especially around market days. And your Uncle Geoff needs that vehicle for his allotment, you know. He’s got prize-winning marrows! Besides, it's good to be prepared. Remember that time we were stuck in Ramsbottom trying to find a spot for the fair? Absolute chaos. More chaotic than trying to explain kilograms to someone obsessed with pounds.      Kilograms are just… better. More scientific. Like, a thousand grams is a kilogram. Makes sense. Way better than stones and pounds like Grandad uses. Makes my head hurt.      Quite right, young man. Metric is the way forward. Though I must admit, when I was a lad, miles felt… more  real . Perhaps it’s a generational thing. Speaking of “real”, did anyone catch that documentary about nudists on Channel 4 last night? Extraordinary.      Dad! Seriously? After talking about marrows and parking, you're bringing up nudists? That’s… a leap. And miles  are  more real, they're what we use for longer distances! Like driving all the way to the Lake District. It just  sounds  further in miles than kilometers.      It does, doesn't it? Though, truthfully, I wouldn’t know the difference if you hit me with it. I’m more practical, you see. I’m measuring babies, not distances. And let me tell you, a tiny baby feels a lot heavier in kilograms when you've been up all night! Reminds me, Sarah, how’s the Law conversion course going? Are they still drilling you with Latin or something?      It's brutal, honestly. They're trying to turn us all into… robots. Memorising case law and statutes. It's a far cry from Shakespeare, which, you know, I actually enjoyed. Though, I guess even Shakespeare had laws of his own. “The course of true love never did run smooth,” and all that.      Shakespeare’s boring. Unless there’s a fight in it. Like, Romeo and Juliet had a pretty good fight at the end, right?      A bit of an oversimplification, my boy! But I understand a young man’s appreciation for action.

…It’s just, I keep thinking about it. This ‘chicken’ is… really good. Honestly, better than some actual chicken I’ve had. But it  feels  weird, you know? Like I’m betraying some deeply held principle. Oh, the existential dread of lab-grown poultry? Completely understandable. It’s cognitive dissonance on a plate. But honestly, if it tastes good and no animal suffered, where’s the harm? I mean, think of the environmental impact of traditional farming. It's insane. Exactly! And let's be real, the suffering  is  immense. People get hung up on this ‘natural’ thing, but a factory farm isn’t natural. It’s industrialised cruelty. At least with cultured meat, you're bypassing all that. It’s… a solution, isn’t it? A slightly unsettling solution, granted. I know, I  know  logically you’re right. It just…it feels like a cheat. Like I should be saving the planet by eating lentils and chickpeas for the rest of my life, not munching on a vat-grown thigh. I’m taking my multi-vitamins though, so I feel a little less guilty about missing out on certain nutrients. Oh, the vitamin tablets are your moral offset? That’s a new one. But seriously, lentils and chickpeas forever is a tough ask, even for the most dedicated veggie. And even then, think about the land use for those crops. It's not zero impact. I read an article the other day comparing the ethical implications of hunting to abattoirs. It was... heavy. The hunter argues they're giving the animal a life, a chance to roam, and a relatively quick death. Which is obviously a completely warped justification, but it got me thinking about how neatly we compartmentalise things. We happily eat pre-packaged meat, completely divorced from the process. That’s grim. But honestly, hunting feels… more honest, in a messed-up way. At least you're acknowledging the taking of a life. An abattoir just feels…hidden. Factory farming… it’s just deliberately  ignoring  suffering. It’s palatable distance. Palatable distance is a  good  phrase. It’s why people can watch those nature documentaries with lions taking down gazelles and be okay with it, but lose their minds over a photo of a piglet. It’s all about how it's presented. Though, I do think there’s something fundamentally different about a predator acting on instinct versus a human exploiting an animal for profit.

…and then she just goes and buys a thirty-foot inflatable unicorn for the garden. A thirty-foot unicorn, I tell ya! Like, where does she even  put  it? Thirty foot? Is that even a thing? Sounds like a right headache to inflate, never mind store. Bet it cost a fortune too. She’s always goin’ overboard online, our Jen is. Remember that life-sized Dalek she ordered? Oh god, the Dalek. That took up half the living room for a month. And she couldn't even  move  it herself. Dad nearly lost his mind. Speaking of online shopping, I ordered those textbooks for uni. They were cheaper on Amazon, but now I’m worried they’ll be late. Induction starts next week. Amazon’s usually good, aye? Though, I ordered a new controller for the Xbox last week, and it turned up lookin’ like it'd been through a washing machine. Had to send it back. Honestly, the state of some of these sellers... They don’t care, do they? As long as they’ve got your money. I’ve been lookin’ at flights online, just…dreamin’ really. Somewhere hot. Anywhere's better than this December. Where were you thinkin’ of goin’? We were talking about maybe a weekend in Edinburgh before uni starts, just to try and squeeze in one last proper hang-out.
