We had it at a little taverna overlooking the harbour. Delicious! The food is genuinely one of the best things about being here, isn’t it? So fresh. Although… I did try a  sheftalia  the other day, and it was… an experience. Very… meaty.  Sheftalia ! Ah, yes. That’s… an acquired taste. It’s minced meat wrapped in membrane, grilled. It's… rustic. My wife, bless her, tried to convince me it was a delicacy. She’s quite adventurous, you see. Unlike me. I stick to kebabs. Safe and reliable. I appreciate a safe kebab. Though I am trying to be adventurous. It’s part of the whole ‘living abroad’ experience, I suppose. Are there any places you’d particularly recommend a newcomer visits?

Honestly, the air was  particularly  grim today. I could practically taste the particulate matter during my tutorial on Romantic poetry. Slightly ruined Wordsworth for everyone, I think. Did you notice it on your cycle in? Grim is an understatement. Felt like chewing gravel. And it wasn't even that windy, so it wasn’t just dust being kicked up. It's just…  there . It's getting worse, isn't it? I keep meaning to get one of those proper masks, the N95 ones, but I always forget. You really should. It's not just a discomfort thing anymore, it's genuinely worrying. Old Mrs. Chen in my building was talking about her grandson’s asthma flaring up again, and she's convinced it’s the pollution. It’s heartbreaking. How was your department meeting? Still battling over the curriculum changes? Oh,  don’t  even get me started. Professor Zhang is, as always, digging his heels in. He thinks any move away from the ‘traditional methods’ is a betrayal of educational values. It’s exhausting. I spent a good forty minutes explaining the benefits of incorporating more digital resources, showing him examples of what other universities are doing… it was like talking to a brick wall. Sounds exactly like Zhang. He’s lovely, genuinely, but utterly inflexible. It’s frustrating because the students genuinely want that stuff. They’re growing up with tech, they learn differently. We’re supposed to be preparing them for the real world, not a museum exhibit. Exactly! And he just kept going on about 'the importance of handwriting to develop cognitive skills'. I nearly lost it. I mean, sure, handwriting has its place, but it’s not the be-all and end-all! Did you hear back from Sarah about the weekend? She texted this morning. She's still on for Saturday, thankfully. She was worried about the air quality too, apparently. Said her little one, Leo, has been coughing a bit. She suggested we maybe do something indoors? A board game night? That sounds perfect, actually. Maybe at your place? Your flat has that air purifier, remember? It's a small thing, but it makes a difference. It's mad, isn’t it? We lived in perfectly breathable air our entire lives and now we're strategizing indoor activities based on pollution levels. It  is  mad. Makes you realise how much we took for granted back in Norwich and London.

Right, onions are nearly done. Honestly, this smells  amazing . Did you remember to get the rosemary, love? It just makes the lamb sing, doesn’t it? Rosemary… rosemary… ah-ha! Found it. Yes, darling, got it with the garlic. You know me, always prepared. Though, I say, looking at these photos on the fridge – little Maisie’s school play, was that only last month? Time just flies. It  does . Honestly, feels like yesterday she was learning to walk. And that costume! A giant sunflower. So cute. Though, judging by the photos, she spent most of the play picking her nose. Oh, don’t remind me! Mrs. Higgins gave me  the look . You know the one. The silent judgement. Still, she was adorable. And she remembered all her lines, which is more than I could have done at that age. So, what have  you  been up to today, love? Anything interesting brewing in the copywriting world? It's been…a day. Client wanted a rewrite on a campaign for dog food. Apparently, “wagging tails and happy tummies” wasn’t sophisticated enough. They wanted “optimal canine digestive wellness.” Honestly? Give me a break. Oh, marketing. Always has to overcomplicate things, doesn't it? “Happy tummies” sounds perfectly lovely to me. I had a nightmare meeting with Procurement, trying to justify the budget for the new software. They look at everything like it’s coming out of their own pockets. Procurement! Don't even  start  me on Procurement. They’re the bane of my existence at the hospital. Always questioning everything. Always. Still, at least we're home now, and we have lamb. And a reasonably sane conversation, mostly. What are we thinking for lunch tomorrow? I was rather fancying a pub lunch. The Ploughman’s Arms does a lovely Sunday roast. Oh, that sounds amazing! I'm in. I need to get  out  of the house tomorrow. Staring at a screen all day makes my brain feel like mush. Plus, their sticky toffee pudding is legendary. The Ploughman's it is, then. Good thinking. We could invite Sarah and David? It's been ages since we've seen them. They were talking about starting that new series on Netflix, “The Gilded Age”. Have either of you seen it? I've heard good things! It's been on my list, but I’ve been hooked on "Call the Midwife" again. It's just…comforting, isn’t it?

… honestly, it’s just taking  ages  to get anywhere now. They’ve changed the bus route again, haven’t they? Like, what was wrong with the old one? It actually  went  to the shops. Mmm? Oh, yeah. I saw something about that on the local Facebook group. Apparently, they’re trying to alleviate congestion near the Science Park. Strategic, I suppose. Though it does seem to mostly alleviate convenience for people who live  here . Strategic for who, exactly? People who teleport? It adds twenty minutes to my journey to get to Mum’s! Twenty minutes! I could nearly walk it in that time, and I  refuse  to walk in this weather. Did you manage to get that book you wanted from Cambridge University Press, by the way? Not yet. I was planning on going this afternoon, but I’ve got this conference call that’s run over. It’s that engineering standards thing again. Endless. They really just like hearing themselves talk, honestly. Figures. You’ll be presenting next time, won’t you? Forced to become one of  them . Sadly, probably. But back to the book… they’ve got that first edition I was after, according to their website. I’m hoping it's still there. It's a bit of a pilgrimage, really. It's the foundational text for pretty much everything I do. It  is  a lovely shop, though. All those old books… proper atmosphere. Not like Waterstones, all bright lights and coffee and…beige. Speaking of atmosphere, did you see that student protesting outside the bookshop yesterday? The one with the placard? Vaguely. Something about divestment from fossil fuels, wasn't it? Cambridge seems to attract a lot of those. Good on him, I suppose. Though blocking the entrance to a bookshop seems a bit counterproductive to me. That was my thought. But he was very passionate, yelling about ethical responsibility and all that. He was a bit gobsmacked when I asked him if he’d even  read  any of the books in there. Fair point. You're always the pragmatist, aren't you? It's a world away from Sunderland, though, isn't it? All this activism... Oh, you have  no  idea. It’s a different breed altogether. At Newcastle, if someone was going to protest, it'd be about the price of a pint, not global warming. Though, come to think of it, probably both. Everything's more...polished here.

…and honestly, the carbonara was  swimming  in cream. Carbonara should be light, you know? A proper guanciale crisp, pecorino, a little pasta water… this was just… heavy. Oh, you and your food standards, love. You’d think you were Italian, the way you carry on. Still, it's good to see you enjoying yourself, even if the chef clearly doesn’t know his elbow from his pancetta. How’s little Leo doing? Is he still obsessed with dinosaurs? He's absolutely  ferocious  about dinosaurs, Mum. It’s all roars and stomping. He tried to explain the Cretaceous period to David last night. David just nodded politely and backed away slowly. Oh, that’s brilliant! He's a little professor, that one. He’s started correcting  my  pronunciation of dinosaur names now. Apparently, I’ve been saying ‘Tricera-tops’ wrong my entire life! Grandchildren, aren’t they just… something else? It's funny, isn't it? When you’re teaching quadratic equations all day, you don’t expect a four-year-old to be the one correcting  your  pronunciation. Speaking of pronunciation, I was thinking about something the other day, and it struck me as odd. What's that, Mum? Well, I was listening to the radio – BBC Radio 4, naturally – and they were talking about how the English language is constantly evolving. And it reminded me of being a teacher, you know? The kids now, they use words… well, they use them  differently . And it’s not necessarily wrong, but it’s…shifted. You mean like slang? Everything changes so quickly. ‘Peng’ was massive last year, and now nobody says it. It’s more than just slang, I think. It’s the subtle changes in meaning. Like ‘literally’. They use it to mean ‘figuratively’ now! It drives me  mad . I spent thirty years drilling into them the importance of precise language in mathematics, and now it’s all… fluid. It's just language adapting, Mum. It always does. It's not a decline, it's just…change. Remember how Dad used to say things? All those old Irish sayings. We probably thought  he  was speaking a different language sometimes. He had a turn of phrase, alright. “As happy as a sandboy,” he’d say. I used to ask him what a sandboy even  was . He’d just grin and say, “Never mind, just be happy.” Aw, that’s lovely. So, anyway, changing the subject slightly… how are things with… Michael?

Honestly, this stretch is nicer than I remember. Last time we walked this way, it was absolutely  heaving  with people – a complete tourist scrum. It’s quite peaceful now, actually. Though, I swear the O2 is getting bigger every time I look at it. It's like a giant, metallic pimple on the skyline. A pimple? That’s…vivid. It  is  enormous, isn’t it? And always lit up. You'd think they'd switch it off occasionally. Still, it’s a landmark now, I suppose. Remember when everyone was saying it was an eyesore? Now everyone goes there. They always say that. Anything new gets instant condemnation, then begrudging acceptance, then suddenly it’s “iconic”. It's the British way. Speaking of acceptance... I’m still fuming about having to get the tube  and  the DLR to get here. Honestly, sometimes I wish we’d just bitten the bullet and bought a car. Oh, here we go again. We’ve had this conversation a thousand times, love. A car in London? It's a money pit, a stress inducer, and you’d spend more time stuck in traffic than actually going anywhere. Besides, we manage. Manage is a generous word. “Existing in a constant state of logistical frustration” is more like it. Especially when planning holidays. Remember trying to get to Cornwall last year? It took us nearly six hours on trains, with a connecting bus that smelled distinctly of damp dog. Okay, Cornwall was…challenging. But the final destination was worth it, wasn’t it? And we saw some lovely countryside from the train. Think of it as part of the adventure. We’re planning Spain this year, remember? That’ll be considerably less…dog-scented. Spain will be good. Though I'm already anticipating the inevitable recipe translation crisis. My aunt Mildred is trying to send me a paella recipe, and it's all in cups.  Cups ! American cups, of course. As if I know how many fluid ounces are in an American cup versus a British one. It's infuriating. Aunt Mildred and her American proclivities. Google is your friend, darling. It’s not rocket science. Though I agree, the whole cup-based measuring system is barbaric. Why not just use grams? Sensible people use grams. Exactly! It feels deliberately designed to cause confusion. It's like…an exercise in controlled chaos. Which, thinking about it, is a pretty good metaphor for life, isn’t it?

Honestly, this rain is  relentless . I swear it’s been chucking it down for a week. Did Leo even  have  a sports day? I barely saw anything beyond a blur of wellies and damp tracksuits. Tell me about it, love. I’ve been soaked through to the bone getting to and from work every single day. And yes, Leo had  some  of a sports day. He mostly spent it huddled under the gazebo with Maisie, clutching that enormous bear you got him. Oh, don’t even  mention  the bear! It’s taken over his entire bedroom. I tripped over the ruddy thing this morning trying to get to the washing machine. Honestly, a ‘Build-a-Bear’ workshop should come with a health and safety warning. They’re weaponized cuddles! You’re not wrong! Leo is utterly devoted to Barnaby, isn't he? Though, I’m starting to suspect Barnaby gets more attention than I do. It’s just… everything is  Barnaby  this and  Barnaby  that. They go through phases, don’t they? Remember when Maisie was obsessed with that plastic dinosaur? That thing followed her everywhere. She tried to bring it swimming with her at the Larkfield Leisure Centre, bless her. Nearly caused a riot. Oh god, the swimming! I’m still trying to get Arthur properly water confident. He screams if I even  mention  the word ‘pool’. It’s like a tiny, aquatic phobia. And potty training… don’t even get me started. I feel like I’m permanently cleaning up accidents. It’s exhausting. Potty training is the worst. Seriously. I’m so glad I’m past that stage with Leo. Though, the constant need for snacks is a whole other battle. It's like he’s powered by biscuits. Speaking of exhausting, how’s work going, Carol? Still dealing with… everything? It’s… challenging. Old Mr. Henderson keeps trying to feed me his digestive biscuits. He thinks I’m his granddaughter! It's sweet, but a bit unsettling. And Mrs. Davies keeps losing her teeth. Literally. Found one in her tea yesterday. It’s not glamorous, I tell you. Though, the company is good, most of the time. Goodness me! Honestly, you deserve a medal, Carol. You’re an angel. I'm trying to convince Mum to get a new washing machine. The current one sounds like a jet engine taking off. She insists hers is perfectly fine, even though it vibrates across the kitchen floor.

…Honestly, I’m still turning it over in my head. Leaving the business, even partially, feels…bigger than I anticipated. It's not just a job, is it? It’s  the  thing I built. I know, love. It’s understandable. You poured your heart and soul, and a frankly alarming amount of money, into ‘Coastal Collective’. But you’ve been saying for six months now you’re burnt out. And this house-sitting gig… it’s been good for you, hasn’t it? Seeing you actually  relax ? It really has. Waking up to the sound of kookaburras instead of spreadsheets is a definite improvement. But relaxing is…easy. The question is, what  after  relaxing? The proposal from Liam and Chloe to come on board with the Collective… it's tempting. Liam's a solid operator, and Chloe’s marketing is brilliant. It would free me up, potentially. Free you up to…? You’ve avoided saying the ‘F’ word – family. Are you thinking about finally starting to try for a little one? We've talked about it for years, and you always said you couldn't devote the time. That’s… a large part of it, yes. Look, I’ve always wanted kids, you know that. But the business… it always felt like it needed me,  all  of me. And now… well, we're getting older. And I don’t want to be that dad who misses every school play because he's closing a deal in Auckland. You wouldn't be. Not if you shared the load. And honestly, Liam and Chloe aren’t daft. They know what they’re getting into, and they’re offering a genuine partnership. It’s not like you’d be handing over the reins completely. You’d still be involved, just…strategically. Strategically. Sounds…safe. Almost  too  safe. But then again, maybe safe is what I need right now. Have you thought about what this would mean for you? Less travel for me means more time with you, obviously. But you're head of department now, prepping for your Master’s… It’s a juggle, absolutely. But a manageable one. And I’d be thrilled to have you around more. Honestly, the thought of you actually being present for weekend brunches, not responding to emails under the table, is… blissful. Plus, with you less stressed, maybe  we  can start planning some actual holidays. Not just ‘work-cations’ where you take calls from the hotel lobby.

Honestly, I still can't get over how different everyone’s accents sound when they try and do a Yorkshire one. It’s…a choice, innit? Like, you’re  committing  to a whole performance.      Aye, it is. Our lass, Sarah, tried it once. Sounded like she was auditioning for a panto villain. Though, to be fair, she’s got a bit of a dramatic flair anyway. Speaking of flair, anyone actually caught any decent Pokémon on that community day last week? I walked miles and only got three shiny things. Three!      Three’s not bad! I was battling lag the whole time. The server kept crashing. Honestly, it was more stressful than a tax return, and  I’m  a student. You know, remembering when Pokémon first came out? I begged my dad to let me skip school to try and ‘catch ‘em all’. He was having none of it. Proper grumpy with me.      Grumpy dads are a universal constant, aren’t they? My dad lectured me for an hour about manners when I asked for a second helping of roast potatoes. An  hour . Like I'd committed some sort of cardinal sin. Though, it’s funny, because he’ll happily argue with the bar staff for five minutes over 50p.      It's all about fight or flight, isn't it? Dad’s all bluster. He’d run first. Remember that time at that awful service station on the M6, near Preston? When that bloke started getting aggressive about a parking space?      Oh god,  that ! He went absolutely pale. Mum had to step in and give him a right telling-off. Honestly, she's the sensible one. Speaking of needing sensible things… anyone fancy popping to the shop? I'm desperate for After Eights. I’ve been craving chocolate all day.      I’ll go. Need to stretch me legs anyway. You want anything else, while I'm at it? Costa run?      Just the After Eights are fine. Though, if you see any decent deals on crisps… go wild. I’m revising and need fuel.      Honestly, revision is just prolonged stress. I keep checking my Fitbit to see how high my heart rate is. It’s constantly in the ‘stressed’ zone. Is that normal?      Probably. It’s Uni, isn’t it? It’s designed to cause stress. Remember last summer, when we all went camping up in the Lake District? That was… relaxing. Until the midges found us.

…and honestly, I still reckon that linesman ‘ad it all wrong. Clear as day, that ball crossed the line. Clear as day! They’ve ruined the game, these VAR lot. Ruined it, I tell ya. Used to be you could enjoy a bit of football without all this…fuss. Oh, Arthur, you say that every time. It’s just you don't like change. And honestly, it  was  a very tight call. You were practically shouting at the television! I thought the roast was going to jump off the plate. Grandma, you are a force of nature when it comes to football. Though, I have to admit, the delays VAR causes are frustrating. It breaks up the flow of the game. Yeah, it's not ideal. It's almost like they're expecting perfection, which isn't realistically achievable. Still, better a correct decision than a blatantly wrong one, I suppose. Speaking of frustrating things, marking essays is slowly killing me. One student just…re-wrote Wikipedia. Word for word. Wikipedia, is it? Sounds a bit daft, that. Back in my day, you got caught copying, you got a right telling off. And maybe a clip ‘round the ear, though that weren’t allowed even then, mind. Proper discipline, that's what's missin’ these days. Oh, Arthur, don't start on the youth of today. They’re just trying their best. Though, rewriting Wikipedia  is  a bit cheeky. Still, the roast is lovely, isn't it, darling? I used a little bit of that rosemary you brought back from the garden, Arthur. It’s delicious, Mum. Really. And Dad, you’re right about discipline being different. It’s more about encouraging academic integrity now, explaining the value of original thought…It’s a long process. We're trying to get them to cite their sources properly. It's a battle. It truly is. I had one argue with me that paraphrasing Wikipedia still constitutes 'original work'. I almost lost it. Original work, eh? Sounds like summat you’d ‘ear down the pub. Though pubs aren't what they used to be either. All that fancy craft beer, and not a decent pint of bitter to be found. Don’t knock the craft beer, Arthur! I quite like a nice pale ale now and again. Remember old Mr. Henderson at the village pub? He used to know everyone’s business. And always had a biscuit for me with my shandy.

…and honestly, the thought of another essay on post-structuralism just makes me want to curl up and  disappear . I swear, Professor Davies actively enjoys making our lives miserable. Tell me about it! I spent all of yesterday afternoon trying to decipher what he  actually  wants from us. It's like he's speaking a different language. You still thinking about… you know… leaving? It’s getting more tempting, yeah. Proper tempting. It feels a bit silly, doesn’t it? Everyone else seems to be thriving, or at least pretending to. I just… I don’t feel like I’m learning anything useful. Back home, I was actually  doing  things, making things. Here, it's just endless theory. It does feel a bit like that, doesn’t it? Though I’m kinda clinging on for dear life, gotta see this through. Mum would have my hide if I chucked it all now. But seriously, if it's truly making you miserable, just dropping out isn’t 'silly'. What did you want to  do  back home, anyway? You never really talked about it much when we first met. Well, I was doing a lot of pottery. And a bit of jewellery making. I had a little stall at the harbour market in Falmouth, selling stuff. It was brilliant. Properly busy in the summer. Made enough to, you know, keep myself in cider and clay. Cider and clay! Sounds idyllic. Loads better than struggling with Derrida. That's a proper skill, though, making things. My Nan always said I was all thumbs. She was a seamstress, brilliant with a needle and thread. I tried, once, to make a cushion cover… it looked like a badger had attacked it. Oh, bless you! My nan was a proper force of nature. Ran a little antique shop. Always smelled of lavender and dust. She had the most amazing stories. Always said my name, Bronwyn, was Welsh for ‘white hill’. Sounded grand, she made it sound. Bronwyn! That  is  a beautiful name. I always wondered where it came from. Mine's just… Aoife. Straight outta Dublin, apparently. My great-granddad emigrated over. Makes me feel a bit disconnected, I dunno? Like I'm not  really  Scouse. Disconnected? You’re the most Scouse person I know! The accent, the sass… it’s all there. And it's a beautiful accent, honestly. It’s… melodic. I always thought my name was a bit pretentious, to be honest.

…and honestly, the carbonara was  criminal . Like, offensively bland. You’d think in a place like this, in Oxford, they’d at least get the basics right. Though, to be fair, I haven’t had proper carbonara since Rome. That’s ruined me, isn’t it? Anyway, enough complaining about pasta. It’s so good to actually  see  you, Liv! It feels like ages. How’s Manchester treating you? Tell me about it! Oxford’s got a reputation, but even chain restaurants do better carbonara. Rome  does  ruin you, though. Once you’ve had the real thing… it’s just not the same. Manchester’s… busy. Really busy. Work is mental, honestly. Pearson are launching this new marketing campaign, and I’m pretty much living at my desk. But it's good busy, you know? Developing skills and stuff. How’s the project co-ordinator life treating  you ? Still wrangling deadlines and keeping everything on track? ‘Wrangling’ is a good word for it. ‘Herding cats’ is another one that comes to mind. It’s okay, though. Honestly, it's a good step up from the internships. More responsibility, obviously, but also more… autonomy? Is that the right word? I get to actually  shape  things. It’s at that renewable energy company, remember? The one I was rambling about during uni? Oh, yeah! EcoFutures, right? That's brilliant, Chloe! Really suits you. You always were the passionate one, always championing sustainability. It's good to see it translating into a career. Are you… enjoying the politics of it all though? Corporate sustainability can be a bit… murky. Murky is putting it mildly! There’s a lot of ‘greenwashing’ going on, definitely. It’s frustrating, but it also means there's a real need for someone to keep things honest. It’s… a challenge. Speaking of challenges, how's the dating scene in Manchester? Still avoiding commitment like the plague? You always said you needed to be ‘completely settled’ before even  thinking  about it. You know me too well! It’s… complicated. I did go on a few dates with this guy, Ben. He's a software engineer. Pleasant enough, definitely tick-boxes on paper, but… no spark. It felt like interviewing someone for a job, honestly. Plus, he kept trying to explain blockchain to me. I swear, if I hear the word 'NFT' one more time… Oh,  no . That sounds truly horrific.

Right, now then. Three quid forty-nine for a pack of…fairy lights? Honestly, you’d think they were made of solid gold. And delivery's another four ninety-nine! Robbery, pure robbery. What are you lookin’ at, Mam? More Christmas stuff already? It’s only November. It’s called being prepared, lad. And it’s not  just  Christmas stuff. It’s lighting for the garden, alright? Trying to get a bargain before everyone else starts panicking. Though, a bargain it ain’t lookin’ like. I swear, these online prices… Have you tried eBay? Sometimes you can get good deals on there. I needed a new graphics card for the computer and found one almost half price. eBay…hmph. I do dabble, you know. Once got a lovely set of vintage teacups on there. But it's a faff, isn't it? All that bidding and waiting. And you never quite know what you're gettin’ ‘til it arrives. Remember that garden gnome your Dad bought? Supposed to be three foot tall, ended up barely a foot! Aye, that was a good one! He was proper fuming. But seriously, eBay’s good if you’re patient. You can set alerts for things. Like, if someone lists ‘fairy lights – long length – warm white’ or whatever, it emails you. Emails, alerts…it’s all a bit much for me, this new technology. Amazon’s simpler, isn't it? Just click and buy. Though, even  they’re  getting pricey. I remember when you could get anything on Amazon for peanuts. Amazon's gone up a lot, yeah. Prime’s still good for quick delivery, though. I need to order some revision guides. History's killin’ me. Mr. Harrison sets the hardest essays. History, eh? Your Grandad was good at history. Used to tell me stories for hours. Though, most of 'em were probably…embellished. All about being a signalman in the war and stuff. Still, fascinating. Now, these lights… let’s see if Amazon has a slightly better deal. It's just… I don't understand how they can charge so much for postage. It’s just a box, isn't it? It’s the logistics, Mam. All the sorting and vans and people and fuel… it all adds up. Plus, they gotta make a profit. That's what Mr. Davies said in Business Studies. He’s a proper smart lad, Mr. Davies.

You know, this is alright. Proper quiet. Not like the bustle down Lewisham, eh? Though I suppose you’re used to it by now. It  is  nice, Grandad. Really peaceful here. Lewisham’s… Lewisham. It has its moments, but a bit of peace and quiet is always welcome. Especially after the week I’ve had. Oh? What’s been the bother then? One of them… spreadsheets giving you grief? You and your computer wizardry. Still can’t fathom what you  do  all day, to be honest. Something to do with making things, isn’t it? Something like that. I’m a Production Controller. Basically, I make sure everything runs smoothly on the factory floor. This week, a key piece of machinery broke down – the one that does the labelling, and suddenly, everything backed up. It was chaos. Trying to reschedule everything, sourcing parts… honestly, I barely slept. Sounds a right headache. All that rushing about. Back in my day, things moved a bit slower. You knew where you were. Though, I suppose ‘knowing where you were’ mostly meant knowing which pub had the cheapest pint. I bet! You always have a story, don’t you? Honestly, sometimes I think you lived a whole other life before me, one filled with…adventure. Adventure? Hardly. Just a lot of… well, not a lot of work, if I'm being honest. My old man, he wasn't one for pushing me. "Find a nice hobby," he said. "Don’t strain yourself." So I found a few hobbies. And then… well, things just sort of drifted. Still, it wasn't a  bad  life. Simple. But you must’ve  wanted  to do something? Something more? Wanted. Yes. Probably. There was a time I thought about being a journalist, you know? Always liked a good story. But… it felt a long way off, didn't it? Mordern wasn’t exactly a breeding ground for investigative reporters. And then… life just happened. It’s never too late, Grandad. You could start a blog! Write about your memories, your stories… People would love to read them. You’ve got a brilliant way with words. A blog? Me? Don't be daft, girl. I can barely work the television remote these days. And who'd want to read about an old bloke rambling on? It’d be full of malapropisms and questionable opinions. I would. And I bet loads of other people would, too.

Right, so we're actually doing this then? Christmas Day…flying? Honestly, it sounds mental, Liv. Mental. Oh, here we go. You said you were keen enough last week, Leo. Don’t get cold feet now. My nan’s really looking forward to having us both down in Cornwall. And yes, it's a bit mad flying  on  Christmas Day, but the flights were ridiculously cheap. Seriously, I checked for months. Cheap is good. Cornwall at Christmas sounds lovely though, doesn’t it? Bit bracing, I imagine, but lovely. Though flying… I’d rather wrestle a Santa-hatted badger. Wrestling a badger? Now  that’s  a Christmas tradition I can get behind. Beats another year of dodgy pavlova, honestly. Though, I gotta say, flying on Christmas Day… feels a bit…off, doesn't it? Like you're missing the whole point. Exactly, Arlo! The whole point is staying in your pyjamas until lunchtime, stuffing your face, and arguing with your relatives. Not being crammed into a metal tube with babies crying and someone’s questionable Christmas dinner smells. Dramatist. It’s a two-hour flight, Leo. We'll be having Christmas dinner at Nan's by 2pm. And it won't be questionable, I promise. She makes a proper roast, not like some people’s attempts at Yorkshire puddings. Hey! My Yorkshire puddings are… developing. They’re a work in progress. Besides, what about the food here? We’ve got to think about what we’re doing for Boxing Day. I was thinking a full English, and maybe a roast chicken. Ooh, Boxing Day roast chicken is a brilliant idea, Leo. I'm coming over for that regardless. Though, I’m still trying to convince my mum to do a proper Christmas pudding this year. She’s gone off the idea, says nobody eats it. Blasphemy, I tell you! Christmas pudding is overrated. Honestly, it’s like concrete with brandy. Give me a good sticky toffee pudding any day. Though, speaking of food… did anyone see that documentary about roadkill on the BBC? Apparently, deer is becoming quite popular. Oh, no thanks. That's…a bit much. I already have enough trouble sleeping after a scary film, I don't need to add ethically questionable venison to the mix. Roadkill deer? Seriously, Arlo? You've got a strange definition of Christmas cheer. I was more worried about the foxes getting into the bins.

… honestly, I still can’t believe Old Man Hemmings tried to tell me my SatNav was broken because it had a 'posh' voice. He reckoned all SatNavs should sound like Doreen from number 32. Oh,  please . Him and his insistence on everything being ‘practical’. He probably thinks Bluetooth is witchcraft. And Doreen? Bless her, but she sounds like she's perpetually disapproving of everything. The voice is crucial though, isn't it? I spent a good hour customising the voice on my GPS for the new game. Wanted something suitably…authoritative. Settled on a Shakespearean actor. Bit much, probably, but it’s hilarious when it shouts “Turn left in two hundred paces!” Shakespearean?! You are mental. I just went for the standard British female. Least likely to irritate me on a long drive. And lets be real, this drive  is  going to be long. Are we absolutely sure about going via Leicester? It adds a good hour, doesn't it? We talked about this, Liam. Aunt Carol specifically requested we collect the raspberry jam from Brenda in Leicester. Apparently, it’s award-winning. And Aunt Carol will never let us hear the end of it if we don’t get it. It’s worth the hour for peace. Besides, Leicester isn't  that  bad. It's got a history, you know. Richard III… all that. Though I mostly remember it for that one dodgy burger van. Dodgy burger van is putting it mildly. It nearly took out my digestive system. Fine, Leicester it is. But if I start exhibiting symptoms, I'm blaming Brenda and her award-winning jam. Honestly, this car is handling the extra distance okay though, yeah? I was a bit worried about putting so many miles on it so soon after the service. It feels solid, doesn't it? You did a good job with the maintenance, Liam. It’s a real improvement on… well, on what your Dad used to drive. No offence. None taken. Dad’s old Vauxhall was held together by willpower and rust. I think the exhaust pipe was actually a suggestion, rather than a functional component. This is a Mk7 Golf, it's practically a spaceship compared to that. Though I still miss the sheer chaos of it. Chaos is good for inspiration, you know? Keeps things interesting. Building digital worlds gets a bit… sterile sometimes. Speaking of which, have either of you seen that new racing game that came out?

Honestly, I still can't believe you’ve never heard of Radiohead, Leo. It’s  criminal . Like, a fundamental gap in your cultural education. Oi, easy there, mate. Criminal? Bit dramatic, innit? I listen to loads of music. Just… not whatever gloomy, arty stuff you lot are into. Give me a bit of grime, a bit of drill, something with a beat. Thom Yorke just sounds like he's constantly having a bad day. He  is  perpetually having a bad day, Leo. That's kind of the point. It’s beautiful melancholy. Besides, “Idioteque” has an insane beat. You gotta admit, that’s a banger. Exactly! And it’s not all depressing! Have you heard "There There"? Properly energetic. It's about… well, it’s layered. It's about tension, and looming disaster, and... Looming disaster? Sounds just like my physics practical last week. Nearly set the Bunsen burner alight trying to heat that magnesium ribbon. Mr. Davies was NOT impressed. He kept going on about oxidation rates and safety protocols. Proper killjoy. Oh god, magnesium. The brightest thing in the room, guaranteed to distract everyone. I had a similar issue with the diffraction grating, kept getting lost in the colours. Honestly, physics is fascinating, but sometimes it feels like deliberate chaos. See, that's like Radiohead, actually. Chaos, but deliberately crafted. It’s… textural. Okay, I’m failing miserably at explaining this to Leo. He wants a beat, I get it. Textural? Right. Look, I appreciate the effort, but I’m more of a Stormzy man, yeah? Lyrics I can actually  understand . Stuff about real life, not… existential dread. What are you even listening to at the moment, anyway, Arlo? Still on that indie rock thing? Actually, I’ve been getting into a bit of Aphex Twin lately. It's… electronic. Very experimental. Quite a lot of it doesn’t  have  lyrics, it’s all about… sound design. Aphex Twin? Sounds like a program you’d use to edit photos. It's definitely not a photo editing program, Leo. It’s… difficult to explain. Think really complex electronic music, almost glitchy. It’s the kind of stuff you'd hear in a really abstract sci-fi film. Speaking of sci-fi, anyone see ‘Dune: Part Two’ yet? Yeah! Saw it last weekend. Visually stunning, absolutely  massive  scale. The sound design was incredible, actually. Very similar vibe to some of Aphex Twin’s work, now I think about it - lots of really deep, rumbling bass.

…and honestly, the whole Balanceability thing has been brilliant for Lily. She was  so  wobbly on her bike before, practically horizontal! Now she’s zipping about with confidence. It’s amazing what taking the pedals off does for their balance, isn't it? It  is  amazing, Mummy! I can go really fast now! Faster than Thomas! No you can’t! I was faster this morning. Ms. Davies said I was doing really good steering. That’s wonderful, Thomas! Ms. Davies is a really good teacher, isn't she? You're both doing so well. It's not always about being the fastest, though, is it? It’s about trying your best and improving. Remember what we talked about with your assessments? You mean the drawing one? I did a really good unicorn! You did! A  very  good unicorn. And it doesn’t matter if someone else’s unicorn was… shinier, or had more sparkles, as long as  you  were happy with yours and tried your hardest. But what if you  want  to be the fastest? That's perfectly okay to want to be the fastest! But you have to remember to be a good sport, too. And sometimes, even when you try your absolute best, someone else will be a little bit quicker. That's just life. Did you see Mia’s new house? She told me her Mum and Dad are making a swimming pool! Yes, I heard! Apparently, they're going to have a whole section renovated. Her Dad was telling me about it at school pickup yesterday. They’re even thinking about a little… what did he call it? A manmade waterfall. A waterfall?! Wow! Can you swim under a waterfall? You can, but you have to be very careful. That brings me to something important. Remember, we always need to check how deep the water is before even  thinking  about jumping or diving in, anywhere. Even in a proper swimming pool. Especially with a waterfall nearby – it could change the currents. It's really important. Like when we were at Great Yarmouth? And you said I couldn't jump in the sea without holding your hand? Exactly! That was a good reminder for me, too – you were so keen! It’s just… you never know what’s hidden under the surface. Speaking of school, what did you both talk about with your friends today? We talked about Pokémon cards.

…and honestly, I’m knackered. Proper knackered. That conference last week nearly killed me. Three days of back-to-back seminars and stressed-out speakers. I lived on coffee and biscuits, I tell ya. Oh, bless you. Sounds brutal. Production’s been… intense too, actually. We're launching the new widget range next month and everything's riding on it. But coffee and biscuits? That’s a dangerous game. You should’ve grabbed a proper meal when you could. Easy for you to say, Miss Smoothie-and-Spinach! When you've got a delegate breathing down your neck because the projector’s not working and another one wanting extra biscuits… food's low on the priority list. I did try to go for a run yesterday to clear my head, but my legs felt like lead. Right, that’s what I mean about needing to prioritise! You need to build that exercise into your routine  before  you get to the “nearly dead” stage. I've been doing that HIIT class three times a week, and honestly, it makes such a difference. Even just 30 minutes. HIIT? Sounds… energetic. I used to be good at netball, back at uni, but haven’t touched a ball since. And frankly, the thought of running around a court right now fills me with dread. It’s just… finding the motivation, isn’t it? It is. That’s why I signed up with Sarah. Accountability partner. We moan at each other to go, and then moan  during  it, but we go! Speaking of motivation... how are things with Tom? Still going strong? That’s… complicated. We had a bit of a row last week. Silly thing, really. He left his socks on the living room floor. Honestly. But it escalated. It always does. Socks? Seriously? That set you off? No, it wasn’t just the socks! It’s… the  principle . It’s the constant little things. The not listening properly, the assuming I'll do everything… it feels like I’m constantly picking up after him. It's exhausting. Even more exhausting than a conference, ironically. Ugh, that sounds awful. It's not about the socks, it's about feeling taken for granted. Been there. Had  that  conversation, more times than I care to admit with… well, you know, with Ben before things ended. Exactly! And I don't want to be like you and Ben.

Aye, that’s better than nowt, isn’t it? Proper good pizza this, lad. Mind you, after Old Man Hemmings and his ridiculous dominoes strategy, I needed summat substantial. He thinks he's a tactical genius, does he? Mmm-hmm. He  is  rubbish though, isn’t he? Always tryin’ to block everyone instead of makin’ his own runs. And he complains if you beat him! Aye, Hemmings is a character alright. Doesn’t know when to quit, that one. Still, keeps the Domino Drive interesting. Though I reckon  you  were playin’ a bit rough tonight, young’un. Nearly had him cryin’ into his tea. I wasn’t  that  rough! I just… optimised my plays. It’s strategy, Grandad! Like in that game we play on the computer. Optimised, is it? Sounds a bit fancy for a Tuesday night in Darlington, doesn’t it? Still, good on yer. You’ve got a knack for it, you have. Reminds me of your dad, always had a head for figures. Speaking of which, did you get those Easter presents sorted for your mum and me? Uh… almost. I was thinkin' about gettin’ you a new book, Miss Thompson? You said you liked that historical one last week. Oh, that’s lovely, pet. You remembered! Anything will do, honestly. I’m not one for fuss. Your Grandad, on the other hand… he expects the moon on a stick at Easter. Now, now, Ethel! I just appreciate a thoughtful gesture. Maybe a new pair of gloves? These ones are gettin’ a bit thin, wearin’ ‘em for haulage. And a nice tin of biscuits. Chocolate digestives, mind you. None of that fancy stuff. Chocolate Digestives, noted. Grandad, did you see that massive log nearly fall out of the fireplace earlier? I thought the house was gonna fall down! Aye, saw it. That’s why I said we need a proper fire guard. Ethel keeps sayin' it ruins the look, but safety first, I say. We’re not gettin' any younger. Oh, don't fuss, Arthur. It was a bit of a fright, but it didn't  quite  fall. And it looks cozy with the open fire. So, you been listening to any good music, lad? You were glued to those headphones after school. Yeah! There's this new band, 'Static Void', they're really good. It’s kinda… electronic, but with a bit of rock. You wouldn’t like it.

Right, so you’re telling me…you’ve  never  had mushy peas with fish and chips? Not once, living in this country for… what, ten years now? Look, I’m a Birmingham lad, alright? We have our own chips-and-dip situation, thank you very much. Usually involving curry sauce. And honestly, the thought of mashed-up peas… it just doesn’t appeal. It looks…sad. Sad?! It’s a cornerstone of British cuisine! Honestly, it’s a textural delight. Smooth, minty… it cuts through the grease beautifully. You're missing out, proper missing out. It's a key component of the full seaside experience. Seaside experience? I went to Skegness once. Once was enough. The wind, the arcades…and I suspect a rogue mushy pea may have been involved, lurking on someone's plate. Trauma, I tell you, trauma. Speaking of things that lurk...did you see that article about Benedict Cumberbatch and his allotment? Cumberbatch and an allotment? Seriously? Is this the slow news day that’s driven us to celebrity gardening? Apparently he's growing all sorts of organic veg. Beetroot, kale, the whole shebang. Apparently, he’s really into it. Quite the contrast to Sherlock Holmes, wouldn’t you say? A massive contrast. Though, I suppose deducing the precise level of compost needed for optimum beet yield requires a rather similar skillset. It's just… less about crime scenes, more about slug pellets. Exactly! Intellectual pursuits, all around. Though, my attempts at growing anything beyond basil usually end in a withered disappointment. You, on the other hand, have a veritable jungle on your balcony. Years of practice, love. And a very forgiving landlord. Plus, I'm a researcher, remember? Data analysis applies to plant growth just as much as focus groups. Though, honestly, some of my tomatoes are behaving like especially contrary focus group participants. So, you’re saying you're applying scientific methodology to your tomatoes? That’s… dedication. We need to get you on Gardener's World. Oh, don't be ridiculous. I just like to know  why  things are happening. Speaking of things happening...did you manage to get that runner bean seed I sent you to sprout? It… didn’t. I think I overwatered it. Or potentially underwatered it. It was a whole debacle, really. Clearly, I am not agriculturally gifted. I'm sticking to buying my vegetables, thank you very much. And maybe enjoying a curry sauce with those chips.

Right, okay,  this  is ridiculous. Rhys, you’re deliberately misinterpreting the rules! It explicitly says ‘sounds, not words!’ You did a whole sentence about a ‘barking dog’! Now, now, Sarah, don’t get your knickers in a twist. A bark  is  a sound a dog makes. Perfectly legitimate. Technically speaking. He’s got you there, really. Rhys is a master of twisting things to his advantage. Remember the Monopoly game in Tenby? The man declared the free parking space a legitimate income source! Oh, that was a classic. He convinced your Auntie Bronwen it was a council scheme. She was furious when she realised she hadn’t been getting a share of the 'parking levies'. Oh, bless her. Bronwen takes everything so seriously. Still, it’s good to see you two behaving like children again. It’s what holidays are for, isn’t it? Escaping the seriousness of life. It’s only frustrating because I  want  to win! And honestly, Rhys, you’re making it impossible. It's supposed to be about acting out sounds, not constructing elaborate justifications for breaking the rules. My turn again… ‘Defibrillator’. Oh, brilliant. How am I supposed to  sound  like a defibrillator? ‘Beeeeeep! Beeeeeep! Thump!’ You’ve got to commit, Sarah! Full body! Beeeep… thud. Bit underwhelming, if I’m honest. You need more dramatic flair. Like you’re trying to restart a dying heart. You could try a really forceful ‘bzzt’ sound, with a little jump. Think electricity. I once saw a demonstration… rather frightening, actually. Oh, dear, let's not dwell on emergencies. Sarah, just go for it! Don’t overthink it. It’s meant to be silly. There! Is that enough drama for you all? Oh, the humanity! I’m saved! You, my dear, are a medical miracle. Rhys, scribble something down! Too theatrical. It felt… staged. Clearly remembered from a TV show. No authenticity. Authenticity? I’m trying to act out a life-saving device with absolutely no props! What authenticity are you expecting? Now, now. Don't fall out over a board game. It’s all a bit of fun. Perhaps a slightly less… vigorous… portrayal next time, Sarah. Exactly. It was certainly memorable, though! Now, whose turn is it? I think it's my turn, isn’t it? Ooh, 'Vacuum Cleaner'. Right, let me show you how it's done... . Oh, that’s brilliant, Gwyneth! You’ve even got the changing suction power!

Honestly, Rhys, you’re ruthless! Another point to the Welsh contingent. It’s becoming a massacre. Ruthless? I prefer strategically brilliant, thank you very much. And it’s not  just  me, you know. Gareth’s offering subtle tactical advice, though he pretends he’s just observing. Observing is a skill, you know. A very underrated one. Besides, somebody needs to make sure you two don’t cheat. Oh, they're both at it! Honestly, you’d think they were battling for the fate of Wales itself, not a slightly battered deck of cards. Remember when your father used to get  so  competitive at Rummy? He’d practically accuse us all of hiding cards up our sleeves. Oh, Dad. He was a force of nature. He’d probably be telling Rhys off for ‘showing off’ his card-playing prowess right now. It's funny, isn't it? Being back in England feels... strange without him. This cottage is lovely, though. Much more peaceful than Cardiff. It is lovely. Mum did well finding this place. Though, I'm starting to suspect she deliberately chose somewhere with terrible mobile reception so we’d actually  talk  to each other. A noble cause, I’d say. We're all glued to our phones normally. Though, I  was  hoping to catch the rugby scores later. Is there wi-fi anywhere? There's a faint signal near the window in the kitchen, dear. Don’t expect to stream anything, mind. It’s mostly for emergencies. Speaking of which, who’s for another cuppa? I’ll put the kettle on. Yes, please! I need something to calm my nerves after this relentless beating. It’s all down to your crazy Welsh card-playing genes, Rhys. South African genes just can’t compete. Nonsense! It's simply superior strategy. And maybe a little bit of luck. Though, I'm beginning to think I should offer Gareth a share of the winnings – he’s the real mastermind. I am  not  a mastermind! I’m simply offering… constructive criticism. Suggesting optimal plays. You know, things like, “Perhaps you shouldn't play your Queen of Spades  now , Rhys.” Oh, do hush, you two. You’re like a pair of mischievous schoolboys. It’s lovely to see you both so animated. You rarely get this worked up about anything usually. That’s because we’re losing, Mum! It’s a deeply upsetting experience. Honestly, I’m considering a tactical retreat.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Proper chaos. Uni is…well, it’s a lot. Especially with deadlines looming before Christmas.      Tell me about it! Though my chaos isn’t essays, it’s Mrs. Higgins and her insistence on rearranging her biscuit tin  every  hour. It’s exhausting, being a care support worker, you wouldn’t believe. At least you get breaks between lectures.      Mrs. Higgins sounds…challenging. I’m glad I went down the apprenticeship route. Accounts aren’t exactly thrilling, don’t get me wrong, but it’s a lot more practical than stressing over theories, isn’t it? And I’m actually  earning  while learning.      Practicality has its merits. Though I did enjoy the theoretical side of engineering. Now, designing combat systems for the Navy? That's a different beast altogether. It's a good job, demanding, but good. Still, sometimes I miss just…thinking about things. No one cares about the  why  when a radar system needs fixing, just the  how .      You all sound so…grown up. I’m still juggling A-Levels and weekend shifts at Boots. It's a nightmare, honestly. Trying to decide what to do next is the worst part. Uni seems good, but the debt scares me.      It  is  scary, yeah. I'm already mentally preparing for a lifetime of ramen noodles. But honestly, the independence is amazing. I've met so many incredible people. And I'm actually studying something I love - history! Though, my mum keeps asking when I’m going to “do something useful” with it.      Oh, mothers. Always thinking about ‘useful’. Mine just wants to know if I’m eating enough. Seriously, I’m 22, Mum! I can manage a sandwich. It’s nice she cares, but it’s relentless. You going home for Christmas, then, Cassie?      Yep, Friday. I'm already dreading the Christmas jumpers my auntie knitted. They’re…unique. Last year’s had a 3D reindeer nose that kept bopping me on the face.      Oh my god, that sounds awful! My grandma’s gone full-on festive this year. Apparently, she's built a life-sized snowman for the garden. In November. It's supposed to be a surprise, but my uncle let slip.      Sounds…ambitious. My family’s trying to tone down the presents this year, apparently. Said we all need to be more ‘mindful’ of consumption. Which is rich coming from my dad who buys a new gadget every week.

Honestly, this is lovely, love. Proper comfort food. Though, a walk afterwards is  definitely  needed. I feel me waistband protesting already. It  is  good, isn’t it? Mum, you always make the best shepherd’s pie. And yes, a walk would be good. I feel like I've been glued to this sofa all day. Did you see that article about Cambridge widening the cycling paths? Cycling paths! More like obstacles for the pedestrians, if you ask me. They just encourage those youngsters on their electric scooters to whizz about like maniacs. Nearly took me legs off last week near the market square. Oh, don't start on those scooters, Geoff! It's the drivers I worry about, honestly. They just aren’t looking where they’re going anymore. I was nearly knocked off my feet crossing Mill Road yesterday. A boy on his phone, completely oblivious. It’s just…everything feels so car-centric still, doesn’t it? Even with the cycling initiatives. So many roads designed  for  cars, not people. I cycled to work today and it was terrifying on Hills Road. Terrifying? You youngsters and your cycling. Back in my day, we walked everywhere. Built character, that did. And you  saw  things. Now everyone’s rushing about in metal boxes, missing all the life happening around them. That’s true, dear. When I was a girl in Essex, we’d walk to school, rain or shine. Even to Southend for a day at the seaside! Can you imagine doing that now? Absolutely not. Everyone’s ferried about by their parents. It’s not always practical, Mum. I mean, my commute is five miles. Walking that would take… hours! But I do wish public transport was better. Maybe then people would drive less. Public transport… Don’t even get me started. Remember that bus route they cancelled last year? The one that went past the shops? Made it impossible for ol’ Mrs. Higgins to get her groceries. Oh, I remember. I wrote a letter to the council about that, I did. Didn't do any good, of course. They just don’t listen, do they? It’s all about the park and ride now, isn't it? Trying to keep the cars out of the city centre, but it just shifts the problem elsewhere. It feels like a temporary solution, anyway. What about that new congestion charge they’re talking about?

...Honestly, the sheer volume of people here is a bit overwhelming, isn’t it? It's good to see so many faces, but I wasn't quite prepared for this level of… networking. Did you manage to grab a decent coffee? The queue was horrifying.      It was! I ended up going for a tea instead, figured it might be slightly quicker. And yes, massively overwhelming. I feel like I've just walked into a room full of very accomplished people and I’m suddenly questioning all my life choices. You work here at the faculty, don’t you? I’m Ellie, by the way. I'm the new Research Administrator.      I am, yeah. I’m Freya. Language Research Coordinator. Nice to meet you, Ellie. It  is  a pretty impressive crowd. Don't worry about feeling out of place – most of them are probably doing the same self-assessment. They just hide it better. What did you study?      Thanks, Freya. That makes me feel a little better! I did my undergrad in Linguistics too, actually, then a Masters in Applied Language Studies. That’s how I ended up here. So, what sort of language research are you coordinating? Is it all Cambridge-centric, or do you work with other universities?      Primarily focused on dialectal variations within the UK, at the moment. Though we do have a small project looking at language contact in the Basque Country, which is fascinating. Have you ever been to Spain?      Excuse me, I couldn't help but overhear you talking about the Basque Country. Remarkable linguistic landscape, isn’t it? A language isolate, completely unrelated to anything else in Europe. I spent some time there years ago, researching their oral traditions. Fascinating people. Name’s Arthur, by the way. Retired lecturer from the History faculty.      Oh, wow, that sounds incredible! I’ve always been intrigued by languages like that – so uniquely preserved. I haven't been to the Basque Country myself, sadly. Mostly just European city breaks, really. I’ve done Barcelona a couple of times. Are you an Alumni, Arthur?      Indeed, a rather long-in-the-tooth one, I’m afraid. Came up through here back in the… well, let’s just say a while ago! Barcelona is lovely, of course. But the Basque Country has a completely different feel. It’s quite rugged, and the culture is… intensely local. It reminds me, in a way, of some of the more remote parts of Wales.

Honestly, Mum’s Facebook is a  minefield . She’s sharing all these… inspirational quotes overlaid on pictures of kittens and then getting into arguments with people about Brexit in the comments. It’s exhausting just scrolling past. Oh, God, you’re so right. She hasn’t changed a bit. Remember when she got completely hooked on Candy Crush and then tried to send everyone invites? I had about fifty notifications a day. It was the ice bucket challenge all over again, except instead of raising money for charity, she was just… trying to get us to play a game. Speaking of the ice bucket challenge, did anyone actually  follow up  on the charities that benefitted? I feel like it was all a bit of a flash in the pan. Great awareness, maybe, but did it actually make a lasting difference? I think some did, yeah. I remember reading about a massive increase in donations to the Motor Neurone Disease Association, at least in the immediate aftermath. But you’re right, the momentum died down pretty quickly. It’s funny, isn’t it, how something so… performative can be effective, even if temporarily? It's all about visibility, I suppose. But Mum didn’t even  do  the ice bucket challenge properly. She used lukewarm water and complained the whole time. Said it “ruined her hair.” Classic Mum. Remember when Auntie Carol tried to convince everyone that Uncle David wasn't  really  her half-brother, that it was all a misunderstanding? That family reunion was… something. Speaking of which, is Auntie Carol still going on about her gluten intolerance? I think so. She cornered me at Christmas and tried to explain the benefits of spelt flour for a full twenty minutes. I just nodded politely and pretended to understand. Honestly, I’m more concerned about Grandad. He’s looking so frail these days. I know. We need to visit him more often. He was asking after you, Ben, last time I spoke to him. Said he wanted to hear about your… “fancy teaching job,” as he put it. He still thinks I'm just making things up. "Teaching  English ? To  foreigners ? What's wrong with teaching them proper English in the first place?" Honestly, the man. Though, he did always appreciate a good moan about paperwork. It’s probably why he’s so fascinated by my job – endless marking! He's always been a character.

Honestly, this coffee machine is the bane of my existence. It either brews something akin to battery acid or lukewarm dishwater. There’s no middle ground. And it was  expensive  dishwater, mind you. Still battling with it, Mary? You’d think after six months you’d have mastered the art of the bean-to-cup. Honestly, I used to just use instant. Less fuss. Speaking of fuss… have you two actually got a proper quote for the removal and storage yet? I’m starting to worry we’ve left it too late. Prices are only going to go  up , you know. Especially with everything… well, everything going on. I spoke to ‘Man with a Van’ down in Penrith yesterday, John. They were surprisingly reasonable, but the storage quote was… astronomical. They want nearly £200 a month for a space barely big enough for a wardrobe and a few boxes. Daylight robbery, I tell you. Two hundred a month! That’s… crippling. Is there no other option? Maybe a self-storage unit? They’re usually cheaper, though admittedly a bit more hassle. Self-storage is alright, but the security can be dodgy. Remember what happened to Brenda’s nephew? Everything gone, vanished into thin air. Still, £200… it’s outrageous. It’s all this Brexit nonsense, isn’t it? Everything is more expensive because of it. Brexit. Don’t even get me started. Honestly, the mess they’ve made of things. And now look at the Labour party. Keir Starmer… he’s about as inspiring as a damp squib. Where’s the vision? Where’s the  passion ? I think he’s trying to be… sensible. After Corbyn, a bit of sensible is probably what the public wants. Though, I agree, he lacks a bit of… spark. It feels like he’s just trying to not offend anyone. Sensible is a euphemism for bland, Louise. Utterly bland. You need someone with a bit of fire in their belly, someone who actually believes in something. Remember Attlee? Now  there  was a leader with a plan. National Health Service, welfare state… radical stuff. Oh, you and your rosy-tinted spectacles, John. It wasn't all sunshine and roses back then, you know. Rationing, austerity… it was a different world. But you’re right, there was a genuine desire to build something better. Today, it just feels like everyone’s scrambling for self-preservation.

Honestly, Mum, the thought of Christmas already fills me with dread. Not the  Christmas  bit, you understand. The  people  bit. Specifically, Uncle Barry’s annual political rant after his third sherry. Oh, Barry. He’s a constant, isn't he? Like the Queen’s speech, but less…refined. You’d think after all these years we’d just tune him out. You’d think! But he  targets  me, you know? He knows I teach, so he starts on about the ‘woke agenda’ in schools. Honestly, it’s exhausting. And Dad just sits there, looking mortified. Your father’s always been a man of few words when Barry’s holding court. Sensible man, your father. Have you at least started thinking about presents? I know you leave it to the last minute usually. A bit. I got Leo a dinosaur encyclopedia – he's obsessed. And I’m thinking a scarf for Sarah, she's always cold. But everyone else…it’s just stuff, isn’t it? They don’t  need  anything. It is, isn’t it? That’s the hardest part. It's the thought that counts, although sometimes I think a nice bottle of something is always appreciated. Are you and Mark doing Christmas at your place this year? We are. Mark’s volunteered - or rather, I convinced him. It means we get to control the music and the guest list, to some extent. Plus, Leo is convinced Father Christmas only visits ‘proper’ houses. Which apparently, our little terraced house is. He’s a charming boy. He has your stubborn streak, that one. So, how’s the teaching going? Any nightmare classes at the moment? It's…okay. Honestly, I’m starting to feel a bit burnt out. It’s rewarding, don’t get me wrong. Seeing them progress is brilliant. But the paperwork! And the constantly changing curriculum. It feels like I spend more time jumping through hoops than actually  teaching . I can imagine. It’s the same in my line of work, with all the health and safety regulations and compliance forms. It can stifle creativity, can’t it? Have you thought about doing any further training? Maybe a TEFL diploma or something? Might open some doors. I have. It's expensive, though. And I'm not sure I want to be tied to another course for a year. I was thinking…a complete career change, maybe? Something a bit less… stressful.

Honestly, I haven't had a decent night’s sleep in weeks. Liam’s snoring is honestly… biblical. It’s like having a walrus in the bedroom. Ah, you’ve reached the ‘walrus’ stage, have you? That’s a good one. Mine used to sound like a broken chainsaw. Though, thankfully, it’s calmed down a bit since I started sleeping on the sofa more often. Don’t tell her I said that. Typical! You two are hopeless. You complain about each other but wouldn’t have it any other way. And you expecting a good night's sleep when you're both out every weekend, eh? It’s different! Weekends are  allowed  chaos. This is a Tuesday night! I need my beauty sleep for spreadsheets. Speaking of needing things... did anyone else get those amazing Eccles cakes from Waterfield’s this week? They were proper lush. Waterfield's are a gift from the gods, aren’t they? Proper dead good. I always get a loaf of their bloomer and a couple of those jam tarts. Though, I’m partial to a good sausage roll myself, and they do a cracking one. I was in there yesterday, getting a loaf for Mum. They’d completely sold out of Richmond sausages.  Completely . It was a disaster. Mum was fuming. She practically interrogated the poor lad behind the counter. Oh, no! Richmond sausages are a  must . They're the proper breakfast sausage, innit? None of that flimsy stuff. Mum will be proper brassed off. Seriously! Mum lives for a Richmond sausage butty on a Saturday. It’s a ritual. Waterfield’s really let her down there. Maybe they had a delivery issue? Likely. They’re usually spot on. Although, I did overhear old Mrs. Higgins complaining last week that their custard creams weren’t as ‘fluffy’ as they used to be. Honestly, some people… Custard creams! That’s important. You can’t mess with a good custard cream. My grandma is the same, she'll write a letter of complaint if her biscuit isn't up to snuff. She carries a handkerchief in her purse  specifically  for biscuit-related crumbs. A handkerchief for biscuit crumbs? That’s dedication. I've not seen anyone use a proper handkerchief in years. It’s all tissues these days, or just… wiping your hands on your jeans. It’s true, isn’t it? Grandad always has one.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of glitter. Everywhere. I’m still finding it in my hair. You’d think after planning kids’ parties for a living, I’d be immune, but no. Little Leo just covered himself head to toe. Leo sounds like a proper little whirlwind, doesn’t he? Your auntie Brenda’s 6th birthday party, was it? A six-year-old and glitter… a potent combination. Worth it though, eh? Seeing her face? Oh, absolutely. She was ecstatic. She kept calling it a ‘princess party’ even though we’d gone for a more woodland creature theme. Honestly, adapting is half the battle. How was  your  weekend, Dad? Anything more peaceful than a glitter bomb? Peaceful? Hah. Not exactly. Old Man Hemmings’ prize bull, Bartholomew, decided he wasn’t happy with his pen on Saturday afternoon. Took me, young Thomas, and half the village to get him back in. Thing weighs a ton, that one. Nearly took out Mrs. Gable’s prize-winning dahlias. Bartholomew, eh? Sounds… dramatic. Was he just being stubborn, or was there a specific reason for the escape attempt? Stubborn, mostly. Hemmings reckons he was lonely. Lonely! It’s a bull, not a labrador. Though, I did notice the gate latch was a bit dodgy. Promised Hemmings I’d have a look at it on Monday, but with the escape and all the calming down, it slipped my mind. Need to call him. You always end up fixing everyone's problems, don't you? It’s that farmer instinct. Speaking of fixing things, did you manage to get that leaky tap sorted in the kitchen? It’s been driving me mad. Dripping, dripping, dripping… Ah, the tap. Got to it Sunday morning. Bit of a stubborn washer, that one. Needed a new one, naturally. Managed to find one down at Wilko’s, thankfully. Shouldn't drip now. You check, but it  shouldn’t  drip. Brilliant! You're a lifesaver. Honestly, I’d have left it for weeks. I’m hopeless with anything practical. I tried to hang that picture in the hallway and ended up with three holes in the wall. Well, you’re a project co-ordinator, not a builder! Different skillset entirely. Though, I'm surprised you didn't delegate  that  task. I did try to get Ben to do it, but he was ‘deep in coding’ or something. You know how he gets.

…and honestly, the kids were lovely, absolutely lovely. But marking 150 essays on the subjunctive  every  week? It just…drained me. I felt like all I was doing was correcting grammar, not actually  teaching  them anything useful. Ugh, the subjunctive. The bane of every French teacher’s existence, isn't it? I remember when I was training, Mrs. Davies, she’d practically weep over a misplaced subjunctive. Though, to be fair, she’d been teaching for about forty years by then. Things were different. Different how? Less focus on perfect accuracy, more…communication? That’s what I'm trying to get to with my current students, little language exchange ones. It's brilliant, actually. Less pressure, more just  using  the language. Probably. Though I think it was less about a conscious shift in methodology, and more about just weathering decades of curriculum changes! Though, you're right, communication is key. My lot at the primary school just want to ask each other what their favourite colour is, which is…a start. What languages are you doing with the exchange students? Mostly English for Spanish speakers. It's fascinating hearing how they approach the language. They pick up things so quickly, but make completely different mistakes to my British students. It’s a good reminder of what’s actually  difficult  about English. That's really interesting. It's funny, isn't it? You forget how weird English is when you're immersed in it. I’ve been trying to brush up on my German, purely for a holiday, and it's humbling. Remember Herr Schmidt in sixth form? He made it look so effortless. Now I can barely conjugate ‘sein.’ Oh, Herr Schmidt! Intense man, wasn’t he? But a fantastic teacher. Though, a holiday needing German…that’s ambitious! Are you going somewhere specifically? We’re thinking Bavaria. Ben’s always wanted to go. And honestly, I thought it would be a fun challenge. Besides, between work and, well…everything else, I need  something  to focus on that isn’t tiny humans or lesson plans. "Everything else" being…? You haven't… oh! Don’t tell me! Are you…? Guilty as charged. Due in December. It's a bit of a shock, to be honest. We weren't exactly planning it. Ben nearly fainted when I told him. Oh, Alice! That's  wonderful ! Congratulations! That's…huge! I’m so thrilled for you both!

Right lovely bit o’ cake this is, Mavis. Best you’ve baked in a while, I reckon. Though, mind you, they’re  all  good. Just this one… well, it’s got a bit of a spring to it, don’t it? Aye, it’s a good ‘un. Bit sweet for me, mind. Keeps tellin’ me off, she does, about the sugar. Gotta watch it, see. This blooming diabetes… it’s a right nuisance. Now, now, Arthur, don’t grumble so. A little sweetness never hurt anyone. And honestly, you ate a perfectly respectable portion. It’s good for the soul! Besides, I used that low-sugar jam. Low-sugar jam? Fancy that. Still tastes proper jammy to me. Look at them blue tits, though! Busy as bees, they are. Been at that new feeder I put up, haven't they? They have. Clever little things. Though I swear, they’re messier than the grandchildren. Scattering seed everywhere… Makes a right state of the patio. Oh, let them enjoy it, Arthur. They need to bulk up for the winter. Did you see the robin building a nest in the hawthorn yesterday, George? Right near the shed. Did indeed. A proper little architect, she is. Though, I worry about it. It’s a bit exposed, that hawthorn. Predators could get to it easy. It's the way of things, George. Nature’s cruel, innit? Though, I remember old Mrs. Higgins down the road… she used to make little ‘dramatic society’ puppets. Birds, mostly. Used to hang ‘em in her garden to scare off the cats. Daft as a brush, but it seemed to work for a while. Puppets! Oh, Arthur, you always come up with the best stories. Mrs. Higgins was a character, wasn’t she? I liked her. Always had a Werther’s Original in her handbag. Reminds me, I saw young Timmy next door trying to build a den in the bushes. All branches and blankets. Looked a right state, but he’s got ambition, that lad. Building things, y’know? That’s important. Like what I used to do…bridges and such. Though, not quite as…rustic. You were a clever man, George. An engineer, weren't you? Always drawing plans. I never could get my head around all them lines and angles. I was happy enough pottering about in the garden. He  was  clever. And very precise. Everything had to be just so.

…and honestly, the meze just  keeps  coming! I thought I’d ordered a small plate, but it’s practically a feast. Are you managing alright with the halloumi, David? You seemed a bit hesitant earlier. Hesitant? No, no, perfectly alright. Just… contemplating. Halloumi's a funny cheese, isn't it? Squeaks when you chew it. Reminds me of old man Hemmings from the council. Used to squeak whenever he disagreed with anything, which was often. Oh, Hemmings! Goodness, I’d almost forgotten him. Always clutching that briefcase, forever complaining about planning permission. This is much nicer company, though. And a nicer view. I still can’t get over how blue the sea is here. It is lovely, isn’t it? Much better than grey old Dudley. Though Elsie, God rest her soul, she’d have said anywhere with sunshine was good enough. She didn’t care for fancy views. Just wanted a cup of tea and Coronation Street. Speaking of Elsie… how's Brenda coping? It’s been six months now, hasn't it? Since… you know. Slowly. Very slowly. She’s joined a bereavement group, which helps, apparently. Says it's easier talking to people who  understand . She keeps busy with the garden, mostly. Roses, you know, Elsie’s favourites. Though ironically, Brenda swears Elsie always secretly preferred begonias. She’s convinced Elsie just wanted to appear sophisticated! That sounds like Elsie. A little bit of a performance, always. It’s funny the little things you remember. I’m still getting used to the quiet without Mum. It’s been… a year next month. A year. Time flies, doesn't it? Though it doesn’t  feel  like it when you're grieving. I’ve been meaning to ask… you mentioned your hearing aid wasn’t playing up? I was worried after you said it was acting strangely last week. Oh, it’s fine now. Had it checked – just needed a new battery, apparently. Honestly, you’d think after all these years, I'd remember to check something so simple! It's embarrassing, really. Especially trying to order in Turkish. I managed “Bira, lütfen” – beer, please – but beyond that, I’m completely lost. I’m trying to learn to count though. “Bir, iki, üç…” “Dört, beş, altı…” There you go. I picked up a bit when we were down here a few years ago. It’s useful for haggling. Though I suspect they inflate the prices for tourists anyway.

Honestly, Mum, this gravy is  divine . You’ve outdone yourself. It's exactly how I remember it – proper Sunday dinner gravy. Though, I still think you sneak a bit of Bovril in there… Don’t be silly, darling! It’s just a good, slow reduction with a touch of Worcestershire sauce, that’s all. You always were a little detective, weren't you? How's the new project going, anyway? Still juggling a million things at once? You have no idea. It’s…intense. We're implementing a new CRM system and everyone’s resisting it. Old habits, you know? Trying to get Brenda in accounts to even  look  at the training manual is a battle. I’m basically a professional hand-holder at this point. Sounds like you need a good rugby match to de-stress. Did you catch England’s game last weekend? Absolute nail-biter! I tried to, Dad, but I was up against a deadline. I saw the highlights though. Looked pretty stressful  watching  it, let alone playing! Your grandfather would have been in his element. He lived for rugby. Remember how he used to try and teach you, Lily? You always preferred drawing, didn’t you? I did, yes. He was a lovely man. I miss him. Though, I think he secretly thought I was a bit…fragile. All that gentle encouragement to "toughen up." He just wanted you prepared for the world, love. It’s a rough place out there. Speaking of rough, have you given any more thought to moving out of that little flat? It sounds cramped, even for one. I'm thinking about it. London is expensive, though. And finding something that's both affordable  and  doesn't involve a 45-minute commute is…challenging. I saw a nice one in Tooting, but the kitchen was TINY. I'd rather stay put for now, honestly. It's convenient, and I like my flatmate, even if she  does  leave her tea mugs everywhere. Tooting, you say? That's quite a way out. When you do look at places, bear in mind this house, darling. We’re seriously thinking about doing that extension, finally. We've had the plans drawn up for ages. A little flat above the garage, completely self-contained. Perfect for you. Wow, Mum, that’s…a big thought. Really? You’d do that? It sounds amazing, truly. But wouldn’t it be disruptive for you both?

Right, so you are  telling  me this lad, this “Mark” you were chatting to for six months… was using photos of a bloke off of Instagram? A fitness influencer?! Honestly, Chloe, you've gotta be kidding me. I wish I was, Sal! Six months! Six months of late-night chats, pretending to like rugby, sending him silly memes… all to a bloke who looks like he's sculpted from granite but is actually…well, Barry from accounting probably. Honestly, I feel so stupid. Oh, love, you’re not stupid. It happens to loads of people. It’s just…the audacity, innit? Six months! That's dedication to a lie. Did he have a whole backstory, the fake Mark? A whole  life , Amy! He was a ‘widowed dad’ running a dog rescue centre in Cornwall. Said his wife died from… I don’t even remember now, some tragic illness. He sent me photos of puppies constantly. PUPPIES! It just seemed… genuine. A widowed dad  and  a dog rescue centre? That's next-level catfish. Sounds like he’d watched too many Hallmark movies. It’s always the heartbreaking stories, isn’t it? Pulls at your heartstrings. Honestly, it’s like a Jeremy Kyle plotline, but without the lie detector. Ooh, don’t mention Jeremy Kyle. Remember that one where the bloke pretended to be a fireman? And then the real firemen turned up? Savage. It was brilliant and terrible all at once. Don't even  start  on Jeremy Kyle. I'm feeling bad enough as it is. It’s not exactly a laughing matter when you've been emotionally invested in someone who doesn't even  exist . I know, I know, I'm sorry. It’s just… the sheer scale of it. And the fitness influencer! Was he at least attractive? Like, did you fall for someone who was genuinely a good looking bloke, even if he wasn't the bloke he said he was? Oh, he was gorgeous. Seriously ripped. That was part of the pull, I guess. I thought I was doing well, chatting up someone decent looking for once. Turns out, I was chatting up someone  else’s  decent looking self. I found his real Instagram account eventually. It was just…normal. Like, really normal bloke. Bit of a belly, photos of his garden, gardening gloves… Ouch. That's a comedown. Gardening gloves are the ultimate betrayal. So, how did you find out?

Honestly, Gran, this ham and pickle is  chef’s kiss . You really haven’t lost your touch, even after, well, all these years of making them. Though, you used to put slightly more pickle, didn’t you? Just a thought. Oh, don’t you start, Leo. A little less pickle is a sign of maturity, darling. At my age, one has to consider digestion, you know. Though, yes, perhaps you're right. I  did  used to be rather generous with it. Reminds me of Paris, actually. The market stalls there, piled high with the most glorious gherkins… Paris? What’s Paris got to do with pickle? You jump about a bit, you know you do. Everything is connected, Leo! Everything! I was learning French properly then, after the war. Trying to lose the last traces of that German accent, you see.
