Keeps suggesting I move back to Enfield and find something in the council offices. Oh, Mum. She’s got a very specific vision of happiness. Mine keeps asking if I’m eating enough.

Now, that Kiev was…alright. Not a patch on the ones your Granny used to make, mind you. She had a touch, she did. A  touch . None of this pre-brined, flavourless nonsense. It was okay. A bit…soggy though, wasn’t it? Like it hadn’t been cooked properly in the middle. And I wanted chips, not roasties. Honestly, Leo, you’d think you were being served prison rations. It’s a perfectly good chicken Kiev. And roast potatoes are  much  healthier. Honestly, the backchat! Ah, leave the lad be, Mary. He's a growing boy. Needs his starch. Though I’ll admit, Granny’s Kievs were legendary. Remember the time she accidentally set the smoke alarm off trying to deep fry them? Oh, don’t remind me! The whole house smelled of burning oil for a week! And she insisted it was ‘just a little bit of character.’ Honestly, that woman. Still, she'd be furious about this rugby result. Wales won, didn’t they? I was hoping for Ireland. Aye, they did. A right hammering, to be fair. Sexton had a shocker, didn’t he? And that ref… questionable decisions all day. I was shouting at the telly like a madman. Gave me a terrible headache now, actually. You and half the country, probably. Honestly, you’d think your life depended on a rugby match! Speaking of headaches, I need to sort out photos for your mother. She keeps phoning asking about them. Apparently, she needs them for…something. Wallies, she called them. Wallies? She’s making a photo album of Leo’s school plays. She  always  calls them 'wallies'. She’s utterly hopeless with technology. I tried to show her Dropbox last time, and she just stared at me like I was speaking Martian. I showed Gran Flickr once. She thought it was a type of bird. Oh, bless her. Honestly, technology is not her forte. It’s easier to just print them and post them. Though that's a fortune these days. It is. Right. We need to get a move on, we’re supposed to be heading to your mother's tomorrow, aren't we? I'm not looking forward to it, between you and me. She’ll be asking about my career again. She just wants to know you're doing well, love. And Leo needs to see his Granny. Though I’m worried about her garden.

Honestly, another three bids on that Shelley Dainty Blue cup. It’s ridiculous, isn’t it? People are  obsessed . I thought I was being sensible at £28, but… it’s climbed to forty-five now. Forty-five? Blimey. You’re getting into serious money for a cup and saucer. Are you  sure  it's worth it? Though, I admit, that pattern is lovely. Very delicate. Is it one you absolutely  have  to have? Well, not absolutely  have  to, but it completes the little set I’m trying to build. I’ve got the teapot, the sugar bowl… just needed the cup and saucer to finish it off. It’s a bit of a silly hobby, I know. Especially when I spend half my life transcribing interviews about far more important things! Not silly at all. It’s your thing. And it’s nicer than, I don’t know, collecting stamps. Though, speaking of things that are surprisingly expensive, have you seen the price of decent buckwheat bread these days? Seriously, £4.50 a loaf! Don’t get me started! I tried making it myself last weekend and… let’s just say the kitchen looked like a flour bomb had exploded. And the bread tasted like cardboard. I’ll stick to paying the extortionate price, thank you very much. It’s much less stressful. Wise decision. Right, dinner. Is this the lentil soup again? Smells good. It is! And it’s extra good because I’m trying to use up all the vegetables before the community market on Saturday. Apparently, old Mrs. Higgins is bringing a mountain of pumpkins. We’ll be drowning in pumpkin soup for a month. Always does. She’s a force of nature, that woman. Did you manage to get a stall sorted for the church this year? Yes, finally! It took some persuading, but I managed to convince Reverend Davies that selling vintage china is indeed ‘community enrichment’. Apparently, a bric-a-brac stall wasn’t posh enough. Oh, he’s such a snob. Still, good for you. You'll clear a fair bit for the roof fund, I suspect. Speaking of clearing things out, did you finalise plans for your leaving do? Almost. I’ve booked The Red Lion for next Friday. Just need to get a headcount. It's going to be… weird, isn't it? Saying goodbye to everyone after fifteen years. It will be.

…and honestly, Dad, I’m tellin’ ya, the essay on post-structuralism is killin’ me. It’s just…words! Fancy words strung together to  sound  clever. What even  is  deconstruction, anyway?      Oh, don’t even get me started on academic theory, Liv. Honestly, sometimes I think I spend more time decoding invoices and tax regulations than grappling with anything remotely philosophical. Though, you know, both can feel equally…obscure.      Aye, invoices. Now  there's  a language I understand. Numbers don’t lie, do they? Unlike some people… .      Oh, here we go. Always with the accusations, lad. I was merely illustrating a point about…complex financial structures. Perfectly legitimate structures, I might add.      Legitimate? That's what you said about that 'investment opportunity' with your mate, Kev, last year. Remember how  that  turned out? Auntie Brenda nearly had a fit when she found out she’d gotten a hefty fine.      Liv, be nice. He’s trying to explain his work. But yes, Dad, perhaps steer clear of ‘opportunities’ involving anyone named Kevin. Especially if they involve offshore accounts. It sounds awfully… murky. I mean, you  are  dealing with a lot of money, aren’t you, with the building company?      I’m a self-employed builder, Eleanor, not Pablo Escobar. It’s all above board, genuinely. But sometimes, things get… complicated. You’ve got subcontractors, materials, VAT… it’s a minefield. And frankly, some of these banks are making it deliberately difficult. They’re asking for so much proof of origin, it’s borderline harassment.      Harassment? Sounds a bit like you're trying to hide somethin’, doesn’t it? Remember Old Man Hemmings? Got caught red-handed launderin’ money through his car wash. Said it was “just complicated accounting.”      Money laundering?! Dad! Are you…?      Absolutely not! That’s outrageous, Thomas! I’m talking about simple, honest business transactions. But they're flagging everything now. Just because I occasionally receive a large cash payment for a job – people  like  paying cash, you know – doesn’t mean I’m running a criminal enterprise. It’s ridiculous! They sent me a letter just last week requesting details of every single transaction over £1000 from the last six months!      That  is  intrusive. But it’s also standard practice now, sadly. They’re under so much pressure to crack down on it. Honestly, you might consider more electronic transfers? It creates a clear audit trail.      Easier said than done.

Honestly, this weather is doing my head in. One minute it’s sunshine, the next it’s threatening a downpour. Makes planning anything impossible. I was thinking of getting the washing line out earlier, and then… well, you know. Tell me about it, Brenda. It's been like that all week. I had a sponsored walk planned for the hospice, trying to raise funds, and nearly got washed away! Had to postpone it, naturally. Luckily, most people were understanding. The rain just  came  at us. Oh no, Dad! That’s awful! Did you manage to reschedule? It sounds like you were really prepared. We’ve pencilled in next Saturday, fingers crossed. The forecast looks… cautiously optimistic. Though I learned my lesson. I’m bringing umbrellas as prizes now. Just in case! That’s brilliant, Dad. Always prepared! So, how was work today, Mum? Anything exciting happen at… well, wherever you are working these days? You’re always so secretive. Don’t start, Chloe. It's just temping, dear. Nothing to get your knickers in a twist about. It was… paperwork. Lots and lots of paperwork. Honestly, I’m starting to dream in spreadsheets. Though, I did overhear a bit of office gossip about a possible restructuring. Not ideal. Oh, Mum, that sounds stressful. I hope it doesn’t affect you. You deserve a bit of stability, you've been hopping around jobs for ages. I know, I know. It’s just… finding something I actually  want  to do, at this age, is proving difficult. Still, it pays the bills. Speaking of which, has anyone remembered to book that sign language class I mentioned? Oh! Nearly forgot! I did, Mum. It's next Tuesday evening at the community centre. 7pm. I’ve put it in everyone’s diaries on the group chat. Good on you, love. I’m really looking forward to that. I think it'll be lovely to learn, and helpful, with the little one on the way. I’ve always wanted to be able to communicate a little with anyone who might need it. Me too! It's a really practical skill, and something I can use at school as well. Some of my pupils have communication difficulties. It'll be wonderful to be able to offer them a bit more support. Exactly. And think of all the baby songs we can learn! I was thinking of teaching the little one from the very beginning.

…and honestly, the phonetic transcription was  awful . Like, genuinely, did they even  listen  to the speaker? The glottal stops were just… missing. Entirely. It’s Bucks, you know? We drop consonants like hot potatoes, it's practically a regional sport! You're sounding very academic, Chloe. I thought language research was supposed to be about appreciating variation, not correcting it to some BBC standard. It  is  about appreciating variation! But appreciating it accurately! When you’re building a corpus, it needs to  reflect  reality, doesn’t it? Not some compromised, smoothed-over version. It defeats the whole point of trying to map linguistic features. I kind of get where you're coming from. We had a similar issue with some dialect recordings for a children’s book we're doing. The initial transcriptions were just flattening everything. My editor was rightly furious, because it completely lost the character of the stories. It's just... tone deaf, isn’t it? Sorry, was I interrupting? Something about missing glottal stops? Sounds… intense. No, not at all, Elina! Just commiserating over the perils of transcription. It’s surprisingly stressful, isn't it? Especially when people think it’s just “writing down what you hear.” I can imagine. I'm still pretty new to the whole publishing process, so I mostly just… fetch coffee and try not to break anything. But even I can tell when something  sounds  wrong. Like, I proofread a manuscript last week and the author kept writing “colour” with a ‘u’ – even though the style guide specifically said ‘color’. It felt… offensive to my inner American. Oh, the great colour/color debate! I used to get so hung up on that when I was interning in New York. My supervisor nearly had a breakdown when I automatically corrected it. Apparently, it’s a deeply held principle. It's funny how specific some of those style points are, isn't it? We had a huge battle over the Oxford comma the other day. Honestly, you'd think lives depended on it. The Oxford comma  does  depend on lives! Okay, maybe not, but good grammar saves ambiguity! It’s a fundamental pillar of civilization! Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm fighting a losing battle to preserve linguistic integrity. Dramatic much? You’re really passionate about this, aren’t you? What are you researching at the moment, anyway? Something related to dialectal variation, I presume.

Right, so I’ve been lookin’ at these visa requirements again for Mongolia. Honestly, it's a right palaver, innit? They want, like, three different copies of bank statements, a letter from me nan confirmin’ I'm a good lad, and a signed affidavit swearing I won't smuggle any… well, anything. Tell me about it. I spent half of yesterday just tryin' to decipher what "proof of onward travel" actually  means . Do they want a return flight? Because that kinda defeats the object of a rally, doesn't it? It's not like we’re goin' for a week in Benidorm. Exactly! I was thinkin’ a bus ticket outta Ulaanbaatar… would that cut it, d’ya reckon? Or do we need to pretend we're off to, like, Vladivostok straight after? It’s mental. And the photos... passport photos are the bane of my life. I always look like I've just been informed of a terrible, terrible thing. Haha, you  do  have a naturally mournful expression, lad. I’ve got a mate who’s a photographer, he owes me a favour. Might be worth gettin' him to do 'em. Avoid the booth nightmares. Speaking of nightmares, have you started properly collectin' donations yet? My uni lot are bein' a bit stingy so far. Slow goin’, yeah. I’ve set up the JustGiving page, obviously, but it needs a proper push. I was thinkin’ about posting an ad on Gumtree. “Two lads, dodgy car, Mongolia, for children!” – somethin’ like that. Bit clickbaity, maybe? Gumtree’s not a bad shout, actually. People respond to a bit of a story. Make it sound properly desperate but for a good cause. Like, "Our car is held together with duct tape and dreams – help us get to Mongolia for [Charity Name]!" We need to emphasize the charity, though. People are more likely to donate if they know exactly where the money’s goin’. Good point. I’ll tweak it. I reckon we need a proper target too. We’ve just got a vague "as much as possible" thing goin' on at the moment. What d'ya think? Five grand? Ten? Considering the cost of the car repairs alone… Ten sounds ambitious but good. It gives people somethin’ to aim for, makes it feel more… legitimate. We’ll need to break it down too. "£5 pays for engine oil", "£20 gets us a spare tyre”, that kind of thing.

Honestly, I still can’t believe you ended up in A&E last night. A dislocated arm because of… what  was  it again? Trying to do an impression of a seagull? Don’t even. It was a  dance move . A really, really bad dance move. And alright, maybe I had had a couple of VKs. But still! It hurt, yeah? Proper hurt. They said it wasn’t broken, just… pop-ped it back in. Felt like my shoulder was on fire for a bit. VKs and questionable dance moves. Sounds about right for a Thursday night with you two. How’s the arm feeling now, love? You were looking pretty pale when you got back. A bit achey, thanks. Still kinda wobbly. Doctor said to take it easy, which basically rules out everything fun for the next week. Fantastic. See? This is why I stick to reading. Much safer. Though even  that  feels exhausting these days. This uni workload is insane. I’ve barely slept all week. I think I’m developing a permanent dark under-eye circle. Tell me about it. I’ve got that essay on Victorian literature due on Monday and honestly, I'm staring at a blank page. It’s just…words aren’t happening right now. Speaking of not happening, have you seen Ben lately, Daisy? You were chatting to him at the welcome party. The one with the ridiculously good hair? Oh, Ben. Um, yeah, briefly. He’s… around. Why? No reason, no reason. Just wondered. He was asking after you yesterday. Said he thought you looked nice. You didn't mention him. Ooh, someone’s got a secret crush! Come on, Daisy, spill! It’s not a crush! He's just… nice. And he's from Plymouth, which is practically next door to Falmouth. So, you know, a familiar face. That’s all. I’m just knackered is all. I think I need more tea. I'm going to make a brew. Anyone want anything? Massive mug of anything caffeinated, please. And maybe a biscuit? I’m operating on fumes here. Just water for me, cheers. Honestly, she’s hopeless at admitting when she likes someone. She's always been like that. Remember that lad, Tom, from sixth form? She denied having the slightest interest in him for months, then turned bright red every time he spoke to her. Right, caffeine delivery system initiated. So, has anyone actually managed to understand this module on post-structuralism?

…Honestly, I’m still knackered from Saturday. Your Auntie Brenda really does know how to throw a shindig, doesn’t she? Though I swear, she had every relative we’ve  ever  had crammed into that village hall. Yeah, it was… a lot. My ears are still ringing from Uncle Barry’s karaoke. He really thinks he’s the next Pavarotti, doesn’t he? Oh, Barry. Bless him. He tries, that’s what counts. But honestly, the sheer number of people! Did you get a chance to speak to Cousin Margaret’s boy, the one who’s studying archaeology? Briefly. He was cornered by Gran explaining the intricacies of her geraniums. Didn’t stand a chance. I mostly just navigated a sea of plates piled high with sandwiches and tried to avoid being interrogated about my A-Level choices. Ah, the interrogation. Standard family fare. Your Grandpa was particularly keen to know if you'd settled on a university yet, weren’t you? He was going on about engineering again. Ugh, don’t remind me. He thinks anything that doesn’t involve a wrench and a good hard day’s work is… frivolous. He kept saying, ‘A proper trade, lad, that’s what you need!’ I told him I was leaning towards history. He just blinked at me like I’d grown a second head. He’s a man of his generation, love. He comes from a time when careers were… simpler. But you need to do what  you  want. And history's a good subject, a proper academic subject. Shows you can think, can research. It’s not ‘frivolous’ at all. Thanks, Mum. It's just... tiring, you know? Having to explain myself all the time. It felt like everyone was trying to steer me towards something  they  wanted, and not what would make  me  happy. I know, I know. It does feel like that sometimes. Especially at these gatherings. Everyone’s got an opinion, and they're all very willing to share it. Did you manage to chat with Lizzie at all? I thought she was looking a bit lost. Yeah, for a bit. She’s stressing about her art portfolio. Says her teacher's being really critical. She was worried she wouldn't get into the art foundation course she wants. Oh, poor girl. She’s such a talented artist, though. That sculpture she did last year, the one with the driftwood… absolutely stunning.

Honestly, Dad, this water bottle is  useless . It’s like, barely a mouthful left. And you said bring plenty! We've barely left Cheshire.      Now, now, Elsie. Don't be dramatic. We’ve got three more filled ones in the boot, and a stop planned at that services near The Cotswolds. Besides, you had a good swig just before we left Manchester. Remember? I even had to wrestle the pen off you to actually  let  you drink it.      That was different! I needed to write down that TikTok idea. It’s gold, Dad, absolute gold. It's about a washing machine that judges your outfits…      A judgmental washing machine? Sounds… modern. You and your TikToks. Look, we’re doing well for time, aren't we? Though this traffic is a bit dodgy. Thought we’d be further south by now. What d'you fancy for dinner tonight? We could find a decent pub in Somerset.      Somerset sounds…beige. Can we not just get a takeaway when we get to the cottage? Maybe pizza? And can we stop at Holland and Barrett? I’m almost out of those IBS support tablets.      Holland and Barrett, of course. Always Holland and Barrett. Though I still reckon it's half the price to get them on Amazon. Speaking of Amazon, remember all that fuss about the delivery when we moved? The sofa arrived three weeks late!      Don’t even  mention  the move! Unpacking boxes is my official nemesis. It took me a month to find my Latin textbook. And then Mrs. Henderson complained about the state of the garden afterwards, even though  you  were supposed to be trimming the hedge.      Now, Elsie, Mrs. Henderson complains if the sun's shining too brightly. It’s her hobby. And your Latin textbook? You haven’t touched that since mocks! Thinking about moving, though… that was stressful. I still don't understand why they made the post code different for the new house. Made it impossible for deliveries.      It was because it’s technically a different county, Dad. Greater Manchester to Dorset. Big difference. You know, I was reading about how counties used to be like mini-kingdoms. Proper historical stuff. Like, imagine being the ruler of Cheshire!      I’d implement a law requiring everyone to eat liquorice. Then I’d regret it immediately. It tastes like medicine. Speaking of, did you take enough for your tummy? You know how easily upset it gets with travel.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of it is just… draining. Three hours of a solicitor reading out clauses about garden fences. Garden fences, David! You’d think people had more pressing concerns when dividing an estate. Well, Aunt Margaret was  very  particular about her roses. And you know how Uncle Alistair always felt the boundary line was…flexible. It’s a wonder they didn't end up in court during their lifetimes. Flexible? Alistair simply believed what belonged to him, belonged to him. He’d ‘borrow’ things from neighbours and then act surprised when they asked for them back. A charming rogue, he was, but a trial nonetheless. Sounds like a right character. Reminds me of old Mr. Evans down the road. Used to ‘trim’ branches off  my  apple tree, claiming they were blocking his sun. Didn't matter that his garden faced north, mind you. Exactly! It's just the detail, isn't it? All this meticulously documented squabbling over things that ultimately…don't matter. I'm supposed to be turning audio into something  useful , not cataloguing decades of passive-aggressive horticultural warfare. You’re a professional, Elspeth. Think of it as… historical documentation. A snapshot of familial relationships, preserved for posterity. Posterity will be utterly bewildered. "Here lies the great legacy of the McTavish family…and a dispute over three inches of lavender." Oh, don't be so cynical, dear. Family history  is  important. It tells you where you come from, the quirks and foibles that shaped you. Alistair’s stubbornness, for instance, is rather evident in young Fergus, isn't it? Fergus? He’s a good lad. Bit headstrong, maybe, but a good heart. He helped me build that shed last summer, didn’t complain once even when I made him hold the wonky post. That's Fergus all over. Always willing to muck in. Though, I suspect he was secretly enjoying the challenge of propping up  your  wonky post, Rhys. You might be right there! I buy cheap timber, what can I say? Keeps me in business, fixing other people’s mistakes. Honestly, you two are a distraction. I need to get back to this recording before I lose the will to live. There’s a particularly heated debate brewing over the ownership of a garden gnome. A  garden gnome , David! A gnome? Good heavens. Was it a particularly valuable gnome? Perhaps antique? Apparently, it was a gift from Uncle Alistair to Margaret when they first moved in.

Right, operation Mother’s Day is a go! Any initial thoughts, team? Honestly, I’m feeling a bit overwhelmed. It feels like every year I try to do something  amazing  and then end up with slightly burnt toast and a wonky card. Can we make her breakfast in bed? Like, proper pancakes, not just toast? With sprinkles! And strawberries! And whipped cream! A  lot  of whipped cream. Like a mountain of it. She likes mountains, doesn’t she? You're both thinking big, which is excellent. Pancakes are ambitious, but doable. We'll need to keep a close eye on the hob. No setting off the smoke alarm again, please. Remember last year? The neighbours thought we were having a bonfire  inside . It wasn’t  my  fault the bacon stuck! It was a little bit your fault. You were trying to flip it with a spatula that was too small. It just…launched. Alright, alright, let’s not start a bacon-related inquest. Focus. Pancakes, potentially bacon , and strawberries. Good. What about a card? Do we want to make one, or shall we brave the shops? Make one! We can draw her a picture of us all at Forest School! Remember when you helped me build that fairy house? And I found that massive stick and pretended it was a dragon’s tooth! It was a really good tooth. Oh, I remember. It was a  very  impressive tooth. Forest School is definitely a good theme. Now, I was thinking, rather than a huge, elaborate gift, maybe we could do something  with  her? She often says she prefers experiences to things. Like what? A trip to the zoo? No! Too cold for the zoo. She said that yesterday. Remember? She said her nose feels like an icicle. You both have excellent memories for snippets of conversation. You’re right, the zoo is out. How about… we take her back to Forest School? Not to  do  Forest School exactly, but just for a walk in the woods? She loves it there. Ooh! And we can collect leaves and twigs and make something! We could build another fairy house! A  super  fairy house with a drawbridge and everything! That sounds lovely. Okay, so pancakes, a handmade card with a Forest School theme, and a walk in the woods. That’s a pretty solid plan. Although… I'm starting to feel like I'm 'burning the candle at both ends' trying to organise it all!

…and honestly, the guilt is awful, isn’t it? Just knowing she put everything on hold for  him . Everything. Her pottery classes, the gardening club, even just meeting us for coffee. It was always “Oh, I need to be available, just in case.” And now… well, now it feels like she wasted good years. It’s not wasted, love. It’s just…different. A different sort of love, a different sort of sacrifice. Mum did the same with Dad, you know? Not quite to the same extent, Dad wasn’t as…demanding, shall we say? But she always prioritized his needs, even when it impinged on her own happiness. It's what that generation were like, I think. I know, I know. Rationally, I understand it. It’s just…seeing Maggie like this. She’s so frail, and the chemo’s just knocking her sideways. She barely recognises the grandkids half the time. And John…he just sits there, looking bewildered. He's utterly lost without her managing everything. He can't even  find  his slippers. He always was a bit helpless, wasn’t he? Bless him. But honestly, it's more than just helplessness. He’s grieving too, in his own way. It’s a weird grief, watching someone fade like that, knowing they’re still…there, but not  really . It's like a slow goodbye. Have you talked to Ben about how he's doing? He hasn’t said much to me. Not really. He’s being… stoic, I suppose. Which is Ben all over, isn’t it? Says he's “handling it,” but he’s lost weight and he’s been snapping at the kids. He’s normally such a patient dad. I tried to bring it up last night, but he just brushed it off and started talking about work. He's throwing himself into that, I think, to avoid dealing with it all. It worries me. That's classic avoidance. He needs to talk. Maybe not to us, initially. Maybe a professional? It’s okay to get help, you know? We pushed each other towards counselling after…well, you know. And it  helped . Even just having a neutral ear. You're right. I should suggest something. It's just…he’s so stubbornly independent. Reminds me of his father. And Sarah, too - she's quiet as anything. I've noticed Sophie's been acting out a bit at school, apparently.

Right, brain officially fried. That deconstruction of Chomsky's Universal Grammar was…intense. Honestly, I feel like I need a linguistics detox. You and me both. Though, I think  I  need a detox from trying to understand  you  explaining it. You get so caught up in the technical stuff! Is that what you were doing with your students this morning? Pretty much. First years. They’re bright, but the concept of innate language abilities…it’s a tough one to get across. Did your seminar go alright? The one on sociolinguistics and regional dialects? Yeah, it was good. We were talking about Estuary English and how it’s creeping further and further inland. Loads of debate about whether it's a 'proper' dialect or just… lazy pronunciation. Typical student stuff. It reminded me a bit of home, actually. Everyone back in Gillingham sounds a bit like that now. It’s fascinating, isn’t it? How language constantly evolves. Though, sometimes I wish it would just…stay still while I’m trying to teach it! Speaking of which, have you checked the university website for the updated timetable? I’m pretty sure my Wednesday afternoon class got moved again. Oh, brilliant. Just what we need, more schedule chaos. No, not yet. I was meaning to, but then I got distracted by trying to figure out what to  do  with all these courgettes. They were a ridiculously good deal at Sainsbury’s. Courgettes are good! We can make that vegetarian lasagne you do. Though, honestly, sometimes I do miss a proper Sunday roast. You and your meat! I know, I know. It’s just…the thought of how those animals are treated…it puts me off. Anyway, lasagne sounds perfect. It's less effort than trying to figure out something with all these aubergines too. Did you see how cheap kimchi was at the Asian supermarket last week? I was thinking of trying to make bibimbap. Kimchi, eh? You're getting adventurous. I’ve always meant to go to South Korea. It looks amazing. Apparently, the societal structure is quite different. Very hierarchical, especially regarding gender roles, from what I’ve read. Yeah, I’ve done a bit of research. It’s a bit…complicated. Apparently, there's still a lot of pressure on women to conform to traditional expectations. Makes you think, doesn’t it? It's a world away from this flat in Sussex, arguing about courgettes.

Honestly, this pepperoni is  chef’s kiss . Although, I’m starting to regret that extra slice. Feel a bit…solid, you know?      Aye, tell me about it. I went for the veggie supreme and I'm regretting every mushroom. Should’ve just stuck with plain cheese like a sensible Yorkshire lass. Did anyone actually win at Articulate last night? I maintain my ‘Renaissance Artist’ description was perfectly clear.      Perfectly clear to  you , maybe! I was convinced you were doing ‘Rusty Nail’ for a good minute. And no, you didn't win. I think Maya took the crown, she’s ridiculously good at that game. Remember when we tried Heads Up and all her clues were just movie sound effects?      Oh god, yes! And Leo was utterly useless. He kept shouting “thing!…it’s a thing!” at the screen. He's hopeless at anything requiring a modicum of…thought. Speaking of hopeless, anyone finish that physics work? My brain is fried. Quantum entanglement is actively mocking me.      Oh, don’t even  start  on physics. I spent three hours yesterday trying to understand something that felt deliberately obtuse. It’s like they enjoy making it difficult. Remember Mr. Henderson in primary school? He used to practically  cackle  when people got the maths wrong.      Oh, Henderson! Now  there  was a character. Always smelled faintly of chalk dust and disappointment. Did he ever actually explain anything, or just enjoy the suffering? My primary school memories are mostly just wishing for lunchtime.      Mine are being terrified of the school guinea pig. It looked at me with such judgement. Anyway, back to more important things - has anyone started thinking about Secret Santa? I got a truly dreadful present last year. A… scented candle that smelled aggressively of pine. In July.      Ouch. I once got a pair of boxers two sizes too small. Seriously uncomfortable. Like a constant reminder of someone’s poor judgement. I’m thinking of just buying everyone socks this year. Safe and practical.      That's… pragmatic. I was considering a Twilight-themed gift basket. Don't judge me, I'm having a moment. It's a guilty pleasure! I need something to distract me from module assessments.      Twilight?! Oh, bless you. Honestly, it's a relic of a simpler time. Though, I will admit, I was Team Edward. Don't tell anyone. Did anyone see Jack Whitehall on The Big Fat Quiz last night?

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of data is mental. Like, I thought my undergrad dissertation was a lot, but this is a whole different kettle of fish. Three terabytes of transcribed interviews, all needing tagging for sentiment, topic, dialect… It's a proper beast. Three terabytes? Blimey. That  is  a lot. What’s it all for then? Some academic study on the decline of… well, what  is  it about? You’ve been a bit vague. It’s a project commissioned by the BBC, actually. They're building a massive archive of regional dialects, trying to digitally preserve them before… well, before they disappear, I suppose. It’s a bit depressing when you think about it. They want to analyze how language changes over time, socio-economic factors that influence it, that kind of thing. That’s… surprisingly cool. So you're basically a linguistic archaeologist? Digging through recordings for lost vocabulary? Something like that! Though 'archaeologist' makes it sound a bit more glamorous. Mostly it’s just me staring at spreadsheets and cursing the inconsistent transcription. Honestly, some of the interviewers clearly hadn’t a clue how people actually  speak  up north. They’d write down “howay” as “however” and then I’m left trying to figure out what on earth they meant! Oh, the horrors. I can imagine. People from outside the area thinking we all talk like the Queen, or… well, like they do in those bad period dramas. Exactly! It’s the same with the Sunderland accent. People think it's just… broad. Like it's all about being loud and dropping your 'Hs'. But there’s so much nuance to it, you know? The way vowel sounds shift, the specific slang… It’s a whole language within a language. My grandma used to have phrases for everything, things I’ve never heard anyone else say. My grandma was the same. Hertfordshire isn’t exactly a hotbed of distinct dialect these days, but she had her sayings. “Butter wouldn’t melt,” was a big one. Used to say it when I was trying to get away with something. Oh, classic! We had “yo’s doin’ alright?" which isn’t a question of how you  are  alright, it's more like a general greeting, you know? A way of acknowledging someone. Then there was “canny,” meaning good. “That's a canny bairn.” It’s… hard to explain if you haven’t grown up with it.

…Right proper brew this is, mind. Though it doesn't quite settle the stomach, does it? This…this little flutter I've been gettin’. Feels like a trapped bumblebee in me chest, it does. Oh, Arthur, you  always  have somethin'. Is it that heartburn again? You know you shouldn’t have that biscuit with your tea. Doctor said, didn't he? Doctor says a lot of things, Doreen. Mostly things I don’t understand involving metres and grams and… and blurry pictures. And it ain't heartburn, not exactly. It’s…a fizzing. A nervous fizzing. Though what I’ve got to be nervous  about  at me age, I couldn’t say. Morning all. Fizzing, Grandad? Sounds unpleasant. Maybe you should actually  tell  the doctor what it feels like, instead of just nodding and agreeing to everything he says. Now, don’t you go tellin’ me how to speak to me doctor, young lady! He's a very clever man, that Dr. Sharma. Bit rushed, mind, but clever. And I  do  tell him things! He just… doesn’t listen proper. He’s always lookin’ at that computer screen. He’s probably just entering the information, Arthur. It’s standard procedure. Though I agree, it can feel impersonal. Still, better to be checked out. How’s your blood pressure been since last week? High. Naturally. Everything goes up these days. Prices, blood pressure, the temperature… spoke to old man Hemmings down the lane. He says his greenhouse tomatoes are sufferin’ in this heat. Says it’s the worst summer he’s seen in fifty years. Oh, don’t even mention the heat! Makes me joints ache somethin’ awful. And the humidity! I swear, my hair’s got a mind of its own. It's been dreadful for the roses too, of course. All mildewed. It is exceptionally humid. The weather patterns are just… off. I was explaining it to my students yesterday – the jet stream is all over the place. It’s a direct consequence of climate change. Climate change? Bah! It's just a hot summer. We had hot summers when I was a lad. We didn't have all this fussin' and botherin' about it. Though, to be fair, we didn't have air conditioning. Just a fan and a damp cloth on the forehead. It’s more than just a hot summer, Arthur. There’s a clear trend. It’s not just the heat, it’s the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events.

…and honestly, the seating plan is giving me actual nightmares. Aunt Carol  insists  on being next to Uncle Barry, despite the fact they haven’t spoken a civil word to each other since… well, since forever. It’s a logistical disaster! Oh god, family weddings are the worst for that. Remember Sarah's? The drama with her cousins over who got to walk down the aisle first? It was  intense . Have you at least got a rough idea of table themes? Might distract from the Carol/Barry situation. Table themes are a good shout, Chloe. Though, really, just separating Carol and Barry as far as humanly possible should be priority one. You’re getting stressed about this way too much, though! It’s a party, not a UN peace summit. Seriously, you're planning your wedding like it's a military operation, Liv! Remember when we were kids and all we wanted to do was wear princess dresses and eat cake? Now it's seating charts and potential familial feuds. Easier said than done when your mum keeps adding people to the guest list! It started at 80, now we’re creeping up to 120. And then everyone  expects  a plus one. Honestly, I’m starting to think eloping to Vegas is a viable option. Vegas would be amazing! Though, your mum would probably track you down. Speaking of which, how's Ben taking all this stress? Is he helping, or is he mainly just…existing? He’s… supportively existing. He’s brilliant at the practical stuff – finalising the band, taste-testing the cake – but the people management side of things is definitely my domain. Which is exhausting. Right, because men are famously good at navigating complex familial relationships. Don’t get me started on trying to explain to  my  boyfriend why my Gran always asks him if he’s eating enough. Oh, I get that! Mark’s nan grilled him for a solid fifteen minutes about his protein intake. Apparently, he looked “a bit peaky.” He's six foot four and goes to the gym five times a week! They mean well, bless them. Though, it’s exhausting. Anyway, back to the wedding… what about the honeymoon? Have you booked anything exciting? Somewhere to escape Carol and Barry, at least. We're going to Italy, which I’m massively excited about. Tuscany, specifically. Vineyards, pasta, sunshine… it’ll be bliss.

…Honestly, this new telly, eh? All these smart bits and bobs. Give me a good old knob twister any day. I spent half an hour just tryin’ to find the news this mornin’. Ended up watchin’ some fella buildin’ a shed in America. Oh, Arthur, you and technology! It’s not  that  bad. Though I will admit, my granddaughter, Lily, had to set up my tablet. I still mostly use it for photos of the little ones. And checking the price of biscuits, naturally. Biscuits are important, that’s true. But it’s the principle of the thing! Back in my day, things were simple. A few channels, a bit of static, and you knew where you were. Now it’s all streaming and on-demand… sounds like a right bother to me. It  is  a bit overwhelming, isn’t it? I have to explain it to my students all the time. They assume everyone’s digitally native, but it’s definitely not the case. It’s about access too, really. Not everyone can afford the latest gadgets, or even reliable internet. That’s right. Young Timmy, the boy I used to mind, his mum was always worryin' about the broadband. Said it was either that or proper shoes for him. Dreadful, innit? And it’s all these online games, too. He was glued to that Fortnite, wouldn't look up for hours! Games. Never understood 'em. When I was a lad, we had a stick and a bit of imagination. Built entire empires in the fields. Much better for you, gettin' fresh air. Though, mind you, old Farmer Giles wasn’t too pleased when we ‘borrowed’ some hay for our castle. Sounds idyllic, actually. A bit chaotic, maybe, but idyllic. My kids are obsessed with Roblox now. It’s… complicated. Essentially, they build and play games  within  a game. I’ve tried to get my head around it, but it's a bit beyond me. It’s a good job I'm a teacher, I need to have some sort of understanding! It’s just… everything’s so expensive now, isn’t it? Even simple pleasures. I used to take the children to the stables, let them stroke the horses. Lovely, gentle creatures. But the price of riding lessons… well, it’s just gone through the roof. Horses. Now  there’s  a proper pastime. My father used to breed 'em.

…and honestly, the sheer variety of accents  within  Birmingham is fascinating. I had a student yesterday, born and raised here, but with a really noticeable Brummie twang - proper ‘ow do ya do’. It's lovely, but sometimes a challenge to decipher when you're trying to focus on French verb conjugations! Ah, Birmingham. Always been a bit of a melting pot, hasn’t it? When I first came down here with the company – back in the seventies, mind you – I thought I’d landed on another planet linguistically. Nothing like Essex, that’s for sure. Straightforward, we are in Essex. A bit blunt, perhaps, but you always knew where you stood. Straightforward is good! Sometimes I feel like I’m constantly decoding, not just the language I'm teaching, but the nuances of  how  people are speaking it. It's exhausting, but rewarding. What were you working on when you first came to Birmingham, if you don’t mind me asking? Manufacturing, mostly. Steel. We had a big contract with a factory just outside of Redditch. Long gone now, of course. All shipped off to China, wasn’t it? That was my life, really. Climbing the ladder at the firm. Started as a junior, ended up Managing Director. Good money, lots of responsibility… and eventually, a bit too stressful. Hence the early retirement. That sounds…intense. I can’t imagine that kind of pressure. I quite like the relative calm of a classroom, even with the occasional teenage drama. Though, my mum keeps hinting I should be “aiming higher” with my career. She’d much prefer I was Head of Department. Mothers, eh? Always wanting the best for you, even if 'the best' isn’t what  you  want. Mine was the same. Wanted me to be a doctor, can you believe it? I barely passed biology! You’re doing something worthwhile, teaching. Shaping young minds. That's important work. Do you enjoy it? I genuinely do. Most of the time! It’s the marking that kills me, honestly. But seeing a student finally  get  something, that's a good feeling. Are you keeping busy in retirement, then? I know you always had a keen interest in gardening. Oh, the garden’s keeping  me  busy! It’s a constant battle with the slugs, I tell you. And the weeds! I’ve got a new variety of roses this year – ‘Peace’ they're called.

… honestly, the whole day was just  a lot . Like, everyone was SO extra. Red roses everywhere, couples practically glued together… it felt a bit suffocating, innit? Especially when you’re just tryna get a decent cuppa. Tell me about it! My timeline was FULL of engagement announcements and couples posting, like, essays about their love. It was… intense. Did  you  get bombarded with anything? Liam sent me a chocolate heart. A chocolate heart, Maya. Like, seriously? Oh, bless. Liam. He’s sweet, but a bit predictable, yeah? Nah, thankfully, nothing. Mum sent a card which was nice, but also subtly hinting about when I’m gonna bring a nice young man home, the usual. Honestly, the pressure! It's Valentine’s Day, Mum, not a marriage proposal deadline! Ugh, parents. Mine were worse. They kept asking if I was going on a 'romantic date' with anyone. I was like, “Mum, I have a bio lab on Friday evening, what date?!”. Honestly, I just wanted a takeaway and to binge-watch something. Yes! A takeaway is the  only  way. Did you end up getting one? I was seriously considering a massive pizza, but felt like I should probably attempt something vaguely healthy… failed, obviously. Ended up with chips and gravy. Gravy is always the answer. I got Thai, which was glorious. And then attempted to watch that new horror film everyone’s been raving about. "Crimson Peak" or something? Ooh, I heard about that! Is it actually good or just hyped up? I'm a bit of a wuss, to be honest. I jumped at a shadow during “Get Out” last year, and my flatmate thought I was being attacked. It's properly creepy. Good atmosphere, proper jump scares... I spent most of it hiding behind a cushion. It wasn’t a brilliant story, but visually, it was amazing. But honestly, the cinema was packed with couples. You could practically  feel  the awkward hand-holding. Ugh, the cinema on Valentine's Day? That's just asking for trouble. It's a minefield of PDAs and whispered sweet nothings. I'm sticking to home viewings from now on. Though, speaking of films, have you seen anything good recently? I need recommendations. Not really. I’ve been mostly catching up on uni work. Actually, that’s kinda my problem. This statistics module is killing me. I just… don’t get it. Oh, no!

…and honestly, the sheer arrogance of it all! He just  assumed  because I’d suggested using more sustainable materials, I was trying to inflate the budget. Like, hello? Reducing our carbon footprint isn’t a luxury, it’s…basic responsibility now. Ugh, tell me about it. Sounds like classic ‘boys’ club’ behaviour, doesn’t it? Still massively prevalent in construction, I imagine. It's the same at the  Mirror  sometimes. Older editors just don't get why focusing on diversity isn’t just ‘wokeness’, it’s…better journalism. It reaches more people, reflects more lives. Anyway, enough work gripes. This Dan Dan noodles is  incredible . Did you go for the spicy one? I did! It's a good heat, isn’t it? Not just for the sake of it. Yours looks…mild. Though, to be fair, anything looks mild compared to my spice tolerance these days. But seriously, the condescension. He literally said, "Are you sure you understand the  economics  of this, darling?" Darling! As if being a woman automatically disqualifies me from understanding finances. Oh,  darling  him! The absolute cheek. It’s this ingrained thing, isn’t it? This idea that certain professions are 'masculine' and automatically assume expertise based on gender. And the economics line… that’s just a deflection. It's the same with housing. Everyone’s moaning about affordability, but nobody wants to talk about the fact that capitalism incentivises keeping prices artificially high. Exactly! It's all about creating scarcity. My parents keep saying "when  we  were young...", and I’m like, “Okay, but that was a different economic model entirely! You could actually  buy  a house on a single salary back then!” Now? Forget it. I'm a qualified architect with a postgraduate degree and I’m seriously considering just… staying with my parents indefinitely. Don’t even get me started. My brother's been looking for ages. He’s got a good job, but everything is just… out of reach. This whole “generation rent” thing isn’t just a hashtag, it’s a reality. And the rhetoric! 'Pull yourself up by your bootstraps' - seriously? When the boots cost a month's wages? I was reading an article about the link between housing costs and the rise of the far-right. People are desperate and feeling disenfranchised. That’s terrifyingly plausible. Actually, talking of disenfranchisement...did you see that report on the stop and search statistics again?

Honestly, this is lovely. Just… a quiet ten minutes. Though quiet doesn’t really  exist  anymore, does it? Not since little Leo arrived. You say that now, but you were the one moaning about being bored before! And it’s not  that  chaotic. Mostly just…sticky. Everything’s sticky. Sticky is an understatement. It's a biohazard. But yes, I did moan. I’m allowed a little wobble now and then, aren’t I? Especially with nursery looming. I’m a wreck about it, honestly. Nursery? Oh, right! Next week, isn’t it? Two days a week to start? Don't worry so much, Mum. He’ll be fine. They’re really good at Little Explorers. Mrs. Davies sent me some lovely photos when I did my volunteer placement there. I know, I know, logically I  know  he’ll be alright. It’s just… letting go, isn't it? He’s still my little baby. And what if he cries all day? What if he doesn’t settle? I’ve been trying to prepare myself, but… They said they're really good with settling-in. Slow introductions, lots of cuddles. And honestly, he’s such a sociable little thing. He loves being around people. He’ll probably be making friends before you’ve even gotten back to the car! You're an optimist. I wish I could bottle some of that. It’s also making me realise how quickly I need to finalise going back to work. My manager's been really understanding, but I need to give them a concrete date. I'm thinking… January? January sounds sensible. Gives you a good chunk of time with Leo first. And allows him to settle into nursery before you disappear for the day. Although, ‘disappear’ is a strong word. He knows you'll come back. It feels like disappearing! And then the guilt… oh, the guilt. It's a whole new level of guilt. I haven't been away from him overnight since he was born. Though thinking about it… perhaps a holiday is needed. A proper one. Now you’re talking! Somewhere warm? We could go somewhere. Just the three of us. Or maybe with Dad? Actually, somewhere  without  Dad might be nice for a change. No offence. No offence taken. He'd probably spend the whole time worrying about whether the hotel had good enough TV channels. Honestly, the man needs to learn to relax.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is a lifesaver. Longest day. Absolutely  longest  day. And to top it all off, they wanted a detailed statement about… well, you know. About young Timmy and the, shall we say, ‘incident’ at the garden centre? Still can’t believe he tried to make off with a gnome. A  gnome , Margaret! A particularly elaborate gnome, apparently. Apparently it was limited edition. They treated it like a robbery, honestly. DS Miller was there, asking all sorts of questions. It was exhausting. And I’m still trying to work out why Timmy even  wanted  a gnome. Classic Timmy. He always did have… unique tastes. Did you tell them he collects garden ornaments? Maybe that would explain it? Perhaps. Though I doubt a collection justifies swiping a limited-edition gnome. Though, thinking about it, he  does  have a lot of those little solar-powered lights… Talking of things that exasperate me, I’ve just had another battle with EE. The phone bill. It's outrageous. They’ve added some data charge, claiming I downloaded three films. Three films! I was at a fundraising dinner for the hospice all evening. Oh, honestly, they are the worst. They always assume it’s you. Have you contacted their customer service again? Three times! Each time I get passed around to a different person who insists they can’t do anything. I’m starting to think I need to write a strongly worded letter. One with capital letters and underlining. Maybe copy in Martin Lewis? He sorts that kind of thing out all the time. Good shout, Chloe. He has a whole section on his website dedicated to fighting unfair phone bills. It's worth a try. Definitely. Right, enough about frustrating companies. How was your day, Liam? Still wrestling with that funding application for the youth centre? It’s… going. Slow. The paperwork is phenomenal. They want everything broken down into microscopic detail. I think I’ve rewritten the budget section five times. It feels like I’m building a house out of spreadsheets. You’ll get there. You always do. You’re brilliant at this stuff, even if you do complain about it. Speaking of brilliant, Chloe, how did things go at the shop today? Any dramas? It was… busy. We had a bit of a queue at the tills all afternoon. And Mrs. Higgins tried to return a tin of peaches that she'd opened.

…and honestly, the wedding was  lovely . Proper lovely. Your cousin, Chloe, she really outdid herself. The venue was…well, it was a bit much, if I’m honest. All that bunting. But the atmosphere was brilliant. You wouldn’t believe the spread. Did you manage to try the canapés? The little smoked salmon things? Nah, missed those. Got stuck talking to Uncle Barry about… honestly, I don't even know  what  he was on about. Something about sea lice and a fishing trip in Wales? He’s a character, that one. Glad you enjoyed it though. It meant a lot to Chloe, having everyone there. Especially you, coming all the way from Bedford. Wouldn't have missed it. It’s just… weird seeing everyone again, you know? Feels like ages since we all properly chatted. Remember when we were kids and obsessed with  Gladiators ? God, that show was rubbish, but we were hooked.  Gladiators ! Don't even! That was peak Saturday night entertainment. Though I was always more into the historical stuff, even then. Remember when I got obsessed with the Romans after that school trip to Colchester? Kept trying to build a miniature Colosseum out of Lego. Oh, I’d forgotten about that! And you insisted on dressing up as a centurion for a week afterwards. Speaking of historical obsession, have you seen the  Spartacus  series? The original one, not the newer stuff. It’s…intense. Yeah, bits and pieces. It’s a bit gory for me, to be honest. I prefer my history a little…less blood and sand. More focused on the bread. Honestly, the Roman bread making techniques are fascinating. Did you know they often used chickpea flour? Really? I did  not  know that. You always have the weirdest, most interesting facts. Speaking of food, I've been trying to get into making my own bread. It’s a disaster. It either comes out like a brick or completely flat. You need a proper mortar and pestle. Forget the food processor, it just doesn't…connect with the ingredients, you know? My Nan used to make the best spice mixes. She’d use a mortar and pestle she brought back from China, apparently. Though she claimed it was originally for grinding herbs to ward off malarials. China? Wow. That’s quite a story. She was a traveller, your Nan. Did she bring you back anything good? I'm always after souvenirs.

Honestly, that English test was  brutal . Mrs. Davies is trying to kill us all, I swear. Did you understand any of that poetry analysis section? I just wrote about… well, whatever came into my head, really. Probably nonsense. Brutal is an understatement! I spent ages on that first question, the one about the metaphors in ‘Ozymandias’, and then I completely blanked on everything else. I think I just summarised the poems instead of analysing them. Are you doing the revision session on Thursday? I am, yeah. Mum practically  forced  me. Says I need to "apply myself." As if I don’t already! It’s just… English isn’t my thing. I much prefer Art. Mr. Henderson’s letting us experiment with charcoal this week. It’s going to be amazing. Oh, lucky you! I’m a bit rubbish at Art, lets be real. I always end up with everything looking muddy and brown. I’m much better at languages. Though, French is…challenging. Madame Dubois just  loves  to ask us ridiculously complicated questions. Tell me about it! She practically interrogated poor Leo today. He went bright red trying to conjugate a verb. It was awful. And then she asked if anyone had watched any French films recently. As if! I’ve barely had time to breathe, let alone watch subtitled movies. Exactly! It feels like she's testing us on our cultural knowledge too, not just the grammar. Anyway, speaking of things that are stressful, have you heard anything more about the wind band auditions? I'm still panicking about it. Oh! Yes! I actually tried out yesterday. It went… okay. My flute playing was alright, I think. Ms. Peterson said she’d put the list up on Friday. Are you auditioning? I am! I’m so nervous. Everyone says Bethany’s going to get first chair on clarinet again. She's annoyingly good. It’s always Bethany. She  is  good. But don't let that put you off! You’re a fantastic oboe player, Chloe. Honestly. Remember that solo you did at the school concert last year? Everyone was talking about it. That was ages ago! And I messed up the high note slightly. No one noticed but  I  noticed! What about the people actually  in  the orchestra – any gossip? Sarah mentioned something about a drama with Ben and Olivia? Oh,  that . Apparently, Ben was trying to flirt with Olivia during rehearsal, and she completely shut him down.

Aye, look at that drizzle. Proper Darlington weather, this is. Honestly, you'd think it was November, not… well, whatever day it is. Feels like ages since I’ve had a proper sunny afternoon. And it’s putting a dampener on me mood, it is. It’s Tuesday, Miss. And it’s not  that  bad. Me mam says drizzle’s good for the garden. Though I don’t see why gardens need that much help. Your mam always did have a green thumb, lad. And she’s right, actually. It’s better than a downpour. Though I’m with Brenda, a bit of sun would be lovely. Especially after… well, never mind that now. Brenda, you look a bit peaky. Everything alright? Just the weather, pet. And thinking about the heating bill, if I’m honest. It's going to be astronomical this winter, I just  know  it. They keep going on about energy prices on the news. It's frightening. Reminds me of the three-day week back in the seventies, though this feels… different. More precarious. Three-day week? What’s that? Sounds ancient. Like something outta history. Oh, you wouldn't remember. Power cuts, everything. Factories shut down for days. It was a bit of a mess, truth be told. It taught you to appreciate a hot bath and having the telly on, though. Simple pleasures, eh? Simpler times, perhaps. Though not necessarily better. Remember when everyone complained about the miners’ strike, Brenda? Now folk talk about it like a golden age. Funny how nostalgia works. Aye, well, everything looks rosier through rose-tinted glasses, doesn't it? Still, I’m worried about young ‘uns like Leo here. Trying to get a decent education with everything going on… and the cost of it all! University fees are a joke. I’m alright, Miss. I'm aiming for a scholarship. And I’m actually smashing it in physics, so… That’s me boy! Good on you, Leo. Physics, eh? Very impressive. You always were a bright spark. It’s just… everything’s so competitive now. And they’re all obsessed with these TikTok videos and things. No concentration span left. Now, Brenda, don’t start on the technology. I remember when computers were the size of a room and you needed a degree just to turn one on! It’s progress, even if it’s a bit… overwhelming. Though I must admit, I struggle with the youngsters’ slang.

Honestly, Dad, you wouldn’t  believe  the traffic getting up here today. Just gridlock on the A11. I swear, everyone decides to visit Norfolk on a Sunday. Aye, well, they’re missing out if they don’t. Best county in England, this is. Though, getting  to  it… that’s another matter. Still worse than trying to find a decent spark plug in this day and age, mind you. Everything’s computerised. Oh, leave the spark plugs alone, George. You miss the old days. Remember when you could fix anything with a bit of wire and hope? I do indeed, Margaret. And a good dose of ingenuity! Now it's all "plug it in, read the code". No skill needed. Speaking of needing things…young Ben was saying he’s putting on weight again. Don’t, Dad. Not during dinner. We’ve talked about this. It's not helpful. He's sensitive about it. He's been stressed with marking lately. Actually, I think it’s more than just stress. It’s…genetic, isn’t it? I mean, look at your side of the family. Everyone’s built like oak trees. Oh, now, don't start with that, David. It’s not genetics, it’s simply a fondness for a good pudding! My mother always said a little bit of everything is good for the soul. Though, she did have a sweet tooth, bless her. And your grandfather... well, he  lived  for a cream tea. Cream teas, alright. And bacon. Mountains of bacon. I'd wager a good bit of it comes down to what folks are eating these days – processed rubbish, all sugar and no substance. My old mate Arthur, had a bypass last year. Said the surgeon told him it was a ticking time bomb waiting to happen. That's awful. How is Arthur now? He's alright. A bit slower, mind you. Doesn’t fancy climbing under cars anymore, that’s for sure. Though, he misses it. Says it’s the only time he feels truly useful. Reminds me, I need to get a quote for Mrs. Higgins – her exhaust is rattling like a tin of marbles. You know, it's funny how people find their purpose. I find fulfillment in my research, but I can totally see the appeal of tangible work. Fixing something,  knowing  you’ve made a difference. It’s probably why I spend so much time with jigsaws.

Honestly, I’m starting to loathe Moodle. Absolutely  loathe  it. I’ve spent the last three hours trying to get the quiz function to do something vaguely resembling what I want, and it’s just…fighting me every step of the way. Three hours? Good grief, Amelia. What’s it doing now? You usually wrestle it into submission pretty quickly. Is it the random question selection again? Because I swear, that algorithm is powered by spite. It  is  the random question selection, but it’s more than that. I want to weight the questions, you know? Some are worth more than others, reflecting their complexity. And Moodle is making it feel like I’m trying to build a rocket ship out of Lego. It keeps resetting my weighting, or applying it to the wrong questions…it’s infuriating! Right, the weighting. Annoying. I had a similar issue last semester when I was setting up the formative assessment for ‘Digital Ethics’. It kept interpreting my percentages as decimals, so everything was skewed. Did you check your locale settings? Sometimes that messes things up. Locale settings… hmm. No, I haven’t. That’s actually a good shout. I’ve been poking around in the quiz settings for so long, I hadn’t thought to look at the global stuff. Let me just…  taps rapidly at laptop  Oh, you know what? You're a lifesaver. It’s set to US locale. No wonder it’s messing with the decimal points! See? I told you I’d wrestled with it before. It's a classic Moodle trap. They assume everyone’s American. It’s digital imperialism, I tell you!  laughs  Digital imperialism! That’s brilliant. Although, I suspect it’s just lazy coding. Right, changing that to UK… Okay, let’s try weighting again.  more tapping  Yes! Finally! It’s holding the weights. You are officially a Moodle wizard. Years of experience, darling. Years of battling the beast. Though, honestly, I still think Blackboard was easier to navigate. Remember those days? Simpler times. Don’t even  mention  Blackboard. The instability was a nightmare. I lived in fear of a mid-term quiz crashing halfway through. Moodle is clunky, but at least it’s usually…functional. Still, they really need to overhaul the interface. It looks like it was designed in the early 2000s. It pretty much was. And the accessibility features are… questionable, to say the least.

… honestly, I still feel like I’m operating on New York time. Woke up at 4 am needing a cup of tea and staring at the cat. She was  not  impressed. Oh, the joys of jetlag. It clings on, doesn’t it? Poor Millie. She probably thought you’d lost it. You were only gone for a week, though, right? Not  that  bad? A week that felt like a month, crammed with conferences and trying to look enthusiastic about early morning keynotes. It's the jump back that gets me. And now, on top of it, we have the 'Amateur Dramatic Society's production of  Midsummer Night’s Dream  looming. Remember we promised Aunt Carol we’d go? Oh, heavens. Yes. Aunt Carol would never let us live it down if we bailed. Though, realistically, is it going to be any good? The last ADS production I saw involved a rather ambitious attempt at a sword fight with pool noodles. Don't remind me! Still, it's the principle. And it's local, supports the community... Plus, it gets us out of the house. Speaking of getting out of the house – do you think we should start seriously discussing childcare for the little one, assuming… well, you know. Assuming everything goes to plan, yes. It’s… daunting, isn’t it? Suddenly thinking about nurseries and availability and costs. It feels like a full-time job just researching everything. It does. I was looking online last night, and the waiting lists are  insane . Some places have lists started before you even know you’re pregnant! I feel awful even  thinking  about it, like I'm fast-forwarding through something precious. I know what you mean. It's all so abstract at the moment. We’re still in that ‘hopeful’ stage, really. But we have to be practical. Especially with both of us lecturing – the university timetable is… flexible, but not  that  flexible. Exactly. And frankly, my mum’s offered, which is wonderful, but she lives in Cornwall. Beautiful for holidays, less ideal for daily childcare. Right. So, we look locally. Maybe that new one that opened up near the park? ‘Little Acorns’ – sounds idyllic, probably costs a fortune. Then there is Mrs. Higgins, she does childcare in her home. Little old lady, but several of my colleagues have sworn by her. Mrs. Higgins… sounds lovely, but a bit… isolating for the baby, maybe?

…and honestly, Karim, I’m starting to think old Manzur is deliberately stringing her along. He  says  he’s applying for the visa, sends all the right noises, but nothing ever materialises. Six months now! Poor Aisha is heartbroken. She just wants to see her sister, you know? It’s not like she's asking to move to bloody Dubai, it's just a short trip to see family in Dohuk. Aye, it’s a nightmare, that visa system. Especially for folks coming from Kurdistan. They scrutinise everything, every connection. You'd think they were expecting a secret army, not a woman going to visit her sibling. Manzur… he's a character, isn’t he? Always has been, a bit… slippery. He talks a good game, but follow-through… well. Is Aisha getting any proper advice, beyond his promises? That’s the thing. She thinks he  is  the advice. He presents himself as knowing the system inside out, because he deals with these things for work, apparently. But I’m telling you, he’s just enjoying the attention, I reckon. I’ve been nudging her to maybe speak to someone at the Kurdish Community Centre, see if they’ve got a solicitor who specialises in this sort of thing. But she’s fiercely independent, Aisha. Doesn’t like asking for help. Understandable. Pride, you know? But sometimes you  need  to swallow it. The Community Centre’s a good shout though. They’ll know the current policies, the loopholes, everything. It changes so quickly. It’s all linked, isn't it? To the oil, to the politics… everything feels interconnected these days. Remember when Libya was ‘opening up’? Everyone was optimistic. Look at it now. Don’t even start me on Libya. A complete disaster. And the fallout… it’s fueled so much of the extremism we’re seeing now, hasn’t it? That whole power vacuum. Although, even before that, you had the Wahabi influence creeping through, particularly in the Gulf and then spreading… It’s a complex beast, isn’t it? And the West just seems to stumble from one intervention to another, making things worse. It is. And it's not just the direct interventions. It's the quiet deals, the arms sales, the supporting of regimes that are… questionable, to say the least, all for the sake of energy security. It’s depressing, really. It makes you worry about the younger generation, doesn't it?

…and honestly, the rosemary really  made  it. Didn’t it, David? It just permeated the lamb. Though I do think next time I’ll give it a bit longer, just to get that lovely crisp on the outside. It was superb, actually, Sarah. Absolutely superb. You always do a fantastic roast. And yes, the rosemary was a stroke of genius. Though, I’m not complaining, it was perfectly tender as it was. Bit better than most pubs manage, I’d say. Oh, you two. Always fussing over the details. It was delicious, dear. Truly. I haven't had lamb cooked so well in… well, since my Angus made it, and that was a good many years ago now. Though he always burnt the potatoes. Always. Glad you enjoyed it, Margaret. Potatoes were a success, then? I was a little worried about the goose fat. Absolutely. Golden and fluffy. Though, you know, I still think having the television on in the dining room is a bit…distracting. Don’t you think, David? It feels very American, somehow. Now, now, Margaret. It's just a bit of background noise. I had the rugby on mute, mostly. It’s nice to have something on, isn't it? Stops the silences. Although, I will admit, it wasn't the most thrilling match. Honestly, I barely noticed it was on. We were too busy catching up. Speaking of distracting, have you tried that new fitness class, David? The HIIT one at the community centre? I nearly collapsed. No, no. I’m still recovering from walking the dog this morning! Old Winston’s getting slower, you know. He demands considerably more stopping for sniffing strategic lampposts these days. Ah, dogs. Wonderful creatures. I always had a West Highland Terrier. Fiercely independent little things. Though, trying to get them to behave in a formal dining room… That was a challenge. Winston’s a Labrador, total softie. Though he  thinks  he’s a guard dog. He barks at the postman with such ferocity, then wags his tail the moment the poor man throws him a treat. Speaking of things that are a bit of a nuisance…have you heard anything more about the landlord selling the building, Sarah? I'm starting to worry. Another landlord...the thought. Apparently, there’s a lot of interest. A developer is sniffing around, apparently. I dread to think what they’ll do. Increase the rent, no doubt.

…and honestly, me mam’s lasagne is just…a different breed, innit? Like, she puts a whole tin of chopped tomatoes  and  passata in it. Passata! Who does that? It's just…too much. Oh, you and your mam’s lasagne. It's legendary, though, isn't it? You complain, but you always have three portions. It  is  good. Very rich. I think she just… loves feeding people. My nan’s the same. Mountains of food, always. Makes you feel a bit guilty if you don't clear your plate. Aye, northern mothers, they show love through food. It's a recognised fact. Speaking of food, anyone fancy ordering a takeaway? I'm absolutely knackered after dealing with Year 7 all day. Proper little terrors, some of ‘em. Takeaway sounds good, actually. I’ve been living on biscuits and regret for the past three days. Uni applications are draining the life outta me, I swear. Still going with Manchester, then? You haven’t changed your mind? Nah, Manchester’s the one. Hopefully. Got my personal statement mostly sorted, just need to get me references chased up. Which is the stressful bit, ‘cause I feel like I’m badgering people. Who'd you ask for references? Mr. Henderson, me history teacher from sixth form, and then Mrs. Davies, the careers advisor. She actually remembered me, which was a surprise. Thought I’d been wiped from her memory after…well, everything. Henderson’s a good shout. He always seemed to rate you. You always asked the proper questions in class, the ones no one else thought of. So, no news on the flat hunt then? Still stuck at your mam’s? Still at me mam’s. It's…cozy. And free. But cozy's wearing thin, y'know? She keeps leaving passive aggressive notes about me leaving me dirty mugs about. Dirty mugs! Like I’m a barbarian. Oh, mums. They find  something . My mum’s been hinting I should start ‘considering’ a proper job instead of just “pottering about” with art. Like it’s not a legitimate thing to do. Honestly. Tell me about it. Mine's constantly asking if I've started revision. Revision for  what  exactly? Sixth form’s finished! I need a break before uni starts. You’ll get used to it. They never stop worrying, do they? It’s their job description. Have you two spoken to Liam lately? Haven’t seen him since Sarah’s birthday.

…and honestly, the buttercream was a disaster. Way too soft. It just  slid  off the biscuits. You’d have thought I’d never made a simple Victoria sponge before! Did it look like a slide, Mummy? A really big, sticky slide? It did a bit, actually, Lily. A very sugary, messy slide. That’s why I’m attempting round two  with  you both as official taste-testers. It’s for the Year 5 lesson on instructions, remember? We're making shortbread and then decorating them. Can I put  loads  of sprinkles on mine? Even the rainbow ones? Of course, Freddie! Within reason. We don’t want to create a sprinkle mountain. Though, that  does  sound rather fun, doesn’t it? Can we make little flags for them too? Like in Tomodachi Life when you decorate the apartments? Ooh, that’s a brilliant idea, Lily! We could use cocktail sticks and little bits of paper. That would be super cute. Right, ingredients. Freddie, can you get the butter out of the fridge? Lily, could you find the icing sugar? Is this it? It looks like snow! That’s the one! Perfect. While we’re baking, I need to quickly tell you about this funny thing that happened in class today. Daniel asked me if dinosaurs had birthdays. Did they get cake? I think they would have  loved  cake, yes. I explained that we don’t really know but maybe they celebrated in their own dinosaur-y way. He then asked if T-Rexes blew out candles with their tiny arms. That  would  be hard! Exactly! It was hysterical. Anyway, back to the shortbread. I also need to remember to tell Mrs. Peterson about the book I found in Morrisons. What book, Mummy? It’s called “The Boy Who Grew Dragons”. It looked lovely, full of beautiful illustrations. I think you’d really enjoy it, Lily. It was in the sale, oddly enough. I like dragons! Can we get it? We might, Freddie. I need to check with your Dad first. I also saw a fantastic book on space for you, all about planets and rockets. It’s called ‘George’s Secret Key to the Universe’ – Stephen Hawking wrote it with his son! Is it good? Is it better than Tomodachi Life? It’s very different! It’s a story, a real adventure. Tomodachi Life is fun, but this is...educational  and  exciting.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of Brenda posting that picture of her new car. It's not even a nice car, is it? It's just…beige. Utterly beige. And she's captioned it ‘Living my best life!’ Seriously? Beige is a strong word, darling. It’s… practical. And Brenda  does  love practical. Remember the sensible walking boots she wore on our hiking trip to the Lake District? Practicality and shouting about it on Facebook are two very different things, Tom. It’s performative practicality! It’s like she’s trying to convince  herself  she’s living the dream. And it's a Kia Picanto! She was moaning about her perfectly serviceable Fiat just last month. Well, maybe she finally succumbed to the marketing. They’re very good, you know. All that ‘freedom of the open road’ nonsense. Makes you want a car, even if you live in Zone 1 and the Tube is five minutes away. Speaking of cars, did you finally get that scratch on yours fixed? The one from Old Man Hemmings’ gate? Oh, don't even remind me. I did! It cost an absolute fortune. And the bloke at the body shop tried to upsell me on a full detailing package. "While we're at it, madam, we could really bring out the shine…" As if a bit of elbow grease and some Autoglym wouldn't have done the trick. It's the principle of the thing! They always do that, don't they? It's the car industry equivalent of ‘Would you like fries with that?’ It’s predatory. Exactly! It feels deliberately designed to make you feel inadequate about your perfectly functional vehicle. It’s the same with those Facebook car ads, isn’t it? Constantly showing you shiny new things you didn’t even know you needed. It is. And the targeting is… unnerving. I was looking at roof boxes the other day – just idly browsing, thinking about the ski trip – and now every other ad I see is for roof boxes, or camping equipment, or SUVs. It’s like Facebook is reading my mind. It  is  reading your mind, darling. That’s the whole point. They Hoover up all your data and then feed you back things they think you’ll buy. It's terrifying, really. I read an article about it… all the algorithms and the psychological manipulation. I try not to think about it too much.

Honestly, this is… a choice. But better than facing another hour of folding jumpers at Next, I suppose. My feet are killing me. It’s good though, isn’t it? Flint Lockwood is brilliant. And Sam Sparks is really cool. She’s, like, a total science genius. Genius who builds a machine that threatens to destroy the world with food. Bit of a mixed message, innit? Though, to be fair, the giant spaghetti and meatballs  do  look amazing. Reminds me of that Italian I had in Leamington last month. Proper good. You always talk about food. Seriously. Even when we’re watching a film about… well, food. Speaking of, do you want more popcorn? I made a massive bowl. Don't mind if I do. Thanks. You’ve gotten really good at making popcorn, you know? Though, you used to burn it  every  time. Remember that? The smoke alarm going off at Mum’s… Stop it! I was eleven! And I was experimenting. Besides,  you  were the one who suggested adding chilli flakes. A fair point, a fair point. Look, can you… wrestle the remote for a sec? I can’t figure out how to turn the volume down. It's shouting at me. This thing has more buttons than a spaceship. Seriously? You’re 23 and you can’t work a TV remote? It’s basic technology. Hey! I’m a practical man, okay? I sell clothes, I don’t navigate complex entertainment systems. It's different skills. Anyway, work was awful today. Mrs. Higgins complained that the blue jumper didn't  quite  match her eyes. Honestly. People. Oh, the drama. It’s always something with Mrs. Higgins. You should’ve told her her eyes were stunning regardless of jumper colour. Reverse psychology. Tempting, but I value my job. Slimy as it is. You still enjoying uni? What are you studying at the moment? Anything interesting? Yeah, it's good. Currently drowning in feminist literature, actually. It’s fascinating, though. Makes you think about everything differently. Like, even this film. Sam Sparks is the only female character with any agency, and even then, she's only validated by Flint. It's… frustrating. Woah, hold up. You’re reading into ‘Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs’ for feminist tropes? That’s…a level of analysis I wasn’t prepared for. I just thought it was a funny film about food falling from the sky.

…and honestly, the sheer arrogance of it all still gets to me, even now. Blair promising a 'new dawn', a 'third way'…it was all just spin, wasn't it? Remember the Stakeholder society? Utterly baffling. Felt like a marketing campaign, not a political ideology. Aye, baffling's a good word for it, Professor. Stakeholder… sounded like somethin' you'd get at the chippy, not run a country on. Though, lookin' back, things were simpler then, weren’t they? Less shoutin' on the telly, less folk gettin’ their knickers in a twist over everything. At least when it came to the footie, we knew where we stood. Simpler, perhaps. Though I’d argue the seeds of much of the current chaos were sown during that period. The erosion of trust in institutions, the widening gap... it all started to accelerate. And the football… oh, the football  was  simpler. Or at least, less… globalized. I still mourn the days when Liverpool teams were predominantly Scouse lads. That connection to the city… it meant something. Tell me about it. Now you've got millionaires from everywhere struttin’ around. Don't get me wrong, some are brilliant players, proper talents.
