We’re aiming for spooky, not traumatic. Are you still planning on being a zombie this year? Yeah! I’ve been practicing my walk. It’s harder than it looks. Got to get the arms right, all floppy and…ugh. And I told Finn he’s being a werewolf, but he’s being all difficult about the ears. Says they’re “uncool.” Teenagers. They do sprout opinions, don’t they? Reminds me of recruiting for the new programme at work. Trying to convince bright young things that researching Victorian sewage systems is…a worthwhile pursuit. It's… a challenge. Victorian sewage? Yuck. That  is  hard sell. You have no idea. It's bringing back some… memories. Actually, it's a bit ironic. My first real research grant, back at uni, involved looking at historical public health initiatives. I remember old Professor Davies being... rather dismissive of my ideas initially. Why? Well, let’s just say he was a rather…traditional academic. He didn't think a young woman – I was fresh out of my teens – had anything insightful to contribute to the field. He kept making little comments about needing to ‘leave the serious thinking to the men’. Looking back, it was blatant discrimination.

…Aye, this is proper good toast, mind. Not like that pap they try to pass off in university halls. You’ve always made a cracking breakfast, Catrin. Glad you like it, Bronwyn. It’s just the usual. Though, I did splurge on proper butter this week. Not the spreadable stuff. You deserve it, having travelled all the way up from York. So, how was the journey? No trouble on the trains? Trains were… trains. Delayed, naturally. A bloke was arguing with the conductor about a pasty. A  pasty , Catrin! On a train to Swansea! Honestly, the world’s gone mad. But I got here eventually. It's lovely to be here, though. Reminds me of when we were both stuck in Japan, trying to decipher the refuse collection schedule. Remember that? Oh,  please . Don’t remind me. Three different coloured bags for three different days! And the sheer shame of getting it wrong! We looked like right fools holding out the wrong bin liner. That was back in the day though, wasn’t it? Feels like a lifetime ago since we were navigating Osaka together. It does. Seems daft now, all that worry about rubbish. Though, speaking of rubbish, is it still the same system here? Honestly, I miss the Japanese efficiency. Everything had a place, a time… It's… evolving. They’re trying to be more environmentally conscious, so more recycling. It’s still a bit of a free-for-all sometimes, truth be told. Anyway! Enough talk of bins. You mentioned on the phone you were thinking of taking flying lessons? That’s right! Back in York, there’s a small airfield. Always fancied it, you know? Just…seeing the world from a different angle. A bit of freedom. And frankly, I’ve earned a bit of recklessness in my old age. Recklessness? You? The most organised woman I know? That  will  be a sight. Are you nervous? Terrified! Absolutely petrified. But that’s half the fun, isn’t it? Though I’m already imagining the social media posts. “Senior Lecturer Takes to the Skies!” It’d be hysterical. Though my department might have something to say about it. They’re a stuffy bunch. You should definitely document it. Think of the students! Give them something to gossip about. What about today, though? Any plans beyond consuming excellent toast? I thought we could potter around Mumbles, maybe get some ice cream?

Right, ‘quizzed’ for 27. Take  that . Honestly, I thought I was going to be late getting here today. The train was absolutely rammed, and then it stopped outside Newport for…well, no one knew  why . Just sat there for twenty minutes. Ooh, good word, Liam. Though, using all your vowels like that… risky strategy. I'm just chipping away at this with ‘axe’. Thrilling, I know. Twenty-two. You’re right about the train though, Cryws Road station is a nightmare to get to sometimes. I almost missed our Scrabble night last month because of signal failures. Twenty minutes outside Newport? Sounds like a Tuesday, to be honest. I had a delivery driver yesterday who was nearly an hour late because of sheep.  Sheep . Blocking the A40. You can't make it up. Though, twenty minutes isn’t bad compared to when I was working back home in Exeter. Old Man Hemmings, our head chef, was perpetually late. Said it was because his mum used to send him to school with a note saying he was ‘feeble’ – apparently it was a local dialect word for ‘a bit under the weather’. ‘Feeble’? That’s… fascinating. Where did that even  come  from? It sounds like something Roald Dahl would invent for a character’s ridiculous ailment. Speaking of which, has anyone else noticed how weird children’s book spellings are? Like, intentionally misspelling things to sound cute or funny. Oh god, yes! It drives me mad. It normalises bad spelling! I'm a linguist, I  should  be bothered by this! And 'feeble' is a good one, Ben. I wonder if it's related to 'frail'? It's all connected, isn't it? The history of language is amazing. You learn so much digging around. It’s the etymology module I’m enjoying the most. Properly geeky, honestly. But discovering where words originate… it’s addictive. Though sometimes it just makes me question everything. Like, why is 'colonel' pronounced 'kernel'? It makes absolutely no sense! You're doing a linguistics degree now, right Liam? I always thought you’d go into history, remembering how you’d drone on about the Tudors at A-levels. You were obsessed! Remember that essay on Henry VIII's wives? Please don't remind me. I wrote that essay three times. My history teacher, Mr. Davies, was convinced I was plagiarising, even after I explained my sources. It was a nightmare.

Lovely brew this, Patricia. Just lovely. Reminds me of me mum’s, though she always did put a dash o’ brandy in hers, the cheeky woman. Not that  I’d  encourage that at this hour, mind. Though, blast it all, a little nip does warm the bones, don't it? Oh, Arthur, you and your mum. Always a story with her. Brandy at ten in the morning! You didn’t get your mischievous streak from nowhere. And no, I don’t think a nip is necessary, not yet anyway. It’s barely past eleven. You’ll be wanting your lunch soon. Lunch, aye. Soup again, I reckon? You make a grand soup, Patricia, truly you do. Though I wouldn’t say no to a bit o’ cod and chips, if truth be told. Haven't had a proper portion in…well, feels like a month o’ Sundays. Cod and chips? Arthur, you know Dr. Peterson said about the salt. And your ankles. Remember last week when they were swelling up like balloons? No, soup it is. With a nice bit of crusty bread. I got a new recipe, parsnip and apple. It sounds a bit odd, I know, but Mrs. Higgins swore by it. Parsnip  and  apple, eh? Sounds a bit…fruity for soup, doesn't it? Still, if Mrs. Higgins says it's good… she always was a sensible woman. Did you hear about her Derek? Rumour has it he's taken up line dancing. Line dancing! At his age! Oh, don't start on Derek! He’s always been a bit of a…character. Line dancing, honestly. Good for him, I suppose, keeps him active. Though I can just see him tripping over his own feet. Speaking of active, did you manage to finish that crossword? The one in the Telegraph? You were wrestling with 17 across all morning. Wrestling is a good word for it! “Obsolete form of transport…” Seven letters. Drove me mad, it did. Tried everything. Horse and cart, steam train, even a rickshaw! Then it came to me, quite suddenly, whilst I were watching the pigeons on the roof. It was ‘Hansom’! A Hansom cab! Smart, eh? Very smart, Arthur. You've still got it. Though I suspect the pigeons gave you a clue. They've seen a few things in their time, haven't they? You spend half your day talking to those birds.

…and honestly, the rosemary really makes it. I got it from Mrs. Higgins’ garden, she had a surplus this year. It’s  so  much better than the stuff you get in the supermarket, doesn’t it, David? Mmmph. Quite. Though I still maintain a good pinch of thyme elevates lamb even further. Rosemary’s good, mind you, very good. A bit… assertive, perhaps? But the lamb is wonderful, Sarah. Truly. You’ve outdone yourself. It  is  lovely, Sarah. And it’s really nice to have a proper sit-down meal like this, isn’t it? End of the holidays always feels a bit melancholic, but a good roast certainly helps. It does, doesn’t it, Carol? Everything feels so rushed during term time. I’m already dreading the mountain of marking waiting for me. Have you finished prepping your lessons for Monday? Mostly. Got the Year 7s sorted, just need to tweak the stuff for the older ones. It’s the new curriculum changes that are the killer. Honestly, they change it so often it’s impossible to keep up! Changing things for the sake of changing things, that’s what it is. Same in management, used to be. Always a ‘restructure’ or a ‘new initiative’. Never actually  improved  anything. Waste of perfectly good time and resources, if you ask me. Dad, not everything is a conspiracy against efficiency! It’s just… educational policy. Maybe, maybe. Though I do miss the days when things were… simpler. Speaking of simpler, have either of you tried that ‘Fitbit’ app everyone’s talking about? Brenda down at the shops was going on about it. Apparently, it tells you how many steps you’ve taken, and even monitors your sleep. Oh, I’ve heard of it. My colleague, Emily, is absolutely obsessed. She's constantly comparing step counts with everyone. I think she's even started taking the long way around the school just to rack up the mileage. I downloaded it a few weeks ago. It’s actually quite motivating, in a slightly annoying way. I’m aiming for 10,000 steps a day, but some days I barely manage 5,000. Especially after a Sunday roast! Ten thousand? Good heavens. I think I manage ten thousand steps getting  to  the newspaper shop. Though, I did walk down to the village for a pint yesterday. Does that count? I think it should! It's exercise, right?

…and honestly, the sheer audacity of it! He just  assumed  because I’d mentioned reading a bit of Shakespeare for my seminar, that I was some sort of expert. Old Davies was going on about the BBC adaptation of  Henry IV  – said it was ‘utterly dreadful, a betrayal of the text!’ as if  he’d  directed it. Davies, eh? Typical. He loves to hear the sound of his own voice. Still, Shakespeare on the telly… it’s a tricky one, isn’t it? They always take liberties. Did you see the recent  Macbeth  with Ruth Negga? Visually stunning, but…well, Shakespeare probably wouldn’t have approved of the lighting choices. Exactly! It’s like they’re aiming for ‘atmospheric’ and accidentally end up with ‘confusing.’ I was trying to politely point this out to Davies, but he just launched into a ten-minute rant about the decline of dramatic standards since, oh, I don’t know, 1953? It was exhausting. How’s your course going, by the way? Still suffering through A-Level history? Suffering is a strong word. Enduring. Definitely enduring. It’s…a lot of memorising dates and battles. Though Mr. Henderson tried to liven things up today by asking us to debate whether Napoleon was a visionary or a tyrant. That was actually alright. Though Ben kept trying to argue Napoleon was secretly a benevolent dictator. Ben’s…unconventional. Sounds like Ben. Remember when he tried to convince everyone on that stag do in Bristol that he was a secret agent? Oh god,  that  stag do. Bristol was…an experience. I’m still finding glitter in strange places. Poor old Liam nearly had a breakdown trying to keep Ben under control. And the karaoke! My ears are still ringing. Seriously. I think Liam aged about ten years in 48 hours. Still, it was a good laugh, even if bits of it are a bit blurry. Speaking of blurry, have you seen anything good at the cinema lately? I was thinking of going to see that new sci-fi one,  Echo Bloom ? I haven’t! Been a bit busy with revision. Although, I did stream that documentary about competitive gaming. Absolutely bonkers. The money those guys make is insane. And the dedication! Hours and hours of practice. It’s basically a full-time job. It's mental, isn't it? My flatmate, Finn, is obsessed with  League of Legends . He spends his entire student loan on skins.

…and honestly, the presentation could have gone  so  much better. Old Mr. Henderson kept interrupting with these really detailed questions about… spreadsheets. Spreadsheets, Liv! Like I'm some kind of coding genius. It's project  coordination , not data analysis! Oh, Henderson. He’s the worst. Still stuck in the nineties, bless him. You handled it though, right? You always do. Speaking of handling things… how’s your mum doing? You mentioned she wasn’t feeling brilliant last time we spoke. She's… okay. It’s just her knees are playing up again. She’s started physio, which she  hates . Apparently, it feels like "being tortured by an enthusiastic teenager." She’s got a very dramatic flair, you know? And Dad's just enabling her, bringing her biscuits and telling her to rest. It’s a whole situation. Typical. They’re a team when it comes to avoiding anything remotely healthy. Though, biscuits are a valid coping mechanism, let’s be real. This cake is amazing, by the way. Lemon drizzle, right? Greens do the best. Definitely lemon drizzle. It’s the only reason I suggested meeting here. So, how’s life in the marketing world? Still battling to convince people that TikTok is important? You have  no  idea. I spent all morning trying to explain to Brenda – Brenda from accounts, remember her? – that a thirty-second video of a slightly quirky kitten has more impact than a full-page ad in the local paper. She just stared at me blankly. I swear, sometimes I feel like I’m speaking another language. Pearson is… traditional, shall we say? Sounds about right. It’s the same at my place. Change is scary to some people. Speaking of scary… have you heard anything from…  him ? Ugh, don’t even. No. Thankfully. Last I heard, via a mutual friend, he's… “finding himself” in Bali. Apparently, yoga and green smoothies are the answer to all life's problems. Of course they are. Honestly, the level of self-discovery he thinks he's achieving is astounding. Remember when he claimed he was a “sensitive soul” after listening to a Coldplay album? Oh god, YES! The sensitive soul! That was… peak Liam. I’m glad we both escaped that particular vortex. Seriously, though, you’re doing so well focusing on your work. It's really inspiring. You always had such a knack for keeping things organised. Thanks.

Right, milk first for me, always. Though Mam always said that’s barbaric. She was a tea purist, you know? Hot water, bag, brew,  then  milk. Never the other way around. Honestly, the drama over a cuppa… Barbarian, eh? Sounds about right for a Sunderland lass. My nan was the same, fiercely protective of her tea ritual. Though her issue wasn’t milk first, it was  how  you stirred. Apparently, you had to go up and down, not round and round, otherwise you “bruised” the leaves. Bruised the leaves! Oh, bless them. They took their tea seriously, didn’t they? It's a national obsession, isn’t it? Speaking of obsessions…look at this monstrosity. It's taken over half the windowsill. I swear it grows an inch a day. Ah, Penelope. She  is  thriving. You've got a real green thumb, you know. I’ve tried, honestly, I have. But anything beyond a cactus seems doomed in my care. What’s the secret? Is it talking to them? Mam always swore by talking to her roses. Talking helps, maybe. Honestly, I think it's just…neglect. I forget to water her for days, then drown her in guilt and a whole watering can. She seems to like the rollercoaster. Seriously though, it’s mostly about light. And not buying plants from petrol stations. That was a mistake. A valuable lesson learned. Petrol station plants…a fate worse than death, probably. I tried growing basil last summer, inspired by all those Mediterranean cooking shows. It lasted about a week. Looked sad and droopy even  before  I tried to make pesto. Oh, pesto. Don’t even get me started. I attempted it last month. A disaster. Too much garlic, not enough pine nuts, and it ended up looking like swamp goo. It tasted…aggressive. Aggressive pesto…that’s a new one. I think I'll stick to shop-bought. Speaking of cooking, how's your brother? Still attempting to recreate Mam’s roast dinners? Last I heard he’d burned the Yorkshire puddings  again . Don’t. Just…don’t. It's a running family joke now. He insists he’s “experimenting” with different temperatures. He’s experimented his way through three smoke alarms and a very angry neighbour. Honestly, he's a good lad, but cooking isn’t his forte. It's a source of endless amusement for us all though. He calls it ‘deconstructed roast’.

Honestly, Alun, this coffee is… robust, shall we say? Not quite how I like to start a Monday. How was your weekend, though? Anything less bracing than this brew? Aye, robust is a polite word for it, Gareth. Tastes like it’s been brewed since Friday. My weekend was alright, alright. Bit of gardening mostly. Trying to get the roses under control before they take over the entire back garden. They’re determined, those things. You do anything interesting? Did Cairo call? Your daughter mentioned she was hoping for a video chat. Cairo didn’t call, no. Time differences are a devil, aren’t they? It's always a fleeting moment when we do connect. I did try to tackle the garden, a bit. Mostly just staring at the weeds and lamenting my lack of a green thumb. Though, I did spend far too long watching football highlights. It's horrifying, isn’t it, seeing pictures of these players' children? Little tykes barely out of nappies, and already being hounded by agents and photographed for… what? Their potential? It feels so exploitative. Oh, it’s dreadful, that. All that pressure on them. I saw something about Wayne Rooney’s youngest, practically being scouted before he could walk. Gives me the shivers. It’s the same with snooker, actually. All those young players, pushed relentlessly by their families. Ronnie O’Sullivan’s story, you know, wasn’t exactly a fairytale upbringing. A bit of a troubled youth, despite the talent. A complicated man, O’Sullivan. Immensely talented, undeniably. But yes, a difficult start. It makes you wonder how much of that early pressure contributes to issues later in life. Speaking of pressures, have you started on the marking yet? The essays on Post-Structuralism are… challenging, to put it mildly. Don't remind me. I’ve marked a handful and I’m already feeling intellectually exhausted. They all seem to think they’re Foucault reincarnated, but can’t actually define deconstruction. It's painful. I’m putting it off as long as humanly possible. Found myself reorganizing my spice rack instead – a clear sign of avoidance tactics. A rational response, I’d say. Far more appealing than grappling with Derrida at eight in the morning. I heard young Davies is thinking of trying for the police force after he finishes his degree. A peculiar choice, given his focus on Romantic poetry. Is he now?

Honestly, this week has been  exhausting . Mr. Henderson is breathing down my neck about the quarterly reports, and honestly, I think he just enjoys making life difficult. It’s like he actively seeks out things to nitpick. Is Mr. Henderson a grumpy monster? Like the one in my storybook? He can be a bit of a grumpy monster, yes, darling. Though thankfully, he doesn’t breathe fire. Just…strongly worded emails. How’s the tower coming? Speaking of monsters, I’m pretty sure my dissertation is turning into one. I’ve hit a wall with the literature review. It’s just… endless. Oh, sweetheart. Still stuck? You’ve been at that for weeks. Want me to make you a fresh pot of tea? Maybe a biscuit? Tea would be amazing, actually. Thanks, Mum. It just feels like everyone else has brilliant, original ideas, and I'm just rehashing what's already been said. Oh no! My tower! It needs a princess! Oh, poppet. Let’s rebuild it, shall we? A princess needs a grand castle, doesn't she? We can use the sparkly blocks this time. Right, tea and biscuits for the scholar, castle building for the princess…but we still need to finalise plans for Grandma’s christening. It's only a couple of weeks away. Right, the christening. Have you managed to book the room at The George yet? I called last week, and they said they were still checking availability. I did! Just this morning. After a  very  persistent phone call. Apparently, there was a wedding enquiry, but they fell through. So, we’ve got it! The private dining room. It's perfect. Will there be cake? A really big cake with pink frosting? Absolutely, darling. A very big cake with  lots  of pink frosting. Auntie Sarah is making it, you know. She’s a whiz with icing. That’s brilliant! Sarah's cakes are legendary. We should probably send out the final invitations, then. I can do that this evening. And have we decided on godparents yet? Yes. Your Uncle David and Auntie Emily. They were thrilled when I asked. Said they’d be delighted. I think they’ve already started brainstorming gifts. Honestly, the sheer volume of miniature outfits is already astonishing. This is a present for the baby! It’s a magic wand! What a lovely present! She’ll love that. Now, about your birthday, darling?

Honestly, this weather is just  relentless . Another grey day. It's enough to make you want to hibernate until spring. Remember that disastrous camping trip to Cornwall when it rained for a week solid? Oh, don't even  mention  Cornwall! I’m still drying out the sleeping bags from that. You insisted it would be ‘character building’ for Lily. It  was  character building! I made a friend, even though we mostly played cards in the tent! And we built a fort out of wet towels! A fort of wet towels, yes. See? Resilience. Though I’ll admit, retreating to a B&B was the best decision of the trip. So, how’s work been, love? Still battling the Black Friday aftermath? You have no idea. People are still returning things! And the complaints… honestly, you’d think we personally stole Christmas. Mrs. Henderson was  furious  her discounted toaster didn't come with a bagel setting. A bagel setting! On a £15 toaster! Oh, the public. Bless them. They expect the world. Speaking of expectations... have you had a chance to look at flights for New York again? I was browsing last night and found a couple that aren't completely extortionate. I did, briefly. Everything seems to have jumped up since we last looked. It’s probably because of the school holidays. I think we need to be clever about dates. Maybe go mid-week? New York! Will there be a big Christmas tree? And shops with  all  the toys? A very big Christmas tree, darling. And shops with more toys than you can imagine. Though Mummy and I might have to impose a limit! Remember what happened with the Beanie Babies when we went to Florida? Don't remind me. We had to buy an extra suitcase just for those things! And Lily insisted on bringing  every single one  to Aunty Brenda’s wedding reception. They were fluffy! And special! They were slightly overwhelming, darling. Still, Brenda was a good sport. Though I think Uncle George ended up sitting on a pile of them all night. It was a good wedding, though, wasn’t it? Despite the Beanie Baby incident. It was beautiful. I remember being so stressed about the seating plan. You were so calm, though, just gliding around making sure everyone had a drink. You  always  excel at the social side of things. I'm more practical, running around making sure the canapés don’t run out.

…and then, right, the methodology section. This is where it gets a bit hairy, innit? Honestly, Professor Davies just  loves  to pick apart how you justify your choices. I’ve basically gone for a mixed methods approach – quantitative data from the survey, you know, the one we both helped distribute around campus, and then qualitative, stemming from the interviews. Mixed methods, yeah, sensible. Davies is a stickler for rigour. Did you at least acknowledge the limitations of using a student population for a broader study? He  will  ask that. It's his favourite question. Of course, of course! Page 17, paragraph three. I've spent half a page admitting our sample isn't representative of the entire…well, anyone really, beyond undergraduate students in Greater Manchester. I’ve flagged the potential for bias due to self-selection, the obvious issues with generalisability… I’ve covered myself! It's all right here, see? Honestly, just looking at it all makes my head spin. Yeah, looks solid enough. You’ve got the reflexivity bit in there too? He’s obsessed with that now. Something about acknowledging your own positionality and how it might impact the research. Oh, God, yeah. That was a nightmare to write. Essentially admitting I’m biased because I’m a northern lad researching perceptions of…well, everything south of Watford. I tried to frame it as having ‘insider knowledge’ but I suspect he’ll see right through that. It’s a tough one. You’ve gotta be honest but not…defeatist. Did you link it back to the historical context of the north-south divide, or did you keep it pretty focused on your own experience? I did a bit of both. I mentioned the industrial revolution, the shifting economic powers, you know, the usual. But then I also talked about growing up hearing… well, let's just say  opinions  about London and the South. It felt a bit exposing, to be honest. Like I was confessing a deep-seated prejudice. It’s good you addressed it. He'll appreciate the self-awareness. Though, knowing Davies, he'll probably ask if  your  upbringing influenced the questions you asked in the interviews. Typical. Don’t even  say  that. I've spent ages trying to formulate neutral questions. I ran them past Sarah in the statistics department, and she said they were pretty unbiased. Have I missed anything crucial? I'm really starting to doubt myself.

Honestly, I had the  strangest  dream last night. I was giving a presentation… to a room full of badgers. And they were all taking notes.      Badgers? Really? That  is  odd, even for your dream-world. Were they critical of your presentation? Prospect Research’s figures not up to badger standards?      Absolutely scathing! One particularly grumpy-looking fellow kept muttering about “lack of granular detail” and “unsound methodology.” It was mortifying. I woke up in a cold sweat.      Mummy, Mummy! Look! I drew a unicorn! It has rainbow wings!      Oh, darling, that’s beautiful! Absolutely stunning. Look at those colours. See?  That’s  constructive criticism. Not badger-based negativity.      I had a dream I was flying! Like, super-high! And I could see all of Comberton!      Wow, that sounds amazing! Better than a room full of judgmental mustelids, certainly. Did you see Mrs. Higgins’ garden from up there?      Yes! And I waved at her cat, but it didn’t wave back.      Cats never do. Speaking of things we’d all enjoy… I was thinking about the Lottery again. Just imagining what we could do if we won.      Oh, here we go. The annual ‘what if’ conversation.      It's fun! And practical planning! Seriously, if we won a significant amount - a truly life-changing amount – the first thing I’d do is finally get a dog.      A puppy?! A fluffy one?!      A fluffy one, potentially. A rescue, definitely. I’ve been looking at labs, maybe a golden retriever… something good with children.      Can it sleep in my room?      We’ll see. It would need its own space, too, you know. It's a big responsibility.      A dog… hmm. That  is  tempting. It’s just the commitment, isn’t it? And the walks. Especially in the winter.      We could share the walks! And think of the cuddles! It would be lovely for the kids, too. They've been asking for years. We  could  make it work. It's just… the money. It feels irresponsible to even consider it without some sort of financial security.      You’re right. It’s a big leap. Though, realistically, the Lottery is a far more likely outcome than me successfully presenting to a panel of discerning badgers.      I want a dog that can do tricks! Like…like roll over and play dead!      And fetch! I want a dog that can fetch really, really far!      We’ll see, loves. We'll see.

… honestly, I still can’t believe your cousin just  ran  into a glass door. A glass door, Leo! What was he even  doing ? I know, right? Apparently, he was showing off to some girls, doing a dramatic entrance, and completely misjudged the distance. Said he thought it was open. He's generally… not known for his spatial awareness. Not known? That's putting it mildly! Is it bad? Like, proper A&E bad? Because I’m imagining a spectacular faceplant and a lot of blood. He’s alright, thankfully. Mostly a really nasty gash on his forehead. They stitched him up at the hospital – A&E was a  nightmare , apparently. Four-hour wait, full of everything from sniffles to suspected broken bones. Mum was with him the whole time, naturally. Four hours! Honestly, A&E is just… a black hole of misery. I had to go after that slip on the ice last winter. Remember? Nearly broke my wrist. Three and a half hours just to be told it wasn't broken, just badly bruised. Oh god, aye, I remember. You were moaning about it for weeks. And you swore vengeance on black ice. So, how's your wrist now, incidentally? Still giving you grief when the weather changes? It's alright now, thankfully. Still a bit sensitive, especially when it's cold, but nothing like it was. But seriously, four hours… It makes you wonder how anyone with a  genuine  emergency gets seen. That's what Mum was saying. Apparently, there was a lad who'd fallen off a motorbike, and they were still waiting for a consultant to come and assess him when she left. It’s just… underfunded and overwhelmed. It’s the same story everywhere. It’s awful. And people just turn up for everything, don’t they? A paper cut, a slightly sprained ankle… it's no wonder the place is swamped. Though, I suppose, if you don’t know how serious something is, where  are  you supposed to go? Exactly. It’s a difficult one. And Cousin Mark… well, he  did  need stitches. It wasn't a paper cut. Just… spectacularly self-inflicted. Mum’s giving him grief, obviously. Oh, she will be. She's got a talent for guilt-tripping, your Mum. Remember when you crashed your dad’s car? The weeks of ‘I just don’t understand how this could  happen ’ were legendary. Don't remind me.

…and honestly, the sheer arrogance of it all! Did you see that report on the Italian Prime Minister? Declaring victory before a single vote's been counted? It's beyond belief, isn't it? Reminds me of young Timmy Hargrave claiming he’d won the school sports day  before  the sack race even began. Ah, Timmy Hargrave. Now  there’s  a name I haven’t heard in a donkey’s years. Always full of bluster, that boy. But you're right, the Italians… they do have a flair for the dramatic. Though, frankly, everything feels rather dramatic these days, doesn’t it? All this talk of escalating tensions in… well, everywhere, really. It does. It's exhausting, isn't it? You try to explain it to the sixth formers, and their eyes just glaze over. They're worried about their TikTok, and I'm attempting to elucidate the complexities of geopolitical strategy. It's a losing battle. Speaking of losing battles, how’s the antique shop doing, Arthur? Still weathering the storm? Oh, it's… ticking over. Ticking very slowly over, more like. Honestly, Bernard, I’m starting to think I need a new angle. People just aren’t buying the mahogany sideboards anymore. They want Scandinavian minimalism. Who knew? I was thinking… maybe diversifying. Diversifying? Into what, exactly? You haven't suddenly developed a burning passion for flat-pack furniture, have you? Good heavens, no! No, I was thinking… online courses. Teaching restoration. I’ve got the knowledge, the workshop… I could film lessons, put them on YouTube, build a little following. Leverage my expertise, as they say. Online courses… Hmm. That’s… actually rather clever, Arthur. You’d be good at that. You always were a patient teacher, even when you were trying to explain cricket to me. A lost cause, that was. Cricket  is  a lost cause for you, my friend. But thank you. I just feel like I need  something  new. It's all a bit… stagnant. And frankly, Mrs. Higgins keeps hinting she's going to sell her collection of porcelain dolls. She's practically my best customer! Oh dear. That  is  worrying. Old Mrs. Higgins is a treasure, and she has exquisite taste. Losing her would be a blow. This online course idea sounds much more proactive though. Have you looked into the practicalities? Website design, marketing, all that malarkey? That’s where I’m a bit stuck, to be honest.

… honestly, I’m still thinking about that shepherd’s pie Mrs. Higgins made last week. It was  divine . We should try and recreate it, though I suspect her secret ingredient is just years of practice. What are you leaning towards food-wise tonight? I’m ravenous. Shepherd’s pie sounds good, actually. Though, recreating Mrs. Higgins… ambitious. I’m thinking maybe something from that little Italian place down the road? They do a wonderful carbonara. Or, well, we could just stick to pub grub here. This place does a decent enough burger. Italian sounds lovely. It  is  chilly, though. A hearty pasta feels more appropriate for this weather. Did you catch the latest  Happy Valley ? Sarah Lancashire is just phenomenal, isn’t she? I was on the edge of my seat the entire time. I did! Absolutely gripping. Though, I’m starting to feel a bit emotionally drained by it, to be honest. It’s so bleak. But yes, Lancashire is incredible. She embodies that weary determination perfectly. Still, I need something a bit lighter after that. Perhaps less… Yorkshire. Oh, don't get me started on Yorkshire! Such a beautiful county, but everything feels perpetually grey on that show. Speaking of grey, have you noticed how surprisingly… nice this pub is? I mean, it’s a Guardhouse, you expect a bit of rough and tumble, but the stained glass is actually really rather lovely. It  is  unexpectedly charming, isn’t it? I’ve been coming here for years with work and never really paid attention to the details. It’s a bit like remembering details about university halls – you were too busy being a student to notice. Do you ever think about St. Mary’s much? St. Mary’s… sometimes. Mostly when I'm wrestling with a particularly complex transcript and feeling grateful I’m not writing essays anymore! It feels like a lifetime ago. Remember Professor Davies and his obsession with post-structuralism? How could I forget? He could talk for three hours on Derrida and still leave you more confused than when you started. Actually, speaking of lifetimes ago, are you still wearing that coat? The navy one? It's… seen better days. Hey! This coat has character! It’s warm, and it’s comfortable. And yes, it’s seen a few winters, so what? It’s a perfectly good coat. You’re just trying to distract me from the fact you’re thinking about ordering the carbonara.

…Aye, look at this one, Hamish. Took it up Glencoe last month. The light was just… unreal. Though nearly froze ma fingers off gettin’ it. Och, Glencoe never disappoints, does it? Though ‘unreal’ light usually means ‘bitterly cold’ in those parts. That  is  a cracking shot though, Alistair. The way the shadow falls on Buachaille Etive Mòr… you’ve a good eye, you do. Better than when we were scruffy students, anyway, blasting blurry pics of each other pullin’ faces. Ach, those were the days. Though I’m fairly certain  your  photos were worse than mine even then. Always fiddlin’ with the settings, never actually takin’ the picture. Still, it's a far cry from point-and-shoot these days. I’m learning all about aperture and ISO and… it's a rabbit hole, I tell ye. A  very  expensive rabbit hole. Tell me about it. I went through a phase with astrophotography. Seriously. Spent a fortune on a telescope mount that ended up gathering dust in the attic. The light pollution in Edinburgh… it’s a nightmare. You need to be properly remote to get anything decent. Where were you headed after Glencoe, by the way? Any other expeditions planned? Aye, I was thinkin’ Skye next. Maybe the Quiraing. Heard the autumn colours are somethin’ else. But I’m keepin’ an eye on the weather. It’s been proper dreich, hasn’t it? Constant rain. Makes gettin’ out a right pain, even for a hardy Scot like meself. Dreich is an understatement. We had a proper monsoon last week. Flooding down in Leith. I had three students stranded at different train stations, trying to get home. It put a real dent in my Friday. Though, admittedly, the moody weather can make for interesting photos. It’s all about knowing how to work with it. Have you tried any long exposures in the rain? I've dabbled. Got some alright shots of Arthur’s Seat shrouded in mist. It’s the gear that’s holdin’ me back, I think. The waterproof bag is alright, but the lenses… They’re needing constant wiping down. Plus, the humidity's a killer. Aye, the lenses are the worry. I've got a couple of decent filters that help protect them. And a good microfiber cloth is your best friend. Though, honestly, sometimes it’s just best to admit defeat and head to the pub.

Right, so… this week. It feels like it’s already galloping away from us, doesn't it? Did you manage to get all your lesson plans sorted for Monday? You were looking a bit frazzled on Sunday evening. Honestly, Mum, frazzled is an understatement. Year twos are… a handful, to put it mildly. Plans are  mostly  done. I’ve got the literacy covered, but the history project on castles is a nightmare. They all want to build elaborate, drawbridge-equipped fortresses out of glitter and cardboard. It’s going to be chaos. Oh, bless ‘em. Sounds… creative, at least. You’re a good teacher, though, you’ll manage. More importantly, have you had any luck with nursery places? I’m starting to panic slightly. The waiting list at Little Acorns is  ridiculous , and Mrs. Henderson at Bumblebees said they’re not taking any more applications until next term. I called both again yesterday. Still nothing. Little Acorns said they’ll put us on a cancellation list, which feels… optimistic. Bumblebees were just… Bumblebees. Mrs. Henderson is lovely, but completely unhelpful. She kept talking about the importance of early socialisation and then said she couldn’t possibly fit another little one in. It's infuriating! It is. Absolutely infuriating. I thought we started this process early enough! Honestly, it's like winning the lottery getting a decent nursery place these days. It wouldn't be so bad if I wasn’t going back to work next month. I was hoping for a smoother transition, honestly. I know, Mum. And Dad’s offered to help a couple of days, which is good, but it’s not a long-term solution. He’s already complaining his back's going. He’s seventy-three, not twenty-three! He does have a point, your father. Always has been one for a good moan. Speaking of moaning, I watched that new detective series on Tuesday,  The Shadow Line . Dreadful. All atmosphere and no plot. Such a waste of time. You wouldn’t believe the twists and turns they tried to pull off. Oh, I saw an advert for that. I’ve been meaning to start  Happy Valley , everyone at school is raving about it. Though, honestly, after a day of twenty seven seven-year-olds, the last thing I want to watch is something gritty. I need fluff. Pure, unadulterated fluff.  Happy Valley  is excellent. Very well acted.

Right, so then Mr. Henderson, bless ‘im, actually  asked  if the bunting was 'period appropriate' for a Victorian themed conference. Period appropriate! Like, it's bunting, innit? What's Victorian about a bit of triangular fabric? Sounds about right, though. Folks get proper fussy with these things. My old man used to do a bit o’ decorating, always getting stick about the shade o’ beige being “too modern” for some old lady’s parlour. Beige! Oh, the lengths people will go to for aesthetic authenticity. I had a supplier once who insisted on only using sustainably sourced, hand-dyed ribbons for a product launch. It nearly bankrupted the whole operation. It was for dog toys, Liam! Dog toys! See! It’s the same sort o’ thing. And he wouldn't even  tell  me what period he wanted it appropriate  to ! Just "Victorian." I ended up sticking with the sparkly gold, hoping for the best. It's a tech conference, not a historical reenactment. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm herding cats. How’s work been for you two? Anything more exciting than Victorian bunting debates? Nah, same old, same old. Site’s a mud bath after all this rain. Been shifting pallets all week. At least the boss brought in some bacon butties on Friday - kept us going. Met a girl, though. Down the pub after work. Oh, really? Tell us more! Is she… a pallet shifter herself? Not exactly. She’s a student, doing art. Sarah. Really nice, proper down to earth. We just chatted, you know? She’s got bright pink hair - a right stand-out, she is. Pink hair’s good! Stands out from the beige, eh Liam? I’m always a bit shy meeting people. Last date I went on… well, let’s just say he spent the entire evening talking about his stamp collection. Like, a  serious  deep dive into perforation sizes and watermarks. Oh, dear. That does sound… niche. You need someone with a bit more… sparkle. Though, to be fair, some people are genuinely passionate about stamps. Passionate about  boring  things! That’s the problem. I’d rather talk about… I don't know, anything! Literally anything. Even Victorian bunting. Speaking of which, did you see that dress on Zara the other day? Proper nice. Floral, midi length, little puff sleeves... The one you sent me a photo of? Yeah, very cute!

…and honestly, Doreen, you wouldn’t  believe  the state of the biscuits. Soft as butter, they were. Proper soggy bottoms, if you catch my drift. Never known it before, mind. Usually, Mrs. Miggins at the village shop keeps a good stock, proper crisp they are. Oh, Arthur, you and your biscuits! Always a drama. I reckon they’ve just been in the damp too long. We’ve had a spell of it, haven’t we? Though, you’re right, Mrs. Miggins usually  is  reliable. I got a pack myself last week and they were alright, bit on the short side perhaps. Speaking of reliable, has anyone tried that new Earl Grey from Fortnum & Mason? Fiona sent me a tin for Christmas. Pricey, naturally, but worth every penny. A bit more…floral than my usual, but very soothing. Oh, Fortnum & Mason! That  is  a treat, isn’t it, Bernard? I treated myself to a small tin of their Rose Congou last year. Lovely with a slice of lemon drizzle. Though, to be fair, my usual Tetley’s does the trick most days. Can’t beat a classic cup of builder’s. Builder’s? Now  there’s  a proper brew, Maggie! Though I prefer Yorkshire Tea myself. Stronger, you see. Gotta have something to cut through the… well, the general gloom these days, eh? Doreen, are you having another biscuit? Don't mind if I have one myself, despite their condition. Just the one, Arthur. I'm trying to be good. Though I must say, a biscuit  does  make all the difference. It’s just…comforting, isn’t it? Reminds me of when the children were small, always wanting a biscuit with their milk. Comfort is key, I think. That’s why I’ve stuck with tea all these years. It’s a ritual. A moment of peace. Although, teaching unruly 11-year-olds, you often needed something  stronger  than tea to get through the day! Oh, Bernard, you could always tell a story! Remember that incident with young Timothy and the glue stick? Goodness me, that was a day. A cup of tea barely touched the sides then. Glue stick, eh? Sounds like my nephew, Kevin. Always getting into mischief. Though he’s a right respectable accountant now, can you believe it? Still, I reckon he’d sneak a biscuit if he thought no one was looking. It’s in the blood, I suppose.

Honestly, this is lovely, Mum. You’ve really outdone yourself with the roasties. They’re perfectly crisp. Though, I still maintain yours are better with duck fat. Oh, don't start, Sarah! Duck fat every time is  your  mantra, not mine. These are perfectly good using vegetable oil, thank you very much. Speaking of good, Rhys, you’re barely touched your Yorkshire pudding! You usually inhale those. It’s… substantial. Good substantial. Didn’t realise Yorkshire puddings were so filling these days. Plus, I had a rather large lunch break in Cardiff – the pub was doing two-for-one on scampi. Couldn't resist. Scampi and protests, Rhys? I heard there was a bit of a kerfuffle down the Bay yesterday, something about the new development plans? Oh, that. Aye, a few of us were down there. Peaceful enough, mostly. A lot of banners, a lot of shouting about preserving green spaces. A bloke even brought a sheep, which was a highlight. Though, trying to explain to the police that the sheep wasn’t  intentionally  disrupting proceedings was… a challenge. A sheep? Seriously? That’s brilliant. Though, I suspect it wasn't entirely sanctioned. Mum, this gravy is amazing. Did you put a touch of sherry in it? Just a splash, love. It makes all the difference. Sarah, are you still on about those CRB checks for the students? You were wrestling with the online portal last I heard. Ugh, don’t even get me started. It’s a nightmare. The system keeps rejecting my forms because apparently, “Norwich High School for Girls” is an invalid institution. It existed! I  went  there! It’s just… infuriatingly bureaucratic. And then they want details about any safeguarding training… it feels like they suspect lecturers are all secret villains. It’s the times we live in, I suppose. They’re covering all bases. Remember when we were kids and a teacher being a bit strict was the worst of it? Now you practically need a security clearance. Speaking of kids…little Leo’s having his naming ceremony next month. Have you lot sorted hotels for the weekend, Ben? London's expensive. We have, thankfully. Found a reasonably priced place near King's Cross. Not swanky, but clean and convenient. It’s a good job really, I'm planning a trip to the National Portrait Gallery while we're there. Have you seen the Holbein exhibition?

…and honestly, the paella was just  sad . Like, barely any seafood, mostly just rice and a vague orange flavour. You would think, being in Spain, they’d nail paella, wouldn't you? Oh god, you’re still on about the paella? You’ve been ranting about it since you walked in the door! Welcome back to reality, though. How was the rest of the holiday? Did you at least get some sun? Sun, yes. Good paella, absolutely not. The rest was… nice? Relaxing? Honestly, I think I spent half the time comparing everything to home. And missing decent tea. Spanish "tea" is a crime against humanity. Oh, you and your tea! You’re such a Brit. I’m glad you had  some  good time though. Work was… interesting while you were gone. Old Mr. Henderson tried to convince everyone he’d invented mindfulness. No way! Henderson? Seriously? That’s amazing. Did anyone humour him? Oh, massively. Poor Sarah nearly choked trying to explain the basic principles back to him after he’d declared his method superior. It involved staring intently at a biscuit. A biscuit?! Oh, I needed to be there. How are things with… Liam, by the way? I haven’t seen a post about him in ages. Oh, Liam. We… well, we broke up. A couple of weeks before you went away, actually. Oh, no! Sarah, I’m so sorry. What happened? I thought things were going pretty well. They  seemed  to be. But it turned out he wasn’t… ready for something serious. Classic, right? Apparently, all the talk about moving in together was just him being… agreeable. He ended up hooking up with someone from his rugby team. What?! That’s awful! The rugby team? Seriously? That’s just… disrespectful. You deserve so much better. You’re amazing. I know, I know. It stung, obviously. But honestly, it was a relief in a way. It was this lingering doubt I couldn’t quite place, and now it makes sense. He's just… not the one. Well, good riddance to him, then! Come on, we’re ordering pizza tonight. Your treat for being a ridiculously good friend who listens to my paella complaints and then deals with dreadful exes. Deal. Pizza sounds amazing. Actually, fancy inviting Chloe and Ben? I could really do with a proper laugh tonight. Good idea! I’ll text them now. They were asking about you too, actually.

…and honestly, the way she talked about the new immunotherapy, it sounded… hopeful. Properly hopeful, not the ‘brave face’ hopeful she’s been doing for months. She actually  smiled  when she was describing how it works. That’s brilliant, isn’t it? Honestly, after everything, she deserves a bit of proper hope. It’s just…watching it all unfold, you feel so helpless. Remember when we first met her and Ben? That beach barbecue? She was absolutely radiating energy. God, yes. Practically bouncing. It feels like a lifetime ago. And Ben’s just…well, he’s Ben. Stoic as ever, but you can see it’s taking its toll. He barely touched his wine at dinner, which is  never  a good sign. He's putting on a strong front, I think. He’s the practical one, always has been. She's the emotional core, you know? That's why it’s so good to hear this immunotherapy is showing promise. It’s just… a massive relief. Anyway, enough gloom. We need to talk about brighter things. Like escaping this tiny flat. Right you are. Distraction therapy. Speaking of escaping, did you see that place on Mill Road? The one with the garden that backs onto the fields? The one Mrs. Higgins was talking about? Apparently, it’s just come on the market. Bit of a fixer-upper, isn’t it? She said the kitchen’s practically prehistoric. A  charming  prehistoric kitchen, apparently. But the bones are good. Plenty of space, south-facing garden. And think of the commute for both of us – ten minutes, max. No more battling the A140. Ten minutes is a luxury. My blood pressure genuinely lowers just thinking about it. But we really need to be realistic. Fixer-uppers always cost more than you think. And we’ve barely touched the savings since… well, since everything with my mum. I know. It's just...I'm starting to feel really stifled here. And I really want a study. A proper one, not just a corner of the living room. I need space to spread out my books and research. And a garden for the dog, obviously. Winston deserves a proper garden. He does. He’s a good boy. A very mud-loving good boy. Okay, let's look at numbers. What’s our upper limit, realistically? Considering we want to leave a buffer for unforeseen…Ben and Sarah-shaped emergencies, for example.

Right, honestly, I'm at the end of my tether with this lift. Absolutely at the end. Another one broken down this morning. Brenda from 304 nearly missed her hospital appointment 'cos of it. Said she had to take the stairs, nearly keeled over apparently. Honestly, what do they  do  with the maintenance budget 'round here? Tell me about it, Liam. It’s a nightmare. I’ve had three complaints already today about it. And Ms. Davies on the second floor is convinced it's deliberately sabotaged by the students. She's started leaving passive-aggressive notes on the lift doors. Sabotaged?! Oh, come  on . Though, knowing some of ‘em… Still, a bit dramatic, innit? But seriously, it's not just the lift. It’s the constant mess in the communal kitchens. I swear, they think the cleaning fairies just magically appear. Found a week-old lasagne in the microwave again last night. A  week  old! Ugh, don't even get me started on the kitchens. Honestly, it's like a biohazard zone after 8pm. And the recycling… they just chuck anything and everything in the mixed recycling. I spent a good twenty minutes this morning fishing pizza boxes out of the glass bin. They’ve no respect, they haven’t. They genuinely don't understand that someone  has  to deal with it. I had a lad yesterday, leaving a mountain of Amazon packaging right outside the fire exit. Said he didn't have room in his flat. Fire hazard, that is. Fire  hazard . I had to explain it to him. Twice. It's the entitlement, isn't it? They seem to think everything is just  done  for them. Like we're invisible. And the noise! The music blasting at 3am… I had a student knock on my door at half past two this morning, complaining about the noise  from another student’s room . Honestly, I felt like telling them to sort it out themselves. Ha! I’d have loved to. But then you get the complaints about  you  for not doing enough. It's a no-win situation. And it's not just the students, mind. It's the parents too, dropping stuff off, parking across the entrance… I had a right barney with a bloke in a Beemer yesterday. Oh, the parents are the worst sometimes. Thinking their little darling is royalty and deserves special treatment. Actually, what really grinds my gears is when they complain about the price of the accommodation and then leave everything a state.

…and honestly, the sheer  number  of Brits in Barcelona was astonishing! Like, you couldn’t swing a cat without hitting someone from Surrey. It was almost comforting, but also a bit… depressing? Like we all flee the country to find sunshine and then just recreate Blighty abroad. Depressing is a strong word, love. It’s just…natural, innit? We’re a travelling people, even if most of us only travel to places with all-inclusive deals and reliable chips. Remember when Brenda and Arthur went on that package tour of Italy? Spent the whole time complaining the pasta wasn’t like Mum’s. Oh,  please . Brenda and Arthur? They'd complain if the sun was too sunny! Though, actually, package tours aren’t always bad. My sister Doreen did one to the German Christmas markets a few years back. Said it was lovely, all cosy and mulled wine-y. Though, she did get stuck behind a gaggle of Essex ladies arguing over a nutcracker. Christmas markets sound nice, though. I was thinking of going to Antwerp this year. Apparently, they’re brilliant. Not a package tour though, definitely not. I want to actually  experience  it, you know? Not be herded around with a flag and a guide. Antwerp, eh? Proper city that. Busy though. You ever try driving in Antwerp? It's like trying to navigate a bowl of spaghetti. Worse than Brighton, and  that’s  saying something. Especially around the Churchill Square roundabout. Oh god, don't even  start  on Brighton traffic. I nearly lost my mind trying to cycle to uni yesterday. It's mental. But Antwerp… I'm trying to brush up on my Dutch, just in case. Duolingo is… helpful, I guess. Mostly it just teaches me how to say "The cat drinks milk." Bless you, trying to learn Dutch! I tried a bit of Spanish before going to Benidorm. Managed “Dos cervezas, por favor” and then relied entirely on pointing. It's good you're making the effort though. Reminds me of your Grandad, always trying to pick up the local lingo wherever he went. Utterly useless phrases, mind you. Mostly greetings and requests for the nearest toilet. He was a character, wasn't he? I miss him. It doesn’t feel right doing Christmas without him. It won't, love. It just won't. Losing your Nan and Grandad so close together… took a toll on us all.

Honestly, Mum, the whole thing with the equality vote is… confusing. Miss Davies tried to explain it in PSHE, but it just felt like a load of jargon. Something about amending the constitution? Why does amending the constitution even  need  to happen for, like, basic fairness? It's a bit more complicated than basic fairness, love, although you're right to think it  should  be basic fairness. Ireland’s constitution, the one they’re changing, used to define a family very specifically – as a husband and wife. This vote is about removing that definition, so that families can be based on other relationships too. Like, two dads, two mums, or even just a single parent. Right, okay. So, it's not like… giving everyone the right to get married if they want? I thought I heard something about that on the news. That's a separate issue, and something that  did  happen a few years ago. This is about recognising different family structures in the constitution. It’s about acknowledging that a family isn’t just one specific template. It's about making sure the law reflects how people actually  live . But why didn’t they just… change the law? Why mess with the constitution? Isn’t that, like, a really big deal? It  is  a big deal. And they  have  changed laws already. But the constitution is kind of the top law. So, to really solidify these rights and protect them in the long term, it needed to be changed. There are people who believe the constitution should be very rigid and not change with the times… and they're the ones campaigning against it. Honestly, it just sounds exhausting. All this politics. It makes my head hurt. You know what  isn’t  exhausting? Planning my birthday. Have you even thought about what we're doing? Of course I have! It’s next month, isn't it? We talked about bowling, and then maybe pizza. Unless you've suddenly decided you want a full-blown rave in the garden? A rave would be good, actually. But yeah, bowling's fine. Although, knowing my luck, I’ll end up in the gutter every time. Like I did with Liam last week. He was gloating  so  much. Liam always gloats. He's a little show-off. Speaking of embarrassing… remember when your Auntie Carol tried to do the floss at Uncle David’s wedding?

Cor, this pickle’s a right good one, ain’t it? Reminds me of old Man Hemmings down the road. Used to grow ‘em bigger than yer fist, he did. Though he weren't one for chatting, Hemmings. All business, that one. More interested in his lathe than folks, I reckon. He was a quiet soul, wasn’t he? Always tinkering. Though I never understood what he  did  with all that turning. Bowls, mostly? He made some lovely candlesticks, actually. Gave one to Mum for her birthday, years ago. Solid wood, beautifully finished. He was a master craftsman, really. More than just bowls. Though I remember him saying something about needing a specific type of tool… a skew chisel, was it? He was ever so particular about his lathe tools. Said the steel had to be just right. Skew chisel, that’s the one! He’d go on and on about the angles, the grind...sounded like another language to me. I tried me hand at it once, you know. Offered to make a little spinning top for young Timmy. Ended up with more splinters than top. Nearly took me eye out. Oh, Arthur! You and anything requiring fine motor skills… a dangerous combination! Remember when you tried to make that bird table? It listed to one side so badly, the birds refused to land on it. Well, it weren’t the bird table’s fault, it was the wood! Knotty stuff, it was. Couldn't hold a nail straight. Speaking of things refusing to land…did you ever find out what happened to Hammy? Oh, not this again… Arthur, we've talked about this. Hammy escaped. He’s probably building a little nest somewhere in the garden. Although, considering the foxes… Escaped? No, no. I tell ya, something else happened. I went to warm up me leftovers last night, put 'em in the microwave…and I swear I heard a tiny squeak. You… you put a hamster in the microwave? No! No, not  in  it! It was near it. I just… heard a squeak, that’s all. And Hammy’s gone missing. It's all connected, I'm telling ya. A suspicious squeak and a vanished hamster. Arthur, you are imagining things. You likely just misheard the microwave humming. And Hammy is a resourceful little creature. He probably found a hole in the shed. But the squeak! It sounded… scared.

… honestly, it’s just baffling. Mirror writing. Apparently, this chap was writing his shopping lists backwards and no one noticed for  years . Years, David! How do you even  begin  to not notice that? Well, you say baffling, but people are odd, aren’t they? I once worked with a bloke who organised his desk entirely by colour. Everything. Pens, files, stapler… completely unusable for anyone else. Though, I suppose worse things could happen. Did they find a reason for it? Some neurological thing? They think it might be a form of dyslexia, but he’s a fully functioning adult. It just…happens. It reminded me of that time Auntie Moira tried to decipher a cryptic crossword using a spirit board. Oh, Moira. Always a character. Though, I always suspected a little bit of trickery with that board. She was remarkably good at getting the answers  she  wanted. Speaking of trickery, have you seen what the banks are up to now? They’re practically encouraging debt with these instant loans. Disgraceful. It’s the modern world, isn’t it? Convenience at a price. Though you’re right, the APRs are criminal. Remember when we were saving for the house? It took us… what, five years? Now people are borrowing multiples of their salary. And the house prices! Don’t even get me started. Young people have no chance. We got lucky, even with that little terrace in Reading. I wouldn’t even  dream  of affording something comparable in London now. Luck plays a part, of course. But hard work too. Your generation, generally, understood the value of a bit of sacrifice. This…instant gratification culture worries me. Though, I did see a rather lovely article about a cat who saved its owner from a house fire. Apparently, it wouldn't stop meowing until someone came to investigate. Now  that’s  a news story. Much better than the American political nonsense constantly scrolling across the telly. Honestly, you'd think the world was ending every five minutes with what they're saying. It’s exhausting. Everything is so polarised. I tried explaining to my niece the complexities of the electoral college and she just looked at me like I was speaking Martian. She gets all her news from TikTok. TikTok? Good heavens. Is that one of those… moving picture things? I’m still struggling with the television remote. Though, I must admit, this new smart thermostat is surprisingly useful.

Honestly, Leo, another hour on that Ninjago game? Your eyes are square. And Maisie, don’t tell me you’re  still  building in Minecraft? It's nearly bedtime! But Mummy! I’m building a proper castle! With a secret lava moat! And glowstone lighting! It’s amazing! You have to see! Yeah, Mummy! I’m defeating Overlord! He’s  really  hard this time. He’s got, like, ten extra health points. Ten extra health points, right… Look, I appreciate the creativity, I really do. But remember that lovely book Grandma sent you both? The one about the constellations? Oh. That one. It’s… boring. There aren't any creepers in space. And no spinjitzu masters. Just… stars. Stars are pretty magnificent, you know. And that book has some beautiful illustrations. It's good for your eyes to look at something  other  than a screen for a bit. But Minecraft  is  creative! I’m an architect! I’m designing entire cities! It’s practically engineering! It  is  creative, darling, and I'm not saying it isn't. But it's different, isn't it? Reading uses a different part of your brain. It makes you imagine things yourself, instead of just seeing them already made. But in Ninjago, I have to  think  strategically! I have to choose the right ninja and their powers! It’s not just button mashing, you know. I know it’s not, sweetheart. You’re both very clever, and I'm not doubting that. It’s just... I worry you're spending so much time in these digital worlds that you’re missing out on the real one. Remember how much fun we had building that den in the garden last week? That was okay… but it rained. And there were spiders. There were indeed spiders. But we overcame the spiders! And we had hot chocolate afterwards. Real-life adventures have spiders  and  hot chocolate. Minecraft just has… pixelated spiders. But Overlord is a  serious  villain. Way scarier than a spider. He might be a scary digital villain, yes. But when you read a good story, the villain lives in your  mind . You create him, you imagine what he looks like, how he moves, what he sounds like. That's a really powerful thing, isn’t it? Hmm… I guess. But it takes ages to read a whole book. I can build a whole castle in Minecraft in, like, an hour.

Honestly, it feels  so  good to just sit. That week in Cornwall was lovely, absolutely lovely, but exhausting! All that bracing sea air and those cliff walks... my legs are still complaining. You say that every time, Mum! You love a good walk, even if you moan about it afterwards. Cornwall sounded amazing though, all those pictures you were sending. Did you actually manage to finish that book you took? Finish it? Darling, I think it gathered dust in the beach bag! There was just too much going on. Poldark’s world is quite consuming enough, without actually  being  in Cornwall. Although, the scenery did feel rather Poldark-esque at times, didn't it? Mmmhmm. Did you go to St Michael's Mount again? You raved about it last time. We did! It’s even more magical when the tide’s right in, you feel completely cut off. And the gardens are just… breathtaking. We had cream tea, naturally. Proper Cornish cream tea – jam first, of course. Don’t you dare argue with me, Chloe! Okay, okay, jam first. You and your Cornish traditions! So, what are we doing today? Anything planned, or just a lazy Sunday? I’ve got a fairly hectic week at the shop, stock take on Wednesday, so I wouldn't mind a relaxed day. I was thinking a gentle potter around Beacon Street, maybe look at that new antique shop? And then we could have a roast at The George. I haven't been for ages. Ooh, The George roast is a good shout. But… is it just the three of us? I promised Liam I'd help him with some coding this afternoon. He’s struggling with a module for uni. Oh, that’s right. Poor lad. University coding is a world away from anything I understand! Well, we can certainly adjust. Perhaps just a quick potter around the shops then, and  then  you can escape to save Liam's academic future. That sounds good. Actually, Mum, I was hoping to have a chat with you both about something. It's a bit… fiddly. Fiddly? Oh dear. What's this about? Is everything alright at work? Work’s fine, actually. It’s… well, I’m thinking about putting down a deposit on a flat. There’s one come up near the shop, which would make my commute non-existent. But it's a big commitment, and I wasn’t sure if… if you'd maybe be willing to, you know, be a guarantor?

Honestly, this meal deal from Greggs is a lifesaver. Mum packed me a banana this morning…a  banana . Like, seriously? It's freezing. You think a banana's bad? My nan tried to send me off to school with a boiled egg and soldiers. In a Tupperware container. Soldiers get  soggy , mate. Soggy soldiers are a crime against breakfast. You two are both dramatic. At least you got  something . My little brother ate my lunch. Again. Said he needed 'sustenance' for Fortnite. Sustenance! He’s eight. Savage. Right, so cards? I’m thinking a quick round of Egyptian Rat Screw before Mr. Davies spots us and confiscates everything. He’s on prefect duty today, isn’t he? The absolute worst. Yeah, Davies is a proper stickler. He actually gave Ben Carter a detention for having his laces undone. Laces! He’s like a retired army sergeant. Always talking about discipline and ‘respecting the uniform’. Honestly, what's he been doing? Was he in the TA or something? My dad says it’s because he missed out on joining the army when he was younger. Apparently he had a dodgy knee. Explains the overcompensation. And the constant lectures about maintaining standards. Remember when he sent Michael home for having slightly too long hair? Oh god, the hair incident. That was legendary. Michael looked like a tortured artist. It's just…weird, isn't it? Getting so hung up on that stuff. It’s not like long hair is going to cause World War Three. Speaking of which, did you see that thing on the news about… well, you know. Everything going on over in Ukraine? Yeah, it's awful. My mum was saying Mr. Kowalski’s family is from near Kyiv. He hasn’t been himself in class all week. It’s just…you read about it, and then you remember someone  you know  is actually affected. It makes it…real. It does. And then you get people online making awful comments. I saw this thread… honestly, people can be so awful. Saying things like… well, I won't repeat it. Just awful stuff about refugees and blaming everyone. It’s just blatant racism. It's disgusting. Actually, reminds me of old Uncle Barry. He’s always coming out with stuff that makes my mum cringe. He thinks everything’s better ‘back in his day’. Which means before anyone from anywhere else arrived.

Honestly, I think Mr. Davies is actively  trying  to make Physics impossible. Like, he enjoys watching us all struggle. Did you understand  any  of that quantum stuff today? It just… vanished over my head. Vanished is a good word. It actively dematerialised from my brain. I got as far as, like, electrons being waves  and  particles, and then… nope. Just static. He explains it like we’re all supposed to be Einstein already. Ms. Peterson, though, she makes everything click. Peterson’s amazing. She actually  cares  if we get it. Davies just… wants to show off how clever he is, doesn’t he? And then he gets annoyed when we ask questions! It's infuriating. Speaking of teachers, have you seen how weird Mrs. Ainsworth’s been lately? Our form tutor. Weird how? She always seems a bit… distant, but is she worse? Worse. Definitely worse. She keeps sighing, like the entire school is a personal burden. And she keeps staring out the window during registration. Today she just… trailed off mid-sentence about careers advice and started muttering something about needing a holiday. A really  long  holiday. Oh dear. Maybe something’s going on at home? It’s just, she always seemed so… organised, you know? Solid. This is unsettling. Remember when she got cross with Ben for humming during silent reading? Pure fury. Ha! Oh, yeah! She’s got a very specific idea of ‘silent’. It’s less silent, more ‘absolute void of all sound’. Speaking of reading, I’m stuck on ‘Great Expectations’ for English. It’s so…slow. Ugh, Dickens. He’s brilliant, obviously, but so verbose. I’m more of a contemporary fiction person, you know? Something that doesn’t take three chapters to describe a hat. Exactly! Although, Miss Roberts is trying to get us to appreciate the  language . She keeps saying it’s ‘richly textured’. I just see a lot of commas. Did you hear about Liam getting detention for… filming a TikTok in the science lab? No way! Honestly, Liam. What was he even filming? Some sort of exploding volcano recreation gone wrong? Apparently, it was a slow-motion video of him dropping a textbook. He said it was ‘art’. Mr. Davis was  not  amused. He gave him a week’s worth of extra equations. Serves him right, really. Totally. Although, a slow-motion textbook drop  is  kind of amusing to imagine. It's just a terrible place to film it.

…and honestly, the library was  dead . I thought, being almost exam time, it’d be rammed. Just five people, nursing coffees, looking utterly defeated. Felt a bit mean even being there, cracking on with my dissertation. You and your dissertation, Leo. You’ve been ‘cracking on’ with it for about six months now. When is this mythical thing actually  due ? It's almost June! Harsh, Millie, harsh. Two weeks. Two weeks and freedom. Then…Transylvania. Remember? Transylvania! Oh, I'm excited for you two. Is Ben still up for coming? He was a bit on the fence last time we spoke. He is! He booked his flights last week. He was worried about time off work, but he managed it. He's proper buzzing, apparently. Wants to learn loads about the folklore. Folklore, eh? Sounds…spooky. You lot going full Dracula tourist? I've always wanted to go to Romania, but I’m picturing myself getting chased by bats. Hopefully not  chased ! More… respectfully observing. We’re doing a guided tour of Bran Castle, obviously. And some hiking in the Carpathian Mountains. Millie's already planned a detailed itinerary - naturally. It wouldn't do to just  wander  around Transylvania, would it? Trust me, I've researched reputable tour guides. You wouldn’t want to end up getting lost in a forest with questionable wildlife. You sound like my nan, Millie! But yeah, sensible. So, aside from Eastern European adventures, what are everyone’s summer plans looking like? I was thinking of doing a little revamp of the café, maybe get some new seating. I’m hoping to get back home to see my family, haven’t seen ‘em in ages. Probably just chill out, go surfing…you know, the usual Aussie stuff. Actually, speaking of home… you guys ever hear me say “chuck a U-ey”? A…what now? Chuck a U-ey! It means to do a U-turn. Like, when you’re driving and you realise you’ve missed your turn, you chuck a U-ey. It's pretty common back home. That's adorable. Sounds like something out of a cartoon. It's cute! We should adopt it. "Oh, I need to chuck a U-ey back to the till!" I can see that catching on. So, weekend plans? Anyone got anything exciting lined up? I'm free. Desperately free, considering my dissertation is basically my only companion right now.

…and honestly, the playlist is the biggest stress. Little Mix is a  must , obviously, but then what? Leo keeps requesting that… that pirate song. You know the one? Drives me absolutely round the bend. Arrr, matey! The one with the parrots? It’s a good song, Mummy! It’s  amazing ! Can we play it five times at the party? Please? Five times is…ambitious, darling. Maybe twice. We need a bit of variety. I was thinking some Dua Lipa, maybe a little bit of Harry Styles… are those okay? It has to be party appropriate, though. No questionable lyrics. Remember Uncle David's face last year when that song came on? Uncle David went red! It was funny! It wasn’t funny for  him , sweetheart. He’s very proper. Right, so music is a work in progress. What about photos? I was thinking we could try and recreate some of those old family photos, you know, the ones of us when we were little? Like the one where you were dressed as Alice in Wonderland? With the giant mushroom? That’s the one! Though I think finding a giant mushroom in Comberton in November might be a challenge. Still, we could get a prop. Or maybe do a new photoshoot altogether? Something… less themed, perhaps? I want to be the Queen of Hearts! And shout “Off with their heads!” Maybe not the Queen of Hearts. We don't want to encourage that. Perhaps a princess? Or a fairy? I’ve got that sparkly dress you love. I want to be a knight! With a proper sword! Not a plastic one. A proper sword is…definitely out of the question. A wooden one, maybe? We'll see. We also need to get some decent family photos taken  at  the party. I'm hoping Auntie Carol will bring her fancy camera. She's quite good. Are we having cake? A big one? With sprinkles? Of  course  we're having cake! A massive one, covered in sprinkles. And crisps, and sandwiches, and… all the good stuff. Are you both hungry now just talking about it? A little bit. Can we have an apple? Absolutely. Just let me finish sorting through this music. Oh, and remember Sarah mentioned she’s attempting the aerial hoop again? The spinny thing? She's really good at it! She is. Though I think she nearly took out the Christmas lights last time.

Cor, this is a good ‘un, this. Proper good. Margherita, is it? Not too much tomato sauce, bless ‘em. Mind you, I remember when pizza weren’t really a thing ‘round here. Just fish and chips, mostly. And eels, if you were feeling fancy. Eels, Arthur? You  always  bring it back to the eels. Honestly. It’s a wonder you didn’t open an eel pie shop, considering how often you talk about them. Though, you're right about the pizza. It  is  good. Better than that cardboard they call pizza at the school fetes. They certainly seem to be enjoying it. And the chocolate roulade looks lethal. In a good way, of course. How were the results, Lily? Any celebrations needed? Okay, I guess. Got a 7 in History, which Mrs. Davies said was good, but I wanted an 8. And an 6 in Maths. I’m just… annoyed. Same! I got a 6 in English Lit. A SIX! Mr. Harrison practically lectured me for an hour about ‘potential unrealized’. It’s so unfair! They put so much pressure on us. Pressure, eh? There’s always been pressure, love. When I were your age, it weren’t about grades, it were about gettin’ a job down the factory. Least yer’ve got choices. Albeit, a lot o’ fancy book learnin’ to sort through first. Your grandfather's right, dear. It  feels  bigger now, with university applications and everything, but it’s just a different kind of pressure. Remember my parents’ evening? Mrs. Peterson went on and on about my artistic flair, but said I “lacked focus.” Apparently, drawing horses in the margins of my geography notes wasn't conducive to learning about the Amazon rainforest. Oh, I can see that! Though a well-drawn horse… it’s a talent! Speaking of talents, Lily, you were telling me you started driving lessons? How’s that going? It’s… terrifying. Mr. Henderson is nice, but he keeps saying I need to be more “assertive” at roundabouts. I just freeze! I nearly caused a pile-up on the A47 last week. No way! Was everyone okay? Yeah, thankfully. But I felt awful. I think I’m going to stick to public transport. Assertive, eh? That's a fancy word for "pushin' in". Back in my day, you just gave ‘em a little toot on the horn and that sorted it. Not that I ever did, mind.

Oh, that felt good. Took him completely by surprise, didn't it? Though, honestly, I think you let me win that one, didn’t you, love? You’ve been awfully quiet. No, Mum, genuinely a good move. You’re getting the hang of it. Though… strategic silence  is  part of the game, you know. It unnerves the opponent. Learned that much from Dad here. He’s a master of the eyebrow raise. Don’t listen to him, Doreen. He's just trying to butter you up so you'll give him first dibs on the raspberries later. They’re looking absolutely magnificent this year, by the way. Best crop we’ve had in ages, despite the funny weather. One minute scorching, the next torrential rain. They  are  lovely, aren’t they? I was thinking of making a crumble with them. Though, I’m still slightly traumatised by the beans last night. Didn’t quite hit the spot, did they? A bit… watery. They were… serviceable. Perhaps a touch overcooked. Though, you can’t win ‘em all, eh? Speaking of things not quite hitting the spot, I had a rather frustrating Zoom call this morning. One of my students in South Korea keeps disconnecting. It’s impossible to get through a lesson! And then trying to explain the nuances of the past perfect continuous to someone who’s never encountered the concept… it’s a linguistic battle. South Korea, eh? Seems a long way to go to learn English. Back in my day, it was all about French and German. Though I did meet a chap at work once who’d lived in New Zealand for a bit. Said it was paradise. Wonder if they have Chinese chess there? Everything has Chinese chess, Arthur, eventually. It’s a universal game! Although, I watched a bit of that Winston Churchill series last night. Fascinating, but truly harrowing. Imagine the pressures he was under. Completely different world. Did you know he liked painting? That’s right. A bit of a hobbyist. Reminds me, I need to get back to marking those essays on  Hamlet . Honestly, analysing Shakespeare feels less stressful than troubleshooting tech issues half the time. They’re all obsessed with the themes of betrayal, which, to be fair, is pretty relevant even now. Shakespeare. Never could get my head around it. Preferred a good war story myself. Speaking of stressful, I’ve got a dentist appointment next week.
