Ah, that was a grand dinner, Mary. Though little Fionn here tried to decorate himself with the carrots again, didn’t you, lad? More! Carrot face! Honestly, Liam, he's a whirlwind. A very cute whirlwind, but a whirlwind nonetheless. How was your day, darling? Anything exciting happen at school? It was alright. We started a new game in computing, kinda like…building a city, but with code. It’s really hard though. Mr. Davies expects us to already know loads of stuff about algorithms. Algorithms, is it? Jaysus, that sounds complicated. Different world to what I was doing at your age. We were mostly just trying to avoid getting detention from Old Man Hemmings. He had a face like a slapped bass. Liam! Don't scare the boy with tales of tyrannical teachers. It's a new school, a new experience. Focus on the city building, that sounds fascinating. So, what sort of things do you  have  to build in this city? Well, like roads and houses and stuff, but you have to write the instructions for everything. Like, if a car goes this way, then do this. And if it hits something, then… it’s a mess. Keeps crashing. It’s frustrating. Sounds like debugging code is a bit like herding cats, eh? Trying to get everything to do exactly what you want. I know the feeling, dealing with servers all day. Though usually, the cats are virtual. Speaking of messes, look at this. He’s decided Rex needs a snack. Did you have a good walk with him earlier, Liam? He was a bit restless this morning. We did. Up to the Regional Park. He loved chasing the pigeons. Near broke my heart when he realised he couldn't actually  catch  one. Started roaring the place down. Good exercise for me, though, dodging a toddler determined to apprehend airborne wildlife. Pigeons are pretty dumb. Easy to catch, I reckon. Oh, are they now? You try it, then. They’re deceptively quick. And, well, they’ve lived with humans for thousands of years. They’ve learned a thing or two about evasion. He has a point. They are quite clever, in their own way. Liam, you were saying the park was busy? I haven't been up there in ages. It was fairly packed. Lots of families, folk walking the dogs. I saw Mrs. O’Malley, you remember her, with her little yappy poodle?

…Honestly, Marjorie, this mince pie is alright. Not quite like me mother used to make, mind. She put a secret ingredient in, she did. Never told a soul. Probably brandy. Oh, Arthur, you and your mother. Everything was better in the ‘good old days’, wasn’t it? I thought  my  mince pies were pretty decent this year, though. Bit more fruit than most, I reckon. They are lovely, Marjorie. Really good. Though, honestly, after the journey… I’m just glad to be sitting down. Norwich traffic was… spirited, shall we say? Ten minutes to get from the A47 onto the ring road! Tell me about it, Mr. Davies. It's always like that. Especially around Christmas. Everyone seems to forget how to drive. Yeah, like, they suddenly think indicators are optional extras! Optional extras! Hah! That’s a good one, young ‘un. Back in my day… we had hand signals! And we were grateful for ‘em too! No fancy electric blinkers then. Just a good arm out the window. Oh, Arthur, don’t start on the “back in my day” stories. They’ve heard them all. So, Chloe, how's the art project going? The one with the… horses, was it? It's okay. It's harder than I thought. Getting the muscles right is really difficult, and making them look like they're  moving . I keep messing it up. Well, anatomical drawing is notoriously challenging. Don’t be discouraged. The key is breaking it down into simpler shapes first. I’ve got a few books on it at school if you’d like to borrow them. She's brilliant at horses, honestly. She spends hours sketching them down at the stables. Good for her. Better than staring at them blooming screens all day, I say. Though, I must admit, I do enjoy a bit of  Antiques Roadshow  myself. You never know what treasures people are hiding. Reminds me, I need to get the car serviced. Been putting it off something fierce. Arthur! You said that last Christmas! The car’s practically antique itself! It’ll likely cost more to service than it's worth. Don't be daft, Marjorie. It’s a solid motor! A bit temperamental, perhaps. But solid. Besides, I need it for the Boxing Day sales. Gotta get a bargain! Speaking of bargains, how's young Daniel getting on, Chloe? Still raiding your sweet stash? Um, yeah.

…and honestly, the state of the night shift is just  dire . We’re down two nurses again, and old Mrs. Higgins nearly took a tumble trying to get to the loo – nobody had time to help her properly because we were all running around like headless chickens. It’s just not fair on the patients, is it? Sounds awful, love. You always take on too much, though, don’t you? You’re a proper grafter, you are. Are they even  trying  to recruit? Management are just letting things get worse and worse. Seriously! I saw a post on LinkedIn just yesterday - another hospital in Essex is offering a fifteen-thousand-pound golden hello just to get nurses in. Fifteen  thousand ! What does that say about the state of the NHS, eh? It says they've left it far too late, that's what it says. And realistically, fifteen thousand is just a plaster on a much bigger wound, isn't it? People are leaving because of the stress, the workload, and the feeling of being utterly undervalued. Still, I did manage to sneak a cuppa and a biscuit with Brenda on my break. She’s turning seventy next week. Ah, Brenda! Lovely woman. Did you remember to get her a card? I know she always sends you a little something. I did, actually. And I got her one of those little tins of shortbread she loves. It’s nothing fancy, but she’s not one for fuss. Speaking of birthdays…have you two forgotten mine’s coming up? Forgotten? No way! We've been dropping hints for weeks, hoping you'd guess! It’s the 23rd, isn’t it? The 23rd. And we’ve got something…well,  I’ve  got something planned. It's a bit of a surprise, so don’t pry. Though, your sister gave me a bit of a telling off for not asking what you actually  want . Apparently, you’re impossible to buy for. Oh, don’t listen to Carol! She always says that. Honestly, I’m happy with anything thoughtful. Although...a weekend away somewhere peaceful would be lovely. Somewhere with a pub and a nice walk. No hospitals allowed. A weekend away sounds good! We could look at the New Forest. I was reading an article about it - apparently, they’ve got some amazing little villages and loads of ponies roaming around. I could write copy for their tourism board, honestly.

…Honestly, this is the life, innit? Peaceful as you like. Though a bit chilly still, even with the blanket ‘round me knees. Remember when we used to ‘ave power cuts that lasted days? Proper hardship that was. No telly, no electric fire… just candles and a good book if you were lucky. Oh, don't  start  on the power cuts, Arthur. They weren’t hardship, they were an inconvenience! And you always had a book, didn’t you? Always buried in a history of… well, something obscure really. I was more concerned about keeping the children warm. No electric blankets then, you know. Just hot water bottles and layers. You two. Always bickering like an old married couple, even after all these years. Though, I must confess, those power cuts  were  a bit of a trial. Trying to run the business on a generator? Nightmare. Kept tripping the thing. Speaking of trials, did you see that article about Big Brother bringing the show back? Honestly! It's unbelievable. The original was… well, surprisingly gripping. But now? It feels so… manufactured. Big Brother? Bah! Waste of time. Give me a good documentary any day. Something about the Romans, maybe. Or the Norfolk Broads. Now  there’s  a bit of history, that is. Though I doubt they’d make a documentary about Costessey, not much happens there. Don't be so self-deprecating, Arthur! Costessey is lovely. Peaceful. Though I do miss Harrow sometimes, you know. The shops... the bustle. I went with Margaret last week, just for a bit of a potter. Found a lovely scarf, though. Bright red. Thought it suited me. Good for you, dear. You deserve a little treat. I was thinking, we should have a small gathering soon. Nothing grand, just the four of us. Perhaps next Saturday? I can order in some nice food. Remember Doris and her… well, her penchant for those little sausage rolls? She'd eat a mountain of them. A gathering sounds lovely, Charles. Though last time Doris was here she was hinting rather strongly that her gardener, young Peter, was much more than just a gardener. Very subtle, Doris isn’t. Mistresses, eh? Always a bit of trouble, that is. Old Man Hemmings down the pub used to be forever chasing after someone. Ended up leaving his wife for a woman who ran the sweet shop. Didn’t last, of course. She wanted a bit more excitement, I heard.

Right, I think this curry’s actually gonna be edible. Took me ages to find decent mango chutney down here, everything’s all…posh. Doncaster does a good chutney, you know? Proper stuff. Not this artisan, small-batch nonsense. Don't start on the chutney, Liv. Cambridge is lovely, but it  is  a bit… curated. Everything’s got a story and a price tag. Still, better than being stuck in Lewisham, honestly. Mum was driving me mad wanting me to move back in after my Masters. “Such a waste of a good degree, staying up North!” she said. As if. Oh, mothers. Mine’s the same. Always hinting I should come “home” and settle down with a nice lad who works at the power station. As if there’s a queue of power station workers lining up for a conference coordinator! Though, to be fair, it  is  steady work, innit? Still, I like me job. Gets me about, you know? Last week I was in bloody Scarborough, this week it's Cambridge for your birthday weekend. Scarborough! Oh god, didn’t you hate Scarborough? You were texting me saying it was like stepping back into the nineteen fifties. It was! Honestly, all beige cardigans and penny arcades. But the venue was alright and the client was sound. Anyway, what are we watching tonight? You said you had a list? I’m happy with anything, really. Just need something brain-off after the day I’ve had. Dealing with a bridezilla who wants a full-scale medieval banquet in a car park…it's been a day. I was thinking… we could finally watch ‘Past Lives’? I’ve heard amazing things, and it’s been on my list  forever . But I’m also open to something completely silly. I did download that awful rom-com you recommended, the one with the talking dog? ‘Marley & Me’! Awful? It’s a classic! It’ll make you weep buckets. Seriously, have tissues ready. But ‘Past Lives’ sounds good too. I’ve seen it getting a lot of buzz. It’s that Korean-American one, right? Yeah, exactly. It's supposed to be really beautifully shot and, like, genuinely moving. Not just manufactured weepiness like… well, like most films. Speaking of family, have you spoken to your nan recently? I was thinking of giving her a ring tomorrow. She always asks after you. I did, actually, just last week.

…Honestly, it's all kicking off again, isn’t it? This talk of another referendum. Makes you wonder if they’ll  ever  settle it up there. Yeah, I saw something about it on TikTok. Loads of people are arguing. Seems… messy. Is it definitely happening then, Gran? Well, not  definitely . Nicola Sturgeon’s pushing for it, wanting a legal one this time, but Westminster’s saying it’s not the right time, that sort of thing. It’s a right pickle, it is. Remember the last one? 2014? You were just a little lad then. Vaguely. I remember Mum and Dad arguing about it a bit. And there being lots of Saltires everywhere when we went to Edinburgh. Aye, that’s right. Saltires galore. I was marking GCSE papers that year, ironically enough. All these kids having to write about percentages and statistics, and the country was deciding its future by percentages! It felt a bit… surreal, you know? So what was the first referendum  about  exactly? Like, why did they want to leave? Oh, loads of reasons. A lot of it goes back a long way. Historically, Scotland’s got a very different identity, different legal system, different church… They felt overlooked, underfunded, that England was always making decisions  for  them, not  with  them. Then there was the North Sea oil, and arguments about who got what from that. Oil? I thought that was all finished. Not finished, no. Still significant, though not what it was. And then more recently, Brexit played a huge part. Scotland voted overwhelmingly to remain in the EU, and felt dragged out against their will. That’s really fueled this desire for independence again. So, they want to rejoin the EU if they become independent? Most of them do, yes. That's the main argument now, I think. They reckon they'd be better off closer to Europe than tied to England. Although, rejoinin’ wouldn't be simple. They’d have to apply, meet criteria… it's not a quick process. It sounds really complicated. Why can’t they just have another vote and get it sorted? That’s what  they  want, lad. But the UK government says it needs to be a “legal” referendum – meaning one that Westminster agrees to. Sturgeon wants to hold one anyway, using the powers they have in Scotland, but it’s likely to be challenged in the courts. It’s a proper constitutional battle.

Oh, love a duck! Did you  see  what Sharon just accused Dave of? Honestly, this is peak daytime telly, isn't it? But I still can't believe people willingly go on this show. Willing, maybe not. Desperate, definitely. And honestly, the way they all talk... it's a linguist’s dream and a nightmare all rolled into one. Listen to ‘em, dropping their ‘h’s like confetti. It’s more than the ‘h’ dropping, innit? It's the whole… syntax. They just flatten everything. It's almost like a different language sometimes. And the elision! "Gonna," "wanna," it’s constant. You lot are proper analysing it now, aren't ya? It’s just folks being… folks. Though, yeah, me grandma would have a fit at the grammar. She was proper strict about that. Everything had to be “correct.” She’d be saying, “Don’t you  dare  say ‘innit’!” She sounds terrifying. Though, she’d probably have a point. I reckon the way people speak on this show is partially why they’re  on  the show, you know? It’s a whole performance. They're playing up everything. Aye, it's a performance. But it's a fascinating one. I’m trying to work out where everyone’s from. That bloke, with the bleached hair, he’s got a definite Scouse twang, hasn't he? Though a right butchered one. Not proper Liverpool. Oh, I heard it. He's trying, bless ‘im. Probably spent all his life tryin' to sound harder. You can always tell the ones who've moved away and are trying to hold onto it. It sounds… strained. Like they're pulling at it. Ours is proper smooth, isn’t it? It is. It’s the nasal tones. And the way we pronounce our vowels. It’s subtle, but it’s there. Though, even  within  Liverpool, you get differences, don't you? Depends on what part you're from. Yorkshire accents are mad, though. You've got like ten different variations within fifty miles. Doncaster sounds completely different to Wakefield, even though they’re not that far apart. You two, being from Wakefield, don’t you have that… flatter tone? We do  not  have a flat tone! It's… grounded. Solid. It's a proper working-class accent. It’s not all frills and fancies like some. Ooh, now you’re getting territorial. Honestly, it's the vowels that give it away.

Honestly, the offside rule is a  nightmare  this season. Even with VAR, they still manage to mess it up. Look at that! Absolutely not offside, is he? Aye, it's a bit dodgy, innit? They're getting so picky. It’s killing the flow of the game. Though, to be fair, I've stopped trying to  understand  the nuances. It’s just easier to shout at the telly. How’s the scarf coming along, by the way? Still aiming for Christmas? Christmas is looking…ambitious. I keep getting distracted. Or, more accurately, distracted by thinking about baby names again. It's a rabbit hole, I tell you. A  rabbit hole . I was on a forum last night until 2 AM. Oh, here we go. Still on the 'Arthur' train then? I thought we’d agreed that was a bit…much? No! Not Arthur. Although, it  is  a good name. I was looking at more obscure ones. I found one – Elowen. E-L-O-W-E-N. Cornish. Means ‘elm tree’. Elowen? Right. Sounds…very woodland fairy. A bit different. Will it get butchered though? People always mispronounce things. I can just see Uncle Barry yelling "Hello-ween!" across a garden. Don't even  say  that. That's exactly my worry! It needs to be pretty, but practical. And not something that’ll inspire a lifetime of nickname torment. It’s harder than choosing a research methodology, honestly. Ha! That’s saying something. Speaking of research, how's the Olympic legacy project going? Still buried in council reports? Awful. Absolutely awful. It’s all interviews and data analysis. Turns out ‘positive legacy’ is a very subjective concept when you’re asking people who had their houses demolished to make way for a velodrome. Ouch. That’s…rough. Remind me again why you signed up for that? I thought you were more of a ‘theory’ person than a ‘grassroots impact assessment’ person. Good money, mostly. And it  is  interesting, in a depressing sort of way. It’s just… exhausting. Makes me want to just knit full-time, actually. Though, if I did that, I’d probably end up naming all my creations after obscure footballers. Now  that  would be a sight. You, running a tiny Etsy shop selling ‘Wayne Rooney’ tea cosies. Don't knock it 'til you try it. Actually, did you see that goal Shearer scored against Barcelona back in '97? Pure class.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of Barry B. Benson, suing the human race! It’s just…inspired. Though I do feel a bit bad for the honey farmers, don’t you? He was a brave bee! He saved all the bees! Did he sting anyone? Bees sting, right? Well, yes, sometimes they do, darling. But Barry was a very special bee. He didn’t want to sting people, he wanted to talk to them. It’s a bit like… King Arthur. He didn’t just go around bossing people about, did he? He tried to be fair. King Arthur had a sword! A sparkly one! Can  I  have a sparkly sword? Maybe for your birthday, we’ll see. But King Arthur’s sword wasn’t just sparkly, it was… important. It showed he was chosen. Which got me thinking… all this royal stuff. We pay to go and look at where they live, you know? Windsor Castle, Buckingham Palace… Mummy, we went to Buckingham Palace! And saw the guards! They didn’t  move ! They didn’t, did they? And we paid a fortune to walk around it! It feels a bit… odd, doesn’t it? Paying to see where someone  lives  just because their family has been doing it for centuries. Why do they live in a castle? Well, historically, castles were for protection. But now… it's more about tradition, I suppose. It makes you wonder about becoming a Republic, doesn’t it? No King or Queen, just… a president or something. I want to be a Queen! I’d wear a crown! And I’d be a knight! With a sparkly sword! You’d both be very good at it. Though being a politician isn’t all crowns and sparkly swords, and I definitely wouldn't fancy  that . Too much arguing! Remember Aunt Millie telling us about the time she met a Lord at a fruit festival? Apparently, he was obsessed with Royal Gala apples. Said they were ‘fit for a King’. Royal  fruit ? That’s silly! It is, isn't it? All the fruit is good! Speaking of good… did you take your vitamins this morning? I forgot! I did! It tasted like dinosaurs! Good boy! Right, vitamins done. Anyone excited about the diving at the Olympic Stadium next week? The  water  park? Not exactly a water park, darling. It's proper Olympic diving. They jump from really high boards and do flips and twists.

Oh, that’s better. Honestly, all that dust at the tip… brings it all back, you know? Used to go with your father, years ago. Always something someone’d dumped – a perfectly good chair, once! He tried to rescue it, naturally. Your father and his ‘rescues’. I remember him bringing home that chipped porcelain doll. Said it had ‘character’. Scared the life out of young Thomas, didn’t it? It  did . It stared at me. Literally. And it smelled of…old people. He had a point about character, though. Everything’s so disposable now. It's a waste. Speaking of waste, did you manage to sort through all those boxes in the attic, Mum? The ones we talked about before coming here? Oh, don't even  mention  the attic. It’s a horrifying archaeological dig. Found Grandfather’s prayer book, which I didn’t even know existed. All in Latin, naturally. And a box full of photographs… Honestly, faces I don't recognise at all. Is that Aunt Mildred in a bathing costume? Goodness me. Mildred in a bathing costume! That's a sight I’d pay good money to see. She was so…reserved. It's amazing what turns up. We’re having a similar clear out at school, getting rid of old textbooks. Most of them are ancient history, quite literally! Ancient history is boring. Is Thirsk market on this weekend? I need a new phone case. Mine’s cracked again. Thirsk? What’s in Thirsk, other than a slightly disappointing racecourse? They've got that phone case stall, and that sweet shop does amazing fudge. And sometimes there's a guy doing magic tricks. Better than being stuck inside. Thirsk… reminds me of my childhood summers. Your grandfather used to take me to the agricultural show. Such a spectacle! All the prize-winning sheep and enormous vegetables. And the smell! A peculiar blend of manure and candy floss. You've got a fantastic memory, you know. I can barely remember what I had for breakfast. Although, speaking of smells, someone was having a hen do last night. The music was pumping until all hours. Thought the windows were going to shatter. Stag or hen, it’s always the same. Loud music, questionable outfits… I saw one lot last week dressed as bananas. Bananas! Sounds epic! Can you imagine, being dressed as a banana? It doesn’t sound very dignified.

Right, so the Tate Liverpool’s doing that new pop art exhibition, yeah? I was thinkin’ we could go Saturday. Unless you've got plans with Sarah or somethin'? No, no plans with Sarah. Though, honestly, battling for a parking space around Albert Dock on a Saturday…it’s enough to put anyone off. Remember last time? We circled for forty minutes! I nearly lost the will to live. Aye, a right nightmare that was. Maybe we could get the train? It’s not ideal luggin’ coffees and stuff, but it’d save a fortune and a lot of stress. Speaking of stress, how did your interview go yesterday? The Masters one? You were looking proper nervous all day. It was…okay. Honestly, I think I bumbled through a lot of it. The questions were tougher than I expected, particularly the ethical considerations around clinical psychology. They really grilled me about confidentiality. And then Professor Davies kept mentioning funding… which, let’s be real, is just code for ‘can your parents afford this?’ Don’t even worry about that, love. You're brilliant. They’d be daft not to want you. And about the funding, honestly, there are scholarships and loans. We’ll figure it out. It’s just…a big step, isn’t it? A full Masters? It is. It would mean a pay cut for a couple of years, obviously. And… well, it brings up the whole 'where are we going' conversation again. Aye. That. I was thinkin’ about it again this morning, actually. Old Mrs. Higgins next door is sellin’ up. Her house is a bit bigger, got a little garden. It's definitely more space for… future possibilities. Future possibilities involving…a miniature schnauzer, I presume? You’ve been researching breeds non-stop for weeks. Guilty as charged. Imagine, a little dog, a proper garden… and a dedicated room for me to mark essays! No more livin’ room table chaos. It'd be good, wouldn't it? Though it would mean more money worries. Buying a place, even a small one… It's a huge commitment. And it's not just the mortgage. Think about council tax, utilities... then there’s Christmas coming up. Your mum already started hinting about wanting a fancy new kettle. Don’t remind me! She pretends she doesn’t need anything, then produces a shopping list the length of my arm. Last year it was a pressure cooker!

… honestly, I just don’t  get  the hype around this new Harry Styles album. Everyone's losing their minds, and it's… fine. Just fine. It all sounds a bit samey to me, innit? Like he's stuck on repeat. Oi, careful now! Don't be blaspheming in the canteen. My cousin’s absolutely obsessed. She's already got tickets to see him, like, five times. But yeah, I can see what you mean. It’s pleasant, but not groundbreaking. I’ve been more into that new girl, Rina Sawayama? Have you heard of her? Rina Sawayama? Nah, doesn’t ring a bell. Is she, like, TikTok famous or something? Everything seems to blow up on TikTok these days, which automatically makes me suspicious. It's all algorithms, yeah? She’s been around a bit, actually. Properly good vocals, and her music's a whole vibe - kinda Y2K pop, but with proper substance. You should check her out. I found her through Instagram, funnily enough. Not a dance challenge, just someone I follow actually posted her. Speaking of Instagram, Leon keeps posting these ridiculously posed photos. It's exhausting!  Leon ? Oh, god, the one who thinks he’s a male model? Trying too hard, that one. Honestly, the filters he uses… he looks like a waxwork. What’s new with him anyway? Still talking about trying to get into that exclusive club downtown? Yep. Still banging on about 'networking opportunities.’ I think he just wants to peacock. He was moaning to me about how he needs a new outfit for it. Apparently, his current one isn’t ‘aesthetic’ enough. Honestly, the state of him. I told him to just wear something comfortable - he'll stand out  more  being genuine. You’re a good friend, trying to keep him grounded. Although, let’s be real, grounding Leon is like trying to herd cats. Did you manage to catch the new episode of  Heartstopper ? I’ve been waiting all week. Ooh, I did! Last night. Honestly, it’s still so lovely and heartwarming, even though it’s getting a bit… tense with the rugby stuff. I always feel so emotionally invested, it's ridiculous. Sometimes I need a palette cleanser after watching, you know? Like, something totally brainless. Tell me about it. That's where Disney comes in for me. I re-watched  The Little Mermaid  last week and it just hits different as an adult.

Honestly, Mum, the new Pokémon game is  way  different. They’ve completely revamped the battling system. It’s not just… picking moves anymore. There's this Tera Raid thing, and you have to really strategize with other players online. It's proper hard. Other players online? Right, that’s the ‘Skype’ bit you were going on about earlier? I still don’t fully understand how you talk to people while playing a game. Sounds a bit chaotic. Are these people… well, are they safe? Mum! It’s not Skype anymore, it's Discord! And yeah, they're safe. You can mute people, block them… it's fine. Everyone’s just trying to beat the big Pokémon. Listen, after dinner, can we maybe look at getting ramen? There’s that new place downtown everyone’s talking about. Ramen! More ramen! Ba-ba! Someone's agreeing with you. Oisin definitely approves of ramen. Though, frankly, he approves of anything remotely edible at this stage. He’s started saying “ba-ba” for everything. It’s bewildering. And yes, ramen sounds lovely. But you need to finish your homework first, Liam. Ugh, Mum,  homework . It's quadratic equations. Seriously? What even  is  the point? I’d rather be levelling up my Charizard. Equations are important, darling. They build your brain. Although, I confess, I haven't used one since… well, since before your father and I met. Speaking of building things, did you ever pick up that guitar again? It’s gathering dust in the corner. I did a bit last week. Trying to learn that new riff from Arctic Monkeys. It’s… difficult. My fingers are all sore. And it sounds rubbish. Everything sounds rubbish at first. Practice makes perfect. You have a natural ear. It's a shame you don’t spend less time staring at a screen and more time with a plectrum. Skinny! Skinny legs! Oisin, not again! And they are  not  skinny! They're… fitted! All my friends wear them. Honestly, it's the style. Fitted, skinny, it's all the same to me. They look perfectly comfortable. Although, you’re shivering. Put on some proper slippers, Liam. Not those ridiculous flip-flops. It's November! They’re not flip-flops, they’re slides! And they're comfy! These socks are itchy. Itchy socks are better than catching a cold. Honestly, boys. You’d think I hadn’t raised you.

Oh, goodness me. Look at this. Remember this, Mavis? Part of our gardening set. Honestly, it feels like a lifetime ago we were ‘gardening’ in your mum’s flowerbeds, digging up more than we planted, I suspect. Oh,  do  I remember! Your mum was remarkably patient with us. And yes, mostly we just made a mess. That little trowel went missing almost immediately, didn’t it? You were convinced I’d buried it. I  did  suspect you! You always did have a flair for the dramatic burial. But no, it turned up in the dog’s basket a week later. Honestly, Buster probably thought it was a bone. It was such a lovely set, though. Bright pink, everything. Seems terribly…girly now, looking back. It was the seventies, darling. Everything was bright pink or orange and avocado green! We didn’t know any different. It’s funny, isn't it, what sticks in your memory? Not the important things, like times tables, but a plastic watering can. Exactly! And remember Bako? Oh, we spent  hours  with that. Constructing these… ambitious, structurally unsound towers. Ambitious is one word for it. Precarious is another. Your brother used to deliberately wobble them, didn't he? The little devil. He absolutely did. Said it was ‘testing the structural integrity’. Little know-it-all. Though, to be fair, they  didn’t  have much integrity. The blue pieces were always the weak point. The blue ones, yes! And getting them to  click  together properly… a feat of engineering in itself. Why are we doing this, though? Honestly, it's all just bringing up memories and making me feel ancient. It’s hard enough trying to clear out a cupboard without a trip down memory lane. I know, I know. It’s just…this stuff. It’s not really  stuff , is it? It’s…evidence of a life. And it's all ending up in a charity shop, or worse. It feels a bit sad. Especially with Mum gone... it's like losing pieces of  her  too, somehow. She’s the one who bought us most of this. You're right. It does. Though, someone else might get some joy out of it. A little girl, pretending to be a gardener. A little boy constructing wobbly towers. That’s something, isn’t it? And honestly, we don’t need to be holding onto every single plastic brick. We barely have room as it is.

Honestly, I swear this tiny human attracts every mosquito within a five-mile radius. I got bitten three times just walking from the front door! And she doesn’t even  seem  to notice them. It's infuriating. You’re telling me. I’ve got a fresh one on my ankle already. It’s ridiculous for late September, isn’t it? Usually they’ve buggered off by now. Climate change, probably. Though, to be fair, the park's looking pretty lush still. Lush and buggy, you mean. We need to invest in one of those mosquito nets for the buggy, don't you think? Though it feels a bit… extreme. And probably ruins the aesthetic. Extreme is being eaten alive! Aesthetic can take a backseat for the sake of our sanity. I'll look online tonight. Speaking of tonight, are you still up for that gig? The new band at The Windmill? Oh, God, yes. I  need  some live music. I feel like I've been grading essays and singing nursery rhymes for approximately seventeen years straight. Though… getting there is the issue. Did you see the traffic report? The A3 is already looking dodgy. Don't even. I checked just before we left. Apparently, there's an incident near Clapham North. They're suggesting using the back roads, which will add at least another half an hour. I’m seriously considering the train. The train? From here? That’s a trek in itself with all the changes. We'd need to get a bus to Waterloo, then the Northern Line…it'd be more hassle than just sitting in traffic, I reckon. You’re probably right. Just grasping at straws, to be honest. I was really looking forward to it. It’s been ages since we've had a proper night out, just the two of us. I know. It feels like a lifetime. Every free evening is spent collapsing on the sofa. Though, on the plus side, this little one is absolutely fascinated by the leaves falling. Look at her, just staring. It's quite sweet. She is, isn't she? Little nature enthusiast. Remember when we used to spend weekends hiking in the Peak District? Feels like another lifetime. Don't remind me. Actually, remember that disastrous trip when it poured down and we got completely lost? And you insisted on navigating using a paper map? Hey! It was a perfectly good map!

Right, that’s me officially knackered. Four hours on the course, chasing that little white ball… honestly, sometimes I think it’s having a laugh at  me . How was your day, then? Any progress in the Great Job Hunt of ‘23? Don't even  start  with the nickname. It makes it sound like a quest involving dragons and questionable weaponry. It was… productive-ish. Applied for another three. All recruitment consultants, so basically glorified email senders, but hey, gotta start somewhere, right? I spent most of the afternoon crafting the perfect ‘cover letter’ – feels like writing a eulogy for a life I haven’t even lived yet. Oh, the cover letter. The bane of every graduate’s existence. It’s just…performance, innit? Pretending you’re desperate for  that  specific role at  that  specific company. I still reckon I could wing a job interview with just charm and a decent handshake. Probably wouldn't work in recruitment though. You  could  charm your way into anything, Dash. It’s unfair, really. All that charisma… wasted on golf. Speaking of wasting time, Mum keeps sending me links to Halloween decorations. Like, I appreciate the festive spirit, but I’m 24, not 8. And she wants me to help carve pumpkins. Your Mum’s a legend. Always has been. Pumpkins are good though, bit messy. Remember that time we tried to make a ghost out of a sheet and nearly took out Old Man Hemmings’ prize-winning geraniums? Don’t remind me! He threatened to call the police. And then Dad tried to smooth things over by offering to pay for new geraniums. It was a disaster. Honestly, the thought of coordinating costumes and trick-or-treaters fills me with dread. It’s all just…a lot. I need a quiet night and a really good TV series. Have you seen anything decent lately? I haven’t had much time for telly, to be honest. Been trying to actually  write  instead. That little short story I was telling you about? I managed another 500 words. It's slow going. Feels like pulling teeth sometimes. That’s brilliant, though! You’re actually doing it! I always say I'm going to start writing, then I end up scrolling through TikTok for three hours. It’s a black hole, swear. What’s it about? Still the thing with the abandoned theatre in Manchester? Yeah, that one.

Right, this stew should be grand. Though I swear, getting a decent carrot in Ballincollig is becoming a national crisis. They’re all…wonky. Dad, can I finish this level? It’s a really hard boss. Lad, dinner’s nearly ready. Put the thing down for five minutes. Your mother’s about to tell us all about the epic battle she had with the supermarket self-checkout. Again. Epic is an understatement, Seamus. It accused me of NOT scanning the broccoli. The broccoli! And then it demanded I put it in the ‘unexpected item in the bagging area’. It's broccoli, for goodness sake! Twinkle twinkle little star, how I wonder what you are… up above the world so high! Ah, there’s the entertainment sorted. Bless him, he’s determined to give us a concert every evening. Leo, sweetheart, that’s lovely, but maybe a bit quieter while we’re talking, yeah? Twinkle… twinkle… Mum, you need to just ask for help. They always have someone hovering around. Easier said than done, darling. I freeze. I just… blank. And then I'm arguing with a machine about leafy greens. It’s humiliating. Honestly, I'm thinking of only ordering things online. It's less stressful. Online’s grand, but sure isn't half the joy of living here getting stuff from the farmer’s market? Although, admittedly, even  they  are struggling with perfectly shaped carrots these days. Can we watch a film after? There's that new Marvel one everyone’s talking about. Marvel, eh? Depends on your homework situation. Did you finish that history essay? The one on…what was it… the Anglo-Norman invasion? Almost. I just need to write the conclusion. It’s just…  so  boring. All castles and battles. You know, I always found history fascinating. Especially the bit about Boudicca. Now  she  was a warrior. A bit scary, perhaps, but a warrior nonetheless. Boudicca's grand alright. Though I prefer the stories about Cú Chulainn myself. Now there's a legend. Speaking of legends, did you manage to sort out that cloud storage issue at work, Seamus? The one with the backups failing? It’s a right headache, that whole cloud situation. Everyone expects it to just  work , doesn’t they? Like magic. Never understand the sheer amount of infrastructure keeping it all afloat. Cloud? Is that like, actual clouds? No, love. It’s where they keep all the computer information, on big computers somewhere else.

Honestly, I still can’t believe we managed to snag this place for the week. Purton Green is  exactly  what we needed. And look at him, completely knocked out… in his pants!      Oh, don’t start. It’s comfortable for him, isn't it? He kicked them off hours ago. Remember last summer when he insisted on wearing his dinosaur onesie to the beach? This is practically dignified compared to that.      Is he dreaming about dinosaurs? I hope so.      Probably. Or maybe he's dreaming of building a massive Lego fortress. Speaking of building… I was sketching out some ideas for the extension earlier.      Oh, go on then. Show me. Though promises, promises, we haven't even sorted out the leaky tap in the bathroom!      Details, details. Think bigger! I was thinking, if we knocked through the dining room and extended back into the garden… we could get a proper, open-plan kitchen-diner. Loads of space for entertaining. And – this is the key bit – a utility room. A proper one. No more drying clothes on the radiator in November.      A utility room? What’s a utility room?      It’s where the washing machine lives, darling. And maybe somewhere to keep all your wellies and muddy boots.      Exactly! And imagine, French doors out onto the garden. We could get a pizza oven!      A pizza oven, really? You’ve been reading too many lifestyle magazines. Remember what happened when you tried to build that bird table? It leaned so far to one side it looked like it was trying to escape.      That's a low blow! It was a perfectly functional bird table. Slightly… asymmetrical, perhaps. And this is different. This is… structurally sound in my  mind . Besides, I’ve been watching loads of renovation shows. I’m practically an expert now.      More Lego… need more bricks…      He  is  dreaming about building! See? It's a sign! We should build something! Can we build a castle, Daddy? A really, really big castle?      We could  design  a castle. On paper, naturally. Maybe as part of the utility room design. A mini-castle for storing… I don't know, cleaning supplies?      You are incorrigible. Alright, alright, let’s see your sketches. But if it involves anything more complicated than swapping a lightbulb, I’m vetoing it immediately.      Deal. Though, just thinking aloud… maybe a small balcony off the master bedroom? Imagine having coffee out there in the morning…

…and honestly, the magnolia was a crime against interior design. Simply a crime. Forty years it’d been there, you know. Forty years! The previous owners hadn’t touched a thing. It’s like stepping back into 1983, but not in a good, retro way. Forty years, eh? Cor, that  is  a long time to let magnolia reign supreme. You’ve gone for something bolder, then? I saw a glimpse of turquoise through your doorway this morning. Turquoise and terracotta. A Mediterranean feel, you see. Trying to bring a bit of Cairo back, perhaps. Though Cairo’s changed immensely since I left, I imagine. Still, the colour scheme evokes… warmth. What about you, Alun? Still battling the beige in your study? Beige is a steadfast companion, I tell you. My wife, Bronwen, keeps suggesting lavender. Lavender! As if a lecturer on 18th-century Welsh poetry needs lavender surrounding him. It just doesn't  feel  right, does it? Speaking of feeling right, have you had any luck with the funding application for the particle decay project? Ah, that. It’s… complicated. They’ve asked for revisions. Apparently, my proposed methodology is “too ambitious” and “lacks demonstrable impact.” As if understanding the fundamental building blocks of the universe isn’t impactful enough! Bureaucrats, the lot of them. They’d rather fund another study on the social impact of reality television, I suspect. The bane of our existence, isn’t it? They want “impact”. They want to see immediate, tangible results. They don't understand the decades of groundwork that often precedes a breakthrough. Remember old Professor Davies and his work on the Hadron Collider? Twenty years of barely scraping by, then suddenly he’s a scientific celebrity. Precisely! And they’d probably want him to justify the cost of the coffee breaks he had whilst contemplating the mysteries of the cosmos. It’s ridiculous. I’m going to have to dumb it down, I think. Less talk of quantum entanglement, more talk of…practical applications. Even if I have to fabricate some. Don’t fabricate, David. They  will  sniff it out. Perhaps focus on the potential medical spin-offs? Radiotherapy advancements, that sort of thing? Gets their attention. Though frankly, I’m more concerned with recent news. Have you seen what’s happening with the water companies? Disgusting, absolutely disgusting. Pumping raw sewage into the sea! Yes, scandalous. Another example of prioritizing profit over people.

Right, operation ‘Sort the Lego Before It Takes Over the House’ is…slowly progressing. Honestly, it’s like an archaeological dig in here. Found a tiny Lego wheel just now – no idea what it came from. Elsie, darling, are you separating the Technic pieces, or just building a very colourful, structurally questionable tower? It’s a castle! For Rapunzel! But she’s a ninja turtle now. And it  is  structurally sound! Mostly. No it isn’t! It just fell down! And I need the red bricks for my spaceship! It’s going to go to Hogwarts! Hogwarts  and  space? That’s ambitious, Leo. Okay, okay, red bricks. Elsie, can you maybe… relinquish a few reds to your brother? We need to share the Lego love, remember? Think of Dumbledore – he was all about collaboration. But ninja turtles need red! They’re…they’re fiery! Fair enough. Fiery ninja turtles. I suppose we can make an exception. Although, you know, Michelangelo is orange. Just saying. Speaking of things needing sorting, did you two see the latest episode of  The Simpsons ? Bart was up to no good, as usual.  The Simpsons  is for grown-ups! I want to watch  Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles  again! With the pizza! We can watch a bit of both later, sweetheart. It’s Easter holidays, we have time for everything. Although, I’m starting to worry about how much chocolate “everything” includes. I swear, I saw you two sneaking Cadbury’s Creme Eggs before breakfast. They were calling my name! Like a magical spell! More like a sugar rush calling your name. Right, focus, Lego. Once this is done, I was thinking we could actually go to the cinema. There’s that new animated film… the one with the fluffy dragons? Dragons are cool! But are there lasers? Spaceships need lasers! Possibly? I haven’t read the reviews closely. It  might  have lasers. We'll investigate. It's definitely an improvement on having to spend the whole of Saturday at Granny’s. Granny’s house smells funny! And there’s dust everywhere! Well, Granny's having a bit of work done, remember? They're finally getting the kitchen redone. It’s been needing it for years. All that demolition is…messy, though. Apparently, they found some  very  old wallpaper. Your Granny thinks it might be from the 1950s. 1950s? Were dinosaurs still alive then? No, darling, dinosaurs were long gone by the 1950s.

…and honestly, the paella was just  sad . Like, they called it paella, but it was basically yellow rice with a few prawns thrown on top. Honestly, Mum makes better paella, and she’s never even  been  to Spain! Oh, no! Seriously? You went all that way to Barcelona and got… substandard paella? That's a travesty. I’m making a massive pot of chilli tonight, to make up for all life’s disappointments. Want some? I’ve got all the toppings. Chilli sounds… significantly better. Yes, please! Huge portion. Barcelona was lovely though, apart from the culinary let-downs. The architecture was incredible, obviously, and the beaches were actually quite nice, even if a bit crowded. How was Portugal? You were gone for just as long, right? Did you at least get good seafood? Portugal was… intense. In a good way mostly. The seafood was phenomenal. I ate my weight in grilled sardines. But mainly, I was doing a volunteering thing at a surf camp. Teaching beginners. It was exhausting but unbelievably rewarding. And chaotic. Picture twenty people simultaneously trying to stand up on a surfboard. Oh wow! That sounds…active. Not exactly my idea of a relaxing holiday. I’m more of a ‘lie on a beach with a book and occasionally dip a toe in the water’ kind of gal. Did anyone actually  learn  to surf? A couple did! One guy, Mark, was a natural. He was terrified at first, but by the end of the week he was catching small waves. It was brilliant to watch. It made the sand in every conceivable place worth it. Anyway, enough about my sunburn and questionable life choices. How was work while you were away? Did old Mr. Henderson finally explode? Don’t even  mention  Mr. Henderson. He was… less explosive, more passively aggressive. He spent the entire week making pointed comments about how ‘someone’ hadn’t left detailed handover notes and how the Johnson account was ‘slipping’. Honestly, I think he thrives on misery. I'm seriously considering looking for a new role. It’s just… stressful. Ugh, he sounds awful. You deserve better, honestly. Project co-ordination shouldn't involve emotional warfare with a septuagenarian. Have you told anyone at work how he’s making you feel? I mentioned it to Sarah, but she just said he's ‘a bit old-fashioned’ and I should ‘just ignore it’. Helpful.

Now then, lad, are you sure you’ve packed enough for your trip to London with school? It’s a long way to go and you don't want to be borrowing socks from your mates, do you? Your Gran and Grandad are proper worriers, you know. Yeah, Mum, I’ve got everything. Checked the list three times. Jacket, trainers, phone charger… the essentials. It's just a couple of nights. Don’t fuss. Essentials, he says! In our day, 'essentials' meant a sturdy pair of boots and a packed lunch. No fancy phone chargers needed! Mind you, we weren’t traipsing off to London, were we? Just the seaside at Withernsea. And  that  was an adventure. Aye, Withernsea. Used to get a right good sunburn down there. And the arcades! Spent a fortune on those fruit machines, I did. Never won a thing, mind. You always said that, Dad. But I seem to remember you bringing home a giant teddy bear once… a very wonky-eyed giant teddy bear. Ah, Bess, you’ve got a good memory, you have. Right, wonky-eyed he were, but little Sarah – that’s your cousin – loved him to bits. Gran, did you and Grandad ever go to London? Oh, once. Years and years ago. For the Queen’s Silver Jubilee. It was lovely, but terribly crowded. All those people! And the pigeons… monstrous things, they were. Nearly landed on your Grandad’s head. He wasn’t best pleased. Best pleased? I nearly had a heart attack! Thing was the size of a small dog. Thought it was going to steal my sandwiches. You and your sandwiches, Dad. Always thinking with your stomach. Now, about this trip, I’ve called the B&B and confirmed your room, Leo. They said they’ll keep your luggage safe before check-in. Brilliant, thanks Mum. You're the best. Do they have wifi? That’s the  real  essential. Wifi! What did we do before wifi, eh? We talked to each other. Imagine that! It's a different world now, Mum. Leo needs it for a school project, apparently. Although I suspect a bit of gaming will be involved too. Gaming, eh? What sort of games does this young’un play? Are they all shooting and explosions? Not really, Grandad. I’m into strategy games mostly. Building stuff, managing resources… it's actually quite complicated. Complicated, you say? Sounds a bit like trying to balance the household budget then!

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt a bit…off. Not dreadful, you know, but not  Peter Pan  either. It felt like they were trying too hard to be dark and edgy, and it lost the magic. Was it better than  Pan  though? Mummy said  Pan  was really rubbish. Like, really,  really  rubbish. Your mum's not wrong, darling.  Pan  was…a choice. A very questionable choice. It tried to be an origin story, and it just…didn’t land. It felt like they’d never actually  read  the book or seen the Disney film. This new one at least  tried  to capture some of the atmosphere, even if it didn’t quite succeed. Did Captain Hook have a hook? In the new one? Because that’s the most important bit. He  needs  a hook! He absolutely did, sweetie. A very shiny, fearsome hook. Though… he wasn’t quite as brilliant as Basil Rathbone, was he? Or even Dustin Hoffman, actually. Basil who-now? Was he in the Disney one? No, he was in a much older film, from the fifties. It’s a classic, but you’d probably find it a bit slow. It was before special effects were very good, so it’s more about the acting. I like special effects! All the flying! Did Tinkerbell fly in this new one? Did they make her really sparkly? She did fly, yes. They used quite clever CGI for her. Plenty of sparkle, though maybe not quite as much as in the Disney film. It’s funny, isn’t it? That Disney version has become  the  Peter Pan for so many people. Mummy said J.M. Barrie made up Peter Pan because of a little boy who died. Is that true? That’s a very thoughtful question, Lily. It's a complicated story. He was very close to the Llewelyn Davies boys, and one of them, George, died tragically young. It definitely influenced his writing, and he became a sort of father figure to the remaining boys. It’s thought that George was a big inspiration for Peter, the boy who never grew up. That's sad. Did Peter get sad when George died? That’s a really good question, Alfie. Peter doesn’t really  understand  death in the story, because he's supposed to be forever young. He’s a bit… detached from those kinds of feelings. But it makes you think about how sad the Llewelyn Davies family must have been, doesn’t it?

Right, nearly there then. Just past Cullompton, isn’t it? Feels like a proper trek to Exeter airport every time, even though I know it’s not  that  far. Still, better than Heathrow, eh? All that fuss. Definitely. And you doing the driving, Dad, is a lifesaver. I’d be a disaster trying to navigate the M5 with all the lorries this early. Did you sleep alright last night? You were tossing and turning a bit, I noticed. Oh, don’t start on his sleep, love. He’s been like that since…well, since Mum passed. A little bit of restless energy, that’s all. He needs a purpose, a routine. This trip, taking Sarah to the airport, it's good for him. Keeps him occupied. Now, now, don’t psychoanalyse me, Maureen! It's just… early mornings. Always hated ‘em, even back at the firm. Though, back then, at least there was a decent coffee waiting. This instant stuff just doesn't cut it. Still, I’m alright. Honestly. You say that, but you’ve mentioned being up three times already. You’re dropping me off and then straight back, aren’t you? No lingering for a chat with airport security? Good heavens, no! Need to be back to sort through those boxes in the loft. Still haven’t found that Christmas decoration Mum particularly liked…the little robin. Remember? Oh, the one with the wonky eye? Yes, lovely thing. We had it for years. Speaking of Christmas, have we finalised plans? Are your sister and her husband coming down from Taunton? They said they were trying to, but work’s been hectic for David. He's got that big presentation in January, so it depends if he can get the time off. I’m hoping they can, though. It’s not Christmas without Auntie Brenda’s questionable sherry trifle. Questionable is putting it mildly! Still, it’s tradition. Reminds me of when we lived over in Colyton. Smallest Christmas gatherings then, weren’t they? Just us and your Aunt and Uncle. Not like the chaos at our house in Paignton. Oh, Paignton! That house was always full to bursting. Remember young Ben running around with that remote-control car, nearly taking out Grandma’s legs? And the time he got into the brandy butter? Oh, the scandal! Good times, though. So, Christmas here then, at the new house? We should really start thinking about a housewarming, too.

Honestly, this sun. Lovely for the roses, mind, but a bit much for digging post holes, even for a working party. Though I suppose it's better than rain, eh? Been a right scorcher all week. You’re tellin’ me. Feels like July, not May. My knees are complainin’ somethin’ awful. Been at it since eight this mornin’, tryin’ to get that fence line sorted. What about you? What bit’ve the track are  you  wrestlin’ with? Oh, the rose garden border, actually. Trying to get it properly defined, ready for a new shipment of David Austin varieties. A bit of a passion of mine, roses. Though my back isn’t what it was. I did treat myself to a Swedish massage last week, though. Helped a little, you know, loosens everything up. You ever had one? A massage? Me? No, never. Sounds a bit…frivolous, doesn’t it? I’m more of a hot water bottle and a lie-down man, if I’m honest. Though my Margaret – my wife, she passed last year, bless her – she was always goin’ on about aromatherapy and things. She was a bit of a free spirit, that one. Oh, I am sorry to hear that. Losing someone…it leaves a hole, doesn’t it? And Swedish massage isn't frivolous, not if it helps! It’s about wellbeing. It's about looking after your body. I used to run a little gallery, you see, and being on your feet all day, shifting furniture… one needs to be practical. A gallery, you say? Fancy that. I was with the Nationwide, accommodation manager, all over the country. Always busy though, always on the move. Never much time for wellbeing, sadly. Margaret did volunteer at a hospice for years, though. She always said it was important to make the end of life comfortable. That's a truly wonderful thing to do. It takes a special person to work in a hospice. I’ve always admired those who do. It’s important work. I did a bit of work with nurseries, actually, years ago. Helping them with their art programmes. Very rewarding, seeing those little ones create. It's amazing how naturally artistic children are, before the world tells them what’s ‘good’ and ‘bad’. Nurseries eh? My granddaughter, little Maisie, she’s just started. Says they’re teaching ‘em all sorts now, equality and such. Good, I suppose, but when I were a lad… well, things were different.

Right, so I’ve been looking at flights again. Honestly, Mum, this is proving…challenging. Everything to Greece in August is just astronomical. August is  always  expensive, love. Everyone and their dog wants to go to the Med in August. Did you try looking at different airports? Maybe flying from Bristol instead of Exeter? I did! Bristol wasn’t much better, actually. And Exeter’s so convenient, you know? Just a short drive. I was hoping to keep it under, well, under a thousand quid for both of us, but that seems… optimistic. A thousand? For a week in Greece, in August? Darling, you’re dreaming. Remember that time we went to Spain, that little village near Valencia? That wasn’t cheap, and that was… oh, goodness, fifteen years ago now. I  know , I know. It just feels like everything’s gone up so much. I was really picturing little tavernas, the sea, you relaxing with a good book… I promised you a proper break. You’ve been working so hard with all the consultancy lately. And I appreciate that, believe me. But honestly, a break at home would be lovely too. I’ve got that garden project I want to tackle, and I could finally sort through all those old photos. Mum! We talked about this. You said you wanted  sun . You said you wanted to escape the Devon drizzle. Don't back out now. I’m not backing out, I'm just being…realistic. Perhaps we could consider somewhere else? Portugal maybe? I heard the Algarve is beautiful, and often a bit more affordable than the Greek islands. Portugal… Hmm. I hadn't really thought about it. What about the language? You're much better at picking up languages than I am. Oh, nonsense. A bit of phrasebook and a smile goes a long way. And many people in the tourist areas speak English. Besides, it’s good for the brain to try! Remember that Italian phrasebook you bought…and then left on the bedside table? Okay, okay, point taken. I’m terrible with languages. Let me have a look at the Algarve then. Maybe if we went a bit earlier in September, we’d get better deals? Now  that  is a good idea. September is still warm, but the crowds start to thin out. And the prices definitely drop. Have you looked at self-catering apartments? Sometimes they can be much cheaper than hotels.

… honestly, I still can’t believe how much that gig ticket was after fees. Sixty quid for one night, it’s daylight robbery! Did you see what happened with the rugby at the weekend though? Absolute scenes at Twickenham. Sixty quid? Lincoln prices, eh? Back home, a fella would be complainin’ if a good rum punch cost that much! And aye, I caught bits and pieces of the rugby. England pulled it back from the brink, didn’t they? Proper nail-biter. Reminded me a bit of when I used to watch my cousin play – he had that same knack for clutch plays. Clutch plays is a good way to put it. I nearly threw the remote at the telly when they were ten points down. Mum was givin’ me grief for shouting, said I was scaring the cat. Speaking of Mum, did she mention anything about Aunt Carol’s hip replacement? She was supposed to call her yesterday. She did. Carol’s doin’ alright, apparently. A bit sore, naturally, but she's stubborn as a mule, that one. Said she was already planning her next cruise, can you believe it? Before she’s even fully recovered! Your Mum’s worried she’s not takin’ it easy enough. Said she’s already booked a bridge club meeting for next week. That  is  Carol. No rest for the wicked, eh? Always busy, always organising something. God bless ‘er. It’s just… she’s getting on a bit. I’m worried she won't listen to the doctors. Right, back to the important stuff – did you see that interview with Tom Holland? He was on Graham Norton, properly hilarious. Tom Holland? The Spider-Man lad? Nah, missed that one. I was tied up with work, dealin’ with a right headache of a situation. Some supplier messed us about with a delivery, put the whole production line off schedule. Spent all day on the phone, sortin’ it all out. It's a constant battle, honestly. You think you've got things under control, then BAM! Something else pops up. Sounds stressful. Management life, I suppose. Still, you handle it. That’s why you're a manager. Speaking of work, how's the new trainee doin'? The one you were mentoring? Young Daniel? He's comin’ along. A bit green around the edges, still, needs to learn to trust his instincts more, but he's got the potential.

Ooh, that’s a good brew, Doris. Not quite as good as what Mavis used to make, mind you, but still… respectable. Though my leg’s playin’ up somethin’ fierce today. Feels like it’s full o’ gravel. Oh, Arthur, you  always  say that about your leg. A bit o’ damp, I reckon. Did you move the footstool? You need to keep it elevated. And Mavis made a good cuppa, alright, but don't go dissin' mine now! It's Yorkshire Tea, you know. Proper stuff. Morning, you two! Everything alright? Sounds like Arthur’s leg’s having a day. It’s looking grey over here in Brum, usual story. Though I was just showing the class a globe – a proper big, old-fashioned one – and it got me thinking about holidays. A globe, eh? Used to have one meself, years ago. Had all the little countries painted different colours. Little Timmy, bless him, used to spin it and pretend he was flyin’ everywhere. Never went much further than Skegness, poor lad. Though we did try a youth hostel once, in Yorkshire. Absolute disaster, that was. Yorkshire! Honestly, Arthur, you and Yorkshire. It’s hills, isn’t it? And wind. And you complaining you can’t walk up them hills with your leg! We went to Scarborough once, that was nice. Flat-ish promenade. Scarborough's lovely. Though, thinking about it, teaching geography now…kids have no concept of scale. They think everything’s a two-hour flight. I had one ask me if you could get the Tube to Australia. The  Tube ! I nearly choked. The Tube! Goodness me. Sounds like a right pickle. They didn’t ‘ave Tubes in Costessey when I was a lad. Just fields. And one shop. Old Man Hemmings’ shop. He sold everything. Even fireworks, though my mother nearly had a fit when she found  them . You were a terror, Arthur. A proper little rascal. Remember that school project you did? The one about… what was it? Ancient Egypt? Using all the wallpaper paste? Ah, yes! Mummies and pyramids! Mrs. Higgins wasn't too pleased when I'd covered half the classroom. She said it looked like a sticky, sandy mess. But it got me an ‘A’, you know? An ‘A’! She just didn't appreciate modern art, that woman. Sounds like a very… hands-on project. My current lot are doing the Amazon rainforest.

Right, so I’ve been lookin’ at flights for Greece. Honestly, it’s a right state. Everything’s gone up since… well, since everything went a bit bonkers, hasn’t it? I was hopin’ for under £200 return, but I’m lookin’ at closer to three hundred now, even flyin’ from Manchester. Ugh, tell me about it. I was trying to book something for a weekend in Amsterdam last month, and the prices were  insane . I ended up just… not going. I’m still a bit gutted, actually. What dates are you lookin' at for Greece? Maybe I can have a quick scout later? I'm a bit of a black belt when it comes to findin' cheap flights, bein' a student for so long. Oh, would you? That’d be champion, love. I was thinkin’ mid-June, maybe the 15th to the 22nd? Just a week, ya know? Enough sun to feel like a proper holiday, but not enough to bankrupt me. Manchester's best for me as it's easier to get to than Leeds-Bradford, but I’m open to other airports if the price is right. Mid-June… right, let me jot that down. Okay, Manchester to… which island were you thinkin’? Corfu? Rhodes? I’m seeing a few options around £270-ish with EasyJet if you’re flexible with the times. Early mornin' or really late at night seems to be the cheapest, naturally. Corfu would be nice. I've never been. My auntie went years ago and said it was beautiful. I don't mind the early starts, honestly. I'm more of a ‘get it done and get on with the holiday’ kinda person. Late flights though… I'm knackered enough as it is! Three hundred is still a bit steep though, innit? It is. It really is. Blame the fuel prices, blame everything. Okay, hang on... I’m playing with the dates a little bit… if you were to go a couple of days later, the 17th to the 24th, there's a Ryanair flight for £230. It’s a slightly longer layover in Stansted, though. Ooh, £230?! Now yer talkin'! A layover doesn’t bother me, especially if it saves that much dosh. Stansted’s a pain to get to from here though, isn’t it? You'd have to practically live on the M11. It is a bit of a trek.

…and honestly, the price of a loaf of bread these days! It’s highway robbery, I tell you. Highway robbery. Used to be, you could get a decent loaf for, what, sixty pence? Now it's pushing towards two quid. Two quid! Dad, you say that every time we see you. It  feels  like more because everything’s going up, but it's not quite as dramatic as you make out. Though, I did notice the price of cheddar has gone absolutely bonkers. Don't even start me on cheddar, love. I was in Sainsbury's yesterday, and they were charging nearly eight pounds for a block of mature! Eight pounds! I nearly left it on the shelf. Still, needs must, doesn't it? Little Timmy loves his cheese and crackers. Eight pounds! Good heavens. When I was a lad, a block of cheese lasted a week. Now, it's gone before you can blink. It’s the portions, you see. Everyone wants bigger portions, everything’s got to be ‘extra large’ and it all adds up. And don't even get me started on banking charges. They find new ways to bleed you dry, they do. You're still with Barclays, aren't you, Dad? I keep telling you to look at Monzo or Starling. They have much better customer service and no hidden fees. I switched a couple of years ago and it’s been a revelation. Monzo? Starling? Sounds like something out of a science fiction film. I’m perfectly happy with Barclays. I know where I stand, even if ‘where I stand’ is being mildly fleeced. It's the devil you know, isn’t it? Besides, I haven’t the foggiest idea how to use one of those fancy apps. He’s a bit of a Luddite, our Arthur. Remember when he refused to get a mobile phone for years? Said it was a waste of money. It  was  a waste of money! All those monthly contracts. Pointless. But you two convinced me eventually. And now they're constantly changing providers, offering deals… it's a nightmare trying to keep track. Vodafone, O2, EE… it's all Greek to me. You're right, it's a constant juggling act. I'm thinking of switching again actually; the signal’s been terrible around my place lately. Thinking about going back to EE, strangely enough. They've been improving their coverage.

… honestly, I still can’t believe how much sun we got in Portugal last summer. It was proper scorching, like. Not a cloud in the sky for ten days. Mind you, I did get a bit fed up with all the tourists. Everywhere you looked, just… orange people. Orange people? That’s a bit harsh, isn’t it, Liv? Though I get what you mean. I went to Cornwall with my family, and it was rammed. Couldn’t move for buckets and spades. Still, at least the pasties were good. Speaking of food, anyone fancy ordering a takeaway? I’m starving. Cornwall sounds lovely, even with the crowds. We didn’t really  do  a holiday, to be honest. I worked all summer to save up for this semester. Though, my auntie sent me pictures from her trip to the Aran Islands. Apparently, the sheep are completely fearless. They just wander right up to you, looking for a biscuit! Oh, the Aran Islands! I’ve always wanted to go there. My Nana’s from Galway, so I've heard loads about it. The scenery is meant to be breathtaking. And fearless sheep… that’s brilliant! Reminds me of the sheep on Snowdon. They’re absolute characters. Now, takeaway...what are we thinking? I could murder a good curry. Curry sounds amazing, Rach. I'm deffo in. I had a really relaxing holiday though, went back to Hartlepool to see me nan. Not exotic or anything, but proper chilled. Loads of walks along the sea front with her wee dog, Winston. He’s a terrier, a right little terror, actually. Winston, that’s a good name! I’ve always wanted a dog, but a flat in Salford isn’t exactly ideal, is it? Too cramped. My Auntie Pam in South Africa has three boerboels – massive things, like miniature lions. They need a whole garden to themselves. Boerboels? Crikey! That sounds…intense. Winston sounds much more manageable. Though, I'm a cat person myself. I grew up with them. They just fit into your life, you know? Less fuss. Although, my patient, Mrs. Higgins, has a Tibetan Mastiff. That thing is  huge . It takes up half the room when she brings it for check-ups. Cats are good. Independent. I’ve always liked them. We had a stray, called Saoirse, that used to hang around our house. My Da would leave out milk for her every evening.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of putting that much beige in one room. It’s a gallery, not a biscuit factory! Did you see Old Man Hemlock's stuff? It was… underwhelming, to put it mildly. Beige is a powerful statement, El. You've gotta appreciate the minimalism. Hemlock’s stuff  was  a bit…safe, though, wasn't it? Like he was worried about offending anyone. My art history lecturer went on for ages about his “subtle commentary on societal conformity.” I was mostly thinking it needed more colour. Subtle commentary?! It needed a sledgehammer to the canvas, more like. Honestly, I'd have done something bolder with my GCSE art, and that was mostly me trying to recreate Van Gogh’s Starry Night with glitter glue. Speaking of which… how's the essay coming? Still wrestling with post-structuralism? Don't even  mention  post-structuralism. It’s actively trying to unravel my brain. I think I've written and deleted the introduction five times now. It needs to be about Baudrillard and simulation, but all I can think about is how much this feels like  being  simulated into exhaustion. Oh, God, Baudrillard. He always felt like he was deliberately trying to be incomprehensible. Remember that seminar? Everyone was nodding sagely, pretending to understand, and I was just internally screaming "What even  is  real anymore?!" Exactly! It's the same feeling I get when I try and explain why I spent six hours yesterday building a virtual farm in Stardew Valley. Like, what am I  doing  with my life? Baudrillard would probably say that’s precisely the point – the hyperreality of escapism. See? He’s ruining everything, even your gaming. You should be out enjoying fresh air, not pixelated parsnips. Though, I'll admit, I dipped back into Animal Crossing last week…purely for research, obviously. Occupational hazard of being a mature student. Mature student? You’re barely twenty-two! And ‘research’…right. You just want to redesign your virtual island. Honestly, I'm starting to wonder if we’ll be ninety, still arguing about the merits of digital landscaping and whether beige is acceptable art. Ninety? Oh, crikey. That’s a depressing thought. Imagine, still arguing about this stuff in a retirement home, surrounded by crocheted blankets and lukewarm tea. “Honestly, Brenda, that watercolour landscape is  tragic .” And you’d be trying to convince Brenda that a well-placed digital fern is far superior.

Honestly, this butternut squash is putting up a fight. You’d think it was personally offended I was trying to make soup. You always attack your vegetables, Liv. It’s quite alarming to watch. Is everything alright? You seem a bit… vigorous. Just a long day. Mr. Henderson decided  today  was the day to completely rewrite the project brief. Again. Honestly, I think he just enjoys watching me scramble. And then Sarah cancelled on drinks tonight. Oh, no! Sarah? What happened? She's usually super reliable. Something about a last-minute date. Apparently, someone from her pottery class asked her out. She was all blushy when she messaged. Good for her, I guess, just… irritating timing. I was really looking forward to a proper vent. A pottery date! That’s… unexpectedly romantic. But yeah, a bit rubbish for you. You deserve a good vent after Henderson’s shenanigans. We can still have a vent session  while  we eat soup, can’t we? Definitely soup is essential. And venting is vital for my continued sanity. How was your day? Besides the obvious - dealing with… everything. You always make it sound so calm when you talk about work. It wasn't calm, truthfully. Old Mr. Davies was having a really rough patch. He kept fixating on his wife, and… well, it hit a nerve, I think. Reminded me of Gran a bit, the way he talked about her. I spent most of the afternoon just sitting with him, letting him talk. It’s draining, but worthwhile. Oh, bless him. And you. You're so good at that - just  being  there. I'd feel completely lost. I'm terrible at the quiet empathy stuff. I bluster and try to fix things, which usually makes it worse. It’s a different skill set. And honestly, sometimes people don't  want  fixing. They just need someone to listen. Although, I did have a patient try to convince me today that he could communicate with pigeons. Oh,  really ? Pigeons? That's… a new one. Do they have important messages? Secrets of the universe? Apparently, they're deeply concerned about the price of breadcrumbs. Very serious business. Actually, it was quite sweet, in a way. He's a lonely soul. Right. Okay, that's… poignant. You really do have the most interesting job. I'm mostly dealing with spreadsheets and passive-aggressive emails. Speaking of interesting, are you still seeing Ben?

Right then, let’s have another look at this consent form, shall we? I’m still not entirely comfortable with the phrasing on section three. It feels… a bit leading, doesn’t it? Like we’re  expecting  them to agree to the recording, rather than genuinely giving them a choice. “Participants acknowledge the benefits of recording for research purposes…” Benefits? What if they just don’t  want  to be recorded? I see your point, Eleanor. It does sound a little pushy. Though, to be fair, the research ethics committee did approve it. They didn’t flag that particular sentence. Perhaps they felt the benefits outweighed any potential discomfort? We are explaining how the recordings will be anonymised and used solely for improving the seminar, aren’t we? Aye, we are, but Eleanor’s right. It's the language. "Acknowledge the benefits…" feels a bit…salesy. Especially for a university setting. We're not selling them anything! Maybe something simpler, like “Participants are aware the session may be recorded for research purposes, and consent is optional”? That's much better, Brenda. “Aware” is a good word. It’s neutral. It doesn’t imply any expectation. And “consent is optional” – absolutely. That’s crucial. I’ll make that change. Now, onto the seminar itself. I’ve been tinkering with the structure a bit. I was thinking we could start with the Hofstede’s cultural dimensions, just to lay the groundwork, then move into some practical case studies. Good starting point, Eleanor. Hofstede is a classic, and it provides a useful framework. Though, we need to be mindful of critiques. It's not without its limitations, is it? We don’t want to present it as the absolute truth. Perhaps a quick disclaimer after we’ve introduced it - acknowledging more nuanced approaches to cultural understanding? Definitely. And maybe we could intersperse the case studies with interactive bits? I’ve had good success with small group discussions. Give them a scenario – a miscommunication between a British firm and a Japanese one, for instance – and get them to diagnose the cultural factors at play. I liked that idea when you first mentioned it, Brenda. It’s good to move away from us just  telling  them things. Gets them actively engaged. I was a bit worried about time though. We only have ninety minutes, and I’m worried about squeezing everything in. We could streamline the Hofstede section, maybe focus on just three or four key dimensions.

Honestly, that seminar was  exhausting . Old Man Hemmings really went on one about post-structuralism again. You’d think after ten years of lecturing, he’d find a new angle. Hemmings is Hemmings. He's a comforting constant, isn't he? Like the smog. Though, I'd trade either for a proper cup of tea right now. This jasmine stuff just isn’t cutting it. Tell me about it. I miss a good builders’ tea. Strong enough to stand a spoon in. Speaking of missing things… have you heard anything more about the housing situation? The estate agent said they’d ring back about that little courtyard house… Nothing, frustratingly. I chased her up this morning, and she was “terribly busy.” Which, knowing estate agents, probably means she’s showing someone else around. It’s maddening. We’ve been looking for six months! Six months! And everything is either a tiny shoebox or requires a small loan to even  consider  viewing. Is it really this bad everywhere in Chengdu, or are we just spectacularly unlucky? I think it’s genuinely competitive. Apparently, a lot of people are moving here for work in the tech sector, pushing up the prices. And most landlords want year-long contracts upfront, which feels… daunting. Remember when we could just ‘wing it’ with a month-to-month in London? Vaguely. Seems like another lifetime ago. I’m starting to think we should just resign ourselves to staying in the university accommodation for another year. It's… functional. And at least we don't have to worry about deposits and lease agreements. Functional is putting it kindly. It’s beige and depressing. And the communal kitchen smells perpetually of instant noodles. We deserve more than beige and noodles, Elsie. We’re lecturers, for heaven's sake! We’re supposed to be cultivating cultured lives. Cultured lives amongst the instant noodles. It  is  a bit of a paradox, isn't it? I had a student today ask me about Virginia Woolf, and I just… felt a pang of longing for a proper garden to sit in while reading her. A garden. Yes. That courtyard house  did  have a lovely little garden. Enough for a small table and chairs, maybe a few potted plants. Imagine… actual sunlight that isn’t filtered through a grimy window. Stop it, you're torturing me. I spent the morning grading essays about the impact of urbanization on community, then came home to live in a glorified student hall.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is  almost  as good as Gran used to make. Almost. She had a secret ingredient, didn’t she? I swear it wasn’t just nutmeg. Probably a hefty dollop of butter, knowing her. Everything was better with butter at Gran’s house. Remember how she’d always have a tin of biscuits, even if it was five minutes before dinner? And you  weren’t  allowed to have one. Torture, absolute torture. Oh, the biscuits! And the floral wallpaper… everywhere. We need to talk about redecorating Mum and Dad’s place. It’s stuck in 1985. Seriously, that armchair is a crime against interior design. Leave the armchair alone! It’s… iconic. Besides, Mum loves that thing. Remember when we were kids and tried to build a fort around it? Though, yes, the wallpaper needs to go. It clashes with everything. Speaking of which, did you see that show, ‘The Great Interior Design Challenge’ last night? I missed it. Was it any good? I’ve been engrossed in that Indian drama, ‘Arranged’. It’s fascinating, really makes you think. The whole concept of dowries… it’s unsettling, isn’t it? And the pressure on these young women. Yeah, I saw a bit of that. It's a world away from, well, everything we know. It makes you appreciate how much things have changed, even if it’s still not perfect. It's a bit different from the whole ‘find your own path’ advice we get at school, isn't it? I mean, careers advice feels so… broad. “Anything is possible!” Yeah, try telling that to someone wanting to be a shipwright these days. It’s a pretty ‘closed’ industry. Exactly!
