It’s all “go to university, get a degree!” – which is good, obviously, but what about the skilled trades? My friend’s son wants to be a mechanic, and everyone’s pushing him towards A-Levels. It’s ridiculous. We need more apprenticeships, more work experience opportunities. I try to push that with my students, but it’s hard when the system isn’t set up for it. It’s true. Though, on the upside, at least  my  industry is booming. Robotics and automation – they can’t get enough engineers. It’s pretty scary though, thinking about the implications of further industrialization. Mass unemployment… all that. That’s why I get so frustrated with food waste. We're creating problems everywhere and then throwing perfectly good food away!

Honestly, this Bolognese is taking  forever . And I’m pretty sure half of it will end up on the floor, courtesy of Leo and his, uh, enthusiastic ‘helping’. You say that every time, darling. And every time, Leo seems to manage to get more sauce  in  his mouth than  on  the floor. Small victories. How was your day at the lab? Anything exciting happening in the world of cortisol and coping mechanisms? Exciting is… a strong word. It was mostly data, data, and more data. Honestly, I’m starting to dream in spreadsheets. Professor Davies is pushing for a publication before Christmas, which is just…stressful. Especially when the data is being incredibly stubborn. It’s like it  knows  I want to prove my hypothesis and is actively working against me. The data has a mind of its own, does it? Sounds familiar. My week hasn’t been much better, to be honest. New standardised tests rolled out, and the teachers are, understandably, up in arms. It feels like every time someone has a good system going, someone else decides to ‘improve’ it. Oh, the joys of education policy. So, lots of complaints then? Mountains. Mostly about the sheer volume of admin now required. It’s taking them away from actually, you know,  teaching . I spent most of today fielding calls and trying to explain why the new system, which nobody understands, is supposedly better. It’s exhausting. Sounds like you need a very large glass of wine. And maybe Leo to ‘help’ you with some colouring in. Distraction tactics, that's the key. Definitely the wine. And yes, colouring is frequently employed as a tactical diversion. Speaking of Leo, have you spoken to your mum about him starting school next September? Briefly. She’s already got a list of schools longer than my arm and is talking about catchment areas and league tables and…it’s slightly overwhelming. I thought we agreed we’d take our time deciding? I know, I know. But you know your mum. She likes to be prepared. I tried to gently suggest we wait until the Open Days next year, but she’s already researching independent schools. It’s just…I’m not sure I want him to go to private school. It feels a bit… isolating. And expensive. Honestly, the state schools around here are pretty good. I agree. And we talked about this. We can look at all the options, of course, but I'm leaning towards state school too.

…and honestly, Doreen, looking at that telly program about coastal erosion… it just gets to you, don’t it? All them houses, just… disappearing into the sea. Makes you think, what’s the point of building anything at all? Seems a bit daft, really. Now, Arthur, don't go getting all philosophical on me at ten o’clock in the morning. It  is  sad, I agree. Dreadful for those folk. But it's happened since time began, the sea taking back what’s hers. Remember Old Man Hemmings’ cottage down at Great Yarmouth? Gone years ago. Not the end of the world, though. Morning you two. Talking about the sea reclaiming land? Saw that programme too. Powerful stuff. Reminds me of a project I did with the kids a few years back – investigating the changing coastline. They were fascinated, but horrifying, wasn’t it? Horrifying is a good word, David. It's not just the houses, mind you. It’s… it’s the feeling of things being… temporary. All this fussing about with decorating and tidying, and for what? It’ll all be gone one day, washed away. Like my mood, some days. Arthur, you're sounding a bit bleak. Is this… is it getting worse again? You were doing so well last week, getting out to the garden and all. Last week the sun was shining. Everything looks brighter with a bit of sun. And I did enjoy that bit of weeding. But then I started thinking about Emily… and how she never calls anymore. Not since… well, you know. Emily? Your daughter? Right. Look, Arthur, you know she's busy with the children. She works long hours. It doesn't mean she doesn't care. Trying to balance everything… it’s tough. You and I both know that, don't we? She’s got her own life now, Arthur. It's hard, but you’ve got to let them live it. Holding on too tight… well, that just pushes them away. It's what I learned with my Michael, wasn't it? Trying to control everything... Easy for you to say, Doreen. You always were the strong one. I'm not built for this sort of thing. This… not being needed. Nonsense, Arthur. You're needed. You're needed  here . You keep Doreen company, you tell me your stories, you… you know a surprising amount about baby blue tits, apparently.

…and honestly, the difference is  night and day . I used to spend ages trying to get volume at the roots, teasing and spraying, and it just looked…sad. This mousse, though? One application, blow dry, and BOOM. Salon-worthy. Ooh, really? You know I’ve got the same problem. My hair’s just…flat. Always has been. I’ve tried everything, honestly. Different cuts, different shampoos, even those root-lifting sprays that smell like varnish. They just make it sticky. What mousse is it? Is it expensive? It's the John Frieda Volume Lift Air Whipped Foam. It’s not  cheap  cheap, I think it was about £8 a bottle in Boots, but it lasts ages. You only need a small amount, see? And it doesn't leave that horrible residue. It actually feels…clean. Have you been to Boots lately? They've got three-for-two on hair stuff at the moment. Oh, that’s good to know! I was in there on Tuesday, actually, getting bits and bobs for Mum. Didn’t see the offer, though. I was too busy queueing, honestly. Old Mrs. Higgins was paying for her shopping with a load of coppers again. Takes  ages ! But three-for-two… I might pop in tomorrow after work. Honestly, do. Honestly, your hair would love you for it. Speaking of looking good, did you see Sarah’s nails on Saturday? She had them done in this incredible shade of burgundy, all sparkly. I was so jealous. Oh, yes! They were beautiful. She said she went to that new place, 'Nail Haven' down by the market? Apparently, they’re really good, and not too pricey. I’m tempted to go myself, but I'd feel so silly. I never bother with nails, usually. Just a quick file and a coat of clear varnish. You shouldn’t feel silly! It's a nice treat. And it makes such a difference, doesn't it? Just feeling a bit…polished. I’ve been having my gels done for about six months now, and I’m hooked. It's a bit of a faff getting them removed, though. That’s the downside. That’s what puts me off, to be honest. I've heard the removal process can be damaging. I’d rather stick to natural, even if it means chipped polish after a day. Have you seen Lisa lately? She's gone and dyed her hair bright pink!

… honestly, the parking situation around the Walker Art Gallery is mental, isn’t it? I was trying to take a class there last week, do a bit of observational writing, and ended up circling for half an hour. Could’ve written a novella in the time I wasted! Tell me about it. Absolutely bonkers. I had a home visit near there last Tuesday, trying to get to a family needing support, and nearly lost my mind. Ended up parking miles away and sprinting. It’s a wonder anyone actually  visits  the museums with that hassle. Though, to be fair, the Tate Liverpool is usually a bit easier. Aye, the Tate's a bit better. Less… prestigious, I suppose. Doesn’t attract the same hordes. Speaking of hordes, how’s work been? Still battling fires with limited resources? You know it. It's relentless, honestly. Funding cuts are hitting everyone hard. I had a case this week with a young lad, proper chaotic home life, needs loads of support, but the waiting list for counselling is six months. It’s heartbreaking. What about you? Still wrangling with teenagers and misplaced apostrophes? You have no idea. Year nines are a special breed. I swear they deliberately misplace punctuation just to wind me up. It’s good, though. Keeps me on my toes. I’m actually thinking about doing a Masters in Applied Linguistics. Got an interview next month at Uni. No way! That’s brilliant, lad! Seriously, that’s amazing. Applied Linguistics, yeah? Good shout. What are your chances like, do you reckon? I’m hoping alright. I’ve got a decent personal statement, and my references are solid. It’s just… the funding. The course fees are a killer. I’ve been looking at loans, but the thought of graduating with even  more  debt is terrifying. I hear you. Debt’s a monster. Maybe there are some bursaries you could apply for? I can have a look, got a bit of experience navigating that sort of thing. Gran used to say, "Look after the pennies and the pounds look after themselves," but honestly… it feels like the pennies are disappearing before I even  see  them. That’d be massive, thanks mate. Seriously. I was talking to Sarah – you remember Sarah, from the pub quiz? – and she’s planning her wedding. Honestly, the scale of it is insane. She’s talking about a live band, ice sculptures… I'm just trying to afford a decent Christmas prezzy for me nan!

…and honestly, the whole thing with Mark’s son, Leo, refusing to even  look  at the Christmas present I got him… it just felt… pointed. Like I'm deliberately trying to usurp his mum, which, frankly, isn't the case. I just wanted to get the boy a Lego set he’d enjoy! Oh, darling, that’s awful. Leo’s always been a bit… reserved, hasn’t he? It’s not  you , it’s him grappling with… well, everything. It must be so hard for him, seeing you become a fixture in his dad’s life. He’s probably just trying to figure out where he fits in now. I know, logically. I  teach  children, for goodness sake! I should be able to empathise. But it still stings. It's been nearly two years, and it feels like I’m still perpetually ‘the other woman’ in his little world, even though his mum and I are perfectly civil. We even had a lovely coffee last month! Civil is good. That’s really good. Sometimes that's all you can hope for with exes, isn’t it? Especially when there’s a child involved. But Leo’s reaction speaks volumes about what’s going on  for him . Mark’s been a bit…blase about it, I think. “Boys will be boys,” he said. Honestly. Exactly! Men. Sometimes I want to shake him. He doesn't seem to understand the emotional complexity of it all. He just wants everything to be fine and dandy because  he  feels guilty, I suspect. It's not about me feeling bad, it’s about Leo needing to feel secure and heard. That’s a really perceptive take, actually. It’s always easier to project the problem onto someone else. It’s funny, isn’t it? We spend so much time building careers, trying to be independent women… and then we end up navigating this minefield of family dynamics. It’s exhausting. Exhausting is an understatement! And it makes me question everything. I thought I was ready for this, for a relationship with a divorced dad. I thought I was strong enough. But then those little moments, like Leo’s rejection, hit you and you feel completely helpless. You  are  strong enough. You're the most resilient person I know! Remember when your mum was ill? You held everything together. This is different though, isn't it? It's not about fixing something; it's about  being  present, and patiently navigating someone else’s feelings.

…and honestly, the sheer  audacity  of that storyline! Like, who decides a vicar secretly runs a competitive ferret-legging ring? It's just… baffling. And yet, I was hooked. Ferret-legging? Right. Sounds about par for British TV these days. Anything to get views, eh? I’ve been trying to avoid screens if I can, though. Dissertation’s sucking the life out of me. Though I did briefly fall down a Pinterest rabbit hole last night. Oh, don't even  start  on Pinterest. I'm convinced it's designed to make you feel inadequate about your life choices. I went on looking for cake decorating ideas for Auntie Brenda’s birthday and suddenly I was viewing minimalist Scandi living rooms and questioning everything. See? It’s a trap! I was looking at… well, don’t judge, I was looking at custom-built bookshelves. For my thesis. To, you know,  inspire  me. And suddenly I was staring at tiny houses and off-grid living. Brenda’s birthday is when, again? End of next month. Sixty-five, can you believe it? She’s already hinting she doesn’t  need  anything, which is code for ‘I want a weekend spa break’. But she also keeps saying ‘don’t spend too much, pet’. You know Brenda. Maddeningly frugal but expecting luxury. The classic Brenda conundrum. We did the spa thing for Mum last year, didn’t we? She loved that, even if she complained about the cucumber on her eyes the whole time. Maybe we could do something similar for Brenda? A slightly less… premium version? Hmm, potentially. I was thinking about a cake, obviously. But Pinterest has ruined me. Everything’s too complicated now. Remember when we used to just slap some icing on a Victoria sponge and call it a day? Those were the days. Before we knew buttercream flowers were even a thing. Though, speaking of friends, have you heard from Liam recently? I haven’t seen him since… well, since ages ago. He was supposed to come down for a weekend. He messaged me last week, actually. He's landed a new job down in London. Something to do with coding for a gaming company. He’s proper chuffed, apparently. Honestly, I'm thrilled for him. He was getting so fed up with that marketing gig. That’s fantastic! He deserves a good break. He always was the creative one. It's just a shame he’s moving even further away.

Oh,  this  one is nice. Look, David, brushed chrome, three lights… a bit modern for the dining room, maybe? But it's only £35.99 with free postage. Hmm. Thirty-five ninety-nine? That  is  a steal, actually. Though I’m still picturing something a little more…substantial, for over the dining table. Something with a bit of a drop, you know? Not just straight down. We need to fill the space. Drop? Like a chandelier? Oh lord, no. Remember Aunt Mildred’s monstrosity? I'm still having nightmares about that thing. No, definitely not a chandelier. Just something… elegant. This brushed chrome isn't terrible though, is it? It'd match the legs on the chairs. No, it’s not  terrible . Just…a little…underwhelming. I've been having a look at houses again, by the way. Oh,  here  we go. Back to the dream. Found anything remotely affordable in our price range that doesn’t need a complete overhaul? Actually, there’s one in Melton Mowbray. Three bedrooms, decent-sized garden. It’s listed at £325,000. Needs updating, obviously, the description says “potential to modernise”, which is estate agent speak for ‘it's a bit of a mess’. Melton Mowbray? That’s…a bit further out than we were thinking, isn't it? And isn’t that pork pie central? It is, apparently. But it's commutable, and the photos look promising. Check it out. . Look at the garden! And it's got a conservatory. Oh, that  is  a lovely garden. But the conservatory looks…dated. And the kitchen…shudders. That avocado suite has  got  to go. It's screaming 1970s. That’s the “potential to modernise” bit coming into play. We knew anything in our budget would need work. It’s a trade-off. More space for more work. We’re fairly handy, aren’t we? “Fairly” is generous. You’re handy. I'm…supportive. I can hold things and make tea. And research light fittings. Which, incidentally, this one with the fabric shades is hideous. . Supportive is excellent! Crucially important! And I’m happy to do the majority of the DIY. We could get a quote for the kitchen, of course, but even a relatively simple re-fit will eat into the budget. It always does. Honestly, I think we should view this Melton Mowbray place. Just to see. Even if we don't like it, it’s good to get a feel for what’s actually available.

…and honestly, the state of the communal bathroom at the hospital is just  dreadful  this week. Someone’s clearly been having a bit of a rough time, judging by… well, let’s just say the state of it. You wouldn't  believe  it. I spent a good twenty minutes cleaning up after someone this morning, and then old Mr. Henderson managed to flood the floor five minutes later. Honestly, sometimes I feel more like a cleaner than a nurse! Oh, bless you, Sarah. That sounds absolutely grim. Hospitals. I wouldn’t last five minutes on a ward these days. Too much…  everything . I’m happy enough pottering about with Mrs. Peterson, even if she insists I call her ‘petal’ all the time. It's a bit much, really. How's Mum doing, by the way? Did she manage to sort out that dodgy step on the patio? Mum’s alright. Still moaning about the neighbour’s cat, of course. Apparently, Winston has been using her prize-winning petunias as a litter tray. Honestly, the drama! And yes, Dad got around to fixing the step, though he nearly took a tumble himself in the process. He's convinced he needs a new shed, now. It’s always something with him. Have you heard anything more from Liam about job interviews? He was applying for that assistant manager role at the supermarket, wasn't he? Morning, you two! Smells lovely in here. Is that that hazelnut coffee you got, Sarah? Lovely. And yes, Liam had an interview yesterday. He said it went alright, but he's being typical Liam - all downplaying and "might have messed up that bit about stock rotation" and stuff. Honestly, he’s his own worst enemy. He’d overthink a cup of tea. Oh, good to hear he had an interview! He  deserves  something better than just being a carer, bless him. It's physically draining, isn't it? Running around all day. I’m starting to feel every one of my years, I tell you. Though, Mrs. Peterson does make a cracking cup of tea, so there's that. He does worry too much, that boy. He's capable, honestly. And you're right, Lizzie, it  is  hard work. It's rewarding, of course, but it takes it out of you. Speaking of draining, my back is killing me. I've been lifting patients all morning. I need to start doing those yoga stretches again.

… honestly, the sheer volume of stuff being published on sleep these days is astounding. Apparently, consistent bedtimes  and  wake-up times are more crucial than the actual number of hours you get. Even on weekends. Who knew? Honestly, that sounds…exhausting. Like, actively trying to maintain a rigid schedule, even when you  could  lie in? I’m a teacher, remember? My sleep schedule is dictated by hormonal teenagers and marking. It’s chaos. Are you actually trying this? I am. Trying. It’s… a work in progress. I downloaded one of those sleep tracking apps, which are probably wildly inaccurate, but it's a good starting point. It told me my sleep efficiency is appalling. Apparently, I thrash around like a landed fish. Oh, you? A landed fish? I can picture it. You're a restless sleeper, always have been. Remember that camping trip in the Lake District, and you ended up half-way down the hill? Don’t remind me. Honestly, that was a disaster. I thought I was orientating myself by the stars, but clearly not. And then the tent pegs… Let’s just say I’m not a natural outdoorsman. Though, speaking of getting lost, have you ever gotten properly turned around in a city? Oh, Cambridge is specifically designed to confuse people. I’ve lived here for fifteen years and still occasionally end up going round in circles near King's College. I once spent a solid hour trying to find Mill Road from the station, and it’s literally a straight line. It’s the clever one-way systems. That’s pathetic! I once got utterly lost in Rome. I was trying to find this little trattoria a friend recommended, and ended up wandering for ages, eventually ending up near the Colosseum, which was… impressive, but not where I wanted dinner. I had to Google Maps it in the end, utterly defeated. Getting into cities is always the hard bit, though. Finding a route that doesn't involve getting stuck behind a tractor is a skill. A very specific skill, honed by years of rural living, I imagine. You'd think with all the tech we have, navigation would be easier. Anyway, enough about our geographical failings. You were talking about sleep. This app… what else did it tell you? That I need a darker room. Apparently, even the tiny LED on the smoke alarm is disruptive.

…and honestly, I still can’t believe Brenda thinks hamsters are ‘low maintenance.’ Low maintenance?! She’s already asking me for advice on the best bedding 'cos Hammy keeps burrowing and making a right mess. Honestly, it's like havin' a tiny, furry demolition expert. Oh, Brenda. She's always been a bit optimistic about animal ownership. Remember when she got that goldfish and was convinced it needed a tiny castle? It ended up floating on its side within a week. Aye, that was a disaster. Though, to be fair, the castle  was  pretty impressive. But hamsters  are  a lot more work than people think. You’ve got the cleaning, the chewing, the nocturnal zooming… it’s a full-time job for a little fella. Exactly! My cousin had one, Kevin, and it escaped like, three times. Found him once in the biscuit tin, another time wedged behind the fridge. Tiny terror, that Kevin. But cute, I’ll give him that. Cute ‘til they start gnawing on your electric cables. Brenda’s got him in a cage that looks like Fort Knox, but I reckon Hammy’s already planning his escape route. Speaking of terrors… anyone else notice how many gingers there are about lately? Gingers? What about them? Just… loads! I swear, every other person I see on campus has red hair. It’s like there’s been a ginger baby boom. My grandma always said gingers were special, you know? Got a bit of magic to ‘em. Oh aye, the fiery temper and the lack of a soul, is that the magic? I’m only jokin’! My little brother’s a ginger and he's alright. Though he  does  burn easily. It's just genetics, innit? Recessive genes and all that. But yeah, I’ve noticed it too. Loads more than when we were at school. Maybe everyone's just bein' more confident rockin' the red. I think it's just a trend. I saw some influencer online raving about ginger hair dye, and suddenly everyone wants it. Though, it does suit some people, I admit. It's definitely a statement. A statement alright! My auntie Hilda always said gingers were descended from Vikings. Honestly, she's a font of information, Hilda is. Mostly made up, mind. But it sounds good, doesn’t it? A lineage of fierce warriors. Yer auntie Hilda sounds brilliant! Vikings with flaming red hair… I like it.

Right, that  should  hold Australia. Honestly, Dad, you're relentless. You keep funneling everything into Indonesia. It’s predictable. Predictable is good, lad. Predictable wins wars. You think Genghis Khan was messing about with fancy maneuvers? No. He just  rolled  over everything. Solid, unwavering pressure. Like me on this board. Oh, don’t romanticize brutal conquest, Brian. It’s a game. A very long game, admittedly. I’ve been planning my North American assault for three rounds now. She’s building up in Kamchatka, you know. Be warned. Mum, you're terrifying. You’re like a silent, strategic menace. Although… weren’t you saying something about needing another chocolate biscuit a few minutes ago? Strategic biscuit consumption? A biscuit break is  essential  for strategic thinking, darling. And this chocolate is rather good. Your mother always buys the best. Speaking of essentials, have you seen Aaron lately? He didn’t come to Christmas, did he? No, not since… well, since things with Emily finished. He hasn’t been the same. Keeps himself to himself. A shame, really. Good lad, Aaron. He’s…processing. And trying to avoid awkward family gatherings, I suspect. He sent Christmas wishes. It’s just difficult, isn't it? Seeing everyone else all coupled up. It is. Though being coupled up isn’t all it’s cracked up to be, trust me. Remember your aunt Susan’s disastrous foray into online dating? The man claimed to be a barrister and turned out to be selling timeshares in Benidorm! Oh, God, yes! And she sent him a Christmas hamper! Full of smoked salmon and posh biscuits! He probably sold them on. This is why I'm delaying settling down. Too much potential for…time-share barristers. Plus, having kids is…a big undertaking. That it is. It changes everything. Though seeing those little ones learning things… your niece, Lily, she’s already reading at five! Five! When I was five, I was probably still trying to draw a recognizable stick figure. They develop fast these days. Different world. Though I still reckon kids need a bit of good, old-fashioned risk-taking. Climbing trees, getting muddy… not just glued to screens. I agree. But the risk feels… different now. Everything's so over-protected. And then you get into the whole ethics of reproductive technology...a friend was talking about IVF and considering pre-implantation genetic diagnosis…it's mind-boggling.

…and honestly, the whole archaeology thing is just… fizzling out, innit? Like a damp squib. Professor Davies keeps talking about meticulous documentation and stratigraphic layers, and all I can think about is the mud. Glorious, Cornish mud is  way  more appealing than Lancashire bog. Lancashire bog has character, love. It’s… brooding. But yeah, I get it. You always were more beachcomber than digger. Thought you were dead set on finding King Arthur’s lost palace or something? That was fifteen-year-old me, fuelled by pasties and a particularly good BBC documentary. Now I'm nineteen, running on instant noodles and the creeping dread of student debt. What even  is  an archaeology job anyway? Museum curator? That sounds…dusty. There's heritage management, field work, even bits with the National Trust. Loads. But if it's not vibing, it’s not vibing. What would you do instead, then? Still fancy opening that little beachside cafe back in Falmouth? Selling clotted cream and overpriced postcards? Don’t mock the postcards! They're artisanal! And…maybe. It feels a million miles away now. Uni’s supposed to be about broadening horizons, right? Instead, I feel like I'm narrowing them down to 'jobs I definitely  don't  want.' You, on the other hand, seem utterly zen about being a future lawyer. Zen is a strong word. Terrified is more accurate. Honestly, having to read all this legislation is turning my brain to mush. Though, I did overhear some older students talking about celebrity law. Apparently, representing someone like Harry Styles pays for, like,  ten  student loans. Oh, brilliant. So your legal career hinges on landing Harry Styles as a client? That’s… a plan. A very specific plan. Though, imagine the paperwork. He probably has separate assistants just for organising his paperwork. Exactly! But worth it. Think of the holidays. The parties. The…free concert tickets. Speaking of things that are immensely stressful… Auntie Brenda keeps asking when  I’m  going to give her a grandchild. Oh, no. The baby question. My nan does the same. It's like, Nan, I can barely keep a succulent alive, let alone a human! Honestly! I pointed out I’m literally drowning in textbooks and she said, “You can do both!” Like it's some kind of multi-tasking superpower. It’s exhausting. Do you ever just… picture yourself running away to a remote island?

…and then Mr. Davies actually said, “The socio-economic impact of the Industrial Revolution wasn’t  just  about factories, it was about…people’s  lives .” Like, no kidding, sir. We all knew that. It felt so patronising. Seriously? Davies is always going on about ‘contextualising history’. You’d think he’d trust us to grasp the basic human element of it all. My group’s doing the post-war austerity period. It’s bleak. Everyone’s nan and grandad basically lived on rations for years. Austerity? That sounds… depressing. Ours is Victorian Slough. Which, ironically, is pretty depressing too, just in a different way. Workhouses, cholera, kids up chimneys… all a bit grim. Makes you realise how lucky we are, doesn't it? Even just having a phone to moan about school on. Lucky is one word for it. Comfortable, maybe. Though "lucky" feels…weird when you see stuff. Old Man Hemmings still sleeps in that doorway near the market, even when it’s freezing. My mum says he had bad luck with business, lost everything. Yeah, I see him sometimes. It’s awful. It makes you think about all this consumerism we’re bombarded with. Like, everyone’s after the latest trainers or phone, and there are people struggling to find a dry place to sleep. It feels…wrong. Totally. And it's not like  we’re  not pressured into it. My dad keeps going on about needing a new car. Says ours is ‘embarrassing’. Embarrassing for who? The neighbours? It’s perfectly functional! It's all about keeping up appearances. My mum's the same with clothes. Always worried about what people think. Though she’s brilliant, she just… gets caught up in it. It’s like everyone's building this perfect image, and pretending everything’s fine. Reminds me of that comic I was reading, ‘V for Vendetta’. All about fighting against a corrupt system. Bit dramatic, I know… No, I get it. Although, 'V for Vendetta' is hardly subtle, is it? It’s all explosions and philosophical monologues. Speaking of comics, have you seen the new ‘Saga’ issue? It's insane. Brian K. Vaughan is a genius. Not yet! I’m waiting for payday. It's expensive, those things. Though cheaper than a new car, I guess. So, back to the school stuff… I’m stuck on the ‘lasting legacy’ part of our project. What's the lasting legacy of Victorian Slough?

…and honestly, the whole recording process was a nightmare. Trying to get a decent vocal take when Mr. Henderson next door decides 3 PM on a Tuesday is the perfect time to practice his tuba? It’s beyond belief. He  knows  I do voiceover work from home. Oh,  no . The tuba? Seriously? Is he still at it? I thought he’d given that up after Mrs. Davies complained about the vibrations shaking her china. Apparently not. And it’s not just the sound, it’s the…commitment. He doesn't just  practice ; he seems to be auditioning for the London Philharmonic. Anyway, I had to keep stopping and starting, and then my throat just seized up. The client was very understanding, thankfully. Though I’m fairly certain I sounded stressed on the final edit. Ugh, that's awful. You deserve some peace and quiet. How's the physio going, by the way? Is it helping with your shoulder at all? You were saying it was giving you gyp last week. It’s…okay. She's convinced it’s all down to my posture. Which, possibly it is, after years hunched over a mixing desk. But honestly, I think it’s just old age creeping in. Everything creaks, you know? My knees are dreadful, especially in this damp weather. Feels like I’m ninety. Ninety? Dramatic much? You’re barely…well, you’re not ninety. It's just bad joints. My ankles are starting to complain whenever I walk anywhere. I haven't even done anything strenuous! Exactly! It’s the British climate. Perpetual dampness. It gets right  into  your bones. Speaking of bones… I was trying on that new dress I bought online – the navy one – and it just felt…wrong. Wrong how? Did it not fit? Well, it fit, sort of. But it highlighted all the wrong bits. I swear I’ve gained a stone. And I’ve been trying to be good! I even attempted that new 'glow-up' diet my niece recommended. Kale smoothies and quinoa… it was miserable. Oh god, kale smoothies. They taste like sadness. I tried one once. Once. I'd rather eat cardboard. And look, don't worry about a stone. Clothes are deceptive. Everything feels tighter after Christmas, doesn’t it? It does. Though Christmas was ages ago! That’s the terrifying part. I’m starting to think I need a complete wardrobe overhaul.

Right, I swear this Yorkshire pudding batter is  never  quite right down here. It just… doesn't  rise  like it does at home. Mum always said it’s the water. Cambridge water's too soft, she reckons. Oh, don’t even start with the water, Chloe. You’ve been saying that since you moved. It’s probably just your technique. Or the oven. Mine’s a beast, perfectly calibrated for soufflés and dramatic pudding inflation. Dramatic pudding inflation? Is that a technical term, is it? Look, I followed the recipe to the letter. Same flour, same eggs...it's the water, I'm telling ya. Doncaster water has  character . This stuff’s… bland. Character in water? You're hilarious. Honestly, I think you just miss being fussed over by your mum, and subconsciously sabotage every Yorkshire pudding. That's harsh! I do  not  subconsciously sabotage puddings. Though…she did always oversee the batter-making with an eagle eye. So, how was work today? Still battling spreadsheets and existential dread? You know me too well. Existential dread is a daily special. We’ve got a new client, a tech start-up. Urgent. Obviously. They need a massive product launch event organised by…next month. It’s a bit of a mess already, honestly. They’ve promised the earth but haven't a clue how to deliver. Oh, bless. Sounds like a typical Tuesday for you, then. And you’re the one who has the fancy postgraduate degree. They should be paying you double. What kind of launch? Big flashy thing? Sadly, yes. Big, flashy, vaguely ‘disruptive’… all the buzzwords. They want lasers, drones, influencers, the whole shebang. My boss is buzzing, thinks it’ll be great for the company portfolio. I just think it’ll be great for my stress levels. Drones? Really? It’s like everyone thinks their product is worth a James Bond opening sequence. You need a holiday. When’s your next one planned? Not until November, unfortunately. A long weekend in the Lake District with my sister. It's not exactly escaping to the Maldives, but it’ll do. What about you? Any trips planned back north? Mum been nagging? Always. She's already planning my Christmas visit. “Don’t forget your wellies, love, and a warm coat!” Like I wouldn’t. I miss proper countryside walks, I do. And a proper brew. This Cambridge tea just isn't the same.

Honestly, I still can't get over  Everything Everywhere All at Once . It was… a lot. Like, a beautiful, chaotic, existential lot. Did anyone else see it? I did! A couple of weeks ago. I felt exactly the same. I walked out of the cinema and just needed to  sit  for a good ten minutes. Processing. It was brilliant, though. Michelle Yeoh is just phenomenal. Aye, it was good. A wee bit too…fast paced for me, maybe? I prefer somethin' I can sink me teeth into, y'know? Give me a good thriller any day. Though, I’ll admit, the hot dog fingers were… memorable. Hot dog fingers! Oh, God, yes! That was genuinely bizarre. I think that’s what sold it for me, actually. The sheer absurdity. I watched it with Elsie last week – she was completely baffled. She prefers period dramas. Period dramas are  boring . Unless there's loads of fighting, like, proper sword fights. Or maybe some sort of mystery.  Everything Everywhere All at Once  was way better. It was like ten films in one. So confusing, but good confusing. I haven’t seen that one yet, it’s on my list though. I’ve been on a bit of a Wes Anderson kick lately. Re-watching  The Grand Budapest Hotel  for the, like, fifth time. It’s just…comforting, isn't it? Everything's so perfectly symmetrical. Comforting isn't a word I'd use for Wes Anderson, but I get what you mean. It  is  visually stunning. I’m more in the mood for something that’ll mess with my head at the minute. Have any of you seen  Annihilation ? That one stayed with me for days. Oh,  Annihilation  is a good shout! Properly creepy. The bear scene… I’m still getting shivers thinking about it. It's one of those films you need to watch again immediately just to try and figure out what actually  happened . Never heard of it, to be honest. Sounds…intense. I was watchin'  The Batman  again last night. Proper dark and gritty. Robert Pattinson was brilliant as Batman, a proper troubled soul.  The Batman  was good! Though a bit long, wasn’t it? Honestly, three hours for a superhero film is pushing it. Elsie nearly fell asleep. I'm trying to get her into  Pan’s Labyrinth . I think she'd love the visuals, but she's terrified of anything remotely scary.

Honestly, I think my feet are  still  recovering from Paris. Never again with the cute-but-absolutely-murderous boots.      Oh, don’t tell me they've claimed another victim? You and your fashion choices, darling. I told you sensible shoes were the way to go! How was it though, really? Aside from the foot torture?      Paris? How was it? Did you manage to see the Mona Lisa without being swamped by tourists? I heard it’s a nightmare.      It was… a lot. The Mona Lisa  was  a nightmare, actually. More elbows than art, honestly. But everything else was amazing. We did the Eiffel Tower, naturally, wandered around Montmartre – it was properly lovely. Though, I did nearly become a casualty on a scooter.      A scooter? What on earth happened? You know you’re a hazard on two wheels, even without Parisian traffic thrown into the mix.      Well, this one wasn’t  my  scooter. A rogue delivery driver cut me up while I was walking. I twisted my ankle a bit. It’s nothing awful, just a bit swollen and sore. Hence the dramatic sigh. And the hobbling.      Oh no! That sounds painful. Did you get it checked out? You know you’re terrible at looking after yourself when you’re busy having fun.      I iced it! I’m practically a medical professional now, clearly. No, honestly, it's fine. It's just annoying. It’s making unpacking even more of a chore. Speaking of chores, Mum, you’ve been amazingly quiet. Everything alright?      Just listening, love. Paris sounds exhausting, even from here. And you always end up with some sort of minor injury on holiday. Remember Brighton last year with the jellyfish?      Don’t remind me! I swore off the sea after that. Although, a jellyfish sting is… different. This is just pure clumsiness exacerbated by inappropriate footwear. Did you have a nice weekend, Mum? Did you manage to get any gardening done?      It was lovely, actually. Quiet. I caught up with Margaret from the school, you know, the history teacher. Her daughter just got engaged. It's all rather exciting. Though, honestly, she was going on  and on  about the wedding plans. It was a bit much.      Sounds intense. Weddings are always a stressful subject. I’m just trying to avoid thinking about Sarah’s hen do next month. She’s gone full-on Pinterest bride and it’s terrifying.      Oh god, Sarah?

Morning, Chloe! Just grabbing a coffee before the 9am. How was your weekend? Anything exciting happen? Mine was… predictably quiet. Mostly grading essays, honestly. Feels like they multiply when you’re not looking. Ugh, tell me about it! Grading is the  bane  of my existence. Mine was alright, actually. Went down to Chichester with my sister, Sarah. She’s trying to find a flat there; thinking of moving. It’s pretty, though a bit…beige, if you know what I mean? All those pastel houses. Beige is a good word for Chichester. I did my placement year teaching near there. It’s lovely for a day trip, but I could see myself getting a bit bored living there long-term. Is Sarah still…with Mark? Actually, no. That’s part of the Chichester trip – she’s scoping out places on her own now. They separated a few months ago. Apparently, it was pretty messy. Divorces are never fun, are they? She's taking it surprisingly well though, throwing herself into finding a new place. It's a big change. Oh, wow, I didn't know that. Sorry to hear it. That’s rough. Speaking of messy, did you see old Mr. Henderson practically having a meltdown about referencing in his BNC lecture last week? Honestly, half the undergrads looked utterly lost. Sometimes I think we need a mandatory module just on the BNC and how to  actually  use it. Henderson  always  looks like he’s about to have a meltdown. It’s his default setting. And you're right, referencing is a nightmare. I swear, half my sessions with retail staff involve explaining the difference between footnotes and endnotes. It’s just…not intuitive, is it? Though, at least retail has consistent rules. Linguistics… it's always changing. Exactly! And then they get confused about passives! “But why can’t I just  say  it normally?” It’s exhausting. Pay day can’t come soon enough, I need a serious caffeine injection. And possibly a weekend that doesn't involve staring at student essays. Amen to that. I’m already planning my next pay day splurge. Thinking maybe tickets to  Wicked . I haven’t been to the theatre in ages. I saw a production of  Les Mis  years ago – proper tearjerker. Are you a musicals person? I’m alright with musicals. More of a straight play kind of guy, to be honest.

Right, so one cup of rice to two cups of water. Seriously, it’s that simple. People overthink it. You’d think it was rocket science the way Mum goes on. Your mum just likes to  feel  useful, love. She’s always been a bit…particular about rice. Says it has to be ‘fluffy’. Mine never bothered, just slapped it on a plate. Though, honestly, even  I  used to mess it up before. It always ended up sticky. Sticky rice is the worst. It’s like…glue. Anyway, I’m making a curry tonight. You ready for a bit of spice? Not too much, I hope? Remember last time with the jalapenos? Don't remind me! My mouth was on  fire . A little spice is nice, but you went a bit overboard. I think I was drinking milk for an hour afterwards. This is why I usually stick to something simple, like pasta. Less risk of culinary disaster. Still, I appreciate you doing the cooking. It’s a nice change. No worries. It’s good practice. Plus, we’ve got that voucher for ‘Spice of India’ still, haven’t we? Maybe next week we can actually go out and  not  rely on my skills. Though, honestly, the takeaway stuff is always loaded with salt, isn't it? It is. And fat. Everything's swimming in it. Doctor was giving me a lecture about sodium intake last week. Trying to be healthy while looking after Leo is…challenging. He only wants nuggets and chips, the little monster. Though he did tentatively try a pea yesterday. Progress! Progress! That  is  progress. Right, water’s boiling. In it goes… See? Told you it was easy. We’ll put the lid on, low heat for about fifteen minutes, then just leave it to steam. While that’s doing bits, I’m gonna check the chicken. I swear, it was fine this morning… but meat goes off so quick, doesn’t it? Especially in this weather. It does. It’s the texture, isn't it? That slightly slimy feel… makes you shudder. Reminds me of…well, never mind. It’s a morbid thought. Reminds you of what? Go on, spill. Nothing, honestly. Just…seeing things when you're tired. Actually, it reminded me of when we went to that marine biology exhibit in London. All those jellyfish. They looked…fragile, but also kind of unsettling.

Right, so then Mr. Henderson, bless ‘im, actually  asked  if I’d applied for any jobs this week. Like he’s me dad or summat. I just… stared at ‘im. He's the one who keeps going on about "finding me passion"! What passion am I supposed to find when I've sent out thirty applications and heard nowt back? Oh, don’t even get me started on teachers and “finding your passion.” Mine were obsessed with it when I was picking my A-Levels. Like, yeah, brilliant, I’m passionate about sleep and avoiding early mornings, is that an option? How’s uni going anyway, are you stressing about applications yet? Uni's… looming. I've started lookin' at personal statements, but it feels so fake, you know? Like, “Passionate about societal change, driven by a thirst for knowledge…” Ugh. It's just words, innit? I’d rather be binge-watching that new true crime doc on Netflix. Oh, the one about the antique dealers? It’s a bit slow, but oddly compelling. Speaking of which, anyone fancy a break after this? I’ve made brownies. Proper gooey ones. Brownies? Now  that's  a passion I can get behind. Seriously though, this job hunt is draining me. It’s not even the work I mind, it's the constant rejection. It feels like everyone’s got it sorted except me. Even Liam's got a summer job at the docks! It's not true, plenty of people are in the same boat. Remember Sarah from school? She graduated last year, still working at the Co-op. It’s a rubbish system, honestly. They want experience, but how are we supposed to  get  experience without a job? It’s a Catch-22. Totally. And it's not like there's loads of amazing opportunities here, is there? Whitehaven's not exactly a hub of exciting careers. I’m half tempted to just move to Manchester, even though it’s expensive. Manchester’s good, but expensive is right. Have you looked at Liverpool? It's a bit closer, still got good energy, and the cost of living is slightly more manageable. Maybe we could have a day trip, just to scope it out? Aye, Liverpool's not a bad shout. I'd need to save up some coin first, though. Which is impossible when I’m surviving on mum’s cooking and the occasional tenner from me grandma.

Right, that were proper lovely, wasn’t it? Your roast potatoes are  always  on point, ANON. Seriously, you should open a little cafe, you’d be minted. Glad you enjoyed it, love. It’s nothing special, just a bit of practice over the years. And a good oven, I’ll admit. Though a cafe… that’s a thought. Bit much work for an old man, though, eh? Keeps me busy enough just pottering about. How’s the work going, anyway? Still wrestling with conference centres and demanding delegates? Oh, you ‘ave  no  idea. Last week were a nightmare. A tech conference, all blokes mostly, and every single one of ‘em thought they were a sound engineer. Kept fiddling with the mics, the lighting… one bloke nearly blew a speaker! I were running around like a blue-arsed fly, I were. Honestly, I need a holiday. Sounds stressful, that does. They always think they know better, don’t they? When they’ve never wired anything up in their lives. You need to learn to delegate, lass. Easier said than done, I know, but let someone else deal with the tech tantrums. Tell me about it. Management keeps saying ‘empower the team’ but then they get involved the minute anything goes slightly wrong. Honestly, it's frustrating. And I’m supposed to be good at this, I’ve got a degree! What’s the point of all that studying if you’re just running around fixing other people's messes? A degree gets you in the door, that's all, love. Real life teaches you everything else. And don’t beat yourself up about it. You’re a hard worker, everyone says so. You just need to find a way to switch off. You should take up something, something just for  you . Like what? I'm knackered after work, then I'm usually just… collapsing on the sofa. I tried joining a yoga class, but I just couldn't get my head round it. All that… breathing. Felt a bit daft, to be honest. Yoga's not for everyone, no. What about walking? There are some lovely walks around Cambridge, along the river. Get some fresh air, clear your head. I used to walk for miles when I was younger, down in Sussex. Cleared the cobwebs right out. That's not a bad idea, actually. I do enjoy a good ramble. But then I feel guilty for not being ‘productive’.

Right, operation clear-up is a go. Honestly, it looks like a bomb’s hit the dining room. Leo, honestly, did you  need  all those bread rolls?      They were good, Mum. And Jamie took three as well.      He's a growing lad, needs his carbs. Though I suspect most of yours ended up crumbled on the floor, Leo. You were attempting some kind of… bread roll juggling act, weren’t you?      No! I was… practicing my hand-eye coordination. For tennis.      Yeah, right. You nearly hit Mrs. Higgins’ cat last week with a tennis ball, pretending you were Federer.      Jamie! Be kind. Leo  is  trying to get better at tennis, and it’s good he’s active. Though, perhaps avoid the residential gardens for practice. It’s just… a bit much. Speaking of which, did either of you remember to put your rackets away?      In the garage. Next to Dad’s… interesting… collection of shaving things.      My shaving things are perfectly organised! I have a beard trimmer, different guards, balm… the essentials. Speaking of facial hair, did you see old Mr. Peterson down the road? He’s attempting a handlebar moustache. It’s… ambitious.      Oh dear. That sounds… a visual experience, to say the least. It rather reminds me of that history documentary we were watching last night. About… well.      Hitler? You mean the bit about the tiny moustache?      Yes, Leo. The bit about the tiny moustache. It’s just… a strange association, isn’t it? Sometimes things just… stick in your head. It’s best not to dwell. Anyway, moving swiftly on. Jamie, how’s the history project going?      It’s okay. I'm doing it on World War One. It’s just… loads of reading.      It’s important, son. Understanding the past is crucial. You learn from those mistakes, try not to repeat them. Which brings me to… Leo, are you still… ‘engaging’ with that girl on Instagram? The one with the heavily filtered photos?      Dad! I’m just… talking to her.      "Talking" usually involves more than just liking every single photo she posts, darling. We've talked about being careful online.      She’s nice! And she likes my tennis videos.      Your ‘tennis videos’ where you miss every shot?      Shut up, Jamie!      Look, Leo, it's good to be friendly. But be aware. People aren't always who they appear to be online. Don’t share too much information, and definitely don’t agree to meet up with anyone without telling us.

…and honestly, the state of that sideboard when it arrived! You’d think for eighty quid, you’d get something that  wasn’t  held together with wishful thinking and wood glue. I swear, I put a magazine on it and it wobbled like it was doing a little dance. Eighty quid? Blimey, Nan. That's…optimistic. You should’ve made them take it back. Did you at least get it from a proper shop, or was it one of those Facebook Marketplace things? Facebook Marketplace, love. She thinks she’s getting a bargain. Always has, that one. Remember when she bought that ‘vintage’ tea set that turned out to be chipped in about ten places? Oi! It had  character . And alright, yes, it wasn't perfect. But eighty quid for a sideboard is taking the mickey, even for second-hand. I’m going to have to get Dave to reinforce it, and he’ll moan for a week. Speaking of things needing fixing, we really need another run to the tip. It's overflowing again. The tip? Oh God, don’t remind me. Last time we went, it was like a scene from Mad Max. All these vans full of builders’ waste and people practically fighting over space. Tell me about it. It’s always worse on a weekend. Right, anyway. Have you heard anything more about Sarah and her family? She said her little boy was still poorly. Yeah, Mum sent me a message earlier. He’s finally on the mend, but it was a nasty bug. She was really worried, said he was properly floppy for a couple of days. Poor things. It’s awful when they’re little and you just feel helpless. Aye, you do. Reminds me of when young Michael - that's your dad, love – had whooping cough. His little chest was heaving, I thought he was going to burst. Took weeks to get over it. Oh, don’t start with the stories of childhood illnesses. Gives me the shivers. Did you hear about Brenda’s daughter, though? Apparently, she lets her sister wash her clothes. No way! Seriously? That's… weird, isn't it? Apparently! Says she can’t be bothered. Honestly, some people. Like, you’ve got a washing machine, use it! It's not exactly climbing Everest is it? It's the younger generation. Anything to avoid a bit of effort. I remember when we all helped each other out.

…and honestly, Mum, the whole thing has been a bit of a blur. They called me into a meeting, all very ‘restructuring’ and ‘difficult decisions’, and then just… told me. Redundancy. After two years! Oh, love, no! That’s awful. Honestly, after everything you’ve put into that place. I always thought they valued you. Were there any clues? Anything at all? None. Absolutely nothing. Everyone was acting normal. Sarah from accounts was even showing me pictures of her new puppy  yesterday . It’s just… so unfair. They’re saying they’re trying to streamline, apparently the project management team was ‘overstaffed’. Overstaffed! When I'm the one dealing with everyone else's mess. Well, it's their loss, isn't it? You're a bright girl, you’ll land on your feet. Have you started looking at other jobs? Is there redundancy pay? Yeah, I’ve had a quick scroll through LinkedIn, mostly just to see what’s  out there . There's… stuff. But nothing that screams ‘perfect fit’ yet. Redundancy pay is okay, enough to cover a couple of months, thankfully. It’s the uncertainty that’s getting to me. That's good about the pay, at least. Don't panic, though. Honestly, sometimes these things are a blessing in disguise. Maybe it’s a sign you need to do something completely different? Speaking of different, are we still on for Saturday? I was thinking we could go into Norwich, do a bit of shopping? Definitely! I need a distraction. Retail therapy is  exactly  what I need. Although, knowing me, I’ll just end up browsing stationery and feeling sorry for myself. Nonsense! We'll get you something lovely. Perhaps a new gym outfit? You’ve been going consistently, haven’t you? I'm proud of you for sticking with it. Mostly. I missed a session last week. The redundancy thing threw me a bit. Just couldn’t face the treadmill. But I’m aiming for three times this week. It's good to have something… solid, you know? Something  I  control. Absolutely. It's a good outlet. It reminds me of your Grandad, always needing a project. He’d be furious hearing about this. He always said you had a good head on your shoulders, just like him. He would. He'd probably be telling my boss exactly what he thought of the situation. He always did have a way with words.

Honestly, Mum, this spaghetti’s amazing. Way better than school dinners. Though, Mrs. Patterson tried to make us all learn Japanese phrases today. It was…weird. "Konnichiwa" and stuff. Why would we need to know that? Oh, bless her. She’s probably just trying to be…broadening, darling. And I’m glad you like the spaghetti. I’m trying to make it a bit more interesting than beans on toast every night, you know? Little Leo over there just wants to fling it everywhere. Goo! Spag! Leo! No throwing! Honestly. Right, Jamie, so, summer holidays. We need a plan. You’re already moaning about being bored after a week. Remember last year? You nearly drove me round the bend. I was  not  moaning! I was…expressing a lack of stimulating activities. And last year was different. I didn’t have Finn to hang out with then. He’s just started watching  Stick with Mick  and it's brilliant. Did you see it?  Stick with Mick ? Is that the one with the…orange fella? Leo seems to like it. He just stares at the telly and makes little noises. It’s practically babysitting. Though, honestly, I can’t understand half of what Mick says. It’s like he’s speaking a different language. No, Mum, he shouts a lot and then does loads of silly stuff. It’s epic. Anyway, Finn and I were thinking we might try and go swimming a couple of times a week. The Leisure Centre is doing cheap sessions. That’s a good idea. Healthy too. We can drop you off, maybe I’ll try and get Leo to a little splash time? Though, getting him  in  the water is another matter entirely. He’s a bit of a scaredy-cat. How about we get your Dad to help with a couple of jobs around the house? The garden's looking a state. Ugh, gardening? Seriously? That's…torture. Can’t I just practice my guitar more? I'm trying to learn that new riff by The Strokes. It's really hard. You can practice your guitar, darling,  after  you’ve done your bit with the weeding. It won’t take long. And it’ll be good to get some fresh air. Your Dad needs help clearing out the shed too. It’s a disaster zone in there. Fine, but Finn’s coming with me to the Leisure Centre.

Right, so the sheer  logic  of this film is astounding. He just… drove a motorbike  through  a market stall? And no one batted an eyelid?      Aye, well, it’s an 80s action film, innit? Logic took a holiday back then. They were more bothered about explosions and massive hair. Speaking of holidays, are you still thinking about that trip to Italy?      Yeah, the Italian thing. I am. I’ve been looking at flights again. Florence looks…expensive. And I'm trying to finish this short story, see. Deadlines are looming like a dodgy dentist appointment.      Dodgy dentist? You’ve had a bad experience, have you? I’m due one myself, actually. Procrastinating massively. My old man always said going to the dentist is the closest you get to flying without leaving the ground. Bit dramatic, that one.      Dramatic is his default setting, isn’t it? And yeah, last dentist I had... let’s just say “enthusiastic” doesn’t quite cover it. Nearly took my fillings out with his elbow. Anyway, Florence. Maybe Rome would be cheaper? Or somewhere a bit further south, you reckon? Need sun. Need pasta. Need to escape the constant drizzle.      Rome’s packed, always. Down south, definitely. Puglia, maybe? I had a mate who went there last year. Said it was dead beautiful. Loads of olive groves and ancient ruins. Plus, the food’s meant to be proper good. Better than what we’ve got here, anyway. No offence to the local chippy.      None taken. The chippy's a lifesaver. But you're right, Italian food… it's on another level. I was reading Italo Calvino the other day, actually. “Invisible Cities.” Absolutely blew my mind. It's… it’s making me want to write something completely different. More poetic, less… gritty realism.      Calvino? Sounds posh. I’m more of a Stephen King kinda guy myself. Give me a good scare, a bit of suspense. What’s this story you’re slaving over, anyway? Still the one about the bloke who collects bottle caps?      Don't remind me. It's… evolving. It’s still about the bottle caps, but now there's a conspiracy, a shadowy organisation, and a surprisingly dedicated pigeon. It's getting out of hand. I think I need a break. Actually, fancy a gig next week? I saw The Lottery Winners are playing at the O2.      The Lottery Winners? Not bad, not bad.

Honestly, this is lovely. Just… lovely to sit and actually  talk  without being interrupted every five minutes. How was school today, love? Anything exciting happen with the little darlings? It was… a day. Little Leo decided glitter was a food group, apparently. Spent half the morning picking it out of his hair and off the carpet. But other than that, surprisingly calm. They’re all getting so excited about Easter, though. Keeps asking about the Easter Bunny. It’s adorable. Glitter, eh? Sounds about right. They’re little chaos agents, aren’t they? Still, at least they're excited. Are you doing the Easter cake bake with them this year? Remember last year’s attempt? A complete disaster! Oh,  don’t  remind me! It looked like a Jackson Pollock painting, not a cake. This year, I’m pre-baking the sponges. They can focus on the decorating. Less mess, less stress. Speaking of stress… I've got some news. Oh? Go on, you’ve got that ‘big news’ face. Is it good news? Bad news? Somewhere in between? Good! Really good, I think. I applied for that Deputy Head position at the school, the one Mrs. Davies is leaving, and… I got it. Oh, Amelia! That’s fantastic! I’m so incredibly proud of you. You’ve worked so hard for this, you absolutely deserve it. Seriously, that’s brilliant. When do you start? Officially, after the Easter holidays. But Mrs. Davies is shadowing me for the next couple of weeks to help with the handover. It’s a bit daunting, to be honest. A lot more responsibility. But it feels… right. Daunting is good. It means you’re stepping up, challenging yourself. You'll be amazing. And it’s wonderful timing, actually. It means you won’t be completely swamped when we start thinking about… well, about the Christening. Right. The Christening. I’ve started looking at venues. It's harder than I thought! Everything feels so expensive. And Mum’s already got a long list of people she wants invited – half of Lichfield, it seems. Your Grandmother's always been… sociable. We’ll manage. I’ve got a few ideas, a nice little place near Tamworth. It’s got a good garden, which is important for the little ones running around. We don’t want another glitter incident at a formal event. That’s a good shout, actually. Somewhere with space.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of marking I had last week was  criminal . Sixteen year olds, bless them, but their essays on dystopian literature were… variable, to say the least. Half of them thought ‘1984’ was a dating app! Oh, darling, you’re telling  me  about variable work. I’ve been wrangling Year 5 with fractions. Fractions! It’s like trying to explain abstract art to a goldfish. At least dystopian literature  sounds  impressive. Fractions just… exist to torment primary school teachers. It’s the entitlement, isn’t it? They seem to think learning just  happens . No effort required. Still, better than dealing with parents, I suspect. I had one email last week… oh, don’t even get me started. Complaining about the complexity of the syllabus. Oh, the parents! A whole other level of chaos. I had a meeting regarding little Timmy’s… creative spelling. Apparently, writing 'becuz' is a valid alternative to 'because'. His mother was  adamant . I had to delicately suggest that standardized spelling tests existed for a reason. Delicately! You’re a saint. I’d have just shown her a dictionary. Speaking of chaos, how’s Barnaby? Still shedding enough fur to knit a second cat? Honestly, it's a full-time job. I vacuumed yesterday and already it looks like a yeti has been having a party in the living room. He’s driving me mad, but you know, he curls up on my lap when I’m marking and it’s hard to be cross. Little fluffy dictator, that one. How’s Winston doing? Still lord of the manor? Very much so. He’s discovered the joys of batting things off shelves. Particularly things I’ve just put there. I found him triumphantly perched on the bookcase this morning, surrounded by my collection of poetry. He looked… smug. I’m starting to think he’s judging my taste. They're so bizarre, aren’t they? Little furry bundles of judgement. Have you… have you started using that serum I told you about? The one with the hyaluronic acid? Oh, the one that promised to turn back time? Yes! And honestly… I think it’s working. Or maybe it’s just wishful thinking. My mum keeps saying I look ‘rested’. Which is code for ‘less tired than usual’, I suspect. No, seriously, it’s brilliant stuff. My skin feels… plumper. And it's not cheap, so it  has  to work, right?

Right, so Auntie Sylvia, you’re  still  saying this is the best charoset you’ve ever had? Honestly, it’s just apples and nuts mashed up. My nan used to put dates in hers. Much more… robust.      Robust? Liam, don’t be rude! It's a family recipe, passed down. Dates are… too chewy. This is  refined  charoset. Besides, you've had three helpings already.      Chloe’s right, darling. It's lovely. A lovely balance. Though, I do remember your grandfather, David, insisting on a splash of Manischewitz in his. Said it brought out the… spiritual notes.      Spiritual notes in apple paste? Sounds a bit much, even for Passover. Speaking of spiritual, anyone actually understand what half of this Seder  means ? I mean, I know the story of the Exodus, but all the symbolism… it's a bit much.      Exactly! It's like a history lesson disguised as a buffet. Though the matzah ball soup is always worth it, gotta admit. Proper comfort food. Reminds me of that trip to New York we took, Chloe. Remember that deli?      Oh, Katz’s! Don’t even  mention  Katz’s. I gained a stone just looking at the pastrami. It was glorious, though. They didn't mess around with portion sizes, did they? I’m trying to keep it a bit lighter now, you know, baking all day doesn’t exactly lend itself to a svelte figure.      You always were a champion eater, Chloe. It's a good quality, a very good quality. Brings people joy. Though, speaking of New York, I heard there's a fantastic new Italian restaurant that got rave reviews in the Times. Apparently, they specialize in regional dishes.      Italy? Now  that  I can get behind. I’ve been meaning to go back. Last time I was in Rome, I spent half my time just eating pasta. Though, I did try to be adventurous and look for something truly authentically Roman… ended up with tripe. Never again.      Tripe?! Oh, God. That is a culinary crime. You’re better off sticking to the carbonara. Or even better, let's go to Paris! I swear, French food is just  superior .      Paris is lovely, but overcrowded. And the bread… don’t even get me started on the bread. It's good, obviously, but it’s not challah, is it? Nothing beats a good, properly braided challah. I've been experimenting with a sourdough starter, trying to get that perfect rise…      Sourdough challah?

…and honestly, the pacing was just  awful . It felt like three books crammed into one. All that build-up with Elara and then…poof! Everything’s resolved in two chapters. It felt so rushed! Anyone else feel that way about ‘The Obsidian Mirror’? Oh, I completely agree, Fiona. I struggled with that too. I kept thinking, “There’s more to come, there  has  to be,” and then it just…ended. It’s a shame because the world-building was brilliant. I mean, the descriptions of Atheria were phenomenal. But the characters felt a bit…flat, don't you think? Like they were just vehicles for the plot. I’m the only one who actually  liked  it, then? I thought it was perfectly paced! Maybe it's because I binge-read it over a weekend – I just got completely sucked into the magic system. I did think Elara was a bit underdeveloped, though, I’ll give you that. But I preferred it to that horrifyingly overwritten fantasy novel we tackled last month. What was it called… ‘The Crimson Throne’? Oh, don’t even  mention  ‘The Crimson Throne’! That was pure torture. Pages and pages of description of embroidered cushions! Honestly, I started skipping paragraphs. Though, on the topic of books versus… everything else... I’ve been experimenting with eBooks more lately. It’s just so convenient when I’m travelling for work. Convenience is definitely a plus. I've got a Kindle, but I still prefer the feel of a real book. The smell, the weight of it in your hands… it’s just a different experience, isn’t it? I’m a bit old-fashioned, I suppose. Plus, my eyesight isn’t what it used to be and staring at a screen all day for work… well, it's not ideal to then do it for pleasure. I’m fully team eBook. My flat is tiny, and I was drowning in physical books. I can have literally thousands on my Kindle. And the built-in dictionary is a lifesaver! I'm reading a really interesting non-fiction one at the moment about the history of crochet… it’s surprisingly fascinating! Crochet, you say? You’ve taken up crochet now, then, Chloe? You’re a busy woman! I’m still stubbornly trying to master the cable stitch in knitting. It’s proving… challenging. Honestly, I think my tension is all over the place.

Right, this is a palaver, innit? Honestly, you’d think after all these years they’d have standardised these things. Feels like I need microsurgery just to get the SIM card in. You and technology, eh? It's not  that  bad, love. Here, let me have a go after. You're making it look like you're defusing a bomb. Though, considering Nokia’s history, maybe you  are  defusing something… a legacy, perhaps? A legacy of brick-like durability, you mean. Remember the 3310? You could’ve used that as a weapon. Still works, probably. This…this is all glass and wishful thinking. And Finnish weather. Not a good combination. Though, Joensuu  is  beautiful. Right, nearly…there! Oh, for crying out loud. It’s a lovely city, isn’t it? And look, you've got it! See? Didn’t need a degree in engineering. So, what are your first impressions of the Pixel 8 then? All that Google wizardry. A far cry from the Nokias of our youth. It's… sleek. Too sleek, probably. And the camera… well, the camera's frighteningly good. I took a picture of that reindeer statue outside, and it captured every single hair. It’s unsettling. Remember when phone cameras were just… blurry rectangles? Oh, absolutely! I had one that took photos in shades of green and grey. Artistic license, it called itself. But honestly, the camera is the main reason I upgraded. For fieldwork documentation, you know? My old phone just couldn’t cope with low light. Sensible. I just felt…obligated, almost. My old one was practically prehistoric. Kept threatening to spontaneously combust. Besides, you convinced me. You said it would sync effortlessly with all your Google stuff. Which, speaking of, I haven't a clue how to set up. That's where I come in. Right, first things first, Google account. Do you want me to walk you through it? It's pretty straightforward, but I know you get twitchy when they ask for permissions to access your entire life. Twitchy is a polite word for it. They want to know my shoe size, my favourite biscuit, and my geopolitical leanings, just to let me check my email! But yes, please. Guide me through the digital minefield. Alright, let’s start with the basics. You’ve got your Google account, password… good. Now, we’ll look at the security settings. Two-factor authentication, definitely.

Right, so Leo genuinely thinks a Malamute is a type of panda. A  Malamooche  panda, he called it! Honestly, Mum, it was brilliant. I was trying to explain what they actually  are  – huge fluffy dogs – and he just kept saying, "But it looks like a panda with legs!" Oh, Leo! He does have a… unique way of classifying things. A Malamooche panda! That’s going straight into the family story book. It's probably because we were just looking at Red Pandas on YouTube, wasn't it? He gets things mashed up in that little head of his. Panda! Fluffy! See? Panda obsessed. Speaking of which, have you seen Winston? He’s been hiding under your bed all afternoon. Probably plotting world domination, as usual. Winston! Oh, that little terror. He’s probably found another sock. Honestly, that cat… He’s the reason I need a new pair every week. Still, he  is  a good cat. Better than anything else I’ve ever owned, really. He is a good cat. Okay, let's talk about Finn’s birthday party. Have you managed to speak to Mrs. O’Malley about the community hall again? I really want to book it for the 18th. Yes, I did. It’s available! Relief. She said we can have it from two until five. It’s a bit pricey, but it’s the only place big enough for everyone, especially if we invite all of Finn's gymnastics class. Awesome! Two to five is perfect. Gymnastics class  has  to be invited. He'd be gutted if they weren’t. What about decorations? Should we do a superhero theme, or… maybe something Red Panda-related? For Leo's sake, obviously. A Red Panda theme might be a bit…niche. Though it  would  be adorable. Let's stick with superheroes. It's easier. We can get those superhero balloons and a cake with Spiderman on it. Leo can have a little panda somewhere in the mix, a tiny panda figure on the cake, maybe? Good compromise. Okay, superheroes it is. And the presents? I was thinking about getting Finn that Lego set he’s been wanting – the spaceship one? That’s a great idea! He's been going on about it for weeks. I was thinking… maybe a new board game? We haven’t played a proper family board game in ages. Something not too complicated, Leo's still a bit young for complicated rules.

…and honestly, Christmas at Nan’s was just  chaos . Proper chaos. Not like a nice, tidy, Hallmark-card chaos, but the sort where you’re dodging flying Brussels sprouts and Uncle Barry's attempting to karaoke. You know, the good stuff.      Sounds…intense. My Mum always went for a very regimented Christmas. Everything had to be  just so . Present opening at precisely nine, dinner at one, Queen’s Speech – no deviation. It was…predictable. Though, I do miss the adobo she'd make alongside the turkey. A little bit of the Philippines on the Christmas table, you know?      Oh, adobo sounds lovely. We always had a traditional Christmas, of course. Turkey, stuffing, the whole thing. But my mother, she insisted on making mincemeat from scratch every year. From  scratch ! It took days, and frankly, it wasn’t any better than the bought stuff, but it was the principle of the thing. A Bath Christmas, you see, had to be…refined.      Refined is putting it mildly, Margaret. Bath was practically a different country back then. Still is, if you ask me. All those antique shops and tea rooms. Give me a good, bracing sea air Christmas any day. Bognor Regis, now  that’s  a Christmas town. Used to be full of funfairs and arcades. Though, things have changed a bit since I was a lad.      Bognor Regis? I’ve never even been! Sounds…sandy. We were always more of a ‘wrap up warm and brave the wind’ kind of Christmas. Barrow’s not exactly known for its tropical vibes. Though, I did spend one Christmas in Spain with a friend once, after sixth form. That was mental. Sangria for breakfast, sunshine…a total shock to the system.      See, that's the thing, isn't it? Everyone’s Christmas is so different. My Lola – that's my grandmother – she’d tell stories about Christmases in Manila. They’d have ‘Simbang Gabi’ – nine days of dawn masses leading up to Christmas Eve. Can you imagine getting up  that  early? We just tumble out of bed when it’s convenient.      It’s fascinating to hear about different traditions. It's important, I think, to understand how others celebrate. I remember a student I had years ago, a young man from Pakistan. He explained how they celebrated Eid, and it opened my eyes to a whole new world. We  must  be more open to understanding different cultures.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of audio I had to transcribe this week was  criminal . Three hours of a solicitor explaining the intricacies of agricultural land disputes. Honestly, give me a good murder mystery any day. Did you two manage to watch the latest episode of ‘Shetland’? Aye, we did. Absolutely gripping, wasn't it? Though, I have to say, the pacing’s slowed down a bit this series. It used to be relentless. Still, Douglas Henshall is phenomenal. Though I'm slightly worried about what they’ll do without him now, aren't you? Oh, terribly. He  was  Shetland. It’ll never be quite the same. Though, I suppose they have to try. Speaking of gripping, I’ve started a new novel, a proper old-fashioned whodunnit, set in a decaying Cornish manor house. Very Agatha Christie. It’s research, you understand. For atmosphere. Research, of course! Though knowing you, Carol, it’s probably just a delightful excuse to indulge a passion. How’s it coming along? Are you torturing any potential suspects yet? Oh, absolutely. A dreadful housekeeper, a brooding nephew, a vicar with a secret…the usual suspects, you might say. It’s flowing nicely. Though the hardest part is remembering all the plot threads! I'm starting to write notes  about  the notes. Sounds exhausting! I’m glad my job just involves spreadsheets and filing. Less creatively demanding, certainly, but…less likely to give me headaches. Did you get a chance to try that new Thai place down the road, Sarah? I was thinking we could all go next week. Oh, that’s a brilliant idea, David. I’ve been meaning to. I saw a review saying their green curry is legendary. Though, realistically, I’m happy with most things involving noodles. What about you, Carol? Fancy a bit of spice? Oh, I adore Thai food. Though, I’m currently trying to cut down on carbs. Doctor's orders, unfortunately. I might just have a salad, but I’ll definitely join you both for the company. Although… I'm bringing my Kindle. I'm  right  at a critical point in my current read. Always with the Kindle! You'd think, being a writer yourself, you'd appreciate the feel of a real book. I do, darling, I do. But the Kindle's just so practical. Especially when travelling. And frankly, I can hold it one-handed while I'm stirring gravy.

Honestly, Doreen, this young chap, what’s-his-name… the one on the telly, talking about ‘digital footprints’ and such. Sounds like somethin’ a dinosaur left behind, don’t it? I mean, footprints are footprints, aren’t they? Digital or otherwise. Oh, Arthur, don’t get yourself in a twist about the television. It’s all just a bit of bother, isn't it? Trying to make everything sound complicated. It means what you do online, dear. Everything leaves a trace. Actually, it’s rather more nuanced than a simple ‘trace’, Doreen. It’s the aggregation of data, the patterns formed by online activity… predictive algorithms… Algorithms! Good grief, Harold, you sound like him! Sounds fearsome. I just want to read about the cricket, not be hunted by algorithms. I tell you, back in my day, if you wanted to be discreet, you wrote a letter and burnt it. Job done. Oh, Arthur, you and your letters. You always worried someone was reading your post. Remember when you were convinced old Mrs. Higgins was intercepting our cards? Well, she  was  a nosey parker, wasn’t she? Always peering over the fence. But this is different. This is… invisible. They’re watchin’ us through the wireless, that's what it is. Not quite, Arthur. It’s not sentient surveillance, despite what the tabloids would have you believe. It's more about companies collecting information to target advertising, or, in more serious cases, potential security risks. Now, I was reading an article about the importance of strong passwords… Oh, passwords. Don’t even get me started. I’ve got so many, I write them all down on a little slip of paper. It’s the only way I can remember them. Doreen, that rather defeats the object, doesn't it? It's like leaving the key under the doormat. You really shouldn’t do that. There are password managers available. They encrypt everything securely. Encrypt? Now you’re talkin’ in riddles again. I still use the same password I’ve had for twenty years. “Norfolk1945”. Simple, to the point. Arthur! You can’t possibly still be using that! What if someone gets into your email? What's anyone going to do with my email? Mostly it’s just chain letters about lucky cats and warnings about Nigerian princes. The point is, Arthur, it’s not about the content of the emails, it’s about the potential for identity theft.

Right, so we’re all agreed, Horace needs  sending off  properly, yeah? Twenty minutes of Horace is a good run for a spider, I reckon. Especially considering he took up residence in the server room.      Twenty minutes is generous, to be honest, considering the near-heart attack he gave Dave from IT. He’s still having nightmares about eight legs. But yeah, a proper send-off is vital. We can’t just…relocate him to the gardens. He's earned a little ceremony. Are we thinking drinks after work then?      Definitely drinks. And maybe a little… tribute? I was thinking a small, artistic rendering of Horace, perhaps made of paperclips? It feels fitting given his location.      Paperclips! Brilliant, Chloe! Though realistically, I feel like any artistic rendering will just end up looking like a vaguely spider-shaped mess.
