To understand the past so we don't repeat it. Though two minutes is a long time to sit in silence, I must say. It  was ! I kept thinking about football. Predictable. So, is anyone thinking about what they want for their birthdays? Yours is coming up soon, isn't it, Leo? I want that new gaming headset. The one with the noise cancellation. Hmm. We’ll see. And yours, Sam? You’re a little further off, but good to start planning, isn’t it?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of Year 6 SATS papers is  criminal . I’ve marked approximately one million reading comprehension answers this weekend. One. Million. Mummy, is a million bigger than a dinosaur? Oh, darling, a million is  way  bigger than a dinosaur. A dinosaur is… well, it’s big, but not  million  big. Dinosaurs had teeth! Really pointy teeth! They certainly did, Leo. Very pointy. Right, okay. Back to slightly less prehistoric concerns. Holiday planning. We need to solidify something. Cornwall again this year? You two seemed to really like Polzeath. I liked building the big sandcastle! It had a moat! And flags! I liked digging for treasure! I found a shiny shell! Excellent memories. It  is  lovely there. Though, remember last year and the traffic getting down? It was…character building. Character building means really, really long! That’s a very accurate assessment, actually. I was looking at some options – maybe a bit further west, towards St Ives? Or even… Newquay? Newquay has Adventure Island! On the telly! They go on rollercoasters and find stuff! They do, don’t they? Now, Newquay would be…different. More bustling. Less… peaceful. But it does have Adventure Island. Hmmm. It’s a tricky one. It would be a bit of a change from our usual rather tranquil Cornwall experience. Can we go on the rollercoaster? The really fast one? We’ll see, sweetie. We’ll see. We'd have to check how tall you are. Anyway, thinking even further ahead, I saw an advert for a V&A exhibition on pirates. It’s on next spring. That might be a brilliant day out for you two. Pirates! With swords?! Swords, treasure maps, everything! It sounds amazing. Although… I’m starting to worry about George's gluten intolerance. Remember that bakery in Padstow last year? The one with the beautiful Cornish pasties? I had to explain for the tenth time that he can’t have wheat. It’s exhausting. George doesn’t eat bread. He eats rice cakes. They’re yummy. They are yummy, aren't they? But it's not just the bread, is it? It's everything. Hidden wheat everywhere. It's a minefield. I think if we do Cornwall, we really need to do proper meal planning. And maybe a self-catering cottage rather than eating out a lot. Can we take the bucket and spade? Even if we go to Newquay?

…and honestly, Mr. Davies just  stared  at me. Like I’d insulted his mother or something. All I asked was if the deadline for the history essay could be pushed back a day, because of the cycling race on Saturday. Seriously? Davies? He's such a dinosaur. Doesn't he remember what it's like to  have  a life outside of dusty old textbooks? I swear, he thinks we just exist to absorb historical facts. Did you actually get an answer, or just the death glare? The glare mostly. Then a very slow, deliberate “No, Thomas. The deadline stands.” Honestly, I thought he was going to pull out a quill and parchment and demand I write it by candlelight. It's not fair! The Slough Sprint is a big deal. I’ve been training for weeks. You and your biking. I still don’t get the appeal. All that lycra… Anyway, worse than Davies is Mrs. Patel. She marked down my Maths coursework just because my handwriting wasn't "neat enough". Neat enough?! It's  Maths ! It’s supposed to be about the equations, not calligraphy. Tell me about it. She's obsessed with presentation. Remember what she did to Benji last term? Because he used a green pen? It's ridiculous. Speaking of ridiculous, have you seen Sarah lately? She's been completely glued to Leo. Ugh, don’t even get me started. It’s all anyone’s talking about. It’s like a full-blown soap opera unfolding in the sixth form common room. I heard Leo's mum is allergic to peanuts, which is…important to know, I guess, if you’re planning on bringing snacks around. Oh, wow. That  is  good to know. Right, no peanuts for the party then. Are you still thinking of having it at your place? Your mum’s pretty cool about stuff like that. Yeah, she said as long as we don’t trash the place. And no one sets anything on fire. Standard mum stuff. Though she did say something about “responsible behaviour” and “prefect monitoring” which… I’m dreading. Prefect monitoring? That’s awful! Especially with  Ethan  as head prefect. He's such a…well, you know. A rule-following robot. He'd probably report us for breathing too loudly. Honestly, he probably reports on people during movies. Exactly! He's the worst. Remember that time he told on Liam for having his phone out during film studies?

…and honestly, the roundabout at the A19 and the A1018 is just  criminal . Every time I go home, it’s a twenty-minute queue just to get onto the dual carriageway. You wouldn’t believe the carnage. Folks just pulling out, thinking they’ve got right of way. It’s a Sunderland speciality, I swear. Right, so still championing the chaos of the North East roadways then? I thought you were supposed to be used to it by now. Hertfordshire roads are…well, they’re  pleasant . Over-engineered, probably, but pleasant. Too many speed bumps, mind you. Pleasant? They're like little motoring obstacle courses! No, but seriously, it’s genuinely dangerous. It's not just aggressive driving, it’s the road layout itself. They need to redesign it. Anyway, enough about my commuting woes. How was the cricket on Saturday? Did you manage to catch any of it? It was good, yeah! Proper nail-biter. England were looking shaky there for a bit, weren't they? Root played an absolute blinder, as always. Although, honestly, I’m starting to think we rely on him too much. Needs some support from the middle order. Tell me about it. He's carrying the team. It’s practically a one-man show. Did you go to the ground, or watch it on the telly? Telly, sadly. Had a site visit down in Reading. Awful journey, actually. M4 was completely gridlocked. Got stuck behind a lorry carrying… I don’t even know  what  it was carrying. Just a massive, green, indeterminate blob. A green, indeterminate blob? Sounds delightful. See? Everyone has road issues. It’s a universal truth. Speaking of journeys, are you still planning on cycling to Brighton for that charity thing? Yep, still on. Training is…going. I did a sixty-mile ride last weekend. Legs felt it afterwards, I can tell you. Though, considering you cycle everywhere in Sunderland, I’m probably complaining about nothing. You're practically Tour de France material. Oh, don’t be daft. It’s just…it's easier than getting the bus sometimes, and cheaper. And the roads are flat-ish, so it's not  too  bad. Although, hills are definitely my nemesis. Are you getting decent kit for Brighton? Proper padded shorts are essential, honestly. I've got the shorts. Bought a fancy new helmet too. Trying to look the part, at least. My bike’s…adequate.

Honestly, this is a nightmare. Three different apps, all saying “temporarily unavailable” or “delivery times exceeding two hours.” What is  happening  tonight? I just want sweet and sour chicken, is that too much to ask? Right? It’s like everyone decided tonight was the night for a Chinese takeaway. I tried Golden Wok, no joy. Then Happy Garden, same story. They’re usually pretty reliable. Did you try Lucky Dragon? They’re a bit pricier, but they usually deliver even when everyone else is swamped. Plus, their dumplings are  divine . Seriously, worth the extra couple of quid. Lucky Dragon… hmm. I thought they’d upped their delivery charge since last time. I’ll check. Hold on… ugh, yeah, £4.99 for delivery! That’s practically daylight robbery. Four ninety-nine?! Seriously? When did that happen? Used to be two fifty. Greedy. Okay, okay, calm down, Scrooge. It  is  a bit steep, but sometimes you just have to pay for convenience. Remember that time we waited three hours for a takeaway from that place near the park? We were practically gnawing on the table. Don’t remind me! My stomach was making noises that scared the cat. But still, five quid… I saw Golden Wok have a deal on earlier, 20% off over £25. If only they weren’t currently experiencing the apocalypse in their kitchen. I’m starting to think we should just give up and make something. But I have zero motivation. And I really,  really  want chow mein. I had a terrible day at work. Chow mein is the only thing that will fix it. What happened at work, then? You were unusually quiet earlier. Oh, it was just… Mrs. Henderson decided that rearranging the stationery cupboard was a crisis that needed immediate project co-ordination. Seriously. An entire meeting dedicated to paperclips and post-it notes. You are not kidding. That sounds… spectacularly dull. No wonder you need chow mein. Okay, okay, operation Chinese Takeaway is still alive. Let me have a look. I’ve got the number for New City Cuisine saved somewhere... they do a decent Kung Pao chicken. It's not as good as that little place we found in Chinatown last year, but it’s a solid option. Ooh, Chinatown! That reminds me of that time we got hopelessly lost trying to find that tiny dumpling shop and ended up in a karaoke bar.

…and honestly, the waiting lists are getting absolutely ridiculous. Old Mrs. Higgins down the road, bless her, has been waiting six months for a hip replacement. Six months! She's practically crawling around the house. You see it at the hospital too, don't you, Sarah? The sheer  volume  of people, and the staff are just…stretched. You’re telling me, Klaus. Stretched is an understatement. I’m run ragged most days. It’s not just the volume, it’s the complexity of cases. More and more people presenting with things that should’ve been caught earlier, because they’ve been putting it off, or can't get an appointment. It’s a vicious cycle. And the paperwork! Don't even get me started on the paperwork. It feels like I spend more time documenting than actually  doing  nursing. It’s a systemic problem, isn’t it? I was reading an article the other day, comparing the NHS to the system in Finland. Apparently, they have a much more preventative approach. Invest more upfront, less crises to deal with down the line. Seems… logical. Though, I suspect the political will just isn’t there. Finland! Always held up as the gold standard. My sister did a study abroad there during her teaching degree. Said it was like a different world - everyone seemed…calmer. Less stressed. And the healthcare, she said, was just integrated, accessible. We're constantly firefighting here, putting plasters on gaping wounds. And the funding… it’s just not keeping pace with the demand. It’s the demand that’s the kicker, isn't it? Population is aging, people are living longer… which is good, of course, but the system wasn’t designed for this. Speaking of aging populations, have you had any more trouble with old Mr. Davies next door? He was giving me the earful again yesterday about the state of the garden. Said the weeds are “bringing the tone of the street down.” Oh, Mr. Davies. What a character. He’s convinced I’m deliberately letting my roses overgrow to block his light. I swear! I told him it’s just a particularly vigorous bloom this year. He just harrumphed and muttered something about 'youthful exuberance' and 'lack of respect'. Honestly, he's a lovely man underneath, but incredibly… particular. Particular is a polite way of putting it. He reminds me of my Großvater, actually. Very set in his ways.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of marking I’ve got this week is criminal. Essays on  Beowulf  – you’d think after all these years, students would have  something  original to say about a bloody Anglo-Saxon epic. It's all just regurgitated SparkNotes, isn’t it? Anyway, how are you doing, Mr. Davies? Still keeping well? Aye, alright lad, alright. Can’t complain, though complainin’ comes natural to a Liverpudlian, doesn’t it? This arthritis is a right bugger though. Feels like someone’s taken a hammer to me knuckles. And the telly’s been nothin’ but bad news lately. Did you hear about Old Man Hemmings down the street? Hemmings? No, what happened? I saw the police vans there a few days ago, thought maybe there was a break-in. Worse. They raided ‘im. Apparently, somethin’ to do with…well, they didn’t say exactly, but somethin’ to do with benefits fraud. Said he was claimin’ for things he weren't entitled to. Terrible thing, though. He’s a bit of a character, Hemmings. Always got a story. Bit of a moaner, mind you, but harmless. Really? That's…rough. I mean, things are tough all round, aren’t they? The cost of living is just going up and up. I was reading a report about food bank usage, it's frightening. It's not just people out of work struggling, you know? Working families too. Aye, it is. I remember when things were simpler. Not  easy , mind you. My da never worked a day in his life, spent most of his time down the pub, but we always had somethin’ on the table. Don’t know how folks manage now. Then you get all these… newcomers, comin’ over here. Now, Mr. Davies… that sounds a bit fraught, doesn’t it? Immigration is a complex issue. Complex? It’s bleedin’ obvious! They come here, take our jobs, overcrowd our schools, and then expect us to pay for it all. I’m not sayin’ they’re all bad, mind. My Doris – God rest her soul – she used to volunteer at the community centre, helpin’ the Vietnamese families who settled here in the seventies. Lovely people, they were. Worked harder than most. But it's different now, isn’t it? More of ‘em. It is different. But the idea that they’re simply ‘taking’ jobs… the demographic projections show a shrinking workforce.

...and honestly, the sheer  volume  of data we’re getting on pronoun usage is just… staggering. Like, I thought ‘they/them’ was becoming more normalised, but the regional variations are absolutely wild. You wouldn't believe how much pushback there is in certain pockets, even in younger demographics. Right? We're seeing similar patterns with the spoken data. It’s not just acceptance, it's  awareness  that’s patchy. I was interviewing someone from a rural area in Norfolk yesterday, and they genuinely hadn't encountered anyone using they/them pronouns before. Said it felt…confusing. Oh, that's fascinating, actually. We've been focusing a lot on lexical variation, but the pronoun stuff is proving really interesting too. Especially when you cross-reference it with social media data. There's a massive difference between what people  say  online and what they report in a formal interview setting. That’s the classic Hawthorne effect, isn’t it? People behaving differently when they know they're being observed. It's a constant headache for researchers. We deal with it all the time with our ELT materials - trying to elicit natural language use is a minefield. How are you guys managing that? Honestly? Badly. We’re trying to use more ‘naturalistic’ prompts, like getting people to describe pictures or retell stories. But even then, you get over-politeness, people trying to sound ‘educated’… It’s a nightmare for someone like me, trying to find authentic voice for publishers. I need the real grit! Tell me about it. I practically have to trick people into sounding like themselves. "Just imagine you're telling this to your best mate," I say. And even  then … I’m from Sunderland, you know? We're pretty direct. Trying to get that same honesty from someone from, say, Cambridge is… a challenge. Oh, Cambridge politeness is a whole other level. It’s practically a competitive sport. Though, honestly, I think it’s lessening with the influx of students from everywhere. I’m from Aylesbury originally, and even  there  things are shifting. It's interesting how strongly tied dialect is to perceived intelligence, isn’t it? I was listening to a podcast the other day about linguistic profiling, and it was pretty horrifying how quickly people make judgements based on accent. Absolutely horrific. And it’s often subconscious. It’s why we’re so careful about representation in the materials we develop.

…and honestly, the recommendations algorithm on iPlayer is just  awful  these days. It keeps suggesting me repeats of ‘Gardeners’ World’. Not that there’s anything  wrong  with ‘Gardeners’ World’, mind you, but I’ve seen, well, most of them. Several times. You’d think after years of watching documentary series on obscure historical farming techniques, it would twig I’m not desperately craving herbaceous borders. Aye, it's rubbish isn’t it? Mine’s obsessed with historical dramas. I watched ‘Victoria’ once, years ago, and now it’s permanently suggesting things with bustles and brooding princes. It’s like it thinks my entire life revolves around 19th-century monarchy. It’s infuriating, especially when you’re trying to find something genuinely  new . Precisely! It feels like it’s actively trying to keep you in a comfort zone, rather than, you know, broadening your horizons. Speaking of which, I was reading an article the other day about the difference in TV consumption habits in Japan. They apparently have a much more curated approach. Less "endless scroll", more dedicated programming blocks. Really? That sounds… civilised. We're just bombarded with content here, aren't we? Endless options, none of them particularly good. It's the paradox of choice, innit? You end up paralysed. Did you see that documentary about the Himba people in Namibia? The cultural differences are just astonishing. Their concept of beauty, for instance… completely different. I did! Fascinating stuff. The ochre paste, the elaborate hairstyles… And the way they view time. It really throws into sharp relief how culturally conditioned our own perspectives are. It’s a good reminder when you’re, well, stuck in the John Lewis cafe debating the failings of iPlayer. Makes it feel rather trivial, doesn’t it? Slightly. Though the failings of iPlayer  are  genuinely distressing. It’s a first-world problem of the highest order, I grant you. I was thinking about it the other day, actually, because I’ve been helping a colleague with some language learning material. She’s trying to teach English to a group of Syrian refugees. It’s amazing how much culture is embedded in language. Even simple phrasing. Oh, that's wonderful, but also… incredibly challenging, I imagine. Beyond grammar and vocabulary. The nuances, the idioms… I attempted to learn Mandarin for a while, utterly failed, but even in those few lessons, I realised how deeply intertwined language is with a way of thinking.

Now then, lad, are you sure you’ve packed enough for your trip to London with school? It’s a long way to go and you don't want to be borrowing socks from your mates, do you? Not a good look. Yeah, Gran. All sorted. Mum checked three times. Got spare everything. Even a portable charger… which is probably useless ‘cause I’ll be with people all the time. Three times, you say, Mary? Sounds like she’s expecting him to be living in the wilderness! London's not  that  dangerous, is it, Arthur? Though the traffic… don’t even get me started. Wilderness? Hull's more like a wilderness these days, Elsie. Though I suppose London has its shares of wild things. Pickpockets and politicians, mostly. Har har! Arthur, always the comedian. It’s just a mother’s instinct, Elsie. Remember when young Thomas went to Scarborough for a week with his scout troop? I packed him enough digestive biscuits to feed the entire beach. Scarborough? Seriously? That’s… a lot of biscuits. Well, he  loved  digestives! And I didn’t want him going hungry. Plus, you never know what the scout food is like, do you? Probably all dried beans and disappointment. Speaking of food, Mary, that Victoria sponge you made was absolutely lovely. Best I’ve had in ages. Though I do think you put a  tad  too much jam in. Sticky fingers for days! Oh, you always say that, Elsie! Just enough jam, I say. It's what makes it a proper Victoria sponge. You’re just a light-on-the-jam type of woman. I'm with Elsie on this one. A bit much, Mary. A bit much. Though, I ate three slices, so I shouldn’t complain, should I? You'd eat ten slices, Grandad. You always do. Now, now, young man. Show some respect. A growing lad needs his sustenance. Though I remember when  you  were little, always refusing your sprouts. Your mother nearly had a breakdown trying to get you to eat green things. Oh, that’s right! He'd only eat beige food for the first five years of his life. Chicken nuggets, chips, custard… a very peculiar diet. I was a connoisseur of beige! It was a sophisticated palette. Sophisticated, my foot! You were a fussy eater. Though, to be fair, your father wasn't much better. Couldn’t stand a vegetable if his life depended on it.

Honestly, this air is… well, it’s not Norwich, is it? But it’s a good kind of different. Still can’t quite believe we’re living in Beijing. No, no Norwich air, definitely not. Though I think after a London winter,  any  air that doesn't immediately freeze your eyelashes feels good. Look at this light though, it’s incredible on the Hutongs. Did you get a good shot of that doorway earlier? The one with the calligraphy? I did! Several. I'm becoming obsessed with doorways, you know? It’s the stories they could tell. I’ll show you later, I’m trying to curate the best ones for a little project. Speaking of which… I finally printed those photos from Sarah's hen do. Prepare for a serious assault on your eyeballs. Oh good! I’ve been wanting to see those. She looked… radiant, from what you told me. Was the karaoke as disastrous as you predicted? Disastrous doesn't  begin  to cover it. Aunt Mildred attempting Whitney Houston was a highlight, though. A deeply uncomfortable, yet hilarious, highlight. Here. Brace yourself. Oh my goodness… Mildred  really  went for it. And is that… is that Chloe trying to teach old Mr. Henderson how to twerk? This is gold. You really should have filmed it. I was too busy trying to prevent a full-scale glitter explosion. Honestly, it was mayhem. But worth it. She deserved a good send-off. It feels so bizarre she’s actually married now. Remember when she swore she’d never settle down? Vaguely. She said that about a lot of things. Like veganism and learning to knit. She commits fully for three weeks, then moves on. But she’s genuinely happy with Ben, you can tell. Makes you think… Don't you  dare  start with the ‘makes you think’ business. We said we were enjoying our… unrestricted freedom. I’m just saying! It’s nice to see people finding happiness, isn’t it? And it reminds me how long it’s been since we had a proper holiday. A  holiday  holiday, not a conference in Hamburg disguised as one. You have a point. We've been so focused on settling in here, getting the courses sorted, dealing with the endless paperwork… It feels like we haven’t had a break. Where would you even want to go? Hmm… I was idly looking at flights to Vietnam the other day.

Honestly, my head is  killing  me. I swear, Leo put something extra in those shots last night. Something… potent. Oh, don’t tell me you fell for the "mystery flavour" again? You  know  Leo thinks it’s hilarious to mess with people. My cousin, Mara, warned me about him. Apparently, he tried to convince her orange juice was tequila once. No, no, it wasn’t the juice. It was after, when he was doing those ridiculous Jägerbombs. I only had two, I swear! But then everything just… blurred. I think I tried to teach Ben how to do the Macarena? You and Ben doing the Macarena? I would have paid good money to see that. Did anyone film it? Please tell me someone filmed it. Ugh, possibly. Chloe definitely had her phone out. I'm dreading it surfacing on Insta. I looked an absolute state. My hair was…doing its own thing, and I think I was wearing your scarf? My silk one? Oh, no! That was a gift from my Nan! Honestly, you're lucky I’m not furious. But yeah, Chloe films  everything . It's both a blessing and a curse. Speaking of gifts, my mum keeps sending me pictures of the new puppy she adopted. It's a Shih Tzu. Ridiculously fluffy. A puppy! Oh my god, send me pictures! I’m a sucker for fluffy puppies. I keep trying to convince my mum we need a dog, but she says our flat is too small. Which is fair, I guess. It's barely big enough for  me  to swing a cat, let alone house a Labrador. It’s adorable. Mum’s named it Coconut. Coconut! She's obsessed with tropical fruit. It’s a bit much, even for her. It's distracting me from revision, honestly. I’m supposed to be doing my sociology reading. It’s so dense. Sociology, yeah, that sounds…fun. I'm trying to get through this Shakespeare essay. It’s about  Hamlet , but honestly, all I can think about is how miserable he was. It's making me feel depressed just reading it. I need sugar. This canteen food is looking… questionable today. Is that lasagne even remotely edible? Definitely avoid the lasagne. Sarah tried it yesterday, and she was regretting her life choices for a good hour afterward. Stick to the chips, they’re usually safe. Or that tiny packet of biscuits.

…and honestly, the audio quality on that one was  awful . Sounded like someone was recording it underwater. You wouldn’t believe the amount of ‘umms’ and ‘ahhs’ I had to edit out. It was a lecture on…Medieval tapestry techniques, of all things. Medieval tapestry? Good Lord. Sounds riveting. Though, anything’s better than another hour of competitive FIFA yelling, isn’t it, Arthur? Don’t start, Moira. It’s a strategy game. A  highly  complex strategy game. Young Leo's getting quite good, actually. He nearly beat me last night. Nearly. “Nearly” implying you let him win, I presume? You always were a soft touch with the grandchildren. Especially Leo. I did  not  let him win. He just… exploited a weakness in my defensive formation. A minor oversight. Strategically, it was brilliant on his part. Right. A “minor oversight.” Sounds like someone's ego has been bruised. So, about your mother, Moira? Has she confirmed the visit yet? We need to figure out transport. She’s not keen on trains, is she? No, still dithering. She called this morning. Said the rheumatics are acting up, and she's worried about the journey. Honestly, I think she just doesn’t want to leave Dublin. She’s been saying for weeks it's "too much bother." Rheumatics are a nuisance. But a weekend with us would do her good. Fresh air, proper food… not just those biscuits she's always sneaking. I told her that, Arthur. I said, “Mam, we’re making a huge effort to have you, and Leo’s so excited.” But she’s always been… resistant to change. And a master of guilt-tripping, let’s be honest. Perhaps I could give her a ring? Sometimes a neutral voice helps. I could emphasize how much  we’re  looking forward to seeing her, rather than focusing on the travel difficulties. That's a lovely thought, Sarah, but she'll see right through that. She knows you're my stepdaughter. She’ll assume you’re taking sides. She’s…particular. It’s that stubborn Irish streak, Moira. You got it from her, you know. Just less… deployed. Oh, I have my moments. Speaking of stubbornness, did you ever figure out who left the garden gate open last week? The sheep were having a field day with Mrs. Henderson’s prize-winning begonias. I suspect Leo. He was kicking a football around out there.

Honestly, this thing is  slow . I think I’m actively breaking it by just trying to load a PDF. It’s like it's deliberately antagonising me.      You and your technology. Remember when you spent three hours trying to connect that Bluetooth speaker? It needed  pairing , Liam. Just pairing.      That was different! That speaker was actively malevolent. This is just… sluggish. Maybe it needs a total system reset. Or throwing it out the window. I’m leaning towards the window, actually.      Don’t be daft, lad. Throwing a perfectly good laptop out of the window? Waste of money that is. You know what needs resetting?  You  need resetting. Too much screen time.      He’s got a point, Liam. You were up late last night, weren't you? Falling asleep with the telly on again? Honestly, it's a wonder you can string a sentence together sometimes.      It was a documentary about the mating rituals of the Bolivian tree lizard! It was fascinating! And I wasn’t  fully  asleep. More… in a relaxed, semi-conscious state.      Semi-conscious and snoring, if I recall correctly. Anyway, speaking of needing things fixed, did you ever figure out how to get that raspberry ripple colour right when you were painting the hallway? It looked… interesting.      Oh, don't. That was a disaster. It was supposed to be a pale peach, but somehow ended up looking like something a flamingo might… deposit. I swear, describing colours is a skill I seriously lack. “Slightly off-pink” doesn't quite cover it.      Flamingo deposits, eh? You’ve got a way with words, I’ll give you that. Reminds me of your Auntie Mavis. She once tried to describe the sea to me and said it was "a very large, moving puddle."      Oh, Mavis! She’s a character. Speaking of large and moving…have you seen the state of the bins? This bin strike is a nightmare. It’s starting to smell.      Tell me about it! I walked past someone’s overflowing bin on the way back from town this morning. It was attracting seagulls the size of small dogs. Though, Brighton is always a bit whiffy, isn’t it? Especially down by the pier.      Speaking of which, I need to figure out how to set up my mum’s new phone. She’s upgraded from a brick – I mean, a very old Nokia – to a Blackberry. She wants voice recognition.

Honestly, this coffee is  much  better than that place we tried near the market. Proper crema, you know? Reminds me a bit of a flat white you’d get in Cambridge, though nothing quite beats a Cambridge coffee, does it? Did you check the football scores? I forgot to last night. Man United were playing, weren’t they? They were, yeah. Lost. Again. 2-1 to Everton. Honestly, I'm starting to think Erik ten Hag needs to be looking for a new job. It’s just… disheartening. But this  is  good coffee. Proper good. It’s a small thing, isn’t it? A good coffee can actually shift your mood. I think I needed it today. Been a bit… bleak. Bleak? Oh, don't tell me you're getting hit with the SAD again. It's getting darker earlier, isn't it? Poland's not exactly known for its sunshine, even in summer. Are you taking Vitamin D? I swear by it, even back home. It’s just… everything feels a bit grey sometimes, and being so far from home doesn't help. Yeah, it's definitely creeping in. And it's not just the darkness. It’s… missing everything. My mum sent me a picture of Winston, and I almost burst into tears. He’s getting so big! She said he chases the postman now. A proper menace. I miss dog hair on absolutely everything. Sounds ridiculous, doesn’t it? Not at all! It sounds perfectly reasonable. Animals are grounding. I miss our garden, honestly. The birds, even. Remember old Mr. Henderson and his prize-winning roses? And that ridiculous collection of umbrellas he had by the door? He must have had twenty! Oh, God, Mr. Henderson! He always had a story about every single rose. And the umbrellas! It was like a museum. Anyway, work's been… draining. I’ve got this student, Tomasz, who’s lovely, but he’s really struggling with the conditionals. I feel so responsible for him doing well in his exam. It’s ridiculous, isn’t it? They pay for a service, it’s not  my  fault if he doesn’t revise. It’s not ridiculous. You're a good teacher, you care. It's natural to feel invested. I used to get like that with my TEFL students. Even now, with just the odd private lesson, I worry about them. Actually, talking of work… or the lack thereof on my part… I had a message from Amelia yesterday.

Right, honestly, this gravy is a disaster. It's like wallpaper paste. Anyone got any tips? I swear, cooking for more than five people is beyond me. It's a whole different ball game to a Pot Noodle, innit? Dunno much about gravy, love. I’m more of a ‘chuck it all in and hope for the best’ kinda chef. Though, speaking of disasters, you wouldn’t  believe  the day I’ve had on site. Bricklaying in this heat… absolutely knackering. And old man Hemmings nearly took my head off with a rogue scaffolding pole. Oh, don’t even  start  on Hemmings. He’s a menace. Honestly, the amount of near misses on that site… you need hazard pay, Leo. And Amelia, honestly, gravy isn't  that  hard. You just need a good stock cube and a bit of patience. Though, I’m more worried about the state of your outfit. That floral dress… is that new? State of my outfit? What’s wrong with my dress? It’s vintage! Found it in a charity shop in Doncaster. It’s proper retro. And yes, it’s new  to me . And patience? Patience is not a virtue I possess, especially when gravy is involved. I’m a Conference and Events Co-ordinator, not Mary Berry! I deal with stressed-out speakers and demanding clients, not roux and reductions. Doncaster, eh? Sounds a long way from Cambridge. Always pictured you lot up north with… well, flat caps and whippets. No offence. Whippets? Seriously? We’ve got culture up north, you know. And proper tea rooms. None of this Pret-a-Manger nonsense. Though, I’ll admit, I miss a decent Yorkshire pudding down here. Finding one that isn’t soggy is a proper quest. You're both hopeless. Leo, you're concerned about whippets and Amelia, you’re mourning the loss of a Yorkshire pudding. Meanwhile, I'm trying to organise a team-building exercise and my boss is breathing down my neck about production targets. It’s chaos. And dating apps are just as bad. Honestly, it’s like everyone’s just looking for a project, not a partner. Dating apps… yeah. Tried ‘Bumble’ for a week. Got matched with a girl who wanted to discuss the socio-political implications of garden gnomes. Seriously? I just want someone to watch the footy with and maybe share a pizza. It’s not rocket science.

Beautiful afternoon, innit? Though I do wish they’d do something about these benches. Always sticky. And honestly, the layout’s a bit… haphazard. Could be so much more with a bit of proper landscaping. All these lime trees crammed together, it’s a bit much. Haphazard is a good word for it, actually. Feels like they just  added  things over time, rather than designed it. Remember Ms. Chen and Mr. Li, when they came over last year? They were utterly baffled by it. Kept asking if it was supposed to look… naturalistic. Naturalistic chaos, more like. They were lovely, though. Bit obsessed with pandas, weren’t they? Everything led back to pandas. “Is this park good for pandas?” “Does London have many pandas?” Oh, definitely. And then they started talking about bears in China. Apparently, they're making real efforts to reintroduce them to certain areas. It's amazing, really, considering how much of the landscape has been…altered. Reminded me of that documentary we watched about the wildlife reserves in Sichuan province. Sichuan, yeah! Stunning landscapes. Although, travelling through rural China... that's a different story. Some of those roads… I wouldn’t attempt it. Remember Dave, from the department? He booked a self-drive tour. Said it was terrifying. Apparently, the local driving style is… enthusiastically optimistic. Optimistic is polite. I heard it's more like a free-for-all. Still, the scenery must be incredible. I've always wanted to go to Tibet. Though getting a permit is a nightmare. Nightmare is an understatement. Speaking of travel, thinking of a weekend away. Fancy getting over to the Isle of Wight? Bit of a trek, though. Trains and ferries... Potentially. Though honestly, I’d rather a quiet weekend in Devon. Just wandering around, visiting little pubs… less faff. And the food’s better. London food is alright, but you can't beat a proper Devon cream tea. Though, they do seem to be getting stingy with the salt these days. Everything’s bland! You’re telling me! I asked for extra salt on my chips the other day and the bloke looked at me like I’d asked for the moon. Anyway, how’s that research going? Still battling with Dr. Albright over methodology? Don’t even get me started. She wants me to completely rework the statistical analysis. Says it’s “not rigorous enough”. It's infuriating.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of data is mental. Like, I thought my undergrad dissertation was a lot, but this is a whole different kettle of fish. Thousands of interviews, transcribed, all needing tagging for linguistic features. It’s just… endless. Wow, sounds intense. Still, good job landing that straight out of uni, eh? Corpus Administrator sounds…proper important. What  is  a corpus, actually? I mean, I know it's something to do with language, but… Aye, I was chuffed to get it. And it  is  important! A corpus is just a big collection of language, like texts or speech. We're building one specifically for Northern English dialects, which is why they hired me – being from Sunderland and all. It’s about documenting how people  actually  speak, not how grammar books say they should. Right, makes sense. So you're like… preserving a way of life, linguistically speaking? That's pretty cool. My lot down south are bad enough just with different accents  within  Hertfordshire, let alone thinking about the whole North-South divide. Exactly! It's more than just accents too, it’s grammar, word choice… the lot. Like, do you know how many different ways there are to say “how much”? Down here, we’ve got “how much is it?”, “how much does that cost?”, “how much’s that?”, “how much will that be?”… it goes on. And it changes depending on who you’re talking to and what you're talking about! Blimey. I probably just say “how much?” and expect to be understood. Maybe I'm culturally insensitive. Don’t be daft! You’re not culturally insensitive. It’s just… different. That’s the whole point of the corpus. Anyway, that’s what I’ve been buried under for the past three weeks. Speaking of buried, are we still on for your mum’s on Saturday? Absolutely. She’s already planning the roast. Said she's attempting a Yorkshire pudding for you, knowing you’re from the North. Prepared to be… impressed or horrified. She’s a bit hit or miss. Oh, posh! Bless her. I do love a good Yorkshire pud. She doesn't have to go overboard, y’know. I’m just glad to have a roast, especially one that isn’t me cooking it. Last time I tried, it ended up looking like something the cat dragged in. I can imagine. You and cooking don’t really mix, do they?

Right, so then Brenda – you remember Brenda from uni, always wore those massive scarves? – she  insists  her cat, Winston, is psychic. Says he predicted her boyfriend dumping her. Honestly. Psychic cat, eh? Sounds a bit… optimistic, doesn’t it? Probably just smelled the breakup coming, cats are good at that sort of thing. Sensing tension and all that. Oh, Brenda. She was always a bit… eccentric. Though, speaking of sensing things, I really thought Mark was going to pop the question on holiday. He was acting so strange, all secretive with his phone. Turned out he was just organising a surprise birthday party for his mum. Aw, that's a bit disappointing. Were you hoping for a ring, then, Liv? I don’t  know . It's complicated. We’ve been together three years, and everyone keeps asking. He’s lovely, really he is, but… I don’t know if he  gets  me, if that makes sense. He's very… practical. Practical’s good! Means he’ll always have a job, put food on the table. My old man always said, “Get yourself a practical girl, son.” Never listened, obviously. You and your string of… adventures, Liam. Honestly, you’ve got the attention span of a goldfish. Anyway, Liv, you’re right to question it. Don't just settle 'cause it's comfy. It's your life, innit? That’s what my mum keeps saying, but it’s hard, you know? It’s not like he’s  bad  to me. He just… doesn't understand my work, for example. I spend all day firefighting production issues, trying to optimise everything, and he just looks at me blankly when I explain it. He thinks I just… shuffle papers. Oh, I know that feeling. Trying to explain my job to me gran is a nightmare. She thinks 'conference and events' just means 'making tea and putting out biscuits'. It’s a lot more than that, love. A  lot  more. Especially when something goes wrong - like the time the AV system completely died at the CEO’s keynote… Sounds stressful. I'm just glad I work with me hands. If something breaks, I fix it. Simple as that. Though, I did spend all last week unblocking drains at that new build site. That weren't glamorous. At least it’s tangible. I feel like I’m constantly problem-solving abstract issues. And then, this week, I’ve got a terrible cold.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of emails already this morning is making me question all my life choices. It’s like everyone decided 8:30am was the perfect time to collectively lose their minds. Ugh, mornings. They’re universally awful, aren’t they? Especially work mornings. What’s prompted the email avalanche? Another crisis with the Henderson account? Worse, actually. Old man Peterson decided  now  is the time to ask for a full report on Phase 3, despite it being signed off three weeks ago. Like, seriously? It felt deliberately passive-aggressive. He barely acknowledges my existence usually, then suddenly wants granular detail. Peterson. The human equivalent of beige. He does that, doesn't he? Thinks keeping people on their toes is good management. It’s just… undermining. Did you at least tell Sarah? She deals with him more regularly. I did. She just laughed and said, “Welcome to the Peterson experience.” Apparently, he pulled the same thing with her last month, demanding a breakdown of the budget for the stationery cupboard. The  stationery cupboard , Liv! Oh, he's something else. Honestly, sometimes I think my job is less stressful. Though, yesterday was… a lot. Young Ben was having a really rough patch. Admitted he’d been self-harming again. Oh, no. Poor Ben. How is he doing now? Have you managed to get him the support he needs? We’ve got him scheduled for a longer session with Dr. Davies, and I’ve looped in his family. It's just heartbreaking. He’s such a bright kid, but just completely lost at the moment. It reminds you why you do the job, you know? Even when it’s completely draining. Absolutely. It must be so tough, constantly being there for everyone else. You're amazing, Liv, seriously. How do you even switch off? That’s the million-dollar question, isn’t it? Badly, mostly. Actually, speaking of switching off, I need to tell you something… It’s about Mark. Oh? What’s happened? Don’t tell me he’s started leaving his socks everywhere  again ? It’s a fundamental lack of respect, I tell you! Worse, actually. We… we broke up. Liv! No way! What? How? You seemed… good. Really good. Last week, you were practically glowing. I thought we were, too. He just… well, he said he needed “space”. Apparently, “space” translates to spending all weekend with Chloe from his book club.

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt a bit…flat. Like, the villain wasn't  evil , you know? Just…disagreeable. Old Man Hemlock in the story just wanted the village to stick to tradition. That’s not exactly world domination, is it? But he  made  little Timmy trip over! And he told Mrs. Gable her prize-winning marrow wasn’t very prize-winning! That IS evil! Oh, darling, that’s just being grumpy. There’s a difference between grumpy and evil. Real evil… Well, think about the stories your Grandpa used to tell, about Black Shuck. Black Shuck’s awesome! He has red eyes! And he’s all… shadowy! He is, isn’t he? A truly terrifying legend. Now,  that's  a proper villain. He wasn't just objecting to jam-making competitions, was he? He was a harbinger of doom! A spectral hound! A harbinger of…what now? Is that like a postman but for bad things? Sort of! It means he warned people something bad was going to happen. Old folk tales are full of them. And Black Shuck isn’t unique. Almost every county has its own version of a phantom black dog. They represent… well, they represent the darkness, the things we fear. Like spiders? Yes, even spiders! And disappointment. And losing your favourite toy. Things that feel really scary when you’re little. But evil, the  really  nasty stuff… that’s about deliberately wanting to cause harm. It's about taking pleasure in other people's suffering. So Old Man Hemlock didn’t  want  Timmy to fall over? I don’t think so, love. He just didn’t approve of Timmy’s modern scarecrow design. He thought it wasn’t… traditional enough. It was a silly disagreement, blown out of proportion. Gran says the fairies can be evil too. If you don’t leave them a saucer of milk. Your Gran is very wise. The fairies are… complicated. They’re not always fluffy-winged and kind. They can be mischievous, and if you disrespect them, yes, they can play tricks. It’s about respecting the old ways, respecting the unseen world. That’s what a lot of those stories are about. Can we read the Black Shuck story again tonight? The one with the church and the storm? Absolutely. But maybe we’ll read the one about Jack and the Giant afterwards? Although, is the Giant really evil?

Right, so, the school filming trip. Apparently, it wasn't  just  a trip to Cambridge. It was a full-on historical re-enactment, wasn't it? You were telling me they were dressing up?      Oh, it was brilliant. Utter chaos, naturally, but brilliant. They went to the Fitzwilliam Museum and did scenes pretending to be Victorian art critics. Honestly, little Maisie was  fierce  giving her opinions on the Pre-Raphaelites.      I  was  fierce! Mrs. Davies said I had very strong opinions.      I was a king! A very important king! With a crown!      A king, eh? Good for you. Sounds…energetic. Did you manage to get any decent photos? I’m hoping for blackmail material for their 18th birthdays.      Plenty! Although mostly blurry action shots of them running around. It was freezing though, even for Cambridge. I was layering everything I owned. Was it warm enough for you last night? I had the heating on a bit.      Yeah, I was fine. Maybe a little chilly at first, but I put another jumper on. Speaking of chilly, how’s your leg, Maisie? Still sore from yesterday?      It's better now. I bumped it on the table at school. It really hurt, but Leo gave me a plaster with dinosaurs on.      I helped pick the dinosaur plaster! A T-Rex is the best!      Good lad, Leo. Always looking out for his sister. It’s good it’s feeling better. Honestly, children are just walking accidents. Right, I'm thinking I need to get myself back to the gym. I've completely fallen off the wagon.      Oh, are you? I was thinking the same. Need to counteract all this…domestic bliss. I’ve been avoiding it, frankly. The thought of those running machines… it’s just soul-destroying.      It  is  a bit grim, isn't it? But I feel so much better afterwards. And they've got a new spinning class. I might give that a go. It's less staring at a wall while pretending to run.      Spinning, hmm. Tempting. Though I think I’d prefer to lift some weights. Or, you know, strategically walk around the supermarket pretending I’m doing laps.      Very strategic. You’re hopeless. You know what I fancy after the gym though? A doughnut. A proper one, with jam and sugar.      Now  that  is motivation. We could… swing by that new bakery on the way home? The one everyone's been talking about?

…and honestly, Arthur, the physio’s given me a whole new set of exercises. It's all about core strength, apparently. Core strength! At my age! Feels like I’m training for the Olympics, not just trying to bend down to tie my shoelaces. Core strength is important, Reginald, even at our vintage. Keeps the biscuit tin safe from raiding, you know. Speaking of which, this Earl Grey is decent. Much better than the stuff Marjorie buys – tastes like dishwater, honestly. Marjorie always did have…economical tastes. Still, she’s a good woman. Though I do worry about her, she’s been awfully quiet lately. Lost a lot of weight too. Says it’s just “not enjoying her food,” but… you know how these things are. Aye, I do. It’s unsettling when they change. My Maureen – bless her – started rearranging the cutlery drawer alphabetically.  Alphabetically , Reginald! Said it brought her order. It was a sign, I tell you, a sign. Good heavens. That  is  a sign. Sounds like she needed a bit of distraction. Did you…did you manage to talk to her about it? Tried. Ended up with a lecture on the benefits of a structured life. Said I was too chaotic. Me! Running a business for forty years requires a bit of chaos, wouldn’t you say? Anyway, enough about my troubles. What about this Green Party nonsense I’m hearing? They're wanting to pedestrianise North Street! Can you imagine? Ah, yes, the Green Party. A bit radical for Brighton, perhaps. Though, I have to admit, their ideas on sustainability are… sensible. I’ve been trying to cycle more often, you know. Though the hills around here make it a bit of a challenge for an old boy like me. Cycle? You? Reginald, last time I saw you on a bicycle you were seven years old and heading straight for Mrs. Higgins’ rose bushes! No, no, pedestrianising North Street is madness. It'll kill the shops. People need to  drive  to do their shopping. Especially those bringing back treasures from boot sales. Boot sales, now you’re talking! I found a first edition of Kipling last week! Only cost me a fiver. The chap didn't realise what he had. A fiver? Honestly, you have a knack, Reginald. I mostly end up with chipped teacups and moth-eaten cardigans. Though I did get a decent set of gardening tools once.

…and honestly, the variegated string of pearls is  thriving . I nearly binned it last winter, thought it’d had it, but no. Just needed a bit more humidity, apparently. You wouldn’t believe the YouTube rabbit hole I went down on succulent care. YouTube rabbit holes are my nemesis, especially when I’m supposed to be writing about the socio-economic impact of post-industrial policy. It’s a bit harder to find a ten-minute guide to ‘Optimising Your Thesis’ than ‘Propagating Pothos’. Tell me about it. My job is ‘research’ but half of it is just googling things I don’t understand. Speaking of googling…have you seen what’s happening with Shein’s fast fashion practices? It’s absolutely scandalous. I was trying to justify a little browse, thinking 'oh, a tenner for a dress', but then I read about the working conditions… Don't even go there. I tried to explain the environmental impact of that stuff to my mum last week and she just said, “Well, it’s cheap, isn’t it?” It's infuriating. It’s like they don’t see the human cost. I’ve started trying to buy secondhand more, or at least look for ethical brands. Though ethical and affordable rarely go hand-in-hand. Exactly! It’s a privilege to be able to make those choices. Which reminds me, have you spoken to your financial advisor recently? I'm trying to figure out this ISA thing and it’s making my head spin. I feel like they’re deliberately using jargon to confuse me. Oh, don’t get me started on financial advisors. Mine keeps suggesting I invest in… well, frankly, it’s stuff that sounds like it was dreamt up by someone who watches too much  Wolf of Wall Street . I'm currently favouring simply shoving everything into a high-yield savings account and hoping for the best. Boring, but less likely to end in disaster. That sounds sensible, actually. Although slightly depressing. It feels like everything is a gamble these days. Even buying a pasty. Remember those awful pasties they served at that conference in Manchester? Oh God, yes. That was an abomination. Grey, lukewarm, vaguely meat-flavoured… Honestly, it was an insult to Cornwall. You can’t just  do  a pasty. It's an art form. A proper Cornish pasty is a thing of beauty. It's a cultural heritage!

Honestly, Mum’s garden is looking  amazing  this year. She’s really outdone herself with the roses. It’s a lovely change from marking student essays on the socio-political implications of… well, honestly, I’ve forgotten what they were on now. Too much postmodern theory for one week, I think. Sounds rough. Still battling the existential angst of undergraduates, I presume? Mine were dissecting the symbolism in  Blue Peter  this morning. Actual, serious academic discussion about a children’s television show.  Blue Peter ?! Seriously? What did they find? Hidden communist messages? Not quite. Apparently, the make segments subtly reinforced societal gender roles. One student had written a fifteen-page paper on it. Fifteen! I did mention, rather pointedly, that I had a Blue Peter badge myself, and I turned out… relatively well-adjusted. Good for you! Though, I suppose even nostalgia can be deconstructed. Did you tell them about the sheer prestige of earning a badge? It was  everything  when we were kids. I remember being so determined to send in a worthy creation. I did. They looked at me like I’d grown a second head. Everything's disposable now, isn't it? No sense of earned achievement. It's all instant gratification. Which brings me to another point - I was reading an article about the increasing violence in children’s TV. Even animated shows are getting… gritty. Oh, don’t get me started. I switched channels the other day and there was a cartoon with a character actively plotting to overthrow a government! It was aimed at six-year-olds! It’s ridiculous. And then people wonder why behavioural issues are on the rise. Exactly! It’s all desensitisation. It’s the opposite of, say, David Attenborough gently introducing us to the complexities of the natural world. Speaking of which, did you see that documentary about orcas the other day? The intelligence is breathtaking. Oh, yes! The ones hunting sharks? Absolutely terrifying, but also… fascinating. It's a completely different kind of intelligence to anything we understand. Reminded me of that squatter community we stumbled across in Brighton a few years back. They were incredibly resourceful, building entire systems of living off-grid. Now  that  was an experience. I'm still not entirely sure whose garden we were technically trespassing in. But they  were  impressively self-sufficient. Though, slightly unsettling how comfortable they seemed with bending the rules.

…Honestly, Doreen, this tea’s a bit weak, innit? Not like Maisie used to make. She’d brew it strong enough to stand a spoon up in. Reminds me of that hostel we were talking about, actually. Run down, everything weak. Needs a proper overhaul, that place. Oh, Arthur, you and your tea. It’s perfectly alright. And yes, the ‘Seabreeze’ is…tired. That’s putting it politely. I saw some photos Brenda sent - the damp patch in room three is spreading, apparently. Poor Brenda’s doing her best, but she’s only one person. It’s a mammoth task, running a place like that, even a small one. It  is  a significant undertaking. Though looking at the photos, it seems less about a complete overhaul and more about consistent, preventative maintenance. A leaking gutter, ignored, becomes a damp patch. A small crack in the plaster… you know the drill. It’s like teaching, really. Nip things in the bud. Preventative maintenance… sounds a bit posh, doesn’t it, David? Back in my day, you just slapped a bit o’ paint on it and hoped for the best. My dad, he’d fix anything. He had that shop, you know, the butcher’s. Proper hardworking man. Always up at dawn, getting the meat ready. Remember old Mr. Hemmings’ abattoir? Dreadful smell, but a necessary evil. Oh, I remember Hemmings’! It was awful, the smell carried for miles. But your father’s shop… that was a proper community hub, Arthur. Everyone went there. And he insisted on everything being just so – the cuts of meat, the cleanliness… he was a stickler. My own parents had a greengrocery. Similar story. Always grafting. Though Mum always complained about the early mornings. She wasn't built for it. It’s amazing what their generation achieved, isn’t it? Building businesses from the ground up, often with very little. My grandfather was a toolmaker. Absolutely fascinated with engineering. He used to explain how things  worked  to me for hours. That’s probably why I ended up in teaching - trying to instill that curiosity in others. Though sometimes I feel I'm fighting a losing battle with TikTok. TikTok? What in the world’s that? Sounds like some sort of clock. My grandad, he was a carpenter. Built half of Costessey, he did. Properly. Solid oak, everything. None of this chipboard nonsense they have now. And he understood physics, even without a fancy education.

… honestly, the essays this year are just… baffling. I’ve marked twelve already, and I feel like I’m wading through treacle. They just don’t  understand  how to construct an argument. It's less about the content, and more about… the fundamental lack of academic writing skills. Really? That’s rough. I haven't started marking yet, thankfully. Though I did have a quick skim through a few of the submitted drafts during the workshops, and even then, I noticed a bit of a disconnect. It feels like they’re writing how they  think  university essays should be, rather than actually understanding the conventions. Exactly! It’s the ‘tell me what you think’ versus ‘show me  how  you think’ thing. They’re very good at regurgitating information from the lectures, but translating that into a cohesive, critical piece of writing? Forget it. Makes me wonder about their preparation in sixth form, doesn't it? Definitely. Or maybe it's just the jump to university level is bigger than they expect. It certainly was for me. Though, and this is going to sound a bit boastful, my background probably helped. Before I started this gig, I was actually in recruitment for a while. Recruitment? You? That’s…unexpected. I always pictured you straight into academia after your PhD. What sort of recruitment? Primarily, graduate roles. Which, ironically, meant sifting through  loads  of applications – CVs, cover letters, sometimes even mini-essays. It was all about quickly assessing writing ability, communication skills, that sort of thing. You'd be surprised how many bright people can’t articulate themselves well on paper. It’s a real skill, clear writing. That’s fascinating, actually. It explains your very precise feedback - it's almost… clinical in its analysis of their weaknesses. I'm coming at it from a different angle, having spent twenty years teaching fifteen-year-olds to write reports. But even that doesn’t entirely prepare you for the leaps and bounds of expectation at university level. They haven't had the scaffolding, I think. I think you're right about the scaffolding. And the recruitment experience gave me a sort of… shorthand for identifying those foundational issues. You could tell instantly if someone had been taught how to structure a persuasive argument, or if they were just throwing ideas at the wall and hoping something stuck. That’s what I'm seeing a lot of in these drafts.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of reading for this dissertation is  criminal . I swear, Professor Davies is actively trying to break us. Did you lot actually get through all of Foucault this week? I actually  tried  to read it all properly, and now my brain feels like scrambled eggs. It’s just…dense. I’m starting to think a career in retail sounds a lot more appealing right now. Though, knowing my luck, I’d end up having to explain Derrida to someone wanting a new phone charger. You sound like you’re all having a bit of a crisis. I’m Priya, by the way. Although, I can write a pretty scathing essay about the symbolism of a chipped teacup if anyone needs one. That's a surprisingly useful skill, Chloe. My uncle’s got one, too. Proper high-tech, it is. He reckons he can run faster with it than his own leg now! Although he’s probably just showing off.

Right, so then Uncle Barry starts goin’ on about his time in the Falklands again. Honestly, you'd think he single-handedly won the war, the way he tells it. It’s always ‘Me and me mates…’, never ‘We and the lads’. Him and boastin’, honestly. Oh, classic Uncle Barry. My grandad was the same with the Second World War. Every family gathering, it was the same stories. Though, to be fair, grandad  did  see some pretty hairy stuff. But still, repetition is… tedious. What was he sayin’ this time? More about the cold? Not the cold, surprisingly. It was about the logistics! Honestly, the logistics of gettin’ tea bags to the front line. Apparently, that was a critical operation. “Critical, I tell ya!” he kept sayin’. I was tryin’ to explain to him that modern supply chains are a bit more sophisticated now… he just looked at me like I was speakin’ Martian. That's brilliant. He's stuck in his time, isn't he? Speaking of sophisticated, have you seen that article in “Wired” about the new quantum computing breakthroughs? It’s totally mind-bending. I’ve been trying to wrap my head around it all day. “Wired”? Nah, I'm more of a "Stylist" gal myself. More pictures, less…numbers. Though, I did flick through a tech mag at the dentist’s the other day. Something about AI writing scripts for films. Seems a bit daft, doesn’t it? Like, where’s the artistry in that? That’s a really good point. I mean, AI can generate  content , but can it create something truly original? I saw a film the other day – “Everything Everywhere All At Once” – and that was utterly bonkers and brilliant. No AI could have come up with that. It was just…weirdly human. Ooh, I've heard good things about that one! Is it worth a watch, then? I'm lookin’ for somethin’ to watch on Netflix tonight. I’ve been stuck in a rom-com rut lately, need somethin’ that'll properly shake me up. Absolutely worth a watch. Prepare to have your brain scrambled. It's visually stunning too. It’s not a simple watch, though. You gotta pay attention. It's not background noise. Which, frankly, is somethin’ I need after spendin’ all day lookin’ at production schedules. Tell me about it. My conference next month is lookin’ like a proper nightmare.

Honestly, that game was  exhausting . My legs feel like jelly. Though, gotta say, Leo really redeemed himself with that three-pointer at the end. Redeemed is putting it mildly! He keeps suggesting we go to these ridiculously fancy restaurants in London, and then quizzing me on my ‘five-year plan’. Like, chill out, mate, I just finished my masters! Like our lives aren’t valid unless we’re brunching in Shoreditch or queuing for overpriced cocktails. Don’t even get me started. My aunt Carol came down last weekend. Spent the entire time complaining about how ‘quaint’ everything is and asking where the nearest Whole Foods is. Quaint! We have farmers markets, Carol! Actual, real food. It's the assumption that everything outside the M25 is just… backwards. Remember when James’s cousin came down and asked me if we had Uber Eats? Like, yes, we’re living in the dark ages here! It's wild. Though, speaking of wild, did you see that article about the new housing development they’re trying to push through near Winchester? Apparently, it's all luxury flats, completely out of character with the area. Oh, that’s infuriating! I saw something about that.

…and honestly, Dad, the window cleaning is the one thing I  refuse  to outsource. It’s therapeutic, alright? Staring out at the South Downs while giving the glass a good scrub…it clears the head. Though, perhaps it’s a slightly obsessive habit.      Therapeutic, you say? Sounds like a load of bother to me. Back in London, we just let the grime build up. Gave the place character. Besides, you young ‘uns and your obsession with cleanliness…      Oh, don’t start, Dad. Liam's not wrong, it  is  nice to see out the windows without a film of…well, everything. And honestly, a clean flat makes such a difference when we're trying to save money. Less need to replace things if they're properly looked after.      Chloe’s right, dear. A tidy space is a tidy mind. Though, saving money is easier said than done these days, isn't it? Utility bills are just…criminal. Reminds me of when I was working nights as a care assistant, barely scraping by.      They are. We’re looking at a hefty increase next quarter, I think. I was actually going to ask you, Dad, if you’d mind holding onto a bit of the cash from Mum’s birthday card for us? Just until payday. Purely a temporary thing, promise.      Borrowing money from your old man? Haven't changed much, have you, Liam? Though I suppose times are harder now. Alright, alright. How much? Don’t be thinking you can get away with a large sum, mind.      Dad! Don’t make it sound like a loan shark situation. It's just for, like, fifty quid. Just to cover a small shortfall. We'll pay it back as soon as Liam gets paid.      Fifty pounds… that doesn't go very far, does it? It’s terrible what things cost these days. Still, fifty pounds is fifty pounds. Remember when a bag of sweets could keep a child entertained for a whole afternoon? Now it’s five pounds for a handful of… those gummy things.      It's the little things, isn’t it? Speaking of little things, have you tried those spiced nuts I got from that shop in Brighton? They're amazing. Little bags of heaven. Though I'm trying to cut back – cholesterol, you know. Senescence and all that. Trying to aim for a good hundred years, like old Mrs. Higgins down the road.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of data we’re dealing with now is mental. It's not just transcribing anymore, it’s tagging, annotating for sentiment, dialect variations… it's a proper headache. I mean, I knew it'd be more than just listening to people chat, but this is another level. Sounds intense. Still, better than modelling drainage systems in a downpour, I suppose. We had biblical rain at the site in Chelmsford yesterday. Honestly, I was soaked through before I even got out of the van. The whole project's on hold now 'til it dries out. Oh, aye? Chelmsford. Sounds… lovely. No, seriously, that's rough. We've had a bit of drizzle here in Cambridge, nothing compared to that, though. Keeps the tourists away, I suppose. Speaking of which, have you seen house prices around here lately? It's absolutely bonkers. Don’t even  start  me on Cambridge house prices. I was looking at a little flat, just a one-bed, and it was going for half a million. Half a million! Back home in Kent, you'd get a decent house with a garden for that. It's criminal. My dad keeps saying it’s all the London money flooding in. He’s not wrong, is he? It's ridiculous. Honestly, I'm starting to consider moving back up north. Sunderland isn't Cambridge, obviously, but at least you can  buy  a house there. My mam keeps sending me Rightmove links. Trying to lure me back with the promise of reasonably priced brick and mortar. A good mam, that one. I can see the appeal. Though, leaving Cambridge… I’m still fairly new here with the job, you know? And it  is  a nice city, when it’s not being overrun with tourists and ridiculously expensive housing. Aye, it has its moments. I’m just… stressed, I think. Work's demanding, and then you add the cost of living… It just feels like you're constantly treading water. I tried to make a shepherd’s pie last night to cheer myself up, and even  that  stressed me out. Got the wrong type of potato, ended up having to order a takeaway. The shepherd's pie defeated you? That's a new low! What kind of potato did you go for? Maris Piper! I thought they were all-purpose. Apparently not for a proper mash. My cousin, she’s a chef, told me off properly over text.

Honestly, this shift last night was  something  else. Old Mrs. Higgins decided she was convinced the curtains were plotting against her. Spent a good hour assuring her they weren't sentient beings, you know? Oh, bless her. Sounds like a typical night, though, doesn’t it? My nan gets like that with the Alexa sometimes. Thinks it’s listening to her thoughts. It’s quite funny until she refuses to tell it the weather, just in case it uses the information against her. You get that on the care side too, definitely. Mr. Davies last week was convinced the television was broadcasting messages  to  him. Specifically, adverts for mobility scooters were apparently a personal attack on his independence. You just have to roll with it, I suppose. It's exhausting though, isn't it? Exhausting is an understatement, darling. It’s the constant vigilance. And the families. Some are fantastic, genuinely appreciative. Others… well, let's just say they think we’re miracle workers with unlimited time. My feet are still aching from running around. Did anyone see what Sharon was wearing to Carol’s party on Saturday? Oh,  that  dress? The one that looked like it was made of tinsel? Honestly! It was a bit much, even for Carol. She always goes overboard though, doesn’t she? I heard Dave nearly tripped over the train on it while getting to the buffet. I managed to avoid the whole tinsel disaster. Had to work, unfortunately. Always seems to be someone needing something on a Saturday night. Though, old Mrs. Peterson did tell me all about it this morning. Apparently, there was a small dance-off. A dance-off? Seriously? Carol  does  love a good theme. I was thinking of trying to get a bit more time off next month. I’m desperate for a weekend away. Somewhere…quiet. Maybe by the sea. Oh, that sounds lovely, love. You deserve it. I was thinking about maybe a little weekend in Brighton with my sister, but she’s been going on about her hip again. Keeps needing to see Dr. Sharma. He’s a lovely man, but she uses any excuse for attention, if you ask me. Dr. Sharma’s good, isn’t he?
